in writing. − i voted for this resolution because i believe that labour inspection plays an important role in protecting employees’ rights. it is the responsibility of companies to ensure legal working conditions but unfortunately they do not always do so. irregularly employed workers suffer from consequences such as the fear of having an accident or being caught, which in turn affects the productivity of companies and the economy as a whole. we need to win the fight against unsafe working environments. also, in this time of economic crisis, undeclared work has negative consequences for member states’ economies and creates social and financial insecurity. for all these reasons, all member states must commit to taking the necessary measures on this issue at national level.
in writing. - i have endorsed this report with my colleagues from the epp, as we all believe that more must be done to combat the use of undeclared work, which has increased considerably as a result of the economic and social changes of the last decades. the shadow economy is harmful to the economy of a country as a whole, because it affects the quality of products and services, as well as the productivity of companies. it also promotes unfair competition in the single market through the loss of tax revenue as a result of tax evasion and non-payment. the report voted by parliament specifically aims to help labour inspectorates operate more effectively, enforcing workers' rights and preventing abuse by employers.
in writing. - while i agree with the content of the report and the text in many respects, i find the paragraphs calling for the labour inspectorate's intervention in cases of undeclared work involving illegal immigrants to prevent the initiation of expulsion procedures for illegal immigrants to be extremely problematic. that is why i voted against.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which clearly and unequivocally reaffirms the importance of labour inspections in improving working conditions. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's social policy is not distorted by the introduction of new forms of work, such as parttime work, temporary work, or the creation of new jobs.
in writing. − the report's content denounces an insufficient and weak control mechanism towards companies that provide their services in an eu country other than their own; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the member states are able to comply with the directive. these points are acceptable, but the text contains some paragraphs concerning workers from third countries (including illegal immigrants): it shall be specified that the controls carried out by the competent authorities must not result in expulsion proceedings or penalties in the event of irregularities. given the ambiguity of the content, i shall abstain.
in writing. − the european union is increasingly confronted with undeclared work and the shadow economy, which have damaging consequences for the economy as a whole, affecting the quality of products and services, the productivity of firms and promoting unfair competition in the market. we support this report which highlights the role of labour inspection systems in the fight against undeclared work in the eu. at present, in many member states, all forms of action against undeclared work are facing difficulties due to the reduction in funding. to have effective labour inspections, europe needs more than non-binding regulatory instruments: we have a great deal of work to do in this area, and we have to do it in a way that is not too difficult to do. this must start with strengthening fundamental social and labour rights in the single market and a commitment to promoting fair competition and workers' rights. this principle should be enshrined in the primary law of the union by adopting a protocol on social progress, in order to protect fundamental social rights from any adverse impact of national reforms and austerity measures.
in writing. - the so-called 'black' labour is a scourge that affects all the countries of the union, from worker safety to tax evasion. it is a highly sensitive issue that must be combated at community level. of course, inspections by the competent bodies to check that workplaces and workers are in good order are the first step, but the funds for such checks do not seem to be sufficient. the aim of the text is to highlight the role of labour inspection systems in combating undeclared work and to increase the funding for inspection bodies.
in writing. - the economic and social changes of the last few decades are having a major impact on the world of work. the globalisation of the world economy has had a negative impact on traditionally safe and fair employment relationships. subcontracting, outsourcing, precariousness, work intensification and job insecurity are undermining the quality of employment in europe. this deterioration in industrial relations is accompanied by a phenomenon of non-respect for labour law and workers' rights. the european union is increasingly confronted with the problem of undeclared work and the underground economy. i hope that what has been agreed today will be able to remedy the many problems with workers' rights.
in writing. - immediate action is needed to increase the resources needed for labour inspections in the member states, the only way to combat undeclared work, shadow selfemployment and social dumping in the long term. national controls also play an important role in implementing social legislation and ensuring a level playing field in the eu.
mr president, we voted today on a resolution on worker participation in the profits of companies. it is an important first step for worker profit-sharing or ownership of enterprises, towards truly inclusive growth. particularly in times of crisis, employee participation develops a sense of belonging to the company, motivation, pride, internal meritocracy. the following are essential to overcome the conflict between owners and workers: all row in the same direction; the responsibilities, choices and strategies are shared; in particular, redundancies and relocations can be avoided; the continuity of the enterprise is defended and the work is defended. it is therefore important that the commission does everything possible to promote forms of employee participation and to ensure that each member state takes this important step.
mr president, the report by the committee on the work of mr bennion contains, in my view, an excellent proposal which i voted in favour of with great conviction. it calls on the member states to consider introducing measures to promote and encourage companies to allow workers to participate in the profits, but also in the capital, of the companies themselves. this could benefit not only large companies but also and above all small and mediumsized enterprises and the workers themselves, with a benefit in terms of the psychological dimension of the worker's contribution. at present, as the crisis has shown, workers are automatically only participating in the losses of the enterprises, through dismissals, forced transfers, reduction of working hours and so on. it is important, however, to imagine that the worker can feel that he is an active part not only of the company's growth but also of its decline. i believe that this is the way forward and it is no coincidence that the party in which i am active, the new centre right, has just made a proposal to the italian government in this regard. i think that is an important point to be made in this house, which today supports this strategic direction.
in writing. - i am pleased with the vote on what was the first report i have been given the task of drafting since i took up my duties as a member of the european parliament. i was asked by the econ committee to draw up part of the report, the main responsibility of which was with the envi committee. this is an interesting parliamentary initiative which may have important developments in the course of the next parliamentary term. i believe that the identification and definition of a common framework for the activation of employee participation in the activities of enterprises can be an interesting means of reviving european, and especially italian, enterprises, with particular reference to small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. - while the idea of workers' financial participation in the profits of the firm is acceptable, i believe that the bennion report actually goes beyond this aim, laying the foundations for the extension of the german model of joint management of enterprises to the whole of europe: i therefore did not intend to vote in favour of this text.
in writing. - in his laborem exercens, published before the crisis hit the western economies, blessed john paul ii had already denounced the risks to human dignity inherent in the processes of dehumanizing the dimension of work, from a value inherent in the development of the human personality to an intangible good, which can be traded like any other commodity. one of the barriers to this is the forms of employee participation in enterprises, the lighter forms of access to the owner company, the forms of joint management as a result of the company bargaining. the report clearly refers to a specific weltanschauung, that of natural law and the social doctrine of the church, in its historical application of the social market economy. as a popular european, i can only vote in favour. the only caveat, rightly noted in the report, is to ensure that the financial participation of workers is not subtly distorted in order to reduce the cost of labour. it is not by chance that the labour market reforms currently under discussion emphasise these aspects as complementary to the anchoring of a future recovery in a climate of social cohesion and of productivity incentives through flexibility, defined largely at the level of supplementary bargaining.
in writing. − in this resolution, the european parliament urges the member states to open up the employee financial participation (efp) schemes to all workers without any discrimination and taking into account the specific situation of small, medium and micro enterprises. the new european guideline also includes a notice that vet may be a form of employee bonus, thereby facilitating participation in capital or specific bonds, depending on the financial product used and the type of company. there is no doubt that a modern industrial relations system is the essential condition for economic growth, development and social cohesion. where companies (e.g. in germany) have promoted and adopted participation, both in financial and managerial terms, very positive economic and productive results have been achieved. in fact, the direct involvement of employees in the life of the company considerably increases the sense of responsibility, both in those who are in charge of the company and in those who work in the company. the full and direct awareness of the difficulties which may arise from the crisis gives those involved in the enterprise and those who share in it a more penetrating view of the causes which have led to it. the european parliament has a duty to ensure that the european parliament is given the opportunity to express its views on the matter.
in writing. - this topic has its pros and cons and before reading the report i was rather puzzled: while employee participation in the company's profits is an incentive to work better and to feel part of the organization, it could also be an excessive responsibility for someone who does not control the entire production process and therefore cannot, for better or worse, be held responsible for the overall result. let me put it this way: i do not think the worker can be held responsible for the success or failure of the sale of the product he helped to assemble. i also think that the title of the report is rather ideologized: the participation in profits must involve risk-taking and therefore also participation in losses. i must say, however, that my group has been able to put forward the right amendments and the report has changed towards being acceptable to my views.
in writing. - i believe that the financial participation of employees in the profits of a company is an opportunity and a tool that should be further explored and used. it is undeniable that such a measure would make employees more responsible, and they would feel more involved in the dynamics of the company's development. i believe that the old paradigm, that of the opposition between labour and capital, is now considered obsolete, both by history and by economic evolution: the reality is now very different, and the challenges are different. the fate of workers and firms is often already tied in two ways, and economic difficulties and the crisis strike both sides. i think that closer participation and cooperation could be useful, especially in certain areas. i believe that every worker should be proud to participate directly in the fate of a company, that is to say, to share fully in its developments. if they are positive, the worker will also be rewarded, while if they are negative he may perhaps be able to understand better the difficult situation in which a firm may find itself. this does not mean that we are all owners and workers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr bennion's report on the financial participation of employees in the profits of the firm because i believe that the participation of employees in the decision-making process encourages small and mediumsized enterprises and guarantees jobs. in a european union seeking smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, encouraging the financial participation of employees means creating the basis for more lasting relationships within the company itself, ensuring its integrity and boosting its revenues and investments, in essence ensuring stability and smart growth.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth stresses the need for 'inclusive growth' that, among other things, promotes citizens' empowerment through employment, investment in skills, the fight against poverty and the modernisation of labour markets and social protection. employee financial participation (evp) provides a tangible means of developing these issues by involving workers more closely in the decision-making process of the companies in which they work, helping to strengthen good governance and guaranteeing a share of the financial benefits of a successful enterprise. i agree with what has been discussed and presented in this house.
in writing. − i believe that the financial participation of employees in the profits of a company is an essential tool of the strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, involving workers in the decision-making process of the companies in which they work, helping to strengthen good governance. such involvement brings economic benefits to workers, but also training opportunities and a long-term approach to one's job, as such involvement develops a stronger mutual relationship between employee and employer. this is particularly true for smes, where employees may wish to invest in shares of the company, capitalizing on its expansion, while providing greater stability and certainty for the company and its related income. unfortunately europe is still lagging behind on this issue, but i agree that action at union level can be affected by disparities at national level, but i believe that the eu can at least provide some general guidelines and orientations that will facilitate national decision-making. finally, i support the proposal to launch a study on methods of promoting financial participation by employees of companies operating at transnational level, in order to make the european market truly single in this respect too.
in writing. - mr bennion's report aims to highlight the positive role that employee financial participation schemes can play in developing the participation of employees in the governance and financial success of the companies in which they work. in particular, the report highlights a number of observations and recommendations on worker financial participation which can help to define a voluntary framework for advising enterprises, employees, social partners and national authorities on how best to develop and facilitate such participation.
mr president, the crisis that has hit europe in recent years has particularly affected certain categories of citizens who are absolutely vulnerable, such as the unemployed, the disabled, single-parent families and, above all, young people. it also made it clear that flexibility in working life was not always accompanied by the right protections, and that is why we have ended up with a social protection system that is often anchored in old logics and patterns, and which has ended up protecting only employees and has given no guarantee to atypical workers and selfemployed workers. i therefore strongly support this resolution and hope that the commission will work to ensure that the member states reform their social protection systems, with social and pension rights and protection for the so-called 'unsecured'.

in writing. − as a result of the crisis, the production structure of the countries most affected is undergoing a profound transformation: the report rightly denounces the need to adapt our social security systems to the new forms of work. the system of social protection, which was conceived in the light of a fordist model, has now entered a crisis and is threatening to exclude whole generations. it is no secret that many new selfemployed people are more of a necessity (often following the loss of a previous employed job) than a free decision: according to unioncamere, some 50,000 new italian entrepreneurs would have taken this path in 2012. the widespread abuse of selfemployment and precarious work institutions in several member states is also alarming, as is well summarized in points (d), (f), (j) and (k). the call to the member states, within the framework of the union's powers of coordination, to review social security systems, adapting them to the new structures and new ways of exercising selfemployment, represents an investment in preventing the explosion of an unprecedented social crisis, as well as a moral and civil imperative. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which clearly reaffirms the importance of ensuring a social protection system for all, including the selfemployed. the difficult economic situation has already had a negative impact on the social services provided, with a reduction, or at least the risk of reduction, of the funds made available for this purpose. the call is therefore primarily for member states to do more to implement structural reforms and measures to create jobs, while recognising that rights can be fully guaranteed when the economy is functioning and producing wealth. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of unemployment, and it is therefore necessary to adopt integrated strategies and at the same time to make greater efforts to combat undeclared work, which is a real scourge for the economies of certain countries.
in writing. − social security for workers is one of the most important elements of the european social model. the transformation of welfare systems must be able to guarantee social rights on the one hand and adapt them to the changed socioeconomic conditions in europe on the other. in particular, selfemployment (whether parttime or not) is the most important area to work on because of the lack of adequate consideration in many national laws for the specific characteristics and special needs of the selfemployed. in my region, veneto, the very large number of micro and small enterprises has given me a thorough insight into the limits of a system of protection for workers such as the italian one, which is unable to take account of the specific characteristics of selfemployed workers. that is why the resolution is moving in the right direction.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs blinkevičiūtė on the social protection of workers. social protection is at the heart of the european social model and its main function is to promote inclusion and social justice, protect incomes and ensure high quality education and healthcare for all. the text particularly welcomes the recognition of the importance of selfemployment in job creation and calls on the member states to eliminate all measures which discourage its development.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by my colleague on the creation of a european quality label, because i believe that this project can make an important contribution to the protection of small rural areas and the quality of their products. a brand that refers to territorial areas would ensure, on the one hand, greater economic development for regions that focus on the quality of products and, on the other, would act as an incentive for the revival of production. this eliminates the prerequisites for the use of relocation, the consequences of which would affect production and involve a reduction in jobs. it will be essential for companies to cooperate with each other, to grow together and develop their potential, to strengthen their image and territorial identity. new governance strategies aimed at developing the regional brand through collective reorganisation and the creation of partnerships between companies and institutions would also be useful, thus promoting the maximum sharing of projects that enhance the value of local products. the creation of the regional quality label will serve the interests of those who operate within the territorial realities, will facilitate the introduction of quality products into the european market and will undoubtedly highlight the differences in quality and origin.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission proposal on community statistics relating to the trading of goods between member states – intrastat – has a number of important objectives. firstly, the legislative proposal aims to align an existing intrastat regulation with the new institutional context after the lisbon treaty. secondly, the commission is proposing to streamline the structure of the european statistical system by replacing the current reference to the committee for trading of goods between member states, the intrastat committee. furthermore, the commission is proposing to clarify the definition of statistical value. the current definition of this data element in intra-eu trade statistics will be aligned with that in the extra-eu trade statistics. it is also proposed to collect information on the movement of certain non-community goods through the intrastat system. this would ensure the quality and coverage of intra-eu trade statistics. finally, this proposal explicitly enables the voluntary exchange of confidential data between member states’ national statistical authorities. this will improve the data quality and the efficiency of the system of intra-eu trade statistics. it will also serve the permanent need to improve the quality of data and increase the efficiency of the system. it should be noted that the exchanged data shall be used solely for the statistical needs outlined in the proposal. it is a matter of principle that respondents continue to trust the european statistical system. therefore, given the importance of the proposal, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr martin, and the members of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, for their interest in it and the support provided so far. the commission broadly welcomes the draft report and its amendments, in particular those improving or clarifying the proposal and ensuring trust in the european statistical system. however, i should also note that a few of the proposed amendments require further elaboration and discussion. as an example, i could mention the time limitation for voluntary data exchange or free-of-charge data transmission, but i am confident that these issues can be successfully addressed during the trilogues. i am therefore looking forward to receiving your support today for the commission proposal. this would allow us to proceed with further steps and enter into interinstitutional discussions.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to take this opportunity to thank mr martin and all the shadow rapporteurs for the scientific discourse they have given on the problem of new statistics at european level, between the member states. this is a purely technical report, it is not a political report, and i am opposed to making it political and to introducing a debate which would certainly take us off the subject. in essence, commissioner šemeta has said very well: the commission has reviewed the proposed regulation on community statistics of trade in goods between the countries of the european union: a new pyramid structure - the sse - which will replace the old infrastat structure. once this report has been launched, the commission will be able to adopt delegated and implementing acts. and this is what we've been working on: i think that this is a very important point, in the sense that we believe that they can no longer impose costs on governments for this new structure and i believe that this has been transposed, thus ensuring the lowest possible cost for the national authorities. the other amendments which have been tabled and also accepted concern the structure of the statistical system and a better definition of statistical value. i agree with you, commissioner šemeta, partly because there are quantitative and qualitative values and methods in statistics and the absolute value must be all-encompassing, otherwise we risk using different languages between the member states. so i think that all this has been done with a view to improving the quality of european statistics in relation to trade in goods, avoiding excessive and unnecessary trickery which would be a burden on member states and others. one last point, mr president, on the exchange of confidential data: we are very cautious, because we risk creating problems which are not on the agenda, at least not in this report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because public procurement is a very important part of economic activity within the eu, where public procurement and concessions are the most frequent forms of it. the preliminary discussion identified two major obstacles: (a) confirmation of the need for a european initiative to at least arrive at a common definition of concessions and their allocation; (b) the need for a 'light' approach, based on a legislative framework sufficiently robust to avoid interpretations, which does not, however, lead to either detailed regulation of the award of concession contracts or additional administrative costs. in this context, i share the four objectives summarized by the rapporteur: 1) the clarification, reorganisation and simplification of the directive to ensure an effective, readable, coherent and pragmatic legislative framework; (2) the specific nature of the concession in relation to the public procurement and the adaptation of the provisions to its characteristics; (3) the affirmation of the full autonomy of public authorities in choosing the legal framework for their action and the freedom to organise themselves in the performance of their tasks; (4) the maintenance of a fair balance between the need for flexibility and the margin of appreciation of public authorities in their choices and the need for transparency for the equal treatment of economic operators.

in writing. the new european concession directive is, in itself, the main innovation in the whole legislative package on public procurement. although the measure has been weakened in the course of the legislative process, it has the merit of introducing a specific framework for both works and service concessions, which until now had as their normative reference only the principles of the treaty. on the procedural side, the directive does not introduce particularly detailed award procedures and, by adapting them, it recovers some of the provisions already contained in the new procurement directives.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the public procurement market represents almost 20% of the union's gdp. this is precisely why the new legislative package on public procurement is important, because it can have a strong impact on growth, generate new public demand and support a new industrial policy of the union. the new measures include the introduction of new simplification measures, greater openness to participation by smes in tendering procedures, increased use of digital communication in tendering procedures, the introduction of social clauses and the preference for quality criteria in the selection of works and services for tendering over the mere criterion of the lowest price. moreover, more transparency in subcontracting. these are all innovations that meet the needs of enterprises, especially smes.

in writing. - i have given a favourable opinion on the report by my colleague on the award of public contracts, because i believe that the directives need to be modernised, simplifying the rules and amending the criteria for the award of contracts. in a time of economic crisis, i believe it is essential to reach out to the industrial sector and to small and mediumsized enterprises by reducing red tape. too often, excessive bureaucracy is a major obstacle for private operators in the process of filing applications and collecting funds, in effect slowing down investment. this directive will make things easier for businesses by drastically reducing administrative burdens and ensuring better and more transparent access to the public procurement system, in order to increase the competitiveness of our businesses. the member states will have time to transpose the directive and will have to organise themselves as best they can, through their control systems, to ensure transparent management and the proper functioning of the procurement system, which also strengthens the grounds for exclusion for companies that will not comply with obligations towards administrations, workers and the environment.
in writing. − the rules adopted today will finally ensure better value for money when public authorities buy or lease supplies, works or services. the new rules on community public procurement will give breathing space to smes, making it easier for them to submit tenders, with stricter provisions on subcontracting.
in writing. − the public procurement market can foster sustainable growth, employment and social inclusion in europe, but only if the updating of public procurement legislation is able to reach the intersection between regulatory simplification and the identification of sound and effective procedures based on award criteria linked to innovation and sustainability. i agree with the rapporteur that it is possible to include environmental impact, safety requirements, in particular for the assessment of product quality, packaging, instructions for use and life cycle requirements in the technical specifications. i welcome the attention paid to smes, especially through the rules on subcontracting, but i do not entirely agree with the provisions allowing the contracting authority to ask the tenderer to indicate in his tender the possible part of the contract which he intends to subcontract to third parties, since the need for performance may change in the long term. finally, in order to lighten the work of contracting authorities, i believe that all the procedures provided for in the directive should be transposed by the member states and that they should provide the authorities with all the financial and technical means to enable them to adapt to the online public procurement procedure.
in writing. the rapporteur, mr tarabella, believes that the modernisation of the public procurement directives should strike the right balance between simplifying the rules and identifying sound and effective procedures based on innovation and sustainability-related award criteria, thus ensuring greater participation by smes and making public procurement on-line more widespread. i share those reasons and therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - i did not support the tarabella report on the reform of the current public procurement rules for public service providers in the water, energy, transport and postal services sectors. the amendments proposed by the text are decidedly unambitious and do not bring any benefits to smes or the controversial subject of subcontracting.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal on the procurement procedures of public service bodies in the water, energy, transport and postal services sectors, because the text adopted, while simplified and revised, does not affect the ability of public administrations to choose whether and how to use the concession instrument. we have all worked in parliament to ensure that this directive does not lead to excessive privatisation or outsourcing. these are services which play a fundamental role. the directive leaves national authorities free to define these services, their organisation and their financing.
in writing. - as these are particularly sensitive areas of public interest, the incorporation of this proposal into the report on public procurement has enabled a more detailed analysis of the subject under consideration. as regards social aspects, these sectors have a potentially much wider impact on society and the environment and therefore merit particular attention, especially through the introduction of stricter constraints on the transparency of the externalities that contracting entities would cause in the context in which they operate. i particularly appreciate the concept of a socially sustainable production process which ensures respect for workers' health and safety and social standards. i also welcome the introduction of the concept of 'most economically advantageous tender' instead of 'lowest price', which would enable contracting authorities to make the most appropriate choice according to their specific needs. once again, i am pleased with the attention paid to smes, which perform a vital function through subcontracting and generate added value for the european economy along the entire production chain. i think, however, that the contracting authorities should be allowed to choose not to state at the outset how much of the contract they intend to subcontract, since requirements may change during the course of the work.
in writing. − with the final adoption of the new public procurement directives, the european union is about to introduce some significant and positive innovations: the new legislative package has the merit of addressing the issue of public expenditure in the member states, with the aim of renewing the capacity of public demand to pursue growth objectives, based on industrial policy logic. in particular, simplification of procedures, in particular the reduction of contract award times in both open and negotiated procedures and restricted procedures, but also the introduction of new procedures such as innovation partnerships, with a view to using public procurement as a tool to support innovation and research policies, should be welcomed. the new directives also promote greater participation by smes in tendering procedures and reduce the administrative burden of submitting the necessary documentation for participation in tenders.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are in a very serious economic crisis and we cannot afford to make any concessions. if we are talking about public procurement, we must be clear: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. not to mention what's happening in china. this lack of reciprocity cannot be accepted. it's a form of unfair competition. the commission's negotiating powers should be strengthened, and the right rules of a genuinely competitive market should be enforced in a non-discriminatory and equal manner.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the caspary report analysing the regulation on access for goods and services from third countries to the internal market for public procurement in the european union. this legislative proposal will make it possible to exclude from european tenders companies based in countries where the same opportunities for participation are not guaranteed for companies in our territories.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because it will allow european companies to gain easier access to international public procurement markets compared to the access the eu already grants to foreign companies. european commission data show that 85% of the eu's public procurement market is already open to international competition, while european companies can bid for only 32% of public contracts in the us and 28% in japan. the proposal represents an important first step towards the introduction of a new instrument to promote greater reciprocity in access to international public procurement markets. in particular, the report confirms and maintains the degree of openness of the eu public procurement market, with no provisions suggesting protectionist returns; in the event of repeated and serious discrimination against european suppliers in third countries, provide the european commission with a mechanism to restrict their access to the eu market; it introduces minimal bureaucratic burdens, with no financial or organisational implications. at the same time, the proposal, by providing the european commission with legal instruments, will make it possible to strengthen the competitive position of european industries at global level, while fully complying with international rules.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation on access for goods and services from third countries to the public procurement markets. i generally agree with the idea of preventing non-european companies from competing for public contracts, unless their home country allows eu companies to do the same. i believe that this instrument, which will be used with the scrutiny of the european commission, will serve to strengthen its role in trade negotiations with third countries.
in writing. - it is now clear to everyone that we must avoid allowing non-eu companies to compete for public contracts worth more than eur 5 million unless their home country allows our companies to do the same. only in this way will it be possible to strengthen the eu's position in trade negotiations with third countries.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation on access for goods and services from third countries to the eu's internal market for public procurement and on procedures to support negotiations on access for eu goods and services to the public procurement markets of third countries is the result of a compromise text which represents an important step towards the introduction of a new instrument allowing greater reciprocity in access to international public procurement markets. the greatest risk in europe is represented by the protectionist policies of many of the eu's major trading partners, which in effect restrict access to their own public procurement markets. european commission data show that 85% of the eu's public procurement market is already open to international competition, while, for example, european companies can only bid for 32% of public contracts in the us and 28% in japan. i voted in favour because i believe that parliament should give a strong signal of the opening of negotiations with the council, and thus also challenge the international community to commit itself to the eu, by opening up procurement markets, boosting the competitiveness of european companies and ensuring a balanced liberalisation of trade.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of this measure as it lays down the rules for access of goods and services from third countries to the european public procurement market on the basis of reciprocity. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a regulation on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. finally, article 1 states that the regulation applies only to contracts above the community threshold and that the goods and services 'covered' and 'uncovered' are defined precisely.
in writing. - i believe that this act is the right compromise between defending european operators in the global procurement market and achieving a level of fair competition with foreign operators. its purpose is not to prevent access to the european contract market for goods and services from third countries. on the contrary, it must encourage their entry, provided that this is done on a level playing field with the offer of european operators. i also fully support the adoption of measures to open a dialogue with those countries which have protectionist rules on access to the procurement market, in order to ensure that european operators who decide to participate in tenders in those countries are not disadvantaged at the outset. i am referring, for example, to the buy local clauses in the united states or the strong restrictions in brazil or china. in this respect, i think the proposal is well balanced, since, contrary to what some colleagues believe, it will not provoke retaliation from the eu's trading partners, but will rather encourage them to adopt more liberal measures so that their operators are not restricted or denied access to the huge and rich market that the eu represents.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to include the acquisition of the right to vote and stand as a candidate in elections to the european parliament. this proposal, put forward by the european commission in march 2012, was the result of a long reflection, supported by the entire european industry, on the protectionist policies put in place by many of the eu's major trading partners to restrict access to their public procurement markets. european commission data show that 85% of the eu's public procurement market is already open to international competition, while, for example, european companies can only bid for 32% of public contracts in the us and 28% in japan. it was therefore necessary to develop a new instrument to allow european companies to gain easier access to international public procurement markets compared to the access that the eu already grants to foreign companies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, pollen is a natural constituent of honey and not an added ingredient. to classify pollen as an ingredient means, first of all, to affect the reputation of this product, which is clearly a natural product. but there would also be negative economic and employment consequences for the beekeeping sector. so no to the increase in production costs to do unnecessary additional testing in addition to labelling charges. there would only be a decrease in consumption and no advantage for the defence of native pollen. there are far more serious problems: firstly, the use of pesticides which pose serious risks to the life of bees. bees are the alarm bell of the loss of biodiversity in our countryside: protecting them is essential for the survival of ecosystems, including human ones.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today we have witnessed a colossal fraud against the citizens of europe. today, the issue is not the labelling of pollen as an ingredient, but the exclusion of the obligation to be informed about a product which is natural today but may not be so tomorrow, because of the massive presence of gmos. today, every farmer is free to use genetically modified seeds, and bees can take and pollinate those products. if, on the other hand, the lepage measure, which parliament adopted by an overwhelming majority, had been approved by the council, we would now have the opportunity to safeguard biodiversity and also to safeguard certain production areas free of gmo pollen. not asking for labelling requirements for the presence of gmos above the regulatory limit is a big scam.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the proposal will allow the commission to amend the technical characteristics of the names, descriptions and definitions of the products in question. therefore, the commission proposal, by allowing a change in the essential elements, falls outside the scope of delegated acts as defined by the treaty. the rapporteur also amended the period during which the power to adopt delegated acts may be conferred on the commission. this period has been changed from an indefinite period to a five-year period which can be tacitly extended. the amendment takes parliament's standard wording on delegated acts.
in writing. - i voted to consider pollen an ingredient . my position is against the use of gmos and i regret to point out that there are european countries which use genetically modified organisms. although there are more than 50 different types of honey in italy - a real production of excellence - we are still forced to import more than half of our production. i therefore believe that it is essential to ensure consumer protection by indicating the presence of gmos on the label. unfortunately, today's vote does not go in that direction. we shall then see what position emerges at the trilogue.
in writing. the content of the report concerns the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending council directive 2001/110/ec on honey. i am voting in favour because i agree with the text, which makes it clear that pollen is not an ingredient in honey but a component.
in writing. - beekeepers and honey producers fear that the position expressed in the envi commission could seriously damage the sector. we cannot ignore the position of the main players in this chain who tell us that classifying pollen as an ingredient will not benefit the sector. the pollens are a natural constituent of honey, and any other approach would be a scientific error and would lead to serious problems for the industry. there would be no advantage for the protection of native pollen and a mismatch would be caused for the honey product, which would be subject to labelling charges below the threshold currently provided for by community legislation. not to mention the increased costs of sampling and labelling honey.
in writing. − the report on the revision of the honey directive (2001/111/ec) raised several problems, mainly as a result of the orientation of the envi vote on the classification of pollen as an ingredient, rather than a natural constituent, of honey. the main concerns were the interests of small local beekeepers, who would be penalised if the house upheld the approach expressed by parliament following the ruling of the european court of justice. the current wording of the directive, as well as the commission's initial proposal, considers pollen to be a natural constituent of honey. a different approach would have led to a mismatch for the honey product, subject to labelling charges below the threshold currently provided for by community legislation and to an increase in sampling and labelling costs. for these reasons i supported and voted in favour of the rapporteur's position, whose motivation i shared was to protect small producers from an incoherent approach, which would have led to a sharp decline in the consumption (both direct and indirect) of italian honey, with direct repercussions in terms of employment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to ensure that honey is also covered by a set of rules which define pollen as a natural component of honey rather than an ingredient. this means that genetically modified pollen must be labelled if it yields more than 0.9% of the honey. the ingredient/constituent dilemma arose because of the labelling implications for each option. if pollen is still considered a 'constituent', the genetically modified pollen present would not need any labelling. this is because the gmo rule requires that only the genetically modified content in quantities exceeding 0.9% be indicated on the label of the finished product. since natural pollen reaches a threshold of around 0,5% per consignment of honey, it could never exceed the labelling threshold. i fully share the parliament's position on this issue, since it has decided to take a stand against gmos, in favour of quality agricultural products which characterise the european market and certain european regions in particular, promoting high quality standards, with an eye to the vast agricultural component of the european economy.
in writing. - mr girling's report concerns the revision of the so-called honey directive (2001/111/ec). the italian and european industry in the sector, together with beekeepers, expressed serious concern before the vote if the plenary session had confirmed the orientation emerging in the envi committee with regard to the classification of pollen as an ingredient, and not as a natural constituent, of honey. the current wording of the directive, as well as the initial proposal of the european commission, consider pollen as a natural constituent of honey. a different approach would be a scientific error in the first place and would lead to a number of problems for the sector, including a sharp decline in the consumption (both direct and indirect) of italian honey, with direct repercussions in terms of employment.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as the representative of the council and the representatives of the commission have pointed out, there are rules, there are abuses and violations of the rules on free movement. i would remind you that under these rules a european citizen can go to any of the other 27 countries, but he must not be a burden on public assistance and must have a minimum income. often these conditions are not met and nobody reacts, enforcing the relevant rules. in italy, the country where i was elected, we have long since accepted, although we have no moratorium, many citizens, especially romanians, especially of a particular strain, who are not registered on the labour lists, so they do not look for work and live mostly on social assistance. we demand that these abuses be stopped and that european rules be respected.

answer to a blue-card question. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have spoken about bulgarians and romanians who are of course european citizens. but the italian people don't care: they're looking for work and they can't find it, and knowing that people come from far away to occupy that place, they don't like it. i say this: there are too many unemployed, too many elderly people who cannot even afford to buy medicine, and people from other countries who want it now. i say this, this is the reality and we must accept it now.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, to call into question the principle of free movement today is not only unhistorical but also absurd. the free movement of persons is a modern right of citizenship and it is surprising that it is being called into question by political sectors which have always been theorists of the most unbridled liberalism and yet, when they speak of the labour market, they even foreshadow a protected, if not autarchic, condition of the same. you have to convince yourself: freedom of movement is important because it is an extraordinary economic lever: there's no way to compete in the global marketplace if you don't also have rules that are enforced and that people who work, and even when they're just citizens, are protected by their communities because it ensures social cohesion, it reduces conflict and it increases participation. so it's a good thing we have freedom of movement.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, european citizenship is closely linked to national citizenship - without one there is no other - and it is an achievement on the road to integration. european citizenship is not an autonomous value, because it cannot be acquired without national citizenship. today we are witnessing too much easy acquisition of national citizenship, which is detracting from european citizenship. while migrants seeking to save their lives are faced with the difficulties that member states impose in obtaining asylum, there are grants of national citizenship, which would also become european, in return for costly fees. it is inconceivable that citizenship can be reduced to the status of a commodity and put up for sale as such. we must, with due respect for national states, establish transparent rules which protect us from the risk of creating new opportunities for criminal and terrorist organisations and which enable us to avoid creating further inequalities between richer and poorer people.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, citizenship has always been a hot topic. in many countries there is a debate, often linked to the topic of immigration, about how citizenship is acquired: does one become a citizen by birth or by staying or residing in the territory of a state? it is the old question of the ius soli or the ius sanguinis, on which public opinion is habitually divided. so, is it jus soli or jus sanguinis? but because we never cease to be amazed, today we learn that there is also the ius pecuniae, that is, the possibility of becoming citizens of a state because you have money to buy what is normally acquired by identity, passion, desire to belong to a community. today the socialist government of malta tells us that citizenship is a commodity, a tax paid to obtain a passport, as if it were a stamp. that is why i agree with commissioner reding that we must reject this method and call on the maltese government to step back, because there is no right that can be marketed. we have worked hard to build our national states, often at great personal sacrifice, and it has taken decades to build and launch the european project. maybe we just wasted time? maybe an auction would have been enough to grant citizenship? i believe that the history behind us points us in the right direction. we are not opening a door through which not only a plethora of unknowns will penetrate but above all a legal monster which risks putting our european construction and our own national states in crisis.

will all be called to account should we fail.

member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, the european commission shares the view, expressed by several groups, that homelessness represents one of the worst forms of poverty and social exclusion and has devastating consequences for the people themselves and for society as a whole. in recent years poverty in europe has risen, mainly in the more peripheral countries and regions, reaching unprecedented levels among those who are more vulnerable, such as the homeless. the rise of poverty has also affected wider layers of society: young people, migrants and families with children. while planning and implementing policies confronting homelessness remains a matter of primarily national competence, the commission fully supports the efforts of the member states in this domain. the eu respects and promotes the right to social and housing assistance under the charter of fundamental rights to combat social exclusion and poverty. the social investment package presented by the commission in february 2013 calls on the member states to eradicate homelessness in a sustainable way by targeting the very different causes of homelessness; implementing comprehensive, preventive, housing-led homelessness policies; and revising their practices on eviction. the package and its dedicated staff working document provide guidance on core elements of homelessness strategies and good practices to foster efficient policy-making in the member states. we will further disseminate this guidance in the forthcoming period by means of a brochure, among other things. strategies to tackle homelessness should not be limited to the provision of crisis interventions through shelter-based approaches. to address street homelessness, shelters are an immediate, but only a transitory, solution. studies show that shelter-based approaches are costly, and they do not lead to getting homeless people out of their situation in a sustainable manner. instead, member states should pursue long-term, housing-led approaches, in other words they should make a serious effort rapidly to re-house homeless people and prevent the loss of permanent housing. we also need better coordination between housing policy actors and housing providers and more engagement with private sector actors to boost the amount of affordable housing available, for example by establishing social rental agencies. the commission is also very attentive to the interactions between state aid rules and housing policies. in the context of active inclusion strategies, specific attention is, moreover, being paid to accompanying measures ensuring access to good-quality social and health services. the social investment package calls upon the member states to spend european structural and investment funds in a more strategic way. these funds are available to improve housing outcomes, and housing remains a funding priority for the 2014-2020 financial framework. the european regional development fund may, for instance, finance integrated housing interventions and energy-efficient housing renovations. the european social fund can complement such integrated investments and can fund enhanced access to quality social services. through the progress programme, the commission finances innovative social projects such as housing first europe, which has delivered evidence that homelessness can be successfully addressed through the re-housing of long-term homeless people. for the period 2014-2020, eur 3.5 billion has been allocated to the recently- adopted fund for european aid to the most deprived to provide non-financial assistance to the most deprived people and explicitly address the food deprivation of homeless people, combined with activities aimed at their social inclusion. we are also aware that we need better-quality, comparable data on housing, and that we should deepen our knowledge of homelessness and of its multiple root causes through eu-wide analysis. to this end, the commission launched a pilot project on the right to housing, which will look into the link between housing evictions and homelessness. in the same vein, this year we will start developing, together with the oecd, a comprehensive database on social policies for housing. we also cooperate with the dublin foundation to monitor how housing quality influences social outcomes. the commission encourages and supports exchanges on inclusive housing policies through the social open method of coordination and by organising thematic events. for instance, last november, we set up a workshop on integrated strategies for re-housing homeless people in the framework of the annual convention of the european platform against poverty and social exclusion. the commission is committed to working with experienced partners at european, national, regional and local level to support the member states in preparing and further developing such national strategies. finally, i would underline that the effectiveness of homelessness-related provisions can also be addressed in the commission’s monitoring exercise within the framework of the european semester. member states are therefore encouraged to report on their homelessness strategies in their national reform programmes. in this connection, the commission has the opportunity to assess and, if necessary, to make proposals for a country-specific recommendation. i am looking forward to hearing the views of the parliament.

in writing. − i believe that the eu must start to have a coherent, informed and forward-looking policy on the authorisation of gmos for cultivation. at the moment, the picture is quite varied: the european legislation leaves it to the member states to decide, but we have a european authority to decide (the efsa) and, above all, we have divided the decision into two parts, one on environmental effects and the other on the effects of food on humans. so it turns out that sometimes we let a man eat what we don't want the insects to eat so as not to disturb the ecosystem. so we import products that put our companies out of business and we don't allow them to grow the same products. in protest at this incoherent attitude, i voted against this resolution.

in writing. - i am voting in favour of this resolution because it is widely established that the genetically modified maize 'pioneer 1507' should not be marketed for cultivation at all, because of its insect-resistant pollen which could harm butterflies and moths, as also confirmed by the european food safety authority. this variety is also resistant to the herbicide glufosinate, which is considered toxic for reproduction in europe and therefore not authorised beyond 2017. the methods of assessing the risks of genetically modified products do not yet allow us to guarantee the safety of these products for human health and the ecosystem, particularly in the long term. my opposition to the marketing of gm products is a clear response to the fears of a large part of the european public, who still have many fears about genetically modified food. my vote is a clear call to the council to reject the commission's proposal and to the commission to refrain from proposing new varieties of gmos and from renewing previous authorizations until the risk assessment methods have been substantially improved.

in writing. - as of 1 january this year, the last transitional barriers to the free movement of bulgarian and romanian workers within the union have been removed, effectively completing a process which had been under way for some time. the fear in some member states that this last provision will be dropped is a good indication of the reality of things, which is unfortunately quite different from what the usual well-meaning people want to portray. the countries that make up the european union are very different from each other in many respects, especially economic and social: it is obvious that a citizen who earns 500 euros a month in his own country would welcome the prospect of moving to earn twice or three times that amount and benefit from a very different social security system. there are many cases of so-called 'tourism for profit', and i also tabled a question on this subject with some colleagues from my group, but it was not accepted: our social security and health care systems are collapsing, and they certainly cannot bear the further, devastating impact of foreign nationals who want to exploit this opportunity. if certain safeguards are not in place, free movement can thus be a dangerous boomerang, threatening to undermine peaceful coexistence.
in writing. − i am voting in favour of the european parliament resolution of 16 january 2014 on respect for the fundamental right of free movement within the eu. the right to free movement, in addition to being one of the four fundamental freedoms of the union, is an essential element of european integration directly linked to citizenship of the union. the benefits of the free movement of eu mobile workers for the development of the host country are visible across europe, particularly in the health, agriculture and construction sectors; mobile workers are net contributors to the economies and budgets of host countries. according to a study by the european commission, mobile workers pay more into the host country's budget in the form of taxes and social security contributions than they receive in benefits. for these reasons i support the position taken by some european leaders who are calling for changes and restrictions to the free movement of citizens and i reject completely any proposal to set a ceiling on the number of eu migrants. in voting in favour of this resolution, i therefore call on the commission and the member states to ensure that union law is strictly applied, so as to ensure that all eu workers enjoy equal treatment and are not discriminated against.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal because i believe that each member state must respect the treaties and the law of the union, in particular with regard to the four fundamental freedoms, the pillars on which the single market is based. nevertheless, i believe that there are indeed cases where national social systems are the victims of fraudulent behaviour by european citizens who want to enjoy public benefits through so-called 'welfare tourism'. however, breaking the word given by a government and a nation cannot be considered the right solution to the problem. i therefore support the general message of this resolution. european citizens have the right to equal treatment and non-discrimination in access to employment, employment and working conditions, pay, dismissal and social and tax benefits, thus ensuring fair competition between businesses. it is the task of the national supervisory authorities to check for fraud against welfare systems and to take action against those found guilty. finally, i share the call to tackle the problem at its root by committing ourselves to combating poverty-driven migration within the eu.

in writing. - i have decided to support this resolution because it is about defending one of the greatest achievements of the union, european citizenship. unfortunately, in some member states there are situations where eu citizenship is sold directly or indirectly to third-country nationals, mostly linked to an economic return in the form of investment in that country, even though the citizens in question do not meet any residence requirement. these mechanisms have a negative impact on european citizens, on the member states and on the union as a whole, since they undermine mutual trust between states, risk being the forerunners of market distortions and, last but not least, they are detrimental to the rights of european citizens deriving from citizenship, by undermining the very essence of it. i fully understand that the letter of the treaties states that citizenship is a matter for the exclusive competence of the member states, but in voting this resolution i feel obliged to join the chorus of voices calling on the commission to evaluate the various national citizenship programmes and to formulate guidelines to steer the action of the states towards european values and law.
