declaration on the resumption of the european parliament session adjourned on thursday 16 january 2014
the agenda includes the report by mr bernhard rapkay on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on promoting the free movement of citizens and businesses by simplifying the acceptance of certain public documents in the european union and amending regulation (eu) no 2014/2012 (com (2013) 0228 c7-0111/2013 2013/0119 (cod).
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report which has been presented to us is an excellent report because it tackles and solves some of the most sensitive problems which people in this part of the world are facing on a daily basis today. freedom of movement is called into question, it is hindered when bureaucracy puts its needs in contrast with those of people who, on the other hand, have to live in sometimes difficult, uncomfortable conditions every day, which are linked to the fact that they live in one country having been born in another, or that they have histories, relationships, even family ones, much more complex than those that were invaded in the past. so, to lighten the bureaucracy, to simplify these processes is very important to give europe a boost. we must ensure that european citizens feel part of a dream and not victims of a bureaucracy that stifles them and makes them experience the birth of the european union no longer as an extraordinary opportunity for growth and placement in the global world, but even as a painful, tiring and difficult condition to bear every day. this is why it has been so important to reduce red tape and shift the burden of costs from citizens to administrations. the citizens, in their capacity as users of public services, must feel rewarded, they must feel free and we have done everything necessary to make that happen. of course, the individual points could have been resolved in one way rather than another, the mediations could have been different from those which were presented, but in my view what counts is the whole of the proposal, and the whole is largely positive, it goes in the right direction, it can give the european union the condition that is missing so that the citizens can live it again for what has been from the beginning an extraordinary dream and not a burden or a constraint.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to draw the commissioner's attention to two negative points which i hope will be corrected in the vote and which concern mr karim's report. there is this reinforcement of the red card which threatens to distort the idea of subsidiarity, we cannot go from one extreme to the other. the risk is that national states and their parliaments will once again be the exclusive owners of many rules which should instead be managed through the joint committee of the european parliament and the european institutions. the second theme concerns the fundamental rights of working people. i have nothing to add to that. i would like to emphasize one point. there is an instrumental use of the size of the small and medium-sized enterprise. when we talk about people and their fundamental rights, it does not matter whether they work in a small or a large company. to make distinctions on this matter is to introduce divisions among people without any justification.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the shirt i am wearing is the symbol of two brothers suffering from muscular dystrophy, the biviano brothers, who have been living in a tent outside montecitorio in rome for seven months in protest, demanding to be treated with professor vannoni's stamina method. i immediately took an interest in the matter, including the european commission, which acted with good sense, confirming the possibility for member states to use the stamps even without specific authorization. this was to clear the field of detractors, that is, those who argued that europe should ban these practices. it is compassionate care, the only source of relief and improvement for the sick who use it. i 've met several patients and their families: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. i want to bring the hope of these people to europe. getting treatment is their right, not a crime. no more polemics and personal attacks, let's think about their well-being and health.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i do not think that anyone in this house is in favour of any form of discrimination, and i think that should also apply to so-called positive discrimination, which is and remains discrimination and therefore unacceptable. i honestly don't see why gays, lesbians or transgender people should be granted special and specific rights. the right to equality and equal treatment must apply to all without any discrimination, either one way or the other. this report is also a clear violation of national prerogatives, indicating that the commission should even make proposals on the mutual recognition of same-sex marriages a priority. as i have already emphasized many times, marriage is only between two people of different sex, for the purpose of procreation, as the same etymological origin of the word says. i therefore call on all those who are against all discrimination to vote tomorrow in favour of the alternative proposal which i have tabled on behalf of the efd group and which seeks to guarantee the rights of all, not just those of the powerful homosexual lobby, which is very active and present in this parliament.
member of the commission. - madam president, i would like to thank you and the rapporteur, mr zwiefka, for the report on the eu justice scoreboard. i thank parliament for its support for the commissionʼs efforts to take this exercise forward. as the report points out, effective civil, commercial and administrative justice is fundamental to the business environment. it is also fundamental to the effective implementation of eu law everywhere in europe and helps foster mutual trust in the european justice area. this is why improving the quality, independence and efficiency of justice systems has become part of the eu-wide priorities in the european semester. in 2013, 10 member states were issued with recommendations on improving their justice systems. these recommendations were made by the commission on the basis, notably, of the findings of the first justice scoreboard, and were endorsed by the member states. this exercise is not a beauty contest. the aim of the eu justice scoreboard is to provide objective, reliable and comparable data on the quality, independence and efficiency of the national justice systems. to be credible, this exercise needs to ensure equality of treatment between all member states. that is why we look at all member states from the same perspective. i can assure you that the commission is impartial and pays particular attention to respecting fully the rich and varied legal traditions in europe. i note with interest your recommendations for the future development of the justice scoreboard. it is indeed an evolving tool. i am confident that we will improve the scoreboard gradually, but it is important to ensure that any developments are based on reliable information. one of the challenges for this exercise is the access to data. member states have those data in their administrations. i therefore fully support parliment’s call to the member states to collect the relevant data and make them available to the commission. in this context, and in order to enhance the information flow, we have asked member states to designate two contact points at expert level, one from the ministry of justice and one from the judiciary. the first meeting of these contact persons took place in december, to put in place good practices on data collection. the justice scoreboard will continue to be fed by a plurality of sources. our cooperation with the european commission for the efficiency of justice will continue in 2014. it remains essential, however, that member states themselves make this cooperation possible by providing timely and good-quality data. with parliamentʼs support, future annual justice scoreboards will continue to assist member states in improving their justice systems, for the benefit of citizens and businesses everywhere in europe.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 4 february 2014. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by elisabeth schroedter, on behalf of the committee on regional development, on the local and regional consequences of the development of smart grids (2013/2128 ((ini)) (a7-0019/2014).
member of the commission. - president, honourable members, i would like to thank the rapporteurs, ms schroedter and also ms ulvskog, for the very thorough work on this report and the suggestions on cohesion policy investment in smart grids. the commission is already working along the lines of several of the main recommendations of the report. going beyond the 20-20-20 target poses a serious challenge which will require further transformation of the energy system, continuous research and innovation and radically novel solutions. as you know, the new cohesion policy period just starting now is more result-oriented and follows a more targeted approach, focusing on fewer priorities and translating the euro 2020 strategy into concrete investment in member states and regions. in this context, cohesion policy is placing even further emphasis on supporting investment linked to the energy targets of the eu. for the period 2014-2020, there will be a significant concentration of efforts on supporting the shift towards a low-carbon economy in all sectors – that is a large focus in renewable energy, energy efficiency and smart grids at the distribution level, as well as sustainable urban mobility and research and innovation in these areas. this will lead to significantly increased amounts for cohesion policy, sustainable energy investments over 2014-2020, representing more than a doubling of the current amount. one investment area will be smart grids, which will be the backbone of the future decarbonised power system. they will enable improved energy efficiency and the integration of vast amounts of renewable energy. the eu is still in the early stages of the actual deployment of smart grids. despite a couple of good examples, there is a considerable gap between actual and optimal investments in europe, which can only be partly explained by the current economic downturn. investors are still struggling to find the optimum model for sharing costs and benefits along the value chain. there are also still some uncertainties regarding whether consumers will embrace these new technologies, how to choose cost-effective technologies and which technical standards should apply to smart grids in the future. public investments in local and regional smart grid pilot projects will substantially help to remove existing technical and non-technical uncertainties associated with the full deployment at national and eu level. in this context, the development of urban sustainable energy action plans and mobility action plans should be encouraged and supported as part of broader low-carbon and urban development strategies. together with the other actors and stakeholders, regions and cities can work to find local tailored solutions, as the covenant of mayors has clearly illustrated. the use of financial instruments for sustainable energy investments, in particular in the urban context, will be further encouraged. they represent a resource-efficient way of deploying cohesion policy resources in the pursuit of the europe 2020 objectives. in addition to cohesion policy investment in smart grids – which we will thus focus on the distribution level – smart grids may also have access to financial support from the connecting europe facility under which an amount of almost eur 6 billion will be made available for improving the trans-european energy infrastructure for the period 2014-2020. in 2012, the commission started the process of identification of potential smart grid projects of common interest in the context of the smart grids task force. such projects need to involve at least two member states. the assessment of two smart grid projects, green-me, which is france and italy, and the north atlantic green zone, uk and ireland, has been concluded positively. both projects are now on the list of projects of common interest and could potentially benefit from support from the connecting europe facility. to maximise european added value, member states and the commission have to ensure that cohesion policy interventions are planned in close cooperation with the support provided from the connecting europe facility, so as to ensure complementarity, avoid duplication of efforts and ensure the optimal linkage of different types of infrastructure at local, regional and national level, as well as across the union. the horizon 2020 research and innovation programme also includes activities to facilitate the development of smart grids. the report mentions several challenges which must be addressed in order to achieve a smarter energy system in the eu regions, and in particular regulatory and legal challenges and challenges linked to data protection and privacy. the commission agrees on the need for consumers to have access and power of decision over the use of their metering and personal data, and for lifting any concerns for data protection and privacy in smart grid environments. in this respect, the commission has already given due attention to the subject in its recommendation on preparations for the roll-out of smart metering systems, setting clear guidelines for member states on data protection, privacy and security on the preparation for the smart metering roll-out. moreover, the commission is currently working with smart grid stakeholders on the development of a data protection impact assessment template and on best available techniques for smart metering and appropriate security measures for the smart grid. the commission has also proposed the reform of the existing data protection legislation, striving to achieve maximum protection with minimum red tape. the roll-out of smart metering and smart grid systems indeed has regulatory implications, for both energy and telecommunications sectors, and calls for a reflection on viable market options. the respective discussion was initiated in the 2012 internal energy market communication, and this will be a focus area for the commission in the next months. in shaping this new open, competitive and transparent retail market, we need to incentivise network operators to invest in new technologies and lay out clear roles and responsibilities for market actors; facilitate the access for new entrants and new business opportunities. finally, the commission recognises that timely development of standards is crucial for the market uptake of smart grid-related technology and has therefore issued specific mandates in recent years to all three european standardisation organisations. the commission has been closely following and coordinating the related activities via the smart grid task force. the report on local and regional consequences of smart grids is indeed very timely. it stresses the importance of networking between regions and smart energy systems and the importance of sharing knowledge in this area. the commission will continue to facilitate cooperation between regions and to support the exchange of experience and good practices in the area of sustainable energy.

i have to say, madam president, small farms in agriculture are important, and i thank mr siekierski for presenting this report. the common agricultural policy certainly still pays too little attention to small farms. and even after this reform, which we have just decided on, it will still be the case that a quarter of the largest farms will receive three quarters of the premiums in the first pillar of the common agricultural policy. and i think that's an unfair distribution. it is also not right to equate small farms with subsistence farming. i come from a region where there are many small farms, but these small farms are normally involved in the market, producing products which are then sold throughout italy and europe, because these farms are organised in cooperatives and producer organisations and are therefore successful on the market. we should also take account of this aspect of small farms and give special support to this association of small farms!
member of the commission. - madam president, we thank parliament for this report on the future of small agricultural holdings. small farms certainly do play an important role in our agricultural sector and rural areas as they create employment, contribute to dynamic rural communities and deliver public goods. this is why the new common agricultural policy (cap) that was approved at the end of last year clearly pays special attention to the problems of small farmers. first let me speak about the first pillar. the new cap offers the member states the possibility of applying a specific support scheme for small farmers: this scheme will replace all direct payments to small farmers with a lump-sum payment. this new payment will reduce costs and the administrative burden for small farmers by easing obligations relating to applications for support, to cross-compliance and to controls. additionally, member states may also tilt payments towards smaller holdings with the new ‘redistributive payment’ which gives a supplementary payment for the first hectares of the holdings. with the new cap, we are also encouraging cooperation among farmers with a new legal framework to facilitate the recognition of producer organisations and support financially their creation. certainly, farmers should work and sell together and thereby gain scale, reduce costs and access the market. cooperation amongst them will be a key step in adapting to the changing economic environment. secondly, on rural development, member states can decide to include some specific actions for small farmers within their rural development programmes. there is, for instance, the possibility of including a thematic sub-programme for small farms or additional business start-up aid for the development of small farms. there is also the possibility of granting payments addressed to those farmers eligible for the small farmers scheme who permanently transfer their holding to another farmer. furthermore, small farmers can benefit from the support for investment in the creation and development of non-agricultural activities, investment in physical assets, participation in quality schemes, and many other actions under rural development. finally, the new rural development policy will also offer many possibilities for helping farmers to sell their products directly to consumers, or at least to become involved in short supply chains and ‘local’ markets. with this set of complementary instruments, we are giving the member states the possibility of supporting modernisation and the creation of added value by small farmers, as well as facilitating their access to the market. we are encouraging member states to exploit all these possibilities in order to support, to their very best, these key beneficiaries of the cap.

the agenda includes the report by pablo arias echeverría, on behalf of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, on an integrated parcel delivery market for the growth of e-commerce in the eu (2013/2043(ini)) (a7-0024/2014).
member of the commission. - madam president, on behalf of my colleague michel barnier, let me first of all thank the rapporteur mr arias echeverría and the committee on the internal market and consumer protection (imco) for their valuable contribution to our common action for the development of the digital single market in europe. just two years ago, the commission launched an ambitious action plan on e-commerce and online services. its objectives are to adapt the off-line environment to evolving on-line realities, and to foster on-line opportunities for consumers and service providers. sixteen actions were tabled by the commission, in many sectors – e.g. modernisation of electronic payment services, net neutrality and copyright. one other important initiative concerned parcels delivery. these activities have a direct impact on our daily lives as consumers or entrepreneurs. delivery is critical to facilitating e-commerce trade. it is a key element for building trust between sellers and buyers. eu consumers increasingly look for online purchases, notably across borders. however, around 45% of consumers declare that they worry about the delivery in cross-border transactions. for e-retailers, and most notably smes, the performance and affordability of the delivery system is a key driver of their business model. yet more than 50% of them consider cross-border delivery to be an obstacle. in short, to further promote the growth of e-commerce, we have to make sure that the off-line structure on which it is built works at its best. we therefore need a delivery system that meets the expectations of both consumers and smes; a delivery system that works smoothly to facilitate their daily lives and businesses; a delivery system that will generate greater confidence in e-commerce. a broad consensus emerged among all parties concerned on the issues identified and on the urgent need to address them, after the public consultation launched at the end of 2012. on that basis, and considering the reflexions set out in parliament’s report, the commission adopted a roadmap in december 2013. this roadmap sets out further actions to address the delivery problems and challenges faced by consumers and e-retailers. the roadmap attributes specific tasks and roles to the various stakeholders – delivery operators, e-retailers and member states – via their regulatory and competition authorities. those actions are focusing on three main objectives: first, more transparency and information for all players along the chain, and notably for consumers and smes; second, improved availability, quality and affordability of delivery solutions, notably cross-border; third, better safeguards for consumers when delivery goes wrong, via complaint handling and redress mechanisms delivery operators, e-retailers and consumer organisations have already engaged in constructive discussions. many operators have started to develop solutions that might better meet the expectations of their customers. the industry is leading the effort. we expect results soon, and will follow up so that commitments are met. we do believe further action is needed, in particular to meet the needs of smes and of less-advanced or less-accessible regions, and to provide e-retailers and consumers with more convenient and transparent services. discussions should also continue among social partners to ensure responsible employment conditions in the delivery sector. the commission will facilitate this collaborative process and involve all stakeholders. we will continue working with parliament to monitor the developments achieved by the sector over the next 18 months and to determine whether any further action is needed.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 4 february 2014.

member of the commission. - madam president, i wish to thank the rapporteur ms nicolai for this report. it rightly reminds us that many migrant women often find themselves in a vulnerable situation states to implement its provisions. for the moment, we have not made plans to revise the directive. the calls in parliament’s report for its swift and correct implementation are, of course, warmly the eu human trafficking is unacceptable. i believe that the eu’s legal and policy framework for addressing trafficking in human beings does take into account the gender dimension of the problem. both the 2011 eu directive on human trafficking and the complementing eu strategy of 2012 recognise and address the gender dimension of human trafficking. at the same time as we address those gender-specific aspects of the human trafficking problem, we have to make sure that the perpetrators profiting from human exploitation end up behind bars. it is the traffickers who deserve punishment, not the victims, who are, unfortunately, too often treated as petty criminals.

in writing. - the report concerns the definition of a 'roadmap' against homophobia to combat discrimination on the grounds of gender identity and sexual orientation with several objectives, including the promotion of these issues in order to educate young people from primary school. other objectives are: provide training to health professionals on lgbti issues, conduct research on health issues specific to lgbti people. finally, the term "sex" should also be understood to include transgender and intersex people. i do not agree with the whole structure of the report and therefore i am voting against the text.
in writing. - the fight against all forms of discrimination has no masters. the union and the member states shall pursue it by means of the instruments for which they are responsible. unfortunately, serious forms of exclusion and violence, both psychological and physical, on grounds of sex, race, religion and gender, still persist. for this reason, we must not let our guard down and refine our community and national safeguards. it is wrong, however, to try to pursue different ends by waving the flag of discrimination. the text of the joint resolution restores the principle of subsidiarity, returning to the national sphere what is part of state sovereignty, but it does not eliminate certain attempts to pass on the recognition of new rights. i thought the resolution tabled by the efd group was a good formula: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work is based on the principle of equal treatment for men and women. my vote in favour of this resolution is a vote against political manipulation and hypocrisy. it is a vote in support of the dignity and freedom of the human person.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the motion for a resolution by the european parliament on the eu roadmap against homophobia and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. as provided for in article 21 of the charter of fundamental rights and article 10 of the tfeu, the european union prohibits all forms of discrimination and has an obligation to combat discrimination in the definition and implementation of its actions. the lgbt survey published by the agency for fundamental rights in 2013 indicates that in the past year 47% of lgbt people felt discriminated against or harassed and 26% were victims of violence or threats due to sexual orientation or gender identity. these alarming figures highlight the need for global policies to combat sex discrimination. for these reasons, through this resolution, i call on the european commission to draw up a roadmap against homophobia and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.
in writing. - i decided to vote against this report because, according to the rapporteur, the term 'gender' should also cover transgender and intersex people, the commission should support member states in training healthcare professionals and specific issues related to transgender and intersex people should be integrated into all relevant eu policies, replicating the approach taken in the strategy for equality between women and men. the commission is also asked to include specific issues related to sexual orientation and gender identity in the implementation and monitoring of asylum legislation.
mr president, i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the unfair commercial practices directive because it identifies a real problem, one which has implications for the functioning of the european market and the free trade area we are trying to create. that is why the penalties must be increased to outweigh the benefits of unfair practices. it is also necessary to strengthen consumer protection, one of the union's fundamental values, by introducing clarifications on the pre-contractual information that the seller must provide to the consumer in relation to the guarantee, such as the price of air transport. i therefore fully support the call for a guideline document to be drawn up so that member states can apply the directive correctly, thereby ensuring an adequate level of consumer protection throughout the european union and increasing their confidence in the single market, while at the same time providing businesses with important legal certainty.
mr president, this measure is intended to protect consumers against unfair commercial practices by businesses towards them and to give them more confidence in transactions in the internal market, while ensuring greater legal certainty for businesses. i believe it is essential that the member states fully implement and correctly apply the directive, and i also stress the need to strengthen cooperation between national authorities. i also voted in favour of the need to ensure that consumers have effective, quick and inexpensive means of redress. to this end, member states should fully implement both the alternative dispute resolution directive and the online out-of-court dispute resolution. i fully share the need to raise consumer awareness and i appreciate the help that can be given to consumers by consumer associations and the network of european consumer centres to help them to be reimbursed.
in writing. - directive 2005/29/ec aims to protect consumers from unfair business practices and to increase their confidence in transactions in the internal market by providing greater legal certainty for businesses. it is, however, essential that all member states apply the directive correctly. it is therefore important to insist on its proper implementation and it is important above all to ask the member states to strengthen prevention and sanctioning systems as effective deterrents. i believe that it is necessary to insist on providing consumers with effective, quick and inexpensive means of redress, and to encourage them to turn to consumer associations and the network of european consumer centres for help and reimbursement.
in writing. - directive 2005/29/ec aims to protect consumers against unfair business practices by giving them more confidence in their transactions in the internal market. i welcome the intention of the european commission to work over the coming months to produce a policy document to accompany this directive. this update will provide an opportunity to clarify the pre-contractual information that the seller must give to the consumer in relation to the guarantee and the practices tolerated in the area of advertising relating to the price of air transport, both important areas from the point of view of consumer protection. i recognize the usefulness of the database on unfair trading practices, but the fact that it is only available in english could pose problems, particularly for small businesses. to this end, i would draw the commission's attention to the desirability of making the database accessible in the various languages of the european union. i also believe that it is equally important to provide consumers with effective, quick and inexpensive means of redress. i agree with the rapporteur that consumers need to be made more aware of the help that can be given to them by the european consumer centres network in obtaining the right to be reimbursed.
in writing. - i see no valid reasons to support the need to revise this legislation in force since 2005, which is why i did not intend to support this text with my vote.
in writing. - the report concerns the application of directive 2005/29/ec on unfair trading practices. these practices, however, do not represent any major concern on the part of our country, but are far removed from the real priorities of this particular historical moment. although the text is in some respects agreeable, there is no clarity on the need to revise the directive. moreover, this standard was applied in 2005 and, since it is not necessary for the real needs of citizens and businesses, it does not need to be renewed. in addition, in the absence of uniform application of the directive, a penalty is provided for against the member states. the latter element cannot be supported by me because consumer protection requires a certain degree of flexibility and there is no possibility of transposing these rules into national law. i therefore vote against.
in writing. - very often, especially when the figures are small, consumers do not react to fraud and deception, especially when they occur online. it is important to bring an action and, thanks also to the valuable work of consumer rights associations, to obtain reimbursement. however, effective, quick and inexpensive remedies must be provided for consumers. member states should therefore implement the directive on alternative dispute resolution and on the out-of-court settlement of online disputes as quickly and as effectively as possible. i believe that a well-integrated deployment of smart grids within regional energy plans will involve citizens in taking an active and responsible role in the energy and network planning of their regions and in reaping the financial and social benefits of these decisions. this involvement will lead to citizens becoming 'prosumers', in the sense that they themselves produce, use and sell their own energy within a smart grid.
in writing. - we share the rapporteur's view on directive 2005/29/ec, which aims to protect consumers against unfair business practices and to give them more confidence in transactions in the internal market, while ensuring greater legal certainty for businesses. there are still too many gaps in its application and the commission must monitor the application of the text closely and not hesitate to take legal action against those states which fail to implement it or ensure that it is applied correctly under the treaty on the functioning of the european union. we strongly emphasize the need to strengthen cooperation between national authorities, in particular with a view to creating a better understanding of the functioning of the system in other member states. the commission will, however, need to update the directive itself in the coming months in order to provide precise information on pre-contractual information in the field of consumer protection and guarantees. finally, we consider it essential to provide consumers with effective, rapid and inexpensive means of redress: member states will have to fully implement the directive on alternative dispute resolution and on the out-of-court settlement of online disputes.
in writing. - there are many points of agreement in this report, all of which are aimed at fair protection of european consumers. much of the text focuses on deceptive practices that have developed in recent years, taking full advantage of the boom in the internet and new technologies. for example, in social networks, forums or blogs, we find ourselves with comments that seem to come from consumers themselves, when in fact they are messages of an advertising or commercial nature generated and financed directly or indirectly by economic operators. another unfair practice, which i have already reported to the european commission, is the so-called 'ip tracking' which aims to record the number of connections made by individual users from the same ip address, in order to artificially inflate prices in relation to the interest shown by similar searches. we all have noticed this and it is important that measures are taken to stop this abuse. in short, there are still many ways and means, and they are constantly changing, by which unscrupulous economic operators are able to harm the consumer, and also distort competition in the market. so we have to keep our guard up to avoid all this.
in writing. - whereas directive 2005/29/ec aims to protect consumers against unfair commercial practices by undertakings towards them and to increase their confidence in transactions in the internal market by providing greater legal certainty for undertakings; agreeing on the need for member states to fully implement the directive on alternative dispute resolution and on the out-of-court settlement of online disputes in order to ensure effective, fast and inexpensive redress for consumers, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i share the view of the rapporteur that the member states must fully implement and correctly apply the directive. i also think that it is not appropriate to extend the scope of the directive to the b2b sector. i believe that it is essential to strengthen cooperation between national authorities within the ctc network and i think that the commission's idea of providing training for these authorities and for those working in the judicial system is an efficient solution, as they should in particular aim at a better understanding of the functioning of the system in other member states. i also share the idea of working over the next few months to update a guidance document accompanying the directive, so as to provide details on the pre-contractual information that the seller must give to the consumer in the matter of guarantees and on the practices tolerated in advertising relating to the price of air transport, both important areas from the point of view of consumer protection. last but not least, it is essential to ensure that consumers have effective, quick and inexpensive means of redress, and this is why member states need to implement the directive on alternative dispute resolution and on the out-of-court settlement of online disputes.
in writing. - the text of the zwiefka report is balanced and acceptable, and i therefore intend to support it with my vote.
in writing. - i join the report's praise of the eu justice scoreboard, in the full conviction that the operation of efficient and impartial justice systems within the various member states is an essential component of the prospect of growth and competitiveness. being fully convinced of the strategic importance of this objective in order to ensure the efficiency of judicial systems, the italian situation (which is in a low average position in the ranking of eu countries regarding the perception of the independence of the judicial system) is an incentive to suggest the use of evaluation tools to achieve a higher degree of reliability of measurements inherent in the independence data. it may be useful to consider the data relating to the organizational system of the judiciary and in particular the possible presence of associations within the judiciary, which are characterized even only by a small degree of political tendency. this certainly seems to be a situation which could have a negative impact on the degree of perceived independence of the justice system, when it seems objectively likely to create even the slightest doubt that the decision on the dispute is influenced by ideological prejudices. in addition, the reference to data on the possible presence of associations between magistrates could be useful for more reliable checks also in relation to the quality profile of the justice system.
in writing. - the report concerns the european union's justice scoreboard, which focuses on civil, commercial and administrative justice in the member states. the framework is a non-binding comparison tool aimed at assessing the effectiveness of national justice systems. the disadvantage is that it is difficult to make objective measurements, such as the fairness and quality of justice. i therefore vote against the text.
in writing. - we have welcomed this own-initiative report because we consider that improving the quality, independence and efficiency of judicial systems is one of the main objectives of the european union's policies. we consider it essential that all necessary measures be taken to ensure that disputes can be resolved within a reasonable time, while promoting the use of alternative dispute resolution mechanisms. this would have the direct consequence of reducing the costs borne by firms and make the member states more attractive to foreign investors. access to an effective judicial system is also crucial for the effectiveness of eu law: it is very important to ensure common rules, as courts must provide effective remedies to any individual who is allegedly violating his rights under european law. particular attention should also be paid to the effective handling of cases with a cross-border element. such cases are usually more complex than those confined to the national sphere: the provision of legal training in eu law and comparative law is of particular importance in this context, as it increases mutual understanding and therefore also mutual trust.
in writing. - an efficient judicial system contributes to the creation of an environment conducive to economic growth. the certainty and timeliness of justice are essential conditions for starting and carrying on business. unfortunately, in some member states, including italy, the time needed to settle civil and administrative cases and insolvency proceedings is longer than in most other member states. in addition, the number of pending cases is considerably high. the eu justice scoreboard published by the commission, by comparing the different national justice systems, contributes to promoting the exchange of best practices within the union and to improving policy-making in the field of justice, while respecting systemic and cultural specificities. the rapporteur's work does not express a value judgment, but provides useful insights to initiate the necessary reform, drawing on best practice. it is an important analytical tool, and i voted in favour of it for the reasons i have just given.
in writing. - whereas the report focuses exclusively on civil, commercial and administrative law, an area where the judiciary is of particular importance for economic recovery, and whereas improving the quality, independence and effectiveness of judicial systems is one of the main objectives of public policy at union and national level; i have voted in favour of this report, bearing in mind that an effective and independent judiciary contributes to a climate of confidence and stability and that predictable, timely and actionable decisions in the field of justice are an important component of an attractive commercial environment.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that access to an effective judicial system is also fundamental to the effectiveness of eu law: when applying eu law, national courts act as 'union courts'. although they respond to different legal traditions, national judicial systems must always act on the principles of timeliness, independence, affordability and ease of access. i therefore welcome the objective of efficient and independent judicial systems in the member states, but i think it is difficult to measure these criteria in different member states. in addition, consideration should be given to cases with a crossborder element, which are generally more complex than those confined to the national sphere. in this regard, the provision of legal training on eu law and comparative law is of particular importance as it increases mutual understanding.

mr president, in a period of rising energy costs, the next structural funds must be spent on the basis of efficiency, avoiding the dispersion of european funds into short-term projects. all regions will have to find solutions to provide a stable and secure energy supply. with the own-initiative report on the establishment of smart grids adopted today, the european parliament is proposing a forward-looking energy strategy which includes increased renewable energy production and energy savings, as well as better use, especially locally, of locally produced energy. this strategy requires an integrated approach, involving other sectors such as transport, housing and urban planning. we must do a good job at this stage, at the stage of programming the funds. as the cases of the most advanced regions in this field have already amply demonstrated, the key to success is the result of openness and transparency between local authorities, businesses and citizens.
mr president, smart grids exploit various energy sources, most of them renewable, and make various communities energy self-sufficient. the successful experiments are mainly on a few danish islands, which have shown the effectiveness of this approach. these networks are the future, and it is towards the future that the european union must commit itself, becoming ever more ambitious in innovation towards sustainability. that is why i voted in favour. i see smart grids as an opportunity especially for the most disadvantaged areas such as the islands of southern europe. they often have higher energy costs, which help to maintain a problematic economic situation. supporting the development of smart grids, especially in island regions such as sardinia and sicily, means promoting their energy independence, economic development and employment, and a sustainable development model that is at the heart of the european project for the coming years.

in writing. - all regions of the european union will soon be called upon to find solutions to provide an increasingly stable and secure energy supply, accessible to all citizens, while respecting environmental and sustainability criteria. in fact, some regions have already adopted solutions and initiatives aimed at so-called smart grids, whereby energy is generated and used close to the production site rather than being transported over long distances, and where two-way communication between the generation and consumption sides is possible. in addition to ensuring security of energy supply and reducing dependence on fossil fuels, smart grids can therefore bring several other benefits to local communities, notably in terms of employment and green jobs. for all these reasons, we voted in favour of this report which shows that a smart grid can be the cornerstone of an increasingly green and sustainable energy agenda, which includes increased production of renewable energy, energy saving and, above all, better and local use of locally produced energy, with significant benefits for all european regions.

mr president, i voted in favour of this report because small farms deserve more attention. small businesses are a great asset. this activity is linked to the lives of many families in italy and europe. these are very important factors which help to maintain excellent, niche and, above all, high-quality production in the agricultural sector. the most important step is the change of generation, a step which must be supported in order not to disperse regional productions which are productions of great value, as well as centuries-old traditions and customs. therefore, invest more in small farms, also through the instruments of the cap and cohesion policy. more resources for infrastructure and for the modernisation of small businesses, for development, for growth and above all for jobs.
mr president, small farming is often not economically profitable and therefore many young people, often the children of farmers, are forced to abandon their activities, to give them up, to escape poverty. this is even more true in regions such as sardinia, which suffers from high transport costs, linked to its insularity - but certainly not only sardinia - and for which rural areas are now being abandoned and depopulated. if this trend is not stopped, it could have dramatic consequences not only for the agricultural sector but also for other related sectors such as tourism, for which cultural and agri-food characteristics are strategic, and for which europe must take responsibility. the reform of the common agricultural policy 2014-2020 introduced important new elements in the support for the establishment of young farmers on which our hope for the survival of small farms is based. in the next few weeks we shall be very attentive to the measures which the commission intends to take to implement these measures. i welcome the report, which has laid the foundations for a sustainable strategy for small businesses.
in writing. - small farms are an integral part of the european countryside. in recent years, there has been a decline in the number of industrial farms in europe. although they are linked to the livelihoods of many families, large farms have traditionally been favoured under the cap. i therefore welcome the new forms of support which, in the framework of the cap reform, are aimed at supporting small farms, even though i consider them to be insufficient. i agree with the rapporteur that in order to solve the problems of small farms, not only the two pillars of the cap but also the cohesion policy of the european union, which should finance the infrastructure essential for these farms in rural areas and, through the european social fund, social initiatives in the field of social integration, education and training, must play a key role. i believe that greater mobilisation by local authorities is also needed: small firms do not have a significant market share and therefore appropriate forms of national support should be provided for at union level, while respecting the principles of competition policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on small farms because, in addition to being an integral part of the european countryside, they maintain the diversity of the landscape, provide for the livelihood of millions of people and enable centuries-old traditions and folk customs to be handed down that would otherwise be destined to disappear. in the cap, large farms are favoured and benefit most from their weight on the market. although small farms are characterised by a lower level of efficiency, highly diversified production and strictly family-generational management, they should be given greater protection and included in a general framework for their safeguarding at eu level, while taking into account the marked differences between the various member states due to historical, social and economic reasons. i agree with the rapporteur that both the pillars of the cap and the eu's cohesion policy must play a key role in solving the problems of small farms, and that the eu's cohesion policy must finance the infrastructure needed by these farms, through the european social fund, social initiatives in the fields of social integration, education and training. the commission is also proposing to increase the number of local authorities.

in writing. - small farms are a fundamental part of the european economic fabric. in the newly acceded countries and in southern europe in particular, they contribute to the livelihoods of millions of people, to the protection of the environment, of biodiversity and to the preservation of cultural traditions and the variety of the landscape. they are also more adaptable to market crises and help to reintegrate the workforce in recessions. nevertheless, they are given less weight in the common agricultural policy, which is based mainly on area and historical production, than the large farms in the sector. in addition, difficulties persist in accessing union funding programmes for the requirements required. this has resulted in a steady reduction in the number of small farms and the sale of their land to large, expanding farms. with the resolution on small farms, which i supported with my vote, the european parliament calls on the member states and the commission to adapt their policies for the period after 2020 to the needs of these small farms. my continued commitment to supporting small farmers and the sustainable business model they represent for many member states is fully welcomed in the resolution.
in writing. - small farms are certainly a peculiar feature of italy compared with other european countries, and this has its roots in the history, traditions and culture of our territories. in many areas, especially in the less-favoured mountainous regions, the presence of farms, often family-run, is the only source of livelihood and the last bulwark against the inexorable depopulation of entire territories, with all the disastrous consequences of the case. it is therefore a duty and a necessity to protect these small but very important things by means of a series of measures. firstly, the criteria for obtaining funds from the european common agricultural policy, which are too focused on farm size and historical production, should be revised. in addition, mechanisms such as direct sales of products should be encouraged, including through a review of rules which are sometimes too stringent and which prevent these small producers from developing. i do not need to say anything more about the quality of these products, because we all know how skilled and efficient the management of these small farms is, which also serve to keep alive the typical recipes and dishes that might otherwise be lost in the globalised agricultural and food market model.

process and also to underline the support shown by the european parliament throughout this period of uncertainty. i am particularly grateful to the committee on international trade and its rapporteur, mr martin, and to the committee on foreign affairs for their support. the union has played a key role in the adoption process to date and will continue to do so in support of the ratification and implementation of the treaty. the commission therefore hopes that ratification by all the member states of the union will not be delayed. the treaty covers to a large extent matters falling within the exclusive competence of the union. it provides, inter alia, for provisions such as import and export controls, which fall within the scope of the union's common commercial policy. during the preparatory stages, the commission, with the support of the european external action service, followed the discussions very closely. it ensured that the final result remained compatible with union law and allowed the parties concerned to benefit from the provisions of the acquis. following the adoption of the arms trade treaty in april 2013, the commission carried out a detailed assessment of its compatibility with the acquis of the european union. it concluded that the texts were fully compatible with union law and that no amendments were necessary. secondly, shortly after the adoption of the treaty by the un general assembly, the commission adopted a proposal for a council decision authorising member states to sign the treaty. this enabled all the member states to sign it at the opening ceremony in new york last june. the union has thus once again demonstrated its determination to regulate the arms trade. the final step before ratification by the eu member states is now in the hands of the european parliament. we know that some european capitals are already awaiting your agreement and the council's authorization. i would like to return to an important point in the negotiating mandate given to the commission in accordance with the provisions of the treaty, namely the accession of the union to the arms trade treaty. this objective, as advocated by the commission, has not been achieved. the commission's proposal for the treaty to allow regional integration organisations to accede to it was rejected at the last conference in march 2013, when china reiterated its firm opposition to eu membership. after this intervention, other major states insisted that the final outcome of the negotiations should not be threatened. that goal had to be abandoned. however, membership of regional integration organisations must remain a long-term objective. the commission welcomes the european parliament's emphasis on this objective in its resolution. finally, i would like to emphasize the support of the european defence industry and its contribution to this process of adopting the treaty. it is clearly in the interests of the arms industry to have the same rules policymakers and national authorities. the commission considers that a high level of competitiveness of companies in the defence sector is an excellent guarantee of compliance with the rules on transparency and ethics. with the implementation of the treaty, we have made a major contribution to ensuring security in the world, while strengthening the regulatory framework for the arms trade.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with this package the european parliament has the opportunity to take a significant step forward towards the implementation of a more coherent and coordinated legal framework for the marketing of products, to the benefit of competitiveness and growth. the internal market has been the great engine of economic growth in the european union for the last 20 years, and we need it even more today, in a time of crisis, to accompany the fiscal compact with strong action, which must be supported by all the community institutions. since 1993, the share of internal trade in gross domestic product has increased by about five percentage points: was around 17% of the union's gdp in 1999 and almost 22% in 2011. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the internal market in products is not undermined. many technical and legal barriers have fortunately been removed, but the commercial environment creates new situations and problems which require decisive action. this is the aim of the present initiative: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is able to take part in the debate on the future of the internal market. the aim is to build a coherent set of rules to ensure fair conditions of competition for european and third country producers, supporting the reindustrialisation of the european union. i can assure you that for two years now our union industry and the supervisory authorities have been looking forward to this moment. the commission would like to emphasize the excellent cooperation with parliament and the council and the great work of the rapporteur, mrs roithová, and of the successive polish, danish, cypriot, irish, lithuanian and now greek presidencies deserves to be recognized. we believe that the final compromise is an excellent update of the rules for a number of product categories. this adjustment package may, it is true, seem very technical; however, it is of great importance for the functioning of the internal market for a wide range of products: electrical and electronic equipment, lifts, explosives, pressure vessels and measuring instruments. the new rules aim to strengthen and modernise the conditions for the marketing of these products within the union and thus contribute to improving the functioning of the market. a recent independent evaluation of the legislation on the internal market for industrial products found the adjustment package to be effective in addressing the latest instances of divergences, gaps, inconsistencies and duplication of legislation and concluded that this package makes a key contribution to the modernisation and reform of the regulatory framework for industrial products. as you know, on 22 january the commission adopted a communication entitled 'a perspective for the internal market in industrial products'. the commission has also adopted a communication on the internal market, which confirms that internal market legislation is appropriate and is an essential factor in the competitiveness of european industry and in the protection of consumers and the environment. the communication also sets out a broad vision for the next decade and identifies the challenges of the future: the need for effective control mechanisms, digitalisation, globalisation and the increasing integration of products with related services. in short, tackling regulatory barriers is becoming increasingly important in a context of rapidly evolving technology and increasing integration of global value chains and the world itself. it is against this background and in view of the imperative to minimise administrative burdens, especially for small and mediumsized enterprises, that the european union must continue to develop its internal product market. the delay in reaching a compromise is not due to the complexity of the subject but to an institutional dispute which has nothing to do with the substance of the proposal. the commission has issued two statements on this subject, covering all eight directives, which i will be sure to forward to the relevant departments of the european parliament. in conclusion, however, i would like to stress that the commission will continue to cooperate effectively with the experts of the member states and with the european parliament within the legal framework established by the treaty of lisbon. without effective cooperation, no progress can be made. i consider the work on the adjustment package to be a valuable example of effective cooperation. i would like to thank parliament and the council again for their decisive contribution.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, as you have said, the package we are going to adopt tomorrow is very important. it is made up of many seemingly minor technical rules, which many outside observers, when they talk about the european union and the work of parliament, consider to be sufficient. the sum of these rules produces effects of the greatest importance, and i would like to mention at least three of them. the first: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on competition are applied in the community. secondly: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a dispute between the commission and the consumer. thirdly, they eliminate red tape and therefore reduce costs, making these sectors and these segments of activity competitive. we need to offer the world models of competition in which respect for the rules, the elimination of bureaucracy and the quality of what is produced are the reference elements, thus avoiding low-level competition which can be of benefit to the emerging countries but which is objectively harmful to europe.

force of the lisbon treaty, and it is significant that it concerns the most vulnerable people moving through the labour market. we will need an increasing proportion of seasonal workers from outside the union for reasons relating to the demographic trends in our countries, as well as the composition of the labour market. so, having these people, as the solution we are discussing defines, receive equal treatment, which does not discriminate against european workers who perform the same work, is very important for the people who work and for the companies. we must never forget that when the rules are the same and must be respected by virtue of the provisions of the rules, including the penalties contained in the rules, companies cannot compete unfairly with each other, because they are subject to a single solution and workers have the same conditions, which concerns the dignity of work, because collective agreements are applied, because the rules relating to general working conditions are defined according to parameters which differ from country to country, but which have the character of uniformity in the same sector. then workers acquire dignity in the work they do and companies can compete freely without any pollution, especially those caused by the violation of rights or the improper reduction of labour costs. the social partners will also have a role to play, because they will define the sectors in which, country by country, objective seasonal activities take place. we 've seen too many deformations . everything had become seasonal, even what was continuous. it is therefore a very important solution, because it allows europe to have the same rules and standards for the most vulnerable workers and to have a competitive capacity of the
