madam president, i voted in favour of agreeing to this directive and i congratulate the rapporteur on his excellent work. the agreement allows the development of a fundamental instrument for the defence of the rights of immigrant seasonal workers. immigrant seasonal workers will no longer be discriminated against against by european citizens in terms of working conditions, trade union rights and the recognition of diplomas and qualifications. these provisions shall be accompanied by effective and dissuasive penalties for any infringements. i am therefore very pleased with the result achieved with this directive, which will make it possible to combat the unacceptable situations of exploitation and abuse of seasonal immigrants in europe.
madam president, i voted in favour of the directive on seasonal workers because i believe it is absolutely important to defend and equalise their rights with those of european workers in order to avoid unacceptable cases of exploitation. finally, this directive establishes equal treatment for seasonal workers, immigrants and european citizens in the fields of working conditions, trade union rights, social security, information, access to employment centres, vocational education and training, and in particular the recognition of qualifications and diplomas, with the provision of verification obligations for the member states. it is also important to ensure that seasonal workers have the right to extend their employment contract beyond the year for which they are being offered, to have a residence permit and to change employers within that year. this will certainly free them from forms of dependence which are sometimes the precursors of unacceptable situations of exploitation. i hope that a similar rule will be made in the field of education and research.
in writing. - the need for seasonal workers is regularly felt in certain sectors where many immigrants work underground and in precarious conditions. clear rules on seasonal work are essential to ensure that non-community workers have adequate working and living conditions and to avoid forms of exploitation that border on slavery. it is also important to set time limits because we cannot allow more than one hundred thousand temporary residence permits a year to be converted into permanent permits or asylum applications. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the conditions of entry and residence of thirdcountry nationals for the purpose of seasonal work. i agree with the rapporteur that this directive is necessary to combat the exploitation of seasonal workers. given the growing need for seasonal labour from non-eu countries, a strong regulatory framework is needed both to manage labour migration and to prevent illegal migration, and to ensure equal opportunities and treatment within the eu labour market, especially regarding pay and working conditions. i therefore welcome the provisions of the directive which provide for greater protection for seasonal workers based on the application of pre-defined common criteria, but i agree with the rapporteur that some amendments are needed on a number of points, including seasonal work permits, length of stay, accommodation, sanctions for employers, access to information, checks and inspections, facilitation of complaints, costs linked to seasonal work and, above all, scope, or extend it to include those who are already in the eu but are not authorised to work.
in writing. - the moraes report analyses the proposal for a directive to regulate the entry and residence of thirdcountry nationals for the purpose of seasonal work. the text, while making sensible proposals such as regulating the entry of seasonal workers only if they have a contract of employment, contains aspects which i do not share at all and which would only increase the burden on businesses. that's why i abstained.
in writing. - the trilogue on the dossier lasted more than a year, but a compromise was reached for an agreement at first reading. we have worked to prevent the illegal long-term stay of seasonal workers from third countries, so as to avoid the transition from seasonal work to asylum seekers. in addition, bureaucracy has been limited for applicants to employers.
in writing. - the recent referendum in switzerland and the fierce controversy surrounding it have brought the issue of labour mobility back into the political debate. the mobility of workers within the european union must be guaranteed and we cannot tolerate restrictions which undermine the rights of citizens. that said, the rules need to be clarified to prevent seasonal work from becoming permanent employment in breach of european regulations. those coming from outside the european union, and employers, must know that we are not kidding here and the laws must be respected.
in writing. - seasonal labour requirements are common to most eu member states. a directive regulating the management of migration could bring useful results and ensure equal treatment for third country nationals within the european labour market. i voted in favour of the report on the seasonal work directive because i believe it can help to combat the exploitation of undeclared work by immigrants working within the member states. the directive will establish the conditions for granting residence permits, which will be linked to seasonal work for a maximum of six months a year, and will clearly define the rights of such workers. the member states will have to take measures to prevent exploiters from taking advantage of the needs of immigrants who leave their countries to escape from extreme poverty. we will have to ensure, firstly, that residence permits for the purpose of seasonal work are granted to those workers who have not had problems with the judicial institutions and, secondly, that inspections are increased to ensure that workers have regular permits and have decent accommodation.
in writing. - the civilization of a people, like the european, is measured by the conditions and protections afforded to the weakest. what happened in rosarno in 2010 and how often it still happens in italy and in many member states must not happen again. the support for this directive is fully in line with the principles of equality, dignity and solidarity enshrined in the treaties. the directive leaves member states wide latitude in the rules and quantities of workers who will be able to have their residence permits recognised for the purpose of seasonal work, thus helping to combat illegal and clandestine situations. moreover, the granting of such rights means at the same time the establishment of common duties and rules in the labour market, discouraging behaviour which would make workers in hiding, who are subject to less protection, seem preferable to european workers in good standing.
in writing. - there are some important points in this directive to regulate the entry and residence of non-community nationals coming to europe for the purpose of seasonal work. i am satisfied that there is a demand for explicit guarantees to deal with their applications, such as the need to have a valid employment contract for the purpose of the stay, which specifies the place and type of work, its duration, the remuneration and the weekly or monthly working hours, the duration of paid holidays and also the date of entry into service. in addition, the applicant must provide proof of health and insurance cover for the period and proof of adequate accommodation for the period. in short, these are a few points, clear and significant, which should enable the worker concerned, for a limited period defined by his contract, to live in dignity and to carry out the profession for which he has been requested. if we want to have useful and sustainable immigration, we need clear rules, because we cannot accept everyone indiscriminately, as some false optimists think, because otherwise the results are disastrous, as the italian situation has amply demonstrated.
in writing. - every year, seasonal workers from third countries enter the territory of the union. this phenomenon concerns jobs related to tourism and agricultural and horticultural labour. with the directive on the conditions of entry and residence of seasonal workers, the eu wants to establish the necessary rules and requirements, and also wants to protect these workers who are too often exploited. the eu's legal immigration programme gives member states the possibility to determine how many seasonal workers will be allowed to enter their territory, seeking to give preference to eu citizens and giving a set of rights to these workers with contracts, working conditions and adequate accommodation over a recognised period of between 5 and 9 months.
in writing. - whereas the need for seasonal labour from non-eu countries is a common phenomenon in most member states and a union-wide framework for managing this type of migration could bring real added value and whereas the introduction of legal channels for migration can play an important role in reducing irregular migration and the exploitation that often accompanies it. i agree with the need to establish an accelerated procedure for the admission of third-country nationals employed as seasonal workers, on the basis of a common definition and common criteria to be applied to seasonal workers, and i have voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the house voted today in plenary session in strasbourg on the report by mr moraes on the conditions of entry and residence of thirdcountry nationals for the purpose of seasonal employment. seasonal workers from third countries will now be able to benefit from better living and working conditions, including adequate housing and a limit on working hours. the legislation stipulates that non-eu seasonal workers will have the same rights as eu citizens with regard to minimum working age, pay, dismissal, working hours, holidays, health cover and safety requirements. the agreement between the ep and the council provides that any request to stay in the community as a seasonal worker must include a contract of employment or a binding job offer, specifying, inter alia, pay and working hours.
in writing. - from now on, seasonal workers from third countries will be able to benefit from better living and working conditions. the right to adequate housing for the period of employment and a limit on working hours will no longer be mere mirages. the aim is to put an end to their exploitation by preventing temporary residence permits from becoming permanent. this is a major step forward in protecting the fundamental rights of the more than 100 000 third country workers who enter the european union each year.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the report because i share many of the points in it which could facilitate and strengthen the implementation of the commission's proposal. firstly, by extending the scope to include third-country nationals who are already resident in the union but who are not authorised to work under the legislation in force, in order to harmonise the legislation. secondly, i believe that access to information is essential and must therefore be guaranteed, in order to help reduce the risk of exploitation. as regards housing, i agree with the rapporteur that reference should be made more strongly to the requirements of national legislation and practice. in addition, employers should bear certain costs directly related to seasonal work, including travel expenses, visa fees and health insurance for periods not covered by the employment contract. the fact that the employer pays the travel expenses makes it easier for seasonal workers to return to their place of origin when their leave expires.
in writing. - the report by mr moraes establishes an accelerated procedure for the admission of thirdcountry nationals employed as seasonal workers, on the basis of a common definition and common criteria to be applied to seasonal workers. the text lays down the conditions for granting a residence and work permit for a maximum of six months per year and defines the rights of seasonal workers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the romeva i rueda report because i believe that we must continue to fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing which still exists in some states. however, in view of the importance of tuna fishing and marketing, in particular for valuable species including bluefin tuna and bigeye tuna, the current complexity of the fisheries and marketing measures of iccat, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas, should be reduced and limited to certain atlantic fishing areas that export mainly tuna and mackerel. for this reason it is still premature to remove all suspicion of countries that potentially resort to illegal fishing practices or to the limits of legality. i therefore believe that the commission proposal (to allow imports in full) should be revised, limiting itself to allowing fishery products from cambodia, equatorial guinea and sierra leone and keeping the ban on bolivia, georgia and the atlantic countries unchanged.
in writing. - i did not support this report because its approval would mean the repeal of the ban on tuna imports from countries which, like cambodia, have never cooperated in the fight against illegal fishing.
in writing. - having regard to the commission proposal for a regulation repealing regulation (ec) no 827/2004 prohibiting the import of products derived from bigeye tuna from bolivia, cambodia, georgia, equatorial guinea and sierra leone, taking into account that at its 14th special meeting in 2004, iccat recognised the efforts made by cambodia, equatorial guinea and sierra leone to address its concerns and adopted recommendations to lift the restrictive trade measures against these three countries in relation to atlantic bigeye tuna and derived products, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the european parliament voted today in plenary on the report by mr romeva i rueda on the proposal to repeal regulation (ec) no 827/2004 banning the import of atlantic bigeye tuna. the regulation dates back to the 1990s, when the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) was at the forefront of the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing, imposing bans on imports of products from countries suspected of allowing fishing vessels flying their flag to flout international rules and standards and establishing blacklists of fishing vessels. consequently, the flags of the fishing vessels were changed and the non-contracting states became contracting parties, thus lifting the import bans. however, iccat considered that the problems had been addressed sufficiently adequately to lift the bans, leading many to believe that iuu fishing has been almost completely eradicated in the area. the commission has also proposed that the fishing opportunities for bluefin tuna be increased by a further 10% in the case of the atlantic salmon.
in writing. - the regulation in question dates back to the 1990s, when iccat had introduced innovative tools in imposing bans on imports of products from countries suspected of allowing fishing vessels flying their flag to ignore international rules and standards, but as a result many fishing vessels changed flags to register with states that allowed tuna fishing, in turn pushing iccat to include as many countries as possible in the convention. the commission has currently identified cambodia as a non-cooperating country under regulation (ec) no 1005/2008.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the renewal of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the gabonese republic. after two years of negotiations stalled, negotiations to allow eu vessels to fish in gabonese waters were concluded in april 2013 and the final text was sealed. in view of the agreement reached on the annual financial contribution to be paid by the eu to gabon, calculated on the basis of tonnage and support for the development of gabon's sectoral fisheries policy, i believe it is right that the eu: comply with the commitments made; provide for corrective procedures where non-compliance with the targets is detected before suspending payments; promote the exploitation of fishery resources by gabon; facilitate the conditions for the operation of the port and tuna processing facilities; facilitate the landing in gabonese ports of catches taken in gabonese waters; verify the availability of fish stocks on a continuous basis, including by monitoring the catches of eu vessels in the gabonese fishing zone; encourage transparency of procedures for identifying total catches and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. - the report is balanced and acceptable and that is why i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. - having regard to the opinion of the committee on development and the committee on budgets, i voted in favour of the proposal, considering that the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and gabon should promote, in the medium term, the exploitation by gabon of its fisheries resources both for internal consumption, in accordance with the needs of its population, and for export, increasing the added value of fisheries activities and thereby increasing the share of the wealth generated that remains in the country.
in writing. - i am in favour of this recommendation because the compromise reached on the conditions for suspending the application of the protocol seems to be balanced and appropriate. i agree that the disbursement of the union's sectoral support should be conditional on the successful implementation of the objectives and actions agreed jointly and that the eu should therefore undertake to verify the basis for the correct use of the aid in accordance with gabon's sovereignty and legitimate choices and priorities. it is true, however, that the monitoring of catches by eu vessels in the gabonese fishing zone needs to be improved: the transparency of the procedures for identifying total catches and measures to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing should be improved. i also believe that parliament should be immediately and fully informed at all stages of the procedures relating to the protocol or its renewal, by means of a report from the commission on the results of the programme and on compliance with the catch reporting obligations.
in writing. - the european union and gabon signed a new partnership agreement on 24 april 2013. the protocol is valid for three years and allows the european fleet to continue fishing in gabonese waters. the aim of the agreement is to support gabon's new strategic plan to improve fisheries governance, protect resources and strengthen control in its waters.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr cortés lastra on relations between the eu, greenland and denmark. the proposal for a council decision is based mainly on the text and results of the previous decision, covering the period 2006-2013, which included education and training, mineral resources, energy, tourism and culture, research and food security as areas of cooperation under the agreement. fisheries issues of major importance to greenland are covered by a specific fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and greenland.
in writing. - in line with the econ vote, in which i took part, i believe that prevention is a highly relevant factor in avoiding loss or damage caused by unforeseen phenomena. i believe that the eu is right and appropriate in its action to spread a culture of awareness and prevention of anthropogenic and natural hazards in an attempt to reduce uncertainty in these areas and to prepare citizens for the consequences of natural disasters. this information campaign must be promoted and continued to encourage responsible behaviour on the part of individuals. at the same time, it is appropriate to urge member states to identify high-risk areas and to establish natural disaster response units capable of coordinating efforts, including at cross-border level, to share best practices and mitigate the effects. in addition, natural and man-made disasters cannot be dealt with together and require different types of insurance, thus creating two distinct insurance markets. insurance companies should be encouraged to adopt different insurance systems and procedures and to differentiate premiums according to risk. in addition, the rules on the type of cover, terms and conditions, procedures, withdrawal and complaint deadlines should be more transparent.

in writing. - i strongly support the ratification of the arms trade treaty by the member states because it establishes the first global regulation for trade in conventional weapons and, to some extent, in ammunition and parts and components. the att will prevent the illegal trade of weapons, international terrorism and organised crime and will limit serious violations of international human rights law and international humanitarian law. the strongest point of the att is that state parties are obliged to establish a national control system for these transfers and to evaluate, before authorising any transfer, the risk that these arms might impair peace and security or could be used to commit serious violations of international humanitarian law or human rights. it is also important that not only trade of arms but other acts such as rental, licensing, grants and transfers of relevant technology also fall under the prohibition.

madam president, the eu produces 26% of the world's arms and 61% of its production is destined for outside its borders. on 2 april 2013, after seven years of negotiations, the un general assembly adopted the first international treaty on the international sale of conventional arms. the treaty requires each country to assess, before any transaction, whether arms sold risk being used by buyers to circumvent an international embargo, commit human rights violations, or be resold to terrorist or criminal groups. it therefore represents an important step towards a more transparent and responsible arms trade. unfortunately, the treaty does not provide for the european union to accede, so a swift accession and ratification by all eu states is needed to give a strong and shared signal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because a legally binding treaty will be able to define international standards aimed at regulating the international trade in conventional arms, making it possible to curb the illegal trafficking and proliferation of arms and, at the same time, generating an environment of peace, security and international and regional stability. moreover, a treaty of this magnitude will increase respect for international human rights and humanitarian law. the failure to regulate the illicit trade in arms means that instability, terrorism, corruption, socioeconomic degradation and violations of various kinds are encouraged. i also agree that the att should be included among the objectives of the cfsp and among the subjects covered by bilateral agreements. while noting some gaps in the current wording and interpretation of the att, i believe that effective implementation of the att and the application of all provisions relating to, inter alia, small arms, light weapons, ammunition and their parts and components, arms transfers and diversion, authorisations, increased transparency in the annual reports and related publications that states parties will disseminate are essential. i welcome the proposal to establish a transparent and robust international monitoring mechanism that promotes the role of parliaments and civil society.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the fjellner report on the proposal for a regulation on protection against dumped or subsidized imports from countries outside the european union. we must do everything we can to protect our businesses and our territories from the aggression of products from third countries which operate outside the rules of competition in the european internal market.
in writing. - i voted strongly for the reform of the trade defence instruments, as significantly rebalanced and strengthened by the vote of the committee on international trade. an effective trade defence system close to business, especially small and mediumsized enterprises, is essential in the complex international economic environment we are living in. it is not a question of raising anachronistically protectionist barriers, but of having effective tools to deal with the growing forms of unfair competition and dumping from non-eu countries, which severely penalise that important part of the european production fabric which continues to believe in the value of producing in europe and which continues to use high production standards, high social criteria and which continues to be an important part of the european social fabric. we are rightly demanding of our companies, but at the same time we must fight to prevent them from being overwhelmed by unbridled competition as a result of the protectionist and distortive policies of others. it is hoped that this strong voice of the european parliament will not be watered down in the trilogues with the council: we call on governments to ensure that there is an effective instrument to protect trade which must remain free, but also fair and based on the principle of reciprocity.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i believe that we should improve the predictability for businesses by informing them of any anti-dumping/anti-subsidy measures at least two weeks before the provisional duties are applied. the committee on international trade unanimously approved a package of 11 compromise amendments on issues such as the creation of an effective help desk for smes, the reduction of the investigation period to 12 months, with the possibility of imposing provisional duties after 6 months, and full and effective information from the commission to parliament. the refund on importers was subsequently cancelled. i am disappointed that no compromise agreement has been reached on the most important and controversial points of the transport clause and the lesser duty rule. the majority of the committee and the members supported the deletion of the 'transport clause' and the extension of the provision not to apply the lesser duty rule. efficiency, reduction of the threat of retaliation, transparency and predictability are key objectives, which together ensure public confidence.
in writing. - the report concerns the amendment of council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 on protection against dumped imports and council regulation (ec) no 597/2009 on protection against subsidised imports. the revision concerns the application of anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duties on those goods entering our market from non-eu countries. i am voting in favour of the report because it aims to combat unfair competition.
in writing. whereas the commission proposal is designed to modernise the anti-dumping and anti-subsidy regulations and whereas the importance of the issue of protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community is taken into account; agreeing that transparency and predictability are essential for all parties involved and are intended to ensure the maintenance of public confidence and the accountability and legitimacy of the instruments, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the european union must raise customs duties as a means of combating dumping by helping small businesses to take advantage of the measures available in this respect. this must also be the case against social or environmental dumping.
in writing. - in recent years europe has seen a progressive deterioration in the global trade situation, due in particular to the increased use of protectionist and distortive policies pursued with determination in different areas of the globe, a situation which is particularly insidious for continental industry. the european commission's proposal provides that, in the event of structural distortions in raw materials, the reasons for such a favourable measure cease to exist and that, in such cases, the level of the applicable anti-dumping/anti-subsidy duty is not limited to the injury margin but may go beyond it. i particularly agree with and support the position contained in the amendments proposed by the inta committee, which confirm and even strengthen the cases in which it would be possible in future not to apply the lesser duty rule, adding in particular, in addition to raw materials, energy and forms of subsidy. i therefore voted in favour of the amendments in question and of the text as a whole voted by the inta committee, hoping that these amendments would contribute to the modernisation of the existing european trade defence instruments in a coherent and balanced way.
in writing. - my vote in favour is linked to those measures in the commission proposal which ensure the effective use of the instruments, such as the reimbursement of duties collected during expiry reviews. i also welcome some of the points raised by the rapporteur, in particular the commission's ability to initiate ex officio proceedings and its real ability to reduce the risk of retaliation, since a producer in a third country can infer which union producer the commission is acting on behalf of. the rapporteur touches on another important point concerning the partial abolition of the lesser duty rule, which could increase the threat of retaliation by favouring the principle of 'paying back with the same coin'. another point which is particularly important to me is access to information, which is very limited for the parties concerned at the moment and which requires a strong approach in favour of a high degree of transparency. in this respect, i welcome the proposal to introduce a notification system whereby legal representatives or interested parties are notified of the addition of new files to the investigation, together with online access to all non-confidential files.
in writing. - in 2010 there was a restructuring of the community fisheries control system which modernised the regime for the control, inspection and enforcement of common fisheries policy measures along the marketing chain. a system that is designed to improve catch traceability, catch quantification, data collection and the application of harmonised penalties across the european union. i support the text of mr thomas' report and especially the proposal to ask the commission to submit a report every three years on the acts adopted during that period, in order to assess the achievement of the objectives and the compliance of the member states with the rules laid down in the regulation on the common fisheries policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the community control system to ensure compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. in accordance with the lisbon treaty, i think it is right to give parliament (and also the council), as suggested in the commission's proposal, greater powers of control and supervision with a view to limiting the powers granted to the commission. i believe that certain points of regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 should be revised because of their impracticability, for example with regard to traceability and landing declarations. the revision process must also provide for a timely alignment of the regulation with the reform of the cfp and for adjustment to certain principles contained in the charter of fundamental rights which are not fully respected at present. i also think it is right that the commission should take care to ensure the safety of seafarers by choosing the least costly and most economically efficient procedural scenario and respecting the three pillars of sustainable development.
in writing. - i did not intend to support the thomas report on the community control system to ensure compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy, because it reserves excessive powers to the european commission alone.
in writing. - our fishing industry has already been severely affected by decisions taken at european level in the past. there has certainly been a shared responsibility, on the one hand, of the italian government which did not intervene in due time and, on the other, of the community authorities which were not able to protect the various types of fisheries present in europe, showing in fact little sensitivity. that 's my wish . i would like to ask the commissioner to give us a clear answer to this question.
in writing. - the report on the community control system to ensure compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy points out that some elements of the regulation currently in force do not appear to be in line with the charter of fundamental rights. there is therefore a substantial need to monitor and adapt european legislation in this area, especially in the light of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and the regulatory alignment that this entails.
in writing. - whereas the international trade in conventional arms is worth at least usd 70 000 million a year, and whereas according to a united nations estimate, almost one million of the eight million weapons produced in the world every day are lost or stolen, generally ending up in the wrong hands, and whereas one person dies every minute in the world as a result of gun violence; i am aware that respect for human rights is the cornerstone of the common values on which the european union is built and that, according to the treaties, trade policy, as part of the eu's external action, should contribute to respect for human rights, and i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report. i agree with the rapporteur that it is necessary to indicate certain principles which must be respected in the light of the treaty of lisbon and in the light of which parliament will monitor the acts provided for in regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 establishing a community control system to ensure compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy, which will be reviewed in the near future. for example, when adopting acts, the commission will have to ensure the safety of seafarers, choose the least costly and most cost-effective scenario and respect the three pillars of sustainable development. the commission is also proposing to extend the delegation of power for a period of three years, after which the commission will have to submit a report on the acts adopted during the period under review, assessing their effectiveness in the light of the objectives of the regulation and the cfp.
in writing. - i am in favour of adopting the proposal, since it highlights some points in the commission proposal which are not particularly satisfactory. i share the principles by which the commission should guide its decisions and by which parliament will scrutinise the acts provided for in regulation (ec) no 1224/2009. in addition, in order to limit the powers conferred on the commission, the delegation of power for a period of three years to the commission, at the end of which it will have to report on the acts adopted during the period under review, seems to me a good compromise. i also welcome the attention paid to the possible violation of the charter of fundamental rights. finally, i support the rapporteur in stressing the importance of respecting the process of 'lisbonisation', focusing solely on the adjustments necessary to bring the text into line with the treaties, while ensuring effective control by the european parliament and proposing a reflection on the powers granted to the commission.

madam president, air transport is of central importance to all citizens, but particularly to island territories, and any disadvantage caused to european citizens living on islands is a denial of their right to free movement, which the union recognises as a fundamental right. too many unpunished episodes in that sense. during the last christmas period the right of the sardinians to move was trampled on, for example, by the new livingston company, which arbitrarily cancelled six flights on the alghero-fiumicino route which it even operates in territorial continuity, but i must say also with the consent of the regional board which governs my island. the revision of regulation (ec) no 261/2004, which we approved a few days ago, finally removes some loopholes in the previous legislation which allowed airlines not to compensate passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation of flights or long delays. in doing so we are finally protecting and strengthening the right of all european citizens to move and it is for these reasons that i have supported and shared the work carried out by my colleagues in the committee on transport.
in writing. - the bach report analyses the proposal for a regulation on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation or long delay of flights and air carrier liability in respect of the carriage of passengers and their baggage by air. i believe that this text is a considerable improvement on the previous proposal and that parliament's work has greatly increased the protection and safety of passengers, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - the proposal for a regulation on passenger rights in the event of delay or missed boarding is particularly necessary as the aviation sector has seen a considerable increase in passenger numbers and flights in the liberalised european market in recent years. the old 2004 regulation was therefore obsolete also in the light of several judgments of the european court of justice in favour of citizens. i therefore agree with the regulation and believe that we should not wait another ten years to extend protection to airport parking costs, which sometimes exceed the price of low-cost air tickets, and to airport reception. i am referring to the lack of access to the controls with the consequent queues, the lack of adequate waiting rooms and the transfer arrangements from the gate to the aircraft which in some cases cause great inconvenience to passengers due to the weather.
in writing. - in recent years there has been a significant increase in the number of passengers and flights. however, this increase has been accompanied by a decrease in the level of services, with negative impacts for travellers. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for an amendment to the regulation establishing common rules on assistance and compensation to passengers in the event of missed boarding, cancellation and long delays because i believe it is important to harmonise the legislation in this area in all member states in order to protect european travellers. it will be important to protect passengers who miss their connections because of flight delays, guaranteeing the same rights as those who have their flight cancelled. passengers are generally not adequately informed about their rights and often have to protest individually against large international bodies. i think it is important to set up national bodies for complaints procedures, to encourage extrajudicial solutions, and it would be desirable for each airport, as is already the case in several, to have a complaints service to speed up the procedures.
in writing. - the rights of the millions of passengers who take advantage of air transport in european skies each year are increasingly exposed to unfair practices and reduced quality of service. although the european parliament has adopted two regulations on this subject, the lack of uniformity and the gaps in the application of these regulations in the member states expose passengers to a lower guarantee of the protection of their rights. the commission's proposal to revise the regulation aims to improve and harmonise the application of passenger rights in all member states by defining rights, simplifying complaint procedures and facilitating the application of sanctioning policies by national authorities. i believe that the strict application of the rules in force on flight cancellations and delays, the transparency of policies on prices, no-show and lost baggage and the effective protection of air passengers' rights must be guaranteed.
in writing. - the house voted today in plenary session in strasbourg on mr bach's report on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation of flights or long delays. i agree with the rapporteur that it is appropriate to facilitate the process of compensating passengers in the event of flight cancellations. the new rules would require air carriers to have contact persons at each airport to inform passengers about their rights, complaint procedures, assistance, reimbursement and rescheduling of flights. finally, national authorities should be given sufficient powers to punish air carriers that violate passenger rights and to assess reports on how passengers have been helped to cope with flight delays and cancellations.
in writing. - passengers on delayed or grounded flights must have certain rights on how to obtain compensation more easily and airlines must have clearer rules on how to handle complaints. air passenger rights concern virtually every citizen of the european union. unfortunately, today only 2 percent of passengers actually get compensation after filing a complaint against an airline. the aim of today's decision is to reverse this negative trend once and for all.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the report because it seeks to eliminate the uncertainties for passengers caused by the incomplete application of the legislation in force. all the main points are analysed and clarified: the right to compensation in the event of prolonged delays, which should be determined in agreement with the european court of justice; denied boarding due to overbooking or, in the case of a return flight, if the passenger has not taken the outbound flight booked. other cases of particular importance are the safeguards in case of repeated flight disruptions, such as in case of insolvency of airlines or failure to establish emergency plans in case of multiple flight disruptions, or the disruption of the flight in exceptional circumstances; the right to hotel accommodation in the event of flight disruption also belongs to this category. all these are cases where there is a high degree of legal uncertainty which is detrimental to passengers. the rapporteur also touches on the right to information, price transparency, complaint procedures, restrictions on checked baggage, loss, damage or delay.
in writing. - although the 2000 regulation is generally considered to be an effective instrument to facilitate crossborder insolvency proceedings within the union, a number of problems have been identified with regard to the practical application of this instrument, including the non-reflection of national practices in insolvency law, in particular with regard to the promotion of the rescue of firms in difficulty, and the description of the subjective and objective elements for access to insolvency proceedings. this is a recurring phenomenon affecting not only large groups but also smes. i agree with the need to shift the focus from merely liquidating companies to giving businesses a second chance. in addition, a public register of cross-border insolvency proceedings is a very useful tool for transparency.
in writing. - the proposal for a directive on the coordination of certain provisions laid down by law, regulation or administrative action in member states concerning the pursuit of television broadcasting activities; the commission's proposals are positive, especially with regard to secondary proceedings, but the focus of eu insolvency law needs to be shifted to giving businesses a second chance. i agree with the rapporteur that i welcome the amendments concerning the scope of the insolvency procedure regulation, because they are necessary in order to bring the text more into line with the acquis. i also welcome the proposal to set up an eu register enabling creditors and courts to check any insolvency proceedings opened in other member states: this will ensure greater transparency. finally, i believe that the commission should concentrate less on the coordination of different insolvency proceedings and delegate the task to a single coordinator who, on the one hand, outlines and recommends a comprehensive set of measures for the resolution of insolvency situations of the companies in the group in order to increase assets and preserve jobs and, on the other hand, is responsible for the coordinated conduct of these proceedings.
in writing. - i think the text is balanced in all its parts and that is why i have voted in favour of the lehne report.
in writing. - the report concerns the amendment of council regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 on crossborder insolvency proceedings, modelled on the uncitral law. these procedures shall apply where the debtor has assets or creditors in more than one member state; the regulation determines the competent court for the opening of insolvency proceedings. the amendments to the regulation are intended to remedy certain 'lack of clarity' which have been noted over the years. i am voting in favour of the text, because the purpose of the regulation is to help a debtor in serious financial crisis, in order to help healthy businesses survive, thus helping entrepreneurs.
in writing. - as this parliament has already expressed in a series of recommendations to the commission, an amendment to the insolvency procedure regulation in the context of eu company law was necessary to harmonise european legislation on insolvency proceedings. we cannot ignore the fact that 'the disparities between national insolvency laws create competitive advantages or disadvantages and difficulties for companies with crossborder activities, which could hinder the successful outcome of restructuring operations of insolvent companies'. i therefore regard the adoption of mr lehne's report as a good result.
in writing. - i support this report with my vote in favour because, on the whole, the commission's proposals are very positive, but sometimes they contain unclear elements, which the rapporteur has well highlighted. one example is the concept of 'centre of main interests', the definition of which should have taken into account factors such as the location, recognisable from the outside, of the main activities of the undertaking, the location of the assets, the centre of operational or production activities, etc. i also support the proposal to set up an eu register, integrated into the european e-justice portal, which would enable creditors and courts to determine whether insolvency proceedings have been opened in other member states. on the insolvency of groups of companies, i share the compromise between the commission's approach, which is based on 'coordination and communication', and parliament's position, proposing the appointment of a coordinator with the task of identifying and making recommendations for the coordinated conduct of insolvency proceedings and presenting a group coordination plan which identifies, outlines and recommends a comprehensive set of measures for the resolution of insolvency situations of the companies in the group.
in writing. - crossborder insolvencies are now a widespread phenomenon affecting both large industrial groups and small and medium-sized enterprises. the availability of sufficient data on the application of the european insolvency procedure regulation makes it possible to address the most urgent issues. the reform process must, for example, aim at a modernisation of insolvency law in the european union that shifts the focus from the mere liquidation of companies to the granting of a second chance to businesses.

mr president, i was just getting the text of the written statement. i believe that by revising the regulation governing air passenger rights this parliament has done an excellent service to the citizens of europe and their demands. with my colleagues in the committee on transport we have approved a more ambitious text than the commission's proposals, which strengthens the level of protection of air passengers, who will finally be able to use new instruments for assistance, reimbursement and competence in the event of flight disruptions. the new text limits to the maximum the grounds on which a carrier can deny compensation to passengers, narrowing the field of what can be exceptional circumstances, to which companies often refer when they deny passengers a refund. the right to compensation in the event of prolonged delays is also guaranteed. another important new feature introduced by the regulation is the prohibition of the 'no-show' policy, the failure to show up for boarding by passengers which occurs when a carrier denies boarding to passengers on a return flight if they have not used the outbound flight of their ticket.

in writing. - i do not agree with the approach of the report which analyses a common framework for climate and energy policies in the context of horizon 2020. the proposals contained in the text will only unfairly penalize european businesses and the economy as a whole. furthermore, there is no trace in the entire text of an assessment of the economic impacts that the proposed measures would have at the level of individual member states and individual industrial sectors, including the impact on employment. for all these reasons i voted against.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it comes at a time when it is more important than ever to choose the right policies for the revival of the european economy. that is why i have always defended, even at the amendment stage, the three binding targets: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme. i believe that only ambitious and binding targets will guarantee the stability and regulatory certainty that will encourage the investments we need. reducing the high cost of energy, which has enormous repercussions for our industries and citizens, can be decisive at this stage. and to do that, we also need to make a strong commitment to energy efficiency, which i believe is the best way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, to foster new technologies, to create jobs and to transform economies to be greener. the import of oil and gas costs the european union more than 500 billion euros, and it is time to change course. we must act quickly and use these resources for the economy and for employment, starting with the green economy.
in writing. - the main problem with the 2030 climate and energy package is that it provides neither concrete measures to boost competitiveness nor signs of medium- to long-term stability to support investment decisions. today's proposal undermines any expectation of european companies to have a solid legislative framework for investment and innovation in europe, making it independent of energy imports. it is pointless to go into the debate on targets, but it is important to note that even the single 40% greenhouse gas target will result in a much heavier target than the current one for the ets (43% compared to 2005 emissions). the question of european compensation for the indirect costs of the ets for the electricity-intensive sectors is not addressed in the ets reform package, whereas the institutionalisation of backloading is proposed. environmental challenges must be supported, but not at the expense of a 15 to 20 per cent increase in the wholesale price of electricity, which further widenes the gap with us industry, which already pays over 50 per cent less for energy than european industry. moreover, the application to member states alone implies further, heavy efforts to reduce emissions by industry, in the face of the indifference of other countries.
in writing. - the report under consideration seems to me to be well balanced and therefore has my full support. firstly, because it does not hide behind a false moralism and recognises the historical responsibility of the eu and other countries responsible for gas emissions. we must not forget, however, that the time available for action is rapidly shortening and that measures to protect the environment are now of paramount importance. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to meet its energy needs. the carbon footprint of transport must be reduced, but we must not forget that biofuels do not yet meet the expectations in terms of significant emission reductions. the proposed approach therefore balances the need to promote emission reductions with the current capabilities of european industry and the economy.
in writing. - today the european parliament wanted to send a strong signal to the eu council of ministers: the banking union must be completed swiftly. the single resolution mechanism must be brought into operation immediately so that banking crises are no longer the burden of the citizens. the aim is to create a single fund which will be effective and, above all, swift in the event of a banking crisis. in addition to supervision, the aim is also to ensure greater access to credit for businesses and citizens. it goes without saying how important this agreement is to prevent new global financial crises. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr ferreira's report because i believe that it is urgent and appropriate to complete the banking union so that the eu and its economy can be supported by a sound and functioning financial sector. harmonising national and european banking policies is essential to stabilise the internal market in financial services and to remedy the fragmentation of individual financial markets which has been the legacy of the crisis. the regulation provides for the creation of a single resolution mechanism, the srm, in which member states are free to participate or not, which will be managed by a single resolution committee. at the same time, the commission also proposed a directive for the establishment of a framework for the reorganisation and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms to be developed at national level. the objective is to harmonise prudential and bank resolution requirements for both srm and non-srm states. the aim of the ssm is to provide effective procedures for the resolution of failing banks, seeking to minimise the impact on taxpayers and the wider economy and in turn complementing the single supervisory mechanism, the ssm.
in writing. - i found the ferreira report unbalanced and unworkable, and that is why i did not vote for it.
in writing. - the house voted today in plenary session in strasbourg on the report by mr ferreira on banks in difficulty. the parliament's negotiating mandate provides for a lean decision-making system capable of liquidating a bank in a weekend. the main role is given to the banking supervisor and the resolution authority to ensure that the process of closing a bank does not lead to political paralysis. the mandate would also allow the resolution fund to tap into funding in its early years, so as to ensure that it is effective from the outset, and not just when it reaches its cruising fund level after 10 years.
in writing. - we must not waste any more time and ensure that the taxpayer is not the first to come to the rescue of the banks in difficulty: the decision-making process for the winding-up of a bank is too complex and politicized. the resolution fund, as structured, would also have great difficulty in gaining credibility. the negotiations currently under way on the single resolution mechanism for banks in difficulty must proceed without the council insisting on wasting time.
in writing. - creating a banking union in the eu to increase financial stability is crucial to ensuring that the european economy can rely on a functioning financial sector. the single resolution mechanism will be a strategic element in achieving this objective. the proper functioning of these mechanisms is, however, linked to the proper application of a single set of rules for all failing banks in the participating member states, while providing effective procedures to deal with bank failures and minimising the cost to taxpayers and the economy. i am in favour of adopting this report because the supervision of banks must be exercised by the same level of authority. furthermore, article 41 of the proposed regulation guarantees the democratic nature of the mechanism, stating that the committee of the mechanism is responsible to the european parliament, the council and the commission for the implementation of the regulation and must send an annual report to the european parliament, the council, the commission and the european court of auditors and its executive director must appear before the parliament, the council and the commission.
in writing. - the objective of the single mechanism is to apply the same set of rules to all credit institutions in the participating member states, as well as to offer effective procedures to deal with banking crises, minimising the costs to taxpayers and the economy. the regulation will establish a single resolution fund for banks in crisis, which will be financed by contributions equal to 1% of the value of their deposits. it is also planned that, at the end of a transitional period of 10 years, the fund will be able to count on approximately eur 55 million.
in writing. - i voted against the implementing act which provides for the possibility of omitting the place of birth of the slaughtered animal, whether it be a pig, sheep, goat or poultry, from the labels.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution by the european parliament, which calls on the commission to withdraw an implementing regulation on the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of fresh, chilled or frozen meat of various animal species. the measure proposed by the european commission was very ambiguous and did not go in the direction of proper information, labelling and traceability, according to a model on which we have been insisting for some time. european consumers must know exactly what they are eating and where the products on our tables come from. generic and approximate indications, such as the mere eu/non-eu designation, cannot be accepted, because they would also risk setting dangerous precedents. we therefore ask the european commission to draw up a revised version of the implementing regulation, which would require the place of birth, rearing and slaughter of the animal to be indicated on the label of unprocessed meat from animals of the porcine, ovine, caprine and poultry species: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's citizens are informed and are able to make better choices.
in writing. - we voted against because the withdrawal of the regulation, the result of a long and painful mediation, would penalise consumers and businesses. we hope, however, that the next legislature will be able to determine an extension of the current regulation which may also indicate the country of birth for pigs, sheep and goats.
in writing. - my vote is to reiterate the need to maintain regulation (eu) no 1337/2013, as this regulation strikes the right balance between the need to inform consumers in the union and the economic costs for industrial companies. the regulation will improve consumer information without compromising the economic challenges facing the european meat industry. the current regulation is already able to provide clear, uniform rules for the three animal species covered and shared by the 28 member states, and also establishes a definition of the term 'raised in' according to the respective production cycles of the different species in order to ensure that the animal in question has spent a substantial part of its life in the member states concerned. finally, i do not think that any changes are necessary, since operators are given the possibility of replacing the words 'raised in' and 'slaughtered in' with the indication 'origin' for meat wholly obtained (born/raised/slaughtered) in a member state.
in writing. - i did not intend to support the delegated act on the application of a system of generalised tariff preferences, because i believe that such a structure would limit the right of parliament to express its views on each individual country.
in writing. - the single delegated act adopted by the commission significantly limits the scrutiny powers of the co-legislators, obliging them, in the event of an objection to a candidate country, to object to the entire delegated act, penalising all eligible candidates included in the delegated act in question. for this reason, i support the objection of the european parliament to the delegated regulation defining annex iii to regulation (eu) no 978/2012 on the application of a scheme of generalised tariff preferences (c(2013) 9133); i also support the request to submit a new delegated act to take this objection into account and to adopt a separate delegated act for each country that it wishes to add to the list of gsp+ beneficiary countries.
in writing. - i did not intend to support with my vote the resolution that analyses the greenhouse gas emission allowances to be auctioned in the period 2013-2020.
in writing. - i am voting against this text because i do not think the commission's proposal is ambitious enough, especially when compared with the great achievements made so far in terms of greenhouse gas emissions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment-related aspects of the environment.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution because i could not agree less with its approach to the ukrainian crisis. ukraine is not an eu protectorate. it is a sovereign country with a freely elected parliament. we should stop telling them what kind of government they should have, what kind of constitution they should adopt, and when and how to hold elections. it is not the european union’s business to ‘liberate’ ukraine or to take sides in its political process. it is ridiculous to ask russia to stop retaliatory measures against ukraine and, at the same time, to threaten eu sanctions if it does not follow our diktat. i believe that the latest events in ukraine show, instead, the need for a thorough review of the eastern partnership project. this policy should be redesigned with a view of including russia in its scope and not antagonising a country which is not an enemy – because russia is part of europe and should be treated accordingly.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the situation in ukraine to express my full support and solidarity with all those who have recently been working for respect for democracy, human rights and the rule of law, in line with the founding pillars of the eu. my vote in favour is intended to condemn the violence and abuse of power against those who are trying to defend their rights in ukraine. i think it is appropriate for the eu to voice its dissent about the continued violation of the inalienable rights of the individual and the lack of dialogue between political leaders. i believe that restoring the balance of power and preventing further escalation of the conflict is the eu's top priority. a joint effort is needed to assist ukraine in overcoming the crisis by identifying ways to provide medical assistance and financial and social support to the victims, and to help it initiate the necessary political reforms. developing constructive relations with russia and the eastern partnership countries will also play a key role, especially with regard to the signing of the association agreement.
in writing. - this resolution should represent the european parliament's view of the dramatic situation in ukraine for several weeks now. in all honesty, i don't feel like making superficial judgments from the outside, about who's right and who's wrong. i am not saying that we should not condemn violence, regardless of who is using it. it is precisely to examine this question in depth, which is also of strategic importance for the future of the european union and its relations with the east, that i have decided to invite natalia vitrenko, an economist and politician from the ukrainian socialist progressive party (psp), to the european parliament at the end of the month. i am bound by a common struggle for the separation of banking, but on this occasion i hope that your presence will also serve to clarify further the situation that the former soviet country is experiencing. in any case, i hope that the ukrainian people will always be the ones to decide their own future, without any interference whatsoever, not even from the european union.
in writing. - today in strasbourg we voted on the joint resolution on the situation in ukraine. in this resolution we condemned the violence against peaceful protesters in ukraine and called on the eu and its member states to take immediate measures, such as travel restrictions and asset freezes, against all ukrainian officials and legislators and their business sponsors (oligarchs) responsible for the repression and death of protesters. we also called for a 'concrete long-term financial support package' for ukraine which should be offered to a new credible transitional government in order to alleviate the current difficult payments situation. following requests from ordinary ukrainian citizens, activists and politicians, we have called on the conference of presidents of the ep to establish as soon as possible a permanent mission of the european parliament in ukraine in order to facilitate dialogue between the parties.
in writing. - the european union and its member states should consider applying targeted sanctions, such as travel restrictions and asset freezes, to those responsible for the killing of ukrainian protesters. all violence must cease immediately. europe must make its voice heard in a convinced, unbiased way, including by supporting the country through a concrete and long-term financial support package to be offered to a new transitional government that is credible and capable of alleviating the current difficult situation in payments.
in writing. - the democratic spirit and resilience shown by the ukrainian people after two months of protests has found my full support and my vote in favour of the joint resolution under consideration. the support and solidarity of the ukrainian people is the least that parliament can do to promote democratic principles in the country. the political crisis in ukraine and the violation of certain basic principles of the human person are very worrying and must be condemned without hesitation. the call to stop the use of force against protesters is accompanied by an appeal to the latter not to respond with the same coin. the eu remains ready to sign the association/free trade agreement with ukraine as soon as this political crisis is over and the applicable conditions are again met. the repeal of the anti-protest laws are already a step forward by the government towards resolving the crisis, but the unconditional release of the protesters would be a further step towards dialogue and social peace.

in writing. - female genital mutilation is a cruel and absurd practice that affects many women, causing devastating physical and psychological damage. despite the fact that 500 000 women in the european union have been subjected to this brutal violence, europe has not yet developed a common policy to combat this horrendous practice. we must aim at actions to combat this sad phenomenon through clear legislation, as happened in italy, for example, by instituting an absolute ban on fgm and by adopting preventive measures that directly involve immigrant parents. it will be important to achieve a level of action against fgm in all member states and it will be essential to promote the exchange of best practices used to date, building on the results achieved, by adopting a coordinated strategy for the total abolition of this practice. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution, with particular reference to paragraph 4, which calls for a legislative act aimed at establishing preventive measures against this form of violence which destroys the dignity of women.
in writing. - for years we have denounced in this parliament the practice of female genital mutilation, a problem which is as present in third countries as it is in europe. in 2008, i was a rapporteur on the anti-fgm working document to the european parliament. we therefore support a motion for a resolution which expressly calls on the commission and the external action service of the union to launch a strong and widespread awareness-raising campaign to bring all the territorial institutions of the member states into contact with each other, to involve the states with which europe has economic and partnership relations in the project and to implement international cooperation projects involving african women's associations in europe. only then will we be able to reduce this abuse against the dignity, the person and the respect of girls. we are also aware that inefficient border controls and the increase in illegal immigration may have increased such practices in our countries. it is a european duty to combat this 'depreciation' and to include in the global strategy to combat violence against women, contained in the recent istanbul treaty, the actions to be taken, at school and society level, against female genital mutilation.

member of the commission. - madam president, while we await commissioner malmström, who is on her way, let me say a few words on behalf of the commission on this topic, which is partly linked to the previous debate on counterfeiting. the confiscation of assets is a very effective tool against organised crime, because it attacks the financial incentive behind crime, helps protect the eu economy against infiltration by criminal groups and returns assets to governments and citizens. at present, the amounts recovered from organised crime in the member states seem modest compared to the estimated revenues of organised criminal groups. today’s tools for freezing, managing and confiscating criminal assets are clearly not effective enough. for this reason the commission proposed, in 2012, the directive which we are debating today to simplify existing rules and fill gaps which benefit convicted and suspected persons. i would like, on behalf of the commission, to thank you, mrs macovei, for your excellent cooperation and for your thoughts on maintaining the added value of the commission proposals on this important directive, which is both technically complex and politically sensitive. with the help of the lithuanian presidency we have reached a compromise agreement in time for adoption before the elections, and the commission welcomes that very much. the directive substantially improves the existing legislation for the union with regard to extended confiscation, third-party confiscation, freezing measures and safeguards. it introduces new provisions on asset management and statistics and allows for confiscation in situations where the suspect or accused person cannot be convicted due to flight or illness. we regret that the provisions enabling non-conviction-based confiscation in case of the death of the suspect or accused person were deleted from the proposal. the council and parliament have made a declaration inviting the commission to analyse the feasibility of introducing rules on non-conviction-based confiscation which might lead to further legal proposals in this field. we will now reflect on how to take this ahead, and we look forward to discussing it in the european parliament in the next months. finally, the directive recognises, in a non-binding provision, that the social reuse of confiscated assets can be a valuable tool in this area. the commission intends to follow that by supporting an exchange of best practices between member states. so thank you very much for your support, so that we can say together as soon as possible, as mrs macovei said: mission fulfilled.

member of the commission. - mr president, let me begin by thanking the rapporteur, mr díaz de mera, for the work he has done on this file. we have had excellent cooperation and i know how hard he worked to get the shadows and all the other co-rapporteurs on board on this very difficult file. it has resulted in a most comprehensive report, and i would like to thank him for that. i would also like to thank all the shadows and the rapporteurs of the other committees who contributed to this report. it is already clear that this report will be further negotiated in a second reading in the next parliamentary mandate, but it is important to have this first reading today. it is a set of negotiating positions rather than the final compromise, and this is normal. there are a number of elements on which we are still not in agreement, but i think we have come a very long way. let me make a few comments on this. the commission’s objective in putting this forward was to make europol more accountable, more effective and more efficient. i think we share those objectives. we are also in agreement when it comes to the need to enhance europol’s legitimacy in the eyes of european citizens by strengthening parliamentary oversight and incorporating robust data protection safeguards. throughout the report, parliament calls for a series of principles and introduces criteria and detailed procedure requirements applicable to data processing activities with the aim of safeguarding fundamental rights. this is also a core concern of the commission, and that is why data protection rules and safeguards are spelt out in chapters 5, 7 and 8. it is also important that eu legislation takes account of the better regulation principles, in order to avoid duplicating provisions set out elsewhere and imposing procedures which would be too cumbersome for practical cooperation. with these two principles in mind, the commission can take on board a number of the suggestions parliament has made to strengthen the text in this area. parliamentary scrutiny is, of course, of the utmost importance to me as well. it is important to recall that article 9 of protocol 1 to the treaty states that the european parliament and national parliaments together should determine the organisation and promotion of effective and regular interparliamentary cooperation within the union. some national parliaments have expressed their opposition to the creation of a new structure and prefer to use the existing forums. the commission believes that it is most appropriate to leave the creation of any new forum to the joint decision of the european parliament and national parliaments. regarding europol’s right to ask member states to initiate a criminal investigation and member states’ corresponding obligations, there are some proposed amendments here that seek to downgrade this right and obligation. we take note of the amendments, but we think that they would weaken to an unjustifiable extent europol’s role in helping national law enforcement authorities to commence investigative action by feeding them with relevant information. concerning member states’ obligation to supply information to europol, it is proposed to reinstate the council decision on language that requires member states to provide data on their own initiative. this amendment deletes the reference to priority crime areas and the obligation to send europol a copy of bilateral or multilateral exchanges between member states. the commission cannot support this part of the amendments because we think that member states should feel responsible for supplying europol in a timely manner with fresh, relevant data to allow the agency to build an accurate picture of criminal threats. turning to government arrangements, it is proposed to delete the executive board from among the agency’s management structures. some proposed changes here would reduce the number of commission representatives on the management board from two to one. these are basic features of the consensus reached among us – parliament, the council and the commission – in the common approach to decentralised agencies. that is why the commission cannot accept them. parliament also proposes assigning to the management board the power to impose a temporary or definitive ban on data processing. this is currently the prerogative of the edps, and therefore we do not support this amendment either. finally, the procedure for appointing the executive director is altered by reducing the commission’s role in a pre-selection committee and by involving the council and the joint scrutiny group in the selection. this again alters the balance of responsibilities agreed under the common approach, so we do not support it. concerning access to europol information for olaf, parliament proposes to remove from europol’s tasks the duty to provide jha agencies and olaf with relevant criminal information and to eliminate the possibility for olaf to have access to europol data. although indirect access could be envisaged, it is important to allow olaf to carry out these tasks in areas which are closely related to europol’s mandate – vat, excise fraud or fraud on eu funds. close cooperation between the bodies is enshrined in olaf’s recent legal basis, therefore we do not support the amendments. let me reiterate that there are areas – i have been commenting on a few of them here – where we do need to find further ground to negotiate on a second reading. but we do agree on many things. we have achieved a great deal together and have made huge progress. we share the objective of more accountability and greater efficiency and effectiveness for europol. i am confident that with some more talks we will achieve the progress and direction that are needed for a more accountable and efficient europol.
