2020 strategy. to do this, we of course count on the social partners and on the contribution of the social ngos, both within the member states and at eu level.
president-in-office of the council. - mr president, honourable members, let me first express my thanks to vice-president olli[nbsp ]rehn for his kind words. i indeed had the chance and the pleasure to work under his political guidance during the very important and historic period of the completion of the fifth enlargement and the opening-up of the european perspective to the western balkan countries. he should be proud of the personal contribution he made to these historic european developments. the debate today has demonstrated clearly that the european semester is not just an obscure bureaucratic procedure of interest to the institutions. we have discussed the issues which are in the forefront of citizens’ minds: public services, wages, unemployment, poverty and education. these are issues of concern to all of us, since they affect all our citizens irrespective of their home country. it is also the case that developments in one member state can have a sometimes significant impact in other member states, and therefore all these issues are of common interest. there is discussion about the situation. i think everybody agrees that there has been progress, but that this progress is not sufficient. i do not think anybody can deny that fiscal adjustment is underway and has given good results so far. let me remind you at this point that my own country has made a tremendous adjustment from a 15% deficit in 2009 to less than 3% today and, already in 2013, to a primary budgetary surplus. reforms are also giving results and, for the first time since 1948, greece has a positive current account balance. other member states which were hit by the crisis, such as ireland and portugal, have also achieved positive results. we should, of course, ensure better balance between economic and employment and social concerns, and the presence here today of both vice-president olli rehn and commissioner lászló andor is symbolic of the balance which we need. the inclusiveness of growth is one of the main principles of the europe 2020 strategy. the priorities of this year’s annual growth survey endorsed by the european council include tackling unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis. let me remind this house also that in the economic field there are binding tools backed by sanctions. in the social field we still largely rely on the open method of coordination. i would also like to recall that the social scoreboard is one of the innovations of the 2014 semester. the commission proposed this scoreboard in its draft joint employment report in the autumn and it was approved by the epsco council and then by the european council in december. we expect the epsco council in march to adopt the joint employment report, including the scoreboard. the debate as a whole underlines that the european semester merits our full attention. i hope that all the issues which were discussed today in this house will be at the forefront of your electoral campaigns so that the citizens of europe can consider they have a direct stake in the policies which have been enacted to achieve a stronger and more competitive european union and a european union with stronger social and economic cohesion.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank my colleagues, the commissioners and the representative of the council for their comments on our reports. i would like to take this opportunity to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken this initiative. we all agree that the european semester is an innovative instrument with great potential. however, in order to make full use of this potential, i believe that the consultation and involvement of the social partners and all forms of collective representation, which are concerned not only with the problems of those working in the strategic sectors which should make up the action of the european semester, but also with the citizens in their capacity as consumers, is crucial. the consultation must take place, it is a substantial element of democracy which we must strengthen, by trying to bring forward as much as possible the discussion on the aspects concerning the priorities and then the individual consequences of each measure, in other words in the construction phase as well as in the verification phase. the second aspect, which is equally important, concerns the content of our actions. we cannot limit ourselves to using quantitative instruments, but we need to focus on quality, that is to say, to verify the effect of the measures we are discussing and then decide to adopt, so that there is the greatest possible return. in this respect, the infringement procedures should also be reviewed. the infringement procedure must be considered the last resort, the last measure to be taken; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. only in this way will we be able to achieve the maximum result from the actions we propose and, above all, will we not have the use of the mere punitive act in the face of the need and the usefulness of promoting and encouraging positive behaviour.

in writing. - since 2009, the combined action of the financial crisis and the economic downturn has undermined the eu's stability and economic growth in almost all sectors. many member states have benefited from macroeconomic adjustment programmes, but the need to rebuild their budgets has made them difficult to implement and, as a result, has undermined the capacity of countries to invest. i voted in favour of this proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1198/2006 to help member states receiving financial assistance, as well as those which could benefit from corrective programmes, to continue to have the financial means to implement their projects under the fisheries sector policy. the proposal aims to extend the duration in order to ensure the proper execution of operational programmes supported through the eff without affecting the union budget. secondly, the proposal helps to simplify and speed up financing by stimulating projects and investments in the fisheries sector, and by facilitating an optimal transition of the programming period between the current and the 2014-2020 period. i believe that this is the only way to encourage the implementation of the projects and investments needed to ensure that the fisheries sector functions as well as possible.
in writing. - austerity alone is deadly. a country that does not invest cannot grow, much less have any hope of getting out of a phase that is predicted to be a recession. the situation of the member states concerned by adjustment programmes is alarming and could worsen if the support measures provided so far are abandoned. the european institutions must therefore be more flexible and more understanding. no use throwing a rope at a drowning man if you tell him to pull it a little at a time.

in writing. - the financial crisis and economic recession have since 2009 seriously undermined financial stability and economic growth in the european union in general and in the member states receiving external assistance in particular. in view of this and given that the present commission proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1198/2006 aims to help member states currently receiving financial assistance, as well as those that could benefit from adjustment programmes, to continue to have financial means to implement their projects under the sectoral fisheries policy in accordance with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - we cannot allow the financial crisis and economic recession to further undermine the financial stability and economic growth of the european union. this is why it is necessary to facilitate the management of the european union funds by encouraging and accelerating investment in the member states receiving financial assistance to revive not only the economy but the whole of european society.
in writing. - the commission proposal is consistent with other initiatives taken by the commission in response to the economic crisis affecting the eu and ensures that the effectiveness of the different funds is not compromised by insufficiently sound macro-financial policies. in addition, the mechanism of support for member states receiving financial assistance is fully in line with the principle of subsidiarity, just as the principle of proportionality is reflected in the extension of the application of the cofinancing rate increased by ten percentage points. in conclusion, i agree with the rapporteur that the commission must absolutely align this proposal for a regulation with the one on the funds in order to ensure that the increase of 10 percentage points in the co-financing rates for each priority axis continues until the closure of the programmes supported by the eff. the commission proposal is particularly urgent, which is why i wholeheartedly support its adoption as soon as possible and my support by a positive vote, in order to facilitate its early entry into force and effective implementation.
in writing. - the financial crisis and recession that have hit europe since 2009 have undermined the financial stability and economic growth of the european union. for these reasons, cyprus, greece, ireland and portugal, the four member states which currently continue to receive financial assistance, are experiencing serious liquidity problems due to the need for fiscal consolidation. the investment capacity of these member states is limited, both in the public and private sectors, which makes it more difficult to use the funds available for growth and competitiveness. it is therefore essential to promote conditions that facilitate the management of eu funds, to encourage and accelerate investment in these countries and to stimulate the projects that are essential to initiate a socioeconomic recovery.

in writing. - the amendment to rule 136 is to publish in the minutes of each sitting the names of members who are absent, who must be justified by the president of the assembly as 'excused absences'; the term 'parliamentarians' means those who, after presenting supporting documents to the competent bodies, cannot be present in the chamber because of maternity or paternity, illness, serious family problems or on a mission on behalf of parliament. i voted in favour of this proposal to amend rule 136 of the rules of procedure on the participation of members in sittings because i believe it provides greater completeness and transparency for the citizens of the union.
in writing. - at present, the concept of maternity/paternity leave is not covered by the legal provisions governing parliamentary mandate. the current wording of the article makes a distinction only between members who are 'present' during a sitting (and sign the attendance register) and those who are not, thus not taking into account any justified absences (authorised by the president and managed by the quaestors, pursuant to article 31 of the implementing provisions of the statute for members). the amendment also proposes that the names of absent members, justified by the president as 'justified absences', be published in the minutes of each sitting, thus reducing the negative impact on the attendance record of members and their 'parliamentary activity indicators' on websites such as vote watch, in duly justified cases. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the amendment of rule 136 must be a priority in order to finally allow the names of members who were not present at the sitting but had been justified by the president, for example, because they were on maternity leave, to be published explicitly in the minutes. motherhood is not a disease: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament.
in writing. - pursuant to rule 212 (1), the committee on constitutional affairs is required to examine the proposal to amend rule 136, which aims to publish explicitly in the minutes the names of members who were not present at the sitting but had been justified by the president (for example because they were on maternity/paternity leave), which is not covered by the legal provisions governing parliamentary mandate. the amendment, which i think is acceptable, provides that members justified by the president (on presentation of supporting documents to the quaestors) on grounds of illness or serious family reasons, or on a mission carried out on behalf of parliament, waiting for the birth of a child or maternity leave, will no longer be considered "not present" on the attendance list, in order to reduce the negative impact on the attendance list of members and on the related "parliamentary activity indicators" of certain websites monitoring the activity of meps, in duly justified cases.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am voting in favour of mr ulmer's report on how to achieve a reduction in co2 emissions from new cars. this is an important agreement for the whole union, which came at the end of a complex and not entirely correct procedure, during which the european union was paralysed for a few months by a german veto on an agreement already reached. but we have now reached a conclusion, and i think it is a good one. the community's average target of 95 grams of co2 by 2020 is significant and is a step in the right direction towards a gradual but steady reduction in the overall emissions of the european union and the decarbonisation of our economy, while allowing industry a reasonable time to make the necessary adjustments.
in writing. - the proposal which we as the ppe group have approved is intended to achieve, through the use of modern drive systems, a further reduction in co2 emissions from new vehicles which is not only substantial but also economically and ecologically viable. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the emission of gaseous pollutants from motor vehicles. the incentive scheme should allow all manufacturers to save up to 2020 on so-called 'super credits', which would be managed by the commission through a public register. manufacturers would thus be able to inform the commission whether or not the super credits saved should be flexibly calculated for each calendar year in order to achieve their individual target. however, manufacturers will only be able to claim supercredits if they do not exceed their specific emissions targets by more than 15% for a given calendar year. the incentive scheme will expire in 2023.
in writing. - i did not support the ulmer report because the positions it advocates coincide with the setting of overly stringent and binding targets which once again penalise the automobile sector, which is already heavily affected by the crisis.
in writing. - in this area we can say that a market-oriented approach has fostered technological improvements in the private sector which qualify demand and allow the legislator a certain ambition. the report maintains this approach - i am also referring to amendments nos 6, 21 and 22 - and proposes a measure in terms of accompanying production processes which are already well established in industry, such as the changeover of parameters from mass to footprint. the expected dominance of conventional engines can be seen as a positive factor for investment in technology. however, we should not forget that in a few years' time, alternative fuel cars are projected to account for 10% of the road traffic and that some observers (e.g. morgan stanley) predict a share of electric vehicles with a high range of around 5% by 2020. so the business-friendly approach pays off, by also guiding consumption along lines of environmental awareness. in 2020 the emission limits set today could be exceeded by a more general discussion of energy budget, mobility management, new modes of mass public transport. i would point out that in italy - which is certainly complicit in the fall in production and the contraction of the domestic market - more bicycles were sold than cars in 2013.
in writing. - i believe that setting a target of reducing co2 emissions from new cars by 2020 is an essential prerogative for the eu. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i voted in favour of the proposal, considering that, secondly, the union will be less dependent on oil, and that this will be due to the increasing efficiency and sustainability of cars, which will make the dependence on 'black gold' less and less. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the high price of fossil fuels is currently a serious threat to economic recovery. the proposed target for 2025 is 70 g co2/km. this target can only be achieved if the assessments of actual emissions are as uniform as possible: i fully agree with the rapporteur that a new test cycle should be developed quickly, which clearly and adequately reflects the real emissions of passenger cars and which excludes divergent interpretations and any differences between member states.
in writing. - the report concerns the amendment of regulation (ec) no 443/2009 by laying down the modalities for achieving the target of 90 g co2/km by 2020; the aim is to reduce co2 emissions from new cars. i am voting against the text because these measures do not help the european car market, but rather penalize it further.
in writing. - the european union has already shown a strong commitment to the 2020 target for reducing co2 emissions and has recently expressed its intention to step up its efforts towards an ecological policy. the eu intends to use initiatives that provide for car manufacturers to install modern drive systems in new passenger cars, further reducing emissions. adapting to new systems can be more costly for manufacturers, especially for high-end vehicles which often serve as a stepping stone to new technologies. the rapporteur therefore proposes the introduction of a system of incentives for the development and promotion of less polluting vehicles, so as to encourage investment by car manufacturers in greener and alternative systems. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that there must be more and more and more consistent efforts to pursue a green policy that protects the health of citizens and the environment.
in writing. - recent statistics show that co2 emissions from the road transport sector account for one fifth of the total co2 emissions in the european union. the worrying fact is that further increases in emissions levels are expected in the coming years. to reverse this trend, the european union has set itself the goal of transitioning to a sustainable and resource-efficient economy. the resolution tabled by mr ulmer is a further step towards achieving these objectives. the amendment to regulation (ec) no 443/2009 will result in stricter limits on co2 emissions from new passenger cars in the eu and incentives for low-emission vehicles. in the belief that these issues can be tackled more effectively at european level, i believe that the actions undertaken will help to increase the efficiency and sustainability of the automotive sector, reduce dependence on non-renewable energy sources and reduce the impact on the environment.
in writing. - in line with the europe 2020 objectives, the reduction of co2 emissions from newly produced cars is a proposal for a regulation which i am in full support of. the regulation is specific in that it sets out the proportion by which car manufacturers will have to comply with the co2 emission ceiling; the limit value to be complied with will increase as the vehicle weight increases and vice versa. the value will therefore be around the community average target of 95 g co2/km for new passenger cars, to be reached by 2020.
in writing. - the proposal under consideration is intended to achieve, through the use of modern drive systems, a further reduction in co2 emissions from new vehicles which is not only substantial but also economically and environmentally viable. given that it is appropriate to encourage manufacturers of new passenger cars and their suppliers to certify and incorporate into new vehicles technologies or technology packages (eco-innovations) designed to further reduce fuel consumption and the associated co2 emissions, and that there are as yet no recognised eco-innovations, as the testing procedure is too long and excessively burdensome, i have decided to vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the european parliament today approved in plenary the report by mr ulmer on the new rules for reducing co2 emissions from new passenger cars. the target set is 95 g/km by 2020. the text provides for an adaptation phase limited to one year (2020) and a system of 'super credits', valid between 2020 and 2022, in which the least polluting cars 'count' more than the most polluting ones. the incentive system allowing manufacturers to compensate for the production of polluting cars with less polluting ones could be active between 2020 and 2022.
in writing. - the path towards the gradual reduction of co2 emissions from new vehicles must continue smoothly in order to achieve the environmental and economic objectives envisaged. the supercredit system must be implemented in order to encourage manufacturers to continue to invest more in alternative transmission systems and to market them, with the ultimate aim of protecting the health of european citizens without penalising their freedom.
in writing. - the carbon dioxide emission limits for new cars are quite ambitious, but they represent an important goal to be achieved, yet in some ways unrealistic. a system is needed to promote the development and use of new, greener transmission systems and the costs of these innovations must not be too heavy for member states' budgets, which are already in serious difficulties. at the same time, however, the economic and productive sustainability of manufacturers must be guaranteed. i therefore believe it is important to encourage manufacturers to incorporate co2-reducing technologies into new vehicles. in addition, consumers should be able to compare different products easily, through a standardized test procedure, the 'new european driving cycle'. finally, i agree with the rapporteur that, given the impossibility of predicting which transmission systems will be accepted by consumers, it is not reasonable to submit a proposal for the revision of the legislation for the period after 2020 as early as 2014.
in writing. - mr ulmer's report aims to achieve, through the use of modern drive systems, a further reduction in co2 emissions from new vehicles which is not only substantial but also economically and environmentally viable. in the coming years, the emission limits for cars will be lowered further, with ambitious targets that will only be possible thanks to the efforts of manufacturers to research new technologies and eco-innovations. for these reasons, it will be important to aim for low co2 emissions while ensuring the survival of a wide range of manufacturers in order to preserve conditions of fair competition among manufacturers of new passenger cars.
it is important to protect and defend our companies against counterfeit goods from third countries, even if they are only in transit through european territory. the community trade mark system needs to be made more accessible to european smes and more efficient by simplifying and speeding up trade mark registration procedures, reducing the costs of the registration system and ensuring better coordination between the office for harmonization in the internal market and national offices, and finally improving the levels of protection of trade marks against counterfeiting.

in writing. - parliament today approved by 578 votes in favour of mrs wikström's report, which suggests the adoption of new rules to ensure that the eu offers better living and working conditions to talented students and researchers from outside the eu. the rules would make it clearer what conditions apply to the entry and residence of foreign trainees, volunteers, pupils and 'alla-peers'. the new rules should give third-country nationals the right to remain in the member state where they have studied or carried out their research for a period of 18 months after completing their research or studies, in order to seek employment or set up a company. the family members of researchers and students should also have the right to stay and work for the same period. the european parliament voted the bill at first reading to consolidate the work done so far and hand it over to the next parliament, ensuring that the elected members of parliament in may do not start from scratch but continue the work done during the current term of office.

in writing. - the new proposal introduces, in addition to some changes, two new categories of paid trainees and persons placed on an equal footing, in order to combat the exploitation of undeclared work. europe will increasingly depend on immigration to fill job vacancies and ensure economic growth. good immigration management is therefore essential to tackle the problems of an ageing european population and the shortage of skilled labour in certain sectors. i agree with the provision on refusal of authorisation on grounds of public policy, public security or public health, which states that refusal should be limited to the personal conduct of the third country national concerned. i also agree with the rapporteur that third country nationals should be allowed a period of residence sufficient to enable them to look for work or to set up a business. as regards intra-eu mobility, i agree with the rapporteur that it is a good idea to extend it to unpaid trainees and volunteers.
the proposal to establish the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps is a good one. solidarity in the form of volunteering is one of the founding values of the european union, which is number one in humanitarian aid. the creation of this body can therefore help to strengthen humanitarian aid operations in third countries in a very concrete way and to promote a sense of european citizenship in a visible way. the european union aid volunteers initiative complements and strengthens the humanitarian action of the european union and is a valuable tool to raise public awareness and to help highlight the value of european citizenship.
the proposal for a regulation establishing the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps bears witness to the values of the union's commitment and solidarity towards people in need. the establishment of a european voluntary service will help to fill the gaps in current humanitarian volunteering and will contribute to raising public awareness of the idea of european citizenship. i agree with the rapporteur that the formation of the voluntary corps must be strictly regulated, with selection criteria based on the specific skills of the volunteers and the use of the corps, but i would point out that it cannot be involved in any way in armed conflicts. i hope that this initiative will help to promote the union's founding values of peace and solidarity.
in writing. - i voted for this report because i support the creation of the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps. the corps will fill the gaps which currently exist in humanitarian volunteer work, and will also help to cultivate public awareness and the idea of eu citizenship. i believe the eu aid volunteers will provide genuine added value for the eu’s humanitarian action. it is important to stress that the role of the volunteers must be clearly defined and that the eu aid volunteers initiative should be an entirely humanitarian instrument supplementing and enhancing the eu’s humanitarian action, with the best possible use of the funding provided.
in writing. - the report we approved as a ppe focuses on the concept of volunteering as an expression of solidarity with those who are subject to humanitarian crises and emergency situations. the rapporteur's proposals also include the establishment of an ad hoc body, the volunteer corps, which should complement existing forms of volunteering and help to raise public awareness. in the face of a steady increase in humanitarian crises, the eu must be able to provide adequate humanitarian aid, capable of supporting all humanitarian operations. i welcome all the ideas put forward by the rapporteur on the added value of volunteering and its impact in mitigating, if not curbing, the consequences of a humanitarian crisis. at the same time, i strongly support the operational objectives and evaluation indicators set by the commission and the definition of the whole regulatory apparatus for volunteers.
in writing. - i found the striffler report to be acceptable and without any particular criticisms. that is why i voted for it.
in writing. - it is significant that while the united states has had a volunteer corps since the kennedy presidency, it is only now that the eu is laying the foundations for a similar initiative. i consider this to be a further sign of progress on the road to integration and therefore i vote in favour. in addition to the eu's primacy in humanitarian aid, it should be remembered that humanitarian aid is today a major foreign policy instrument, comparable in importance to the right of intervention theorised at the time of the balkan crises. it is a paradox to find in countries such as ukraine american volunteers or volunteers from individual member states, but not volunteers from the european union as such. the time has come to give political and institutional value to the financial commitment and the culture of volunteering, which is very developed and widespread in europe, in relation to the shared value of solidarity and subsidiarity. but in this - i want to be very clear - we will have to be very strict in eliminating redundancy, excessive spending and miscoordination of investment between member states, even at the cost of offending certain sensitivities and questioning established policies in the traditional 'areas of influence', in order to adopt a genuine european strategy aimed at leveraging goodwill in the context of security and neighbourhood policies.
in writing. - i believe that the establishment of a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps represents an exciting challenge for the european union and that its regulation is a necessary step to make it more effective in the various theatres of global crises it will face. i would like to stress the issue of volunteer safety: i therefore agree with the rapporteur's request that volunteers should not be sent to places where there are armed conflicts or internal disturbances. i also agree with the request for adequate financial resources for this project: we must not forget that the european union provides about 50 per cent of the world's humanitarian aid. i think that the commission should be able to take account of the fact that the european parliament has already been consulted on this matter. the commission has already proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european voluntary service. for these reasons, i vote in favour.
in writing. - the number, scale and complexity of humanitarian crises around the world have increased considerably over the years, resulting in an increasing demand for humanitarian workers. the deployment of eu volunteers addresses the real needs expressed at local level by the host organisations and provides real added value to the host organisations and local communities. solidarity is one of the most beautiful values and i cannot but applaud the daily work of volunteers engaged in humanitarian missions. i therefore think it is appropriate that their role be clearly defined.
in writing. - we welcome the commission's proposal to establish the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps, as provided for in article 214 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, with the task of expressing the union's humanitarian values and solidarity towards people in need. we are confident that this corps will contribute to enhancing the union's response capacity to humanitarian crises and to strengthening the capacity and resilience of vulnerable or disaster-affected communities in third countries. solidarity is a fundamental value of the union and volunteering is a concrete and visible expression of this solidarity. the volunteer candidates will be identified and selected on the basis of specific skills and know-how. the identification and selection will have to respect a diversity of profiles and skills among young people and experts, in response to concrete needs. the training programme developed by the european commission will have to be based on existing standards and in partnership with specialised institutions in all member states.
in writing. - the establishment of a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps can make an important contribution to the response to humanitarian distress and to the management of emergencies arising from natural disasters, both within the borders of the european territory and in non-european territory. the current emergency management system can certainly be improved by a homogeneous and coordinated action that leverages the unification of the different energies of the european countries. i hope that the organisation of the european voluntary corps will be able to take as an example the excellent systems already in place in some member states, including italy, where they are immediate and efficient, especially in the management of emergencies following natural disasters. the creation of the european voluntary corps should be characterised by strong humanitarian values and the principle of solidarity, which is a fundamental value of the union and which can be reflected in the persons who are involved in volunteering missions. only by involving the best organisations in the eu can we start the process of training volunteers and give them the recognition they deserve in the professions.
in writing. - the text just adopted establishes the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps (eu aid volunteers). the european charter of human rights, in line with the new treaty on european union, encourages european citizens and authorities to take the ideals of solidarity and respect for human life beyond the geographical borders of the eu. the european humanitarian aid corps will facilitate eu intervention in international humanitarian crises by making the work of european volunteers and institutions more visible and effective.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps 'eu aid volunteers'. solidarity is a fundamental value of the union and volunteering is a concrete and visible expression of that solidarity. the union must therefore ensure adequate humanitarian aid in the face of the increase in the number and scale of humanitarian crises. for these reasons, the commission and the european parliament have allocated eur 210 million over the period 2014-2020 for the establishment of a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps (evhac). the objective of this volunteer corps is to strengthen the union's capacity to respond to humanitarian crises and to develop a general framework of rules and procedures for the creation of a network of humanitarian aid volunteers who are sufficiently trained and qualified and whose safety is ensured at the highest level.
in writing. - the purpose of this proposal is to express the union's humanitarian values and solidarity towards populations in need, through the promotion of an effective and visible european voluntary humanitarian aid corps, which will contribute to improving the union's response capacity to humanitarian crises and to strengthening the capacity and resilience of vulnerable or disaster-stricken communities in third countries. moreover, its establishment would fill the gaps in current humanitarian volunteering, while also helping to raise public awareness of european citizenship issues. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps must be able to express the union's humanitarian values and solidarity towards populations in need, acting effectively and with visibility, and contributing to improving the union's response capacity to humanitarian crises. in particular, the ability to respond quickly to vulnerable or disaster-stricken communities is exponentially increased, and this is precisely the direction we must insist on.
in writing. - the establishment of the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps is an expression of the union's commitment to humanitarian values and solidarity with people in need. its establishment would make it possible to fill the gaps in current humanitarian volunteering. this body should be used during humanitarian aid operations in third countries, but i agree with the rapporteur in the proposal to explicitly exclude the contexts of armed conflict and internal unrest, in order to guarantee the safety of volunteers. as regards the indicators for measuring operational objectives, it is necessary to establish qualitative criteria as well as quantitative ones in order to ensure that humanitarian contribution is effective and measurable. on the administrative burden, i agree with the rapporteur that the commission should develop a simple system of certification mechanisms, seeking synergies in particular with existing partnership instruments and humanitarian standards. volunteers should also be identified, selected and trained in an efficient manner, with clear and timely rules, according to the assessment of specific skills and know-how, diversified for young and experienced profiles, and employed according to the specific needs of the different situations in which they operate.

i would like to stress the importance of today's act, the approval of the european fund for aid to the poor, an important act which marks the need on the part of the european union to address a poverty which, also on our continent, is becoming increasingly evident. the new fund provides for the continuation of community support for the provision of food aid, but it has also had to supplement this with basic consumer goods such as clothing, footwear or personal hygiene products, as well as social inclusion measures. the increase in this appropriation for the implementation of the fund is eur 3.5 billion, compared with the previous eur 2.5 billion, and it is envisaged to strengthen the principles of partnership at all stages of the programme. what i think is very important is to involve all the charitable organizations and ngos active in the social field who will have to fully monitor and activate for this to happen. it is an important act and this report is a strong signal of the european union's support for the millions of its citizens who are at risk of poverty or social exclusion today and who are in a state of severe need.
the spread of poverty in europe is a matter of concern, especially when children and adolescents are the victims. in italy, for example, food poverty is increasing: in fact, there are about 4 million people in extreme difficulty, including 400,000 children who suffer from hunger. the european parliament has greatly improved the commission's initial proposal, and has now approved a budget of eur 3.5 billion. i hope that the aid from the fund will be of practical help to the many people who are now paying in critical conditions and will provide widespread and constant support to all the institutions that are trying every day to tackle the most extreme poverty. i also support the rapporteur's proposal to combat food waste along the whole food chain, which amounts to about 190 kg per year per european citizen.
the european fund for the poor is one of the most important instruments of european solidarity, first and foremost for those individuals and families living in poverty - of course, mr angelilli recalled the numbers in italy - and food and material deprivation, as well as for those associations and organisations which manage the actual implementation of aid in the various territories of the union. parliament has certainly improved the commission's proposal, but it would have been even more necessary, in this period of deep economic crisis, to strengthen the fund and to provide it with greater financial resources, given that it is already able to cover only a minority of the population groups who would need help. however, the instrument itself is very positive and that is why i supported the report, despite the lack of elements because of the limited funds available.
the adoption of this regulation on the european fund for aid to the most deprived is first and foremost a due act. the fact that in recent months some states have questioned this instrument does not help to strengthen the idea of europe as a place of cooperation and solidarity between peoples. i do not think there is much to be said about the shortsightedness of those who do not see the suffering of millions of people who, during these years of crisis, have been rapidly sliding from a state of relative prosperity into a state of poverty. so these funds are in many cases the only chance of survival for millions of people. that is why the three and a half billion over seven years represents a real opportunity for millions of people and, thanks to the work of thousands of voluntary associations, we are able to promote an idea of europe which is not just budgetary discipline and austerity but something else as well.
when we voted in this house on the europe 2020 strategy, we set ourselves the target of reducing by at least 20 million the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion by 2020. today, with this regulation, we are making available a sum of two and a half billion, which goes directly to the poor and to families in need in the member states. to this sum must be added eur 1 billion which is allocated specifically by the social fund, although it must be remembered that this fund is directly intended for the activation of the labour market. it goes without saying that these are limited resources, which is certainly not a sufficient fund. it is a signal, however, because the commission's proposal is to be welcomed because the fund will continue to contribute directly to the eradication of a number of poverty cases.
in writing. - i fully support the creation of this regulation because, as the economic crisis is exacerbating poverty and social exclusion across the union, we must take tangible actions to alleviate the needs of the most deprived persons. in fact the aim of this fund is to establish a new, broader instrument, able to relieve the most severe forms of poverty such as food and material impoverishment. although the budget for the fund is still far from being enough, nonetheless it does have the potential to play an important role ensuring the predictability of the support, which is essential for the charities and civil society organisations. i also believe that it is important to stress that this kind of fund should remain a complement to national policies, as the obligation to combat and eliminate poverty remains the responsibility of member states.
in writing. - the european union, in the framework of the europe 2020 strategy, has set itself the objective of reducing by at least 20 million the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion by 2020. according to the data, in 2011, almost 120 million european citizens including over 25 million children were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, or about a quarter of the total population. in the light of the foregoing, i welcome the commission's proposal to set up a european fund for aid to the poor, although the resources proposed for this fund are very limited and not sufficient to cover real needs. it is estimated that this would benefit two million people each year across the union. in my view, the support provided by this specific fund should not be seen as an attempt to replace the overall policies needed to help reduce poverty: this remains a challenge for both the union and the member states. however, i believe that this new initiative is necessary and fully justified in the current historical context of increasing levels of poverty and social exclusion throughout the union, especially with regard to the reality of childhood.

in writing. - i think the proposal to amend the regulation on biocidal products is appropriate. these are found in many consumer products, from household disinfectants to insecticides, from antibacterial detergents to disinfectants. the use of these products is massive and it is sometimes forgotten that these are substances which are at least irritating or sensitizing. although the use of biocides is intended to ensure human well-being and the preservation of many products, the chemicals they contain can have harmful effects on the environment and human health. i therefore support the adoption of this amendment to make the necessary corrections and clarifications where technical errors and unintended consequences have been identified in the regulation.
in writing. - the report on biocidal products is part of the framework of regulation (eu) no 528/2012 on the making available on the market and use of biocidal products. this is important legislation, the result of a review of existing legislation on biocides to regulate their placing on the market and use. the aim is therefore to harmonise national provisions on biocides while maintaining a high level of protection for human and animal health and safeguarding the environment. in line with the rapporteur's position, i voted in favour of this report because i think it is wrong to reopen certain political issues on which agreement had already been reached during the negotiation of the original regulation. i therefore welcome the amendments contained in this report.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the italian railway sector is in dire need of modernisation. the high speed, the only one the rapporteurs have considered, connects only a very few lines and the rest of the network is in a deplorable state. in my region the situation is worse than elsewhere: the distance between the port of genoa, one of the most important in the mediterranean, and the french border is 147 km and a train takes three hours to travel there, with at least half an hour waiting at ventimiglia or mentone due to a lack of agreement between french and italian railways. and we are here to talk about a european railway package? after yet another interruption to remove a train, it took 38 days and 2.5 million euros for unexplained organizational delays. i would therefore point out that in liguria the infrastructure is obsolete and the citizens are severely discriminated against because they pay too high a price for a service which is frankly unacceptable.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, for years there have been attempts to introduce real competition in the union's rail transport sector. however, what has been achieved so far has been nothing but confused market manipulation, which is harmful to both companies and users. i therefore welcome the new measure, but i cannot hide some reservations, some doubts. i am concerned that the opening up of railway markets may be a one-way street, that is to say, only to the benefit of certain undertakings and certain member states and to the detriment of others. it is no secret that some member states ignore the principle of reciprocity by investing outside their borders and yet keeping their markets closed to foreign competitors. this must be prevented and severely punished, otherwise the same injustices will continue to be perpetrated in the railway market, which is europe's fault and which is harmful to citizens, businesses and the economy. the liberalization of the railway market cannot and must not put at risk the jobs of certain categories of workers who have also expressed strong and justified concerns about this. we will ensure that the fourth railway package, once it has been adopted, is fair and does not lead to redundancies, wage cuts for workers and no benefits for passengers. italian passengers are dissatisfied, very dissatisfied with rail transport, which in recent years, despite the advent of technology, has definitely worsened with longer journey times. unfortunately, the real problems of our citizens will not be solved by this fourth package.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i generally agree with the main objectives of the fourth railway package. however, these principles will also have to be changed to take account of national specificities and the particular conditions of entry into the markets of the individual member states, and to create conditions of effective reciprocity and equality between the different european markets and between operators. the opening up of national passenger markets should be achieved by including conventional transport, and not just the so-called high-speed lines, also to ensure efficient services on smaller and less profitable lines. i therefore fully agree with what mrs de martini said a moment ago. in fact, alongside the high-speed trains, symbols of efficiency and modernity, there are still anachronistic situations on secondary lines, with the use of obsolete materials and inadequate services, at the mercy of any trivial weather or logistical inconvenience, which cause inconvenience to citizens, in particular commuters, and can compromise the tourist and economic development of many territories.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the fourth railway package is moving towards harmonization and interoperability in order to develop a single transport system in europe. this modernisation action unfortunately comes up against a tragic reality which is known to european citizens on a daily basis. we have a double track: we have the high-speed rail, the profit rail, but we also have a provincial, territorial and regional network that is going into a dead end. i think that in the next legislature we must adopt a new package so that there can be subsidiarity between these two types of speed. this package, however, is a step forward. in this context i gave my support to the proposal for a regulation to repeal regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. this is an outdated regulation which was adopted when railway budgets were still included in the state budget and it was necessary for the state to provide financial supplements for pension and insurance treatments or when it had to compensate for infrastructure investments, such as level crossings. the 1969 regulation provided a harmonised framework for all such compensation, removing the potential charge of state aid, but it was reserved for only 36 companies in each state. it is clear that the regulation in question made sense when railway undertakings were only in external competition and had no internal competition, as liberalisation now allows. it is not even conceivable today that there can be economic sustainability by extending this kind of skills to everyone. the railway reform, approved last november, requires railway companies to be run on the same principles as commercial companies. we must therefore proceed with this repeal. however, to meet the concerns raised by some colleagues who wanted the repeal to be linked to the transposition of the railway reform by the various member states, we have provided for the entry into force of the regulation to take place two years after its publication in the official journal of the european union.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank the rapporteurs for this very important and significant work, even if it may not seem satisfactory enough to some. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the railways are not used for the transport of dangerous goods. unfortunately, we have very low data on transport use. one of the major weaknesses for a european railway area is certainly the railway network, which is insufficient, especially because it has bottlenecks in cross-border sections because of the low income they represent. this is therefore an element which should be addressed in particular by the commission, including in terms of financial support. another weakness is certainly the congestion of very different standards - some have counted over 11,000 - that characterize the technical and safety matters in rail transport. another element that some people consider a weakness - and i am one of them - is the way transport is managed. there are, of course, those who have the truth in their pockets, those who have an ideological position, arguing that the separation of network management and transport management is the solution. there are no examples in the world to justify this kind of theory, because the interconnection between network and management is a very complex interconnection, which is not comparable with other systems of public services, such as gas, water or energy in general. the question here is very complicated and complex. some people also remembered that this only generates interest on high-yielding lines. we believe that what has come out of the committee on transport is not enough. we therefore propose amendments which, in the context of transparency, will make it possible to maintain integrated firms, which are still a value for the european system.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i support and share the commission's proposal for the harmonised introduction of an interoperable ecall service at european level, since it aims to ensure that emergency calls are handled properly by the emergency services by applying the so-called 'crucial hour' principle, which is estimated to save up to 2,500 lives in the european union every year. the ecall system needs to be integrated within the vehicle in order to make the service reliable and available to all, which is what nomadic systems do not provide. to ensure full functionality throughout the life cycle of the vehicle, the ecall system shall be subject to periodic functional testing. the commission shall consider submitting a legislative proposal by 2014 to regulate the ecall platform. as a platform providing a public emergency service, it is necessary to ensure free access and the protection of personal data. finally, i am in favour of the possibility of linking other additional on-board services to ecall, which would ensure full accessibility for the repair and maintenance of the public emergency service.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as you know, security is a fundamental right of citizenship, but so is confidentiality, privacy. so finding a balance between two separate issues that ensure respect for fundamental rights was not easy. i think that the report we are discussing has succeeded in doing that and that is a good result for everyone. it goes without saying that we must defend and protect people who travel, who move, and unfortunately the number of fatal accidents is very high and death often survives because of a delay in intervention. the ecall can solve this problem. but it is equally important not to expose people using a means of transport to the risk of having information about them used for purposes which may be very different but which are nevertheless such as to infringe their privacy. we 've managed to keep these two things together: i am not going to go into the details of the commission's proposal.

answer to a blue-card question. first of all, formally, the adherence to the optional method is not only the seller's business. you can tell me that the consumer does not have the means to interpret this fact, because when he goes shopping he buys and does not care about which right he is defending or not. that makes sense. we are convinced, however, that the experiment with this instrument of optional legislation is to create a system which will be widespread in all countries, a system which will be unique and alternative to that of individual states and individual civil codes, and which will enable consumers to become accustomed to the international nature of their protection. now, of course, consumers only know the rules of their own country, their own state. so it is in the dynamic that is created by this measure that we have confidence. it is also true that there are some states which have superior protections, and you have mentioned the right ones. that's the truth. but what is our response now? first of all, the average level of consumer protection is much higher, and this will create a condition for the promotion of european consumer law which will be strengthened in a dynamic of this kind. so we are confident that in the two states you mentioned, effective protection will remain essentially the same.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because cohesion policy is the decisive instrument for the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. this report assesses how, in the context of cohesion policy, regions and cities can contribute to the different types of growth envisaged by europe 2020. it calculates the distance of cities and regions from the national 2020 targets proposed in the national reform programmes. future cohesion programmes will need to reflect these diversities in order to better concentrate resources, maximise effectiveness and tackle problems where they are most acute. on the basis of these considerations, future cohesion programmes will place particular emphasis on incentives to growth and investment in job creation. a clear reduction in unemployment will only be possible through targeted policies and a stable recovery.

every day dozens of people lose their lives on the streets of italy. in my region, sardinia, along the sassari-olbia highway alone, 100 lives have been lost in the last 20 years. much has been done in terms of prevention and the results are in plain sight. the number of road deaths has halved in the last ten years. in order to get as close to zero as possible, there is still a lot of room for improvement in terms of the timeliness of the rescue. in this regard, since 2005, the commission has called on car manufacturers to implement the ecall electronic emergency call service in their vehicles, but to no avail. today, by approving this report, we have made the system mandatory for all new vehicles registered from 2015. this is, in my view, a classic example of how the union's action can be of tangible and concrete benefit to the citizens of the community and to those who live in europe.
the adoption of the report on the ecall system is a clear signal of parliament's support for road safety. in 2012, over 1 million road accidents occurred on the roads of the european union, resulting in 28 000 fatalities and over 1.5 million injuries. the ecall system does not anticipate accidents or reduce them, but it can provide very rapid response procedures. in fact, the time is reduced by about 50% in rural areas and up to 40% in urban areas and you can help reduce the congestion that forms in these situations by up to 20%. in addition, such a system can ensure adequate intervention, especially when people in a state of shock are unable to communicate their position during an accident.
at a time when there is a lack of confidence in the work of the european institutions, this parliament is showing its closeness to the demands of the citizens by approving a text which protects their health and physical safety. the proposal for a regulation introducing the obligation to equip road vehicles with an electronic ecall system, capable of automatically alerting the authorities in the event of a road accident, will not only make our roads safer but will also help save thousands of lives every year. at present, only 0.7% of cars registered in the union are equipped with emergency call systems, but these are services offered only in high-quality cars that not all citizens can afford. the approved regulation provides for the mandatory installation of the system on all vehicles from 2015 so that all european drivers can benefit from the emergency call service regardless of the brand and at an affordable price.
in writing. - i share the de backer report which analyses the electronic emergency call service e-call. i believe that equipping all vehicles with an automatic emergency call system can significantly reduce the number of road fatalities and i therefore believe that e-call should be introduced in a compulsory and free way. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. - as i was in favour of the july 2012 report, i confirm with my vote my strong support for the e-call project. in the united states, the first projects for electronically integrated first responders networks date back to the 1980s, and advanced experiments have been under way for decades in many european cities and regions, even those with small populations. not to mention the individual devices, widely used in telemedicine, which are already in their third generation, capable of operating clinical trials remotely. i also recall that these aspects were already included in road safety plans more than ten years ago, which responded to the european objective of reducing road deaths. so the time is ripe. two concerns remain, both of which are also mentioned in the report: the first is part of the more general title of the maturation of an ict culture in an ageing population; the second, more sensitive, concerns the relationship between the right to privacy and civil liberties more generally, on the one hand, and the new safety and security systems, on the other. it must be acknowledged that the news of the past year has raised additional concerns which the information campaign to citizens on the unified number 112 will have to address in detail.
in writing. - safety is and always should be a priority. it is always and in any case pursued in all its forms, including the road. it is in this spirit that i have followed this proposal and especially the privacy aspect. i believe that in the face of an accident, sending life-saving rescues should take priority over even thinking that individuals' privacy might be violated. it doesn't want, at least from my perspective, to be a form of intrusion or surveillance at all costs, but simply a way to use technology to our advantage. if there are any negative aspects, they should be properly considered, but if it is not possible to have more security without reducing the level of confidentiality, i certainly prefer the former. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal for a directive.
in writing. the moments immediately following a car accident are crucial. anyone who works in an ambulance knows that to save a person's life, you have to run, every second counts. europe is helping motorists and rescuers with a sensor that, once installed in the car, is activated at the moment of the collision by contacting the emergency numbers. the instrument, which also allows the vehicle to be located, ensures that rescue teams arrive immediately at the scene of the accident, thus considerably reducing the time required for intervention.
in writing. - parliament will use a regulatory approach to accelerate the deployment and maximise the potential of the ecall system, which will be made available to all european citizens. the ecall system is an eu-wide public emergency call system installed on board vehicles which is automatically activated as soon as the on-board sensors detect a major accident. once activated, the system calls the european emergency number (112) and establishes a telephone link with the emergency centre and sends the details of the accident to the emergency services, including the time of the accident and the exact location of the vehicle involved. i believe that today's vote is a great signal and a fundamental and very impactful intervention in our daily lives. this innovative system will be able to speed up emergency response times by 40% in urban areas and 50% in rural areas, with a marked improvement in the timing of rescue operations.
in writing. - every year in europe tens of thousands of people are killed and 1.5 million injured in road accidents. with regard to the proposal for a decision on the introduction of an electronic service called ecall in the european union, i gave a favourable opinion because i believe that such a system can be useful and innovative in providing important guarantees on the timeliness of emergency calls in the event of road accidents. the emergency call system will be installed on all new vehicles with the aim of reducing the number of deaths due to accidents by automatically, immediately and free of charge sending a call for help from the car to 112. i hope that this measure will make a significant contribution to saving lives and reducing the severity of injuries caused by accidents, and will save valuable time. in defining this project it is important that member states ensure good organisation in the management of calls and encourage the establishment of appropriate infrastructures to receive and manage ecalls within their territory.
in writing. - according to the bill voted today with colleagues, emergency call devices that automatically alert the emergency services in the event of a road accident will have to be installed on all new models of cars and light trucks by october 2015. mr sehnalová explained that in the event of a serious road accident, the on-board ecall system uses the 112 telephone number to automatically alert the emergency services. it indicates the exact location to allow faster access to the accident site, save lives and reduce the severity of injuries. the bill gives car manufacturers a deadline of october 2015 to install ecall devices on all new models of cars and light vans. in the draft law, however, parliament has stressed the issue of data protection to ensure that vehicles equipped with ecall are not traceable or subject to constant monitoring.
in writing. - it is time for the european commission to take all the necessary steps to make ecall a mandatory service for new vehicles, considering that since 2005 only 0.7% of vehicles have installed the system on a voluntary basis.
in writing. - ecall is part of the e-safety applications which aim, in particular, to reduce the consequences of road accidents. the service is designed to automatically send an emergency call in the event of a major accident. immediate notification of the accident, as well as correct location, will reduce the time needed to provide effective assistance, as it allows for faster intervention by the emergency services at the scene of the accident. i share the principle of a more accessible europe for all and i think it is appropriate to apply this system.
in writing. - i strongly support the commission's proposal to make ecall mandatory in all new vehicles from 1 october 2015. in addition, the 112 service already exists and psaps have already been set up and are functioning properly and some states are already equipped for the implementation of the ecall 112 service. in addition, since the 112 service is not yet well known to the public, member states should increase this awareness through publicity and awareness-raising campaigns, in coordination with the commission, in order to ensure greater consistency in their action. a key problem is the exact location of the source of the call, through gnss location systems extended to as many citizens as possible.

in writing. - the commission recalled the central role of the reformulation of vat returns at european level in a wide range of acts, programmes and initiatives to reduce administrative burdens. the vat return is a pillar of the single market. as a strong supporter not only of bureaucratization but also of value added tax as an alternative to taxation schemes on individuals and labour which damage productivity and depress aggregate domestic demand, i am convinced that the single declaration, in a simplified electronic format, will have a positive effect on the whole of the european business system, particularly in those countries where the legislation and the resulting obligations on businesses are more complex. simplicity is also inherent in legality: a simplified system reduces errors and the possibility of willful misrepresentation. it is a powerful tool to combat tax evasion and offers a chance to reduce under-taxation and increase overall tax revenue, which is a necessary prerequisite for recovery policies and investment. it is not excluded that, if the results are satisfactory, member states will be stimulated to redistribute the tax burden in favour of households and enterprises. i therefore strongly support the report.
in writing. - the european union's value added tax (vat) is a broad-based general consumption tax calculated on the basis of the value added of all commercial activities involving the production and distribution of goods and the provision of services. i voted in favour of the proposal because, by introducing the standard vat return, it will be possible to reduce the administrative burden of vat collection by up to eur 15 billion per calendar year. the aim of the report is to improve the efficiency of vat collection, while cutting red tape and reducing the costs of vat collection for member states' administrations and taxable persons. the proposal will help to reduce the burden on business activities and to remove obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market. in summary, the introduction of a standard vat return should reduce unnecessary costs caused by the diversity of rules and procedures currently governing the presentation of vat returns in the union and should help to facilitate both the collection and payment of vat and the control of vat returns by member states' administrations.
in writing. - any rule that allows for the reduction of bureaucracy meets my favor. this is the case, for example, of this proposal for a directive, which finally allows for a standard model for vat returns, reducing what is known in english as 'red tape', i.e. the bureaucratic burden on the shoulders of companies. i am thinking of small businesses and artisans who do not have the manpower to afford an accountant and who can reduce their administrative costs thanks to this measure. but i also think that accounting professionals will be able to pursue more satisfactory activities from a professional point of view and will not have to run the risk of making mistakes in the interpretation of the forms.
in writing. - to simplify, to simplify, to lighten the burden of constraints to make life easier for our entrepreneurs. this is the europe we like, the europe which is close to the citizens and the workers. the proposal on the common tax system will simplify the work of companies working with foreign countries. the same forms and deadlines for all eu countries will ensure speed and clarity. once the new directive comes into force, annual summary declarations will be abolished and companies will be required to submit only the monthly declaration, while micro-enterprises will only be required to submit the quarterly declaration.
in writing. - directive 2006/112/ec has allowed member states wide discretion over the information to be requested in the vat return, giving rise to disparate rules and procedures within the eu, which have created additional administrative burdens for businesses. these disparities have created loopholes and generated fraud to the detriment of the member states themselves. mr strejček's legislative resolution proposes to amend the directive by introducing the standard vat return. at a time of crisis such as the one we are experiencing, i believe it is important to support the provision of uniform rules for the definition of mandatory information, both in order to reduce further burdens on businesses and to improve the functioning of the internal market and, at the same time, to combat tax evasion.
in writing. - the aim of this proposal would be to create a single vat return valid in all the countries of the european union, in such a way as to simplify the different models currently in existence by standardizing them through a common standard. the european commission's estimates are a little too optimistic in my view when they speak of possible savings of up to 15 billion euros a year due to the reduction in administrative burdens provided for by this measure. even if that figure is not reached, i am convinced that it can be a useful tool, especially for small and mediumsized enterprises, which are often burdened by similar bureaucratic problems which take up a lot of time and money. i hope, therefore, that the model proposed by the commission will be as simple and clear as possible, because i would not want this initiative to turn from useful to harmful if it is applied in the wrong way.
in writing. - there is a need for a more effective system of vat collection, given that as much as 12% of vat revenue is not collected each year due to various types of fraudulent activity. the introduction of the standard vat return and the reduction of bureaucracy and costs must be the basis of any innovation process in this direction.
in writing. - the european union's value added tax (vat) is a broad-based general consumption tax calculated on the basis of the value added of all commercial activities involving the production and distribution of goods and the provision of services, with only a few exceptions. vat is generally not applied to goods sold for export or for the supply of services. however, it applies to imports, so that eu producers can compete on equal terms in the internal market with suppliers of imported goods or services based in a third country. the rapporteur appreciates that the aim of the commission's proposal is to improve the efficiency of vat collection, while cutting red tape and reducing the costs of this both for the member states' administrations and for taxable persons. he welcomes the aim of limiting information requests to what is strictly necessary for the control and collection of the tax. the proposal strikes a reasonable balance and proportionality between the need to reduce the burden on business and the need to remove the obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market.

in writing. - parliament today approved new rules to ensure greater competition in the railway sector with the aim of providing better rail services to passengers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to meet its obligations under the treaty. new and small operators would have easier access to railway infrastructure and the complex authorisation procedures for putting trains on the track would be simplified, while public service operators, selected by the authorities, would be obliged to ensure working conditions for staff in accordance with binding national, regional or local social rules and rules on the transfer of workers in the event of a change of operator. the proposed rules also aim to create opportunities for new operators to provide services and to ensure equal access to infrastructure for all operators, while safeguarding the key role of public service contracts.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur that the threshold expressed in train-kilometres could be changed in the case of direct award in order to make it more realistic to award direct public service contracts in the field of rail passenger transport which are very small. in addition, the decision to award a direct contract should be accompanied by a justification, in order to allow other interested operators to scrutinise it and, where appropriate, to object in a timely manner. i support the weight given to the competent authorities, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. they should be responsible for preparing a local transport plan and for assessing the services needed for public passenger transport, as well as for defining public service obligations. the competent authorities are in the best position to assess which public service obligations should be defined on the spot, for which sections free access should be allowed and for which sections free access should instead be restricted by the award of a public service contract.
in writing. - the commission states that there are over 11,000 national technical rules governing railway operations in europe, issued by 27 national authorities which are totally different in terms of legal status, powers, competences, resources and training of staff. these numbers tell us two things: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem. the proposal to reduce the time taken for companies to enter the market and the time and costs involved in the certification of rolling stock is therefore welcome. this will be achieved by strengthening the european railway agency, which will become a single point of contact and issue the 'european vehicle passport', bringing about uniformity in decision-making and reducing unacceptable bureaucratic labyrinths.
