in writing. - the barandica report, which analyses the interoperability of the eu rail system, is balanced and acceptable. i think it would be desirable to centralize the technical certification of undertakings and the authorization to market vehicles. this would lead to the removal of technical barriers, creating a genuine single rail market and reducing costs for industry and operators.
in writing. - the rapporteur highlighted the economic potential of interoperability in the current fragmentation scenario. i would add that it is strange to think that, while the principle of free movement of persons within the european area has been in force for over 20 years, the necessary practical prerequisite of interoperability has not been considered. we have a railway system that is at the crossroads between the 21st and the 19th centuries, in which it is virtually impossible to develop operators on a continental scale capable of dealing with a massive and disorderly technical regulation. i therefore welcome the report because, at its core, it should set in motion processes of harmonisation of operating, safety and entry standards in a climate of collaboration with the national authorities, through the european railway agency. this process, duly extended to the collateral areas of the relationship with the user for example in ticketing, crm and with industrial chains, is likely to further strengthen and qualify the offer of european companies on the global market in the field of railway technologies, design and operation.
in writing. - recent studies have shown that by 2050 more than half of all passenger transport will be by rail. in this respect, achieving full interoperability in the sector must be of paramount importance. the data show that rail transport now accounts for more than eight billion journeys a year, covering about 10% of goods, with a revenue balance of 13 billion, 73 billion in revenue and 800 000 jobs. i have expressed my opinion in favour of interoperability because it will bring benefits to all rail transport by optimising time and costs. the heavy burdens on the railway industry are in fact a brake on its development. eliminating them will improve the service to users and make this industry an opportunity for entrepreneurs to invest in it, allowing for the creation of new jobs. the interconnection of rail networks will also facilitate and improve rail transport not only within and between individual member states but also with neighbouring third countries, facilitating the movement of people as provided for by one of the pillars on which the european union is founded.

i supported the commission's proposal on the need to repeal regulation (eec) no 1192 of 1969 on the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. it is a regulation adopted over 40 years ago, in an ice age, when railway budgets were still part of the national budgets and it was necessary to make up for losses and to ensure that there was an integration of pension and insurance provisions or to compensate for those infrastructure measures that were being put in place by companies which in fact represented the member states themselves. today that regulation is obsolete and represents a form of circumvention of the state aid and unlawful state aid system. for this reason they cannot be extended to all other companies and for this reason they should be repealed.
in writing. - the report we approved as a ppe focuses on the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. in view of the still fragile economic situation and the existence of railway systems still underfunded in some member states, it seems premature to repeal regulation (eec) no 1192/69 directly without having duly assessed the impact of the legislation currently in force. a compensation mechanism for the railway sector for certain compulsory payments under national law could remain a viable solution before introducing completely different legislation ex novo. therefore, the best scenario seems to be to postpone the repeal decision and ask the commission, after further analysis, to amend the existing regulation where necessary (for example by extending such compensation to all railway undertakings), adapting it to the current legal framework.
in writing. - i find the kohlíček report to be agreeable and balanced. i believe that the legislation currently in force on the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings should be amended in order to eliminate the current market distortion situation which allows access to compensation mechanisms to a limited number of railway undertakings operating in europe. for the reasons stated above, i intend to support the text with my vote.
in writing. - the adoption of the fourth railway package entails the repeal of the rules contained in regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. these rules concern the possibility for member states to compensate railway undertakings for the payment of obligations which undertakings in other transport sectors are not required to bear, such as special payments in the event of accidents at work or pensions for workers claiming early retirement for reasons connected with arduous work. i voted in favour of this proposal for repeal because the needs of the sector have changed and an update is most necessary. the main reason for this was that railway companies not included in the list were discriminated against against those included in the list. secondly, it has been noted that there has been little use of the regulation by the member states. in this sense, the repeal of the regulation by the commission is also necessary in view of future increased employment in the union.
in writing. - the report concerns the proposal for a regulation repealing council regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the standardization of the accounts of railway undertakings. i am voting in favour of the text because i believe that the repeal of the regulation is indispensable. in 1969 (the year of the enactment) the budgets of the railways were included in the state budgets and the state had to guarantee pension or insurance provisions, whereas today they are no longer required or enforceable by the state budget funds.

in writing. - the report concerns the proposal for a regulation on the development of the ecall in-vehicle system. the aim of this legislative proposal is to provide an 'ecall' system on all motor vehicles, which automatically alerts emergency services in the event of an accident (by calling the telephone number 112). the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem.
in writing. - according to the european commission, in 2012 there were approximately 28 000 deaths and over 1.5 million injuries due to road accidents in the union. these are dramatic numbers, causing pain, suffering and bereavement for many individuals and families. the death toll on our roads is still too high, despite constant police checks and the increasingly high safety standards of our vehicles. the ecall system, which we voted on today in two different reports, is one of these new technological aids and is automatically activated as soon as the on-board sensors detect a serious accident. once activated, the system calls the european emergency number 112, establishes a telephone link with the emergency call handling centre and sends details of the accident to the emergency services, including the time of the accident, the exact position of the vehicle involved and the direction of travel. the ecall system can also be activated manually by pressing a button in the vehicle, for example by a witness to a major accident. this should save considerable time in the field of intervention, and we know how important this is in limiting the tragic consequences of accidents.

in writing. - this morning, in the plenary session of the european parliament, i expressed my favourable opinion on the report by mr langen on the updating of community rules on information and advice given by insurance salesmen, since it counters the widespread phenomenon of information asymmetries to the detriment of citizens in the conclusion of insurance contracts. before signing a contract, information such as the type of insurance, the obligations arising from it, the insured and excluded risks, the means of payment and insurance premiums should be provided, as well as the total cost of the contract and the contact details of the insurance company. all insurance distributors should be registered with the competent authority in their member state. in addition, in order to further protect the rights of purchasers, insurance companies should undertake to provide cover of at least eur 1 250 000 in cases of professional negligence and to have a permanent financial capacity of 4% of the sum of all annual premiums received, in order to be able to pay a premium at all times. finally, customers should always be able to purchase the various components of an insurance package together or separately according to their needs and receive any useful information for each individual component.
in writing. - the financial crisis has undermined consumer confidence in banking and insurance products. insurance intermediaries are a valuable resource for the industry, providing in-depth knowledge that consumers now rely on. the commission's recast proposal is a good starting point for ensuring the protection of consumers, who are extremely vulnerable in this area. in particular, legal clarity is needed and i agree with the rapporteur that the concepts of tied sales and aggregate sales, as well as the rules on remuneration, need to be clarified. in addition, they agree with the clarification of the geographical scope in order to allow sales between registered intermediaries within the single market and their external counterparts. finally, the scope of the directive should be extended so that more stringent obligations can be imposed on price comparison websites that have been aligned with intermediaries operating in non-virtual venues.

in writing. - the health for growth programme will be used to achieve some of the objectives of the 2020 strategy, such as health innovation and sustainability, improving the health of european citizens and protecting them from cross-border threats. the new financial envelope of eur 446 million for the period 2014-2020 should also serve to respond to the growing demand for care generated by the demographic ageing of the european population, which is expected to reach 40% by 2030, and to provide quality care for future generations. for example, prevention and information campaigns could be launched that should involve all policy makers to disseminate strategies to promote virtuous behaviours to accompany the elderly population to a healthy and active ageing, improve access to health services, encourage telemedicine and train medical and paramedical staff on the specific needs of the elderly.
in writing. - the report we as the epp have approved focuses on the 'health for growth' programme, which is part of the europe 2020 strategy and has a substantial budget. the aim of this programme is to encourage research and innovation in health care, improving the quality of services offered to citizens and, consequently, their well-being. in my view, the health sector must not be solely responsible for therapeutic progress as such, but must be a pillar of the important european economy and a high-tech industry. i welcome the programme's objectives in terms of prevention and identification of risk factors, including poor dietary habits and sedentary lifestyle, and in terms of protecting the health of the individual, especially the elderly, with the consequent reduction of medical and social costs for national health systems. i also think it is reasonable to focus more on neurodegenerative diseases and other forms of dementia which, unfortunately, continue to have the greatest human impact (for the patient and those who care for him), health, economic and social impact. i therefore expect the programme to take an integrated approach which will encourage research into age-related diseases.

in writing. - ensuring a high level of protection of human health is a principle enshrined in article 168 of the lisbon treaty and article 35 of the eu charter of fundamental rights. the union must therefore ensure that health is perceived as an essential value by complementing national policies in this field. the commission shall, by means of implementing acts, lay down the rules for the application of this regulation and the rules for the application of the delegated and implementing acts referred to in article 5 of regulation (eu) no 1290/2013. i voted in favour of this measure because i believe that such a programme can stimulate a sector, the health sector, which can be compared with that of high-technology industry. increasing the potential and resources of this sector will create the conditions for the creation of new jobs, a substantial proportion of which will be for graduates, and will also make it possible to anticipate the consequences of the constant ageing of the population by means of ad hoc jobs such as home care. preventing disease, as provided for in the third of the four objectives, is a vital link in view of the fact that having a 'healthy' population means increasing its productivity and international competitiveness.
in writing. - the report concerns the establishment of the health for growth programme, the third multiannual eu action programme on health for the period 2014-2020. the objectives are to prevent disease, promote healthy vine styles, improve access to health care, etc. i am voting in favour of the text because it is indispensable and useful to the citizens of the member states.
in writing. - while scientific progress in the medical field opens the way to the detection of new diseases, the bureaucracy of the states is not keeping up, retaining complex and outdated recognition procedures. this situation constitutes a clear violation of the right to health and care and in fact discriminates against persons suffering from non-codified diseases, who are not guaranteed access to the same social protection schemes as those provided for citizens suffering from listed rare diseases. the european parliament voted on the third multiannual eu action programme on health, which calls on member states to give more support to patients with rare diseases so that they can benefit from cross-border healthcare, and to promote european coordination on research, prevention and treatment of rare diseases, including through the definition of common criteria for inclusion in national and regional lists. i believe that a pan-european approach and close coordination between the various member states can make an effective contribution to improving the conditions of patients suffering from rare diseases not yet codified, including by streamlining the recognition process.
in writing. - with today's vote, this programme will be able to use its overall financial allocation of €446 million until 2020 to achieve the main objectives of european health and its citizens. national authorities, international organisations and non-governmental bodies will have to make the best use of these resources to demonstrate that even in a period of economic crisis, health is not synonymous with a deficit but an opportunity to revive highly skilled employment in health protection.
in writing. - the health action programme aims to avoid duplication and to make the best use of scarce financial resources by concentrating on a limited number of priority objectives. i agree with the rapporteur that the allocation of the budget between the four objectives of the programme must not be static, as it could limit the scope of certain projects. with regard to prevention, it is necessary to be able to identify risk factors effectively, in particular in relation to the development of preventive measures against chronic diseases. the ageing of the european population must be duly taken into account, as the increase in life expectancy will result in a significant increase in the proportion of older people in the population, which is expected to reach 40% by 2030, posing challenges for both the economy and society. therefore, emphasis should be placed on neurodegenerative diseases, which particularly affect this population group.

in writing. - i found the report analysing the transeuropean telecommunications networks to be balanced and acceptable, and i therefore voted in favour of it.

in writing. - we must immediately clarify a misunderstanding which has not been made clear in this report either: when we talk about prostitution, we must absolutely distinguish between what is voluntary and what is forced, and therefore criminal. the latter must be fought vigorously, because violence and exploitation lie behind it. i think that voluntary prostitution is quite different, that is, the free choice to pursue a profession through the use of one's own body. in this case i am in favour of complete legalisation, following the model already adopted in several european countries where this activity is regulated and where prostitutes are subject to tax, social and health obligations. we can 't be hypocrites . when we say that it is the "oldest profession in the world", it is certainly true and from here we must start for a proper analysis. we are not going to allow the european parliament to be the arbiter of the decisions of the council of ministers. i am firmly in favour of the latter hypothesis and that is why, at italian level too, i am fighting for the repeal of the merlin act by means of a referendum. i'm sure the vast majority of people feel the same way.

the agenda includes the discussion of the statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the use of armed drones (21014/2567 ((rsp)).
this parliament is taking a very important position on the issue of the use of armed drones. the resolution agreed upon is the first step towards the total prohibition of the use of this horrible weapon. if there is one reason to forbid forever the use of drones it is simply the fact that they are a new weapon. we received a nobel prize for peace, and one of the main points is this: stop inventing new weapons; stop using technology and science to invent new weapons. so i am really surprised by all these limitations that are put by some colleagues on this issue. international law prohibits arbitrary killings, and this should be the main reason, in addition to what i have already said, for having a firm position against this new weapon. so i hope that this resolution will be the first step towards a total ban on this weapon.
president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. - madam president, i would like to thank the members for their remarks on this important topic. i would like to the highlight the following. first, the way in which the policy on rpas will develop will be influenced by two main parameters: firstly political parameters – member states, the european institutions, and our electorate – and secondly, it will be influenced by technology and industry. institutions can, of course, guide the markets, but this will be an interactive process. one thing is clear. there will be a large market for rpas. as the work mandated by the european council progresses, some member states will consider what sort of rpa they might develop, possibly together with the help of the european defence agency. but we are not yet at the stage where the decision to develop an rpa has been taken. as that debate develops, let us remember the context. we need to look at europe’s role in the world and decide what we need. i also want to refer to compliance with international law and repeat that we believe that all armed conflicts should be consistent with international law. we discuss such topics with all our international partners. reference was also made to the ethical aspects of the use of drones. ethical frameworks regarding human rights already exist, and the charter is just one example. as the technology evolves, we will of course examine their compatibility with these instruments. concerning the legality of the use of drones, our view – and this was raised by many members – is that their use should be consistent with international law.

the agenda includes the report by mr louis michel, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union (2012) (a7-0051/2014).
on behalf of the ecr group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, it is paradoxical that in 2014 we still have to talk about the failure of the member states of the union to implement the values of democracy and the rule of law that should have been the foundation of european integration. there are still many gaps in various countries. in italy there are still prisons where thousands of prisoners are held in unacceptable conditions. in germany, in the greater germany, institutions such as the jungendamt continue to exist to the detriment of the freedom and rights of children of binational couples and the rights of both parents. europe has opened its borders to goods, but some countries have closed them to children. few countries have signed the istanbul convention against violence against women, children and the elderly, and not all states have agreed to require their police officers to use identification numbers. there are many open questions on civil rights, refugee protection and freedom of expression. beyond our borders, men and women are fighting for those rights that have been denied them. it is also becoming increasingly necessary in europe to ensure that fundamental rights are no longer negotiable. we also need a common charter of duties, of the duties of the institutions towards the citizens and of the citizens towards the institutions.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i shall vote against this resolution because this europe is imploding, not because rights are not being respected, but because duties have been completely forgotten. we give freely of our rights and freedoms, without demanding in return that we comply with our duties and respect the rules. before we worry about discrimination against roma and immigrants - and even mention suspected terrorists as the categories that should be protected - we have to worry about discrimination against citizens. in my country, italy, it is italians who are discriminated against in the allocation of public housing, places in public day nurseries, subsidies and social pensions. as a former immigrant and proud italian citizen, as a sociologist and journalist who has been dealing with immigration for 35 years, i feel it is my duty to warn this europe against the explosion of a wave of racism, not because, as this motion for a resolution would have us believe, immigrants or suspected terrorists are discriminated against, but because citizens of european countries are discriminated against because of our submission to a globalist, immigrationist, goodness-loving and relativist ideology. i am opposed to the europe envisaged by this resolution. i say no to a europe that looks like a wasteland, where everyone who comes sets up his own tent and dictates his own conditions, and ends up turning us into a land of conquest.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have heard the rapporteur, mr michel, ask us to reconsider the possibility of presenting our report, even calling it disturbing. let us begin by discussing the situation of fundamental rights, the first of which should be respect for the ideas of others. what is there to be alarmed about when we write that we want an absolute ban on torture and cruel treatment, when we stress that we want to fight with strength against terrorism and organised crime? what is disturbing when we condemn any form of discrimination based on sexual orientation, when we recognize freedom of thought, conscience, religion, belief and disbelief, and the practice of the religion of one's choice? what is there to be alarmed about when we want the rights of refugees and migrants and humanitarian assistance to migrants in distress at sea to be respected and protected? what is disturbing when we are concerned about the fact that people with disabilities continue to be victims of discrimination and exclusion and when we condemn any persecution, violence, discrimination against roma in the european union, and many other things? what does not convince me personally - and i do not want to say that it is disturbing, for the sake of mr michel's report - is the high ideological level with which it is infested and which really risks jeopardising the realisation of fundamental rights because, through the appearance of fundamental rights, it enters into situations which in all our states are still controversial, are partisan political discussions and have nothing to do with fundamental rights.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union is undoubtedly a very important and advanced reference point. i would like to congratulate mr michel on the excellent work he has done for this parliament. in fact, this resolution contains in a clear and strong way, in all fields, what the fundamental rights must be that are to be guaranteed by a european union which wants to be at the forefront of the world in the field of democracy and freedom, as has been said of a europe which has the ambition to be an example and a moral force. however, the gap between what should be and what actually happens in the countries of the union in terms of respect for these rights is often very large. it is enough to think of women's rights, respect for sexual differences but also freedom of thought, association, politics and culture. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the information is not distorted. it is therefore essential that this resolution goes ahead, is adopted and gives the powers of the european parliament to all the institutions so that we can make a very important leap forward towards all public opinion.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european arrest warrant and the european criminal investigation warrant are two key issues in the construction of a european criminal area. the report by mr melo introduces more appropriate instruments to combat crime than those offered by traditional judicial cooperation. at the same time, the need to ensure respect for fundamental human rights, as expressed in the echr, in the conduct of investigative activities is an objective to be pursued. in this respect, the provisions of articles 5 and 6 seem to be appropriate. monitoring of the application of the arrest warrant has revealed significant differences in the application of the instrument by the various states. they are accompanied by regulatory gaps which make the protection of the fundamental rights guaranteed by article 6 of the echr more than uncertain. i think it is important to point out that the authority which issues the european mandate must check that the measure is proportionate, which is essential if we are to reduce the unbalanced use which has been made of it in practice. another recommendation plays a key role in the protection of human rights: i refer to the obligation on states to guarantee the right to an effective remedy under article 13 of the echr against a request for the enforcement of an instrument of mutual recognition.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner reding, there is no doubt that the judicial measures we are discussing today are of undeniable importance in the construction of a single area of justice, also from the criminal point of view. however, the credibility and effectiveness of justice require concrete and effective instruments, for which full and mutual recognition and rapid enforcement between member states are essential. as regards the arrest warrant, the rapporteur, mrs ludford, is right to suggest that it should be used in accordance with strictly proportional criteria, because there is a need, on the one hand, to protect fundamental rights and, on the other, to gain certainty in respect of a possible criminal offence. i congratulate my colleague nuno melo on the excellent work he has done on the european investigation order: the collection of evidence according to rigorous and concrete criteria that promote legal certainty. there is no doubt that judicial and police cooperation is essential at this time in the construction of this area of justice. to do this, it is obviously necessary to restrict the use of the european arrest warrant to cases where there is a conflict with transnational crime and in all those cases where it is necessary to resort to a precautionary measure. as regards the european investigation order, it is important to provide that the costs are to be borne by the executing state, just as it is important to have thought of and recognised the hearing of witnesses also by videoconference. there is no doubt that the computer system is a model of reference also at the organizational level. i would like to conclude, madam president, by saying how important these instruments are also in relation to the european public prosecutor's office, on which the next plenary session in march will discuss a preliminary report which we hope will guide the next work of the commission and the council.
vice-president of the commission. - president, let me remind the house that there are specific rules in the justice and home affairs domain. they are different to the rules in other political domains. for instance, according to the lisbon treaty, member states can make legislative proposals without the commission. this is the case for the european investigation order. fortunately, in this case, the european parliament is in codecision mode and could present proposals which reconciled security with rights. the second element is that before lisbon the member states could present proposals without the commission, without the european parliament, without the scrutiny of the court of justice. fortunately, this period ends as of 1 december. we will be out of the state of exception then. on the european investigation order, let me stress that i hope that this time this directive is implemented and applied, unlike the evidence warrant framework, which was only implemented by two member states. and i am also telling the parliament that the implementation of this directive can then be monitored by the commission. the commission will not hesitate to launch infringement proceedings for failure to transpose or apply the rules adopted. the same will be the case for the european arrest warrant, because on 1[nbsp ]december the transitional phase of the treaty of lisbon will end, and as from that date the commission will be able to launch infringement proceedings for failure to correctly apply the european arrest warrant. we will then work towards full implementation and in the case of instruments like the european supervision order, we can help to reduce pre-trial detention in european arrest warrant cases, so it will be important to have all the instruments functioning together. let me underline once more the kind of work we have been doing for several years now. i refer here to fair trial rights, which are directives presented by the commission on the basis of the lisbon treaty to reconcile security considerations with the rights of individuals. all these directives contain specific elements which strengthen the application of the arrest warrant, the right to interpretation and to translation, the right to information about rights, the right to have access to a lawyer, and even to have access to a lawyer in the country of origin and in the country of destination under the arrest warrant, and these are rights which you have on the table now. legal aid, presumption of innocence, procedural rights for children and vulnerable people, all these are very important so that we have this equilibrium which unfortunately in pre-lisbon times we did not have. parliament now has the possibility to implement those. i just regret that some member states refuse to participate in those elements of fair trial rights. that is not positive for the development of the european union.

in writing. - the common european sales law is an important element in the full exploitation of the common market by both businesses and consumers. the legal barriers often present in the various member states often discourage the sale (and purchase) of products abroad. increasing consumer rights and protections, especially in the case of increasingly online shopping, is now a top priority. similarly, for companies, promoting exports to new markets represents an important opportunity to exit the crisis. these measures are therefore useful in promoting intra-community trade and, above all, in making the rules uniform in relations between businesses and consumers in different countries.

in writing. - as a member of the imco committee, i am particularly interested in the subject of the common european sales law. it is clear that the digital dimension of the internal market is becoming essential for both consumers and professionals, given that online sales are becoming more widespread and have acquired enormous potential. i therefore felt that a revision of the regulation on the common european sales law was necessary in order to achieve uniformity in the regulation of these transactions, as many consumer associations also wanted. i agree with this and i think that a review of the consumer rights directive is also necessary in order to ensure that consumers are protected in a harmonised way in all the member states. harmonising the common european law on sales would enable small and mediumsized enterprises to benefit from uniform rules which, by applying the same contractual clauses, could thereby facilitate cross-border trade, reducing their transaction costs and removing the obstacles to cross-border trade which contract law places in their way. only in this way will the persisting national differences which are detrimental to trade and bear additional costs dissuade the parties from establishing contractual relations from coming to light.
in writing. - the establishment of a common law at european level on the contract of sale is a wise choice in order to harmonize the rules between the member states. this will improve trade relations and benefit the economy. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - the commission's proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a common european sales law is an innovative initiative of fundamental importance for consumers and businesses in the internal market. one of the main issues concerns the improvement of the balance with regard to the free choice of remedies, bearing in mind the lack of correction by the seller, the absence of the obligation to notify the termination within a certain period and the general principle of no payment for use. i agree with the proposal to reformulate and restructure the rules on refunds. the aim is to provide a solution that ensures a sustainable balance between the two parties, so that it is clear and predictable to consumers what they are required to pay or return. in this way they will be able to exercise their rights with confidence.
in writing. - the directive on the marketing of tobacco products dates back to 2001, so it was essential to update it, also in the light of developments in the sector in recent years. the priority remains the protection of health, in particular prevention for young people. the commission has therefore decided to take the necessary steps to ensure that the information on products is as accurate as possible and that the choice is made in an increasingly conscious and informed manner. it has also decided to prohibit the use of flavourings or additives which could in any way subtly attract adolescents to these products. i also share the commission's view that there should be uniform eu rules governing the trade in electronic cigarettes.
in writing. - the original proposal of the european commission had created some confusion about the exclusion of sugar from the list of additives allowed in the tobacco processing process. if this principle of exclusion had been passed, it would have caused enormous damage to italian and european agriculture, since the use of sugar is necessary for the processing of our tobacco and for making it usable in the production of cigarettes and other tobacco products. moreover, that measure would be unjustified, since the addition of sugar does not create any additional risk to the health of smokers. the positive cooperation between the agriculture and environment committees has fortunately corrected this aspect, which had no reason to exist, especially since we cannot guarantee our fellow citizens the same health checks on tobacco imported from many third countries as we do on what is produced in europe.
in writing. - the report we have approved as a ppe provides for some amendments to the directive on tobacco products currently in force. the legislation in force has often been the subject of legal action by the tobacco industry, which nevertheless has never had any significant consequences. i think it is right to share the commission's efforts to promote health as a value by combating smoking and its spread, especially among young people: the fight against smoking is of course part of a wider effort to encourage healthy behaviour and lifestyle which is also promoted by other international organisations such as the who. an important element is the result achieved on the sale of electronic cigarettes, which were previously allowed only in pharmacies in accordance with the initial draft of the directive. we have decided, by voting in favour, to refer the matter to the member states, which will now be able to decide on the sale and distribution of electronic cigarettes and their components in complete autonomy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mcavan report analysing the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the processing, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products, as i share the views expressed in it.
in writing. - i wish to express my vote in favour of the agreement reached in the trilogues with the council on this important european directive. like any compromise, the new directive certainly has its improvements and its shortcomings, but it has the merit of making the regulation of a complex and constantly changing market such as that of tobacco products, the consequences of which are well known, more modern and effective. apart from some of the ideological positions which were the precursor to prohibitionism, such as the complete standardization of the package, many of the rules laid down in the directive can provide a useful starting point for a more effective fight against smoking in europe and for the protection of public health as a whole. in particular, i refer to the new rules on packaging and effective warnings, the provisions on the presence of additives, flavourings and ingredients in cigarettes, the measures on traceability and safety and the regulation of e-cigarettes. these measures represent a significant step forward in a serious campaign to reduce smoking, to prevent its terrible and now well-known consequences and to provide consumers with full and informed information.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the tobacco directive which seeks to introduce new rules to regulate this phenomenon, that of smoking, which is so widespread in our civil society. the work carried out is the result of a careful assessment of the various interests involved, all of which deserve protection: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's environmental legislation and will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's environmental legislation. i think the final result is a good balance, with new legislation: two thirds of the package dedicated to warnings, new rules also for e-cigarettes, menthol cigarettes banned by 2020, limits and bans for flavourings and additives. we now hope that the council will approve the text as soon as possible, so that the two-year deadline for transposing the directive into national law can be triggered from that moment.
in writing. - smoking kills around 700,000 people in the eu every year and is the leading cause of preventable deaths. seventy percent of smokers start before the age of 18, and among these the percentage of very young people is very high. i voted in favour of the proposal for a new directive on the provisions concerning the processing, presentation and sale of tobacco because i believe that more efforts are needed to safeguard the health of citizens, especially in view of the good results achieved with the measures of recent years. the proposal for a directive contains measures to reduce the number of young people who smoke by eliminating packets of less than 20 cigarettes, by eliminating flavoured cigarettes and by making it compulsory to put on packets deterrent images covering 65% of their surface. the commission will be able to decide whether to market e-cigarettes as medicinal products to help people stop smoking or as other tobacco products. i believe that these measures can be useful in reducing the number of people, especially very young people, who start smoking and the number of premature deaths caused by smoking.
in writing. - europe's task should not be to criminalise smoking, but to carry out information campaigns on the dangers of smoking, and i say this as a non-smoker. the commission should act as a super partes, taking into account the freedom of choice of every informed consumer. one of the biggest risks is that the imposition of limits will encourage smuggling of cigarettes, of which over 80% come from china. in north africa, smuggling is worth about $1 billion a year and is run by terrorist cells that fund themselves by facilitating and speeding up illegal shipments. perhaps we should stop seeing smuggling of tobacco as a minor offence and see it as a real scourge of society. it is necessary to inform young people, including children, from primary school onwards, of the health risks involved in using tobacco products.

in writing. - if the single market is to work for the benefit of citizens and businesses, it is essential to improve the information available to people and businesses about their rights in the single market and the rules in force in the different member states. for these reasons, we must contribute to a better functioning of solvit, which was set up in 2002 and should be primarily a tool for identifying problems linked to the implementation of the single market. we have examples of late or incorrect implementation or examples of national rules which are in conflict with eu law. solvit really needs to become the place where citizens and businesses make the authorities realize that something is not working as it should. it still doesn't happen today. to give just one example, solvit should finally resolve the issues related to the recognition of professional qualifications, such as the clear distinction between tourist guides and tourist companions, which is far from being resolved, but still has cases of incorrect translation and terminology. i have put a question on this very point.
in writing. - solvit is an online network for the resolution of crossborder disputes arising from the non-compliance with and the imprecise and/or incorrect application of the single market rules. in this case, the disputes are between natural or legal persons and national administrations in the eu and are not the subject of legal proceedings at national or eu level. despite the results of solvit, there has been a steady increase in registered disputes, mainly related to social security, residence rights, recognition of professional qualifications and vat refunds. it is necessary to provide for new measures to enable solvit to adapt to new requirements and to function better. in addition to spreading the usefulness of this mechanism through ad hoc programmes, it would be necessary to eliminate any incompatibilities with certain national rules in many member states which are in conflict with eu single market legislation. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the progress of the infringement procedure. the committee also calls on the commission to review the potential use of the 'naming and shaming' principle, so that member states apply and transpose single market legislation according to the timetable.
in writing. - solvit is an online network for the informal settlement of crossborder disputes relating to the incorrect application of single market rules involving citizens, businesses or national administrations in the eu, to the extent that such disputes are not the subject of legal proceedings at national or union level. over the years, the volume of cases submitted to solvit has increased exponentially, with tangible results that have demonstrated the effectiveness of this tool for the single market. despite the positive results, there is still a great deal of room for improvement in enabling citizens and businesses to fully enjoy their rights in the single market through the solvit instrument. in my view, in order to ensure that the single market works for the benefit of citizens and businesses, it is essential to improve information on their rights in the single market and on the rules in force in the different member states, as well as to provide the necessary assistance to solve crossborder problems. in this context, i welcome the new commission recommendation to help improve the functioning of solvit and, in particular, the rule that solvit centres must work with the applicant to clarify the individual cases to be dealt with.
in writing. - as a member of the imco committee, i am particularly interested in the development and strengthening of the network introduced by the creation of the solvit network in 2002, as i believe that the presence of this instrument is beneficial to citizens and businesses. solvit is an online network for the informal settlement of cross-border disputes relating to the incorrect or inaccurate application of the single market rules, through which citizens have the opportunity to have their problems resolved and to receive advice on various issues relating mainly to the exercise of rights and the operation of procedures in other member states, in particular relating to: the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which aims to promote the development of the european union's environmental policy. solvit currently receives around 3[nbsp ]000 complaints per year, of which almost 90% are dealt with within 10 weeks of receipt. i have spoken in favour of the need to improve this network, because having a well-functioning, integrated, strengthened solvit and ensuring uniformity between the various member states is the key to unlocking the potential of the single market and increasing its growth.
in writing. - each year we vote on a report assessing the trends and developments of solvit, an online network for the informal settlement of crossborder disputes relating to the incorrect or inaccurate application of the single market rules involving citizens or businesses and national administrations in the eu. it must be said that since its introduction in 2003, its effectiveness has increased significantly, both in terms of its use and its satisfaction with dispute resolution. solvit started with less than 200 complaints and currently receives around 3000 a year. 89% of the cases handled were resolved or cleared within 10 weeks, with an average time required of 68 days, a marked improvement on previous years.
in writing. - the solvit online network has seen a steady increase in the number of cases submitted, with a resolution rate of 89% within 10 weeks. the results are therefore concrete and tangible and the commission's recommendation is a step forward in determining which structural cases should be handled by solvit centres. i agree with the report that a serious problem is the national rules of some member states which are in conflict with the eu single market legislation. the commission could also give serious consideration to the principle of 'naming and shaming'.
in writing. - mr løkkegaard's report focuses on solvit, looking at its operation from a broader perspective in the context of the governance of the single market. solvit has achieved tangible results and has demonstrated its effectiveness and value for the single market. however, there is still room for improvement in enabling citizens and businesses to fully enjoy their rights in the single market.
in writing. - i share the aim of streamlining and simplifying the legal framework for mutual assistance and timely assistance between judicial authorities of the member states in the taking of evidence in cases with a cross-border dimension, inspired by the principle of mutual recognition, towards an approach which takes account of the flexibility of mutual legal assistance and, at the same time, safeguards respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. the innovations introduced include: systems for judicial validation of orders issued by non-judicial authorities; increased guarantees for the execution of investigative measures abroad and incidents on the personal freedom of persons subject to such measures; the grounds for refusing to execute the order, based on the risk that the order may result in the infringement of a fundamental right of the person concerned.
in writing. - the report on the draft european parliament and council directive on the european criminal investigation order was adopted today. at the moment there is a certain difficulty in adapting traditional judicial cooperation to the current developments in european reality. we cannot deny that the directive is an important step towards the creation of a european criminal area, but the question remains of how to achieve this without affecting the fundamental rights and freedoms of every european citizen. following the reinforcement of police and judicial cooperation, which is also a milestone in the history of the eu, the time has now come to take the next step, namely to build a homogeneous criminal area according to well-defined guidelines to establish an area of freedom, security and justice. the guidelines to be followed include coordination of investigations, mutual recognition and protection of fundamental rights during criminal proceedings under article 82 tfeu.
in writing. - promoting the free movement of persons while ensuring the security of peoples through the establishment of an area of freedom, security and justice remains one of the cornerstones of the achievement of full european integration. over the years, police and judicial cooperation have been strengthened as measures to compensate for the abolition of internal borders and i am convinced that today it is necessary to go further, towards the creation of an effective criminal area. i voted in favour of this measure because i believe that the creation of this european criminal area is the last practical step needed to achieve one of the objectives that the 'founding fathers' of the eu had in mind. it is vital to improve 'strategic axes' such as mutual recognition, coordination of investigations and protection of fundamental rights in criminal proceedings. judicial cooperation must not undermine some of the core principles on which the union itself is founded, such as security and the protection of fundamental rights. in this way the cornerstones of freedom, security and justice must not be called into question; the guarantee that this will happen must be real, going hand in hand with judicial control over the respect of fundamental rights.
in writing. - the directive in question contributes to the concrete strengthening of the construction of the european criminal area. the importance of the latter is clear, as are its positive consequences for the life of the union and its citizens, and i therefore vote in favour of this report. i agree with the priorities identified, namely mutual recognition, coordination of investigations and protection of fundamental rights in criminal proceedings. i also think it is essential to stress the complementarity between harmonization and mutual recognition, but i stress that the latter cannot be achieved without harmonization.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the list of countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and the list of countries whose nationals are exempt from this requirement, annexed to regulation (ec) no 539/2001. these lists are to be kept under continuous review in the light of developments in the eu's external relations with third countries: each country is a case in itself and as such different criteria must be taken into account. the european commission has proposed to exempt citizens of the republic of moldova from the visa requirement in the light of the considerable progress made by the country in recent years in the framework of the liberalisation dialogue and the association agreement recently signed with the eu at the eastern partnership summit in vilnius. moldova is currently the first eastern partnership country to meet all the requirements of the visa liberalisation action plan. i welcome the commission's proposal and hope that this initiative will be a step forward in eu-moldova cooperation and further strengthen economic and trade relations between the two parties, bringing benefits and benefits to both.
in writing. - i can only vote in favour of this report for more than one reason. firstly, because exempting moldovan citizens from the visa requirement when crossing the borders of the european union rewards the efforts made by the republic of moldova in recent years to meet the requirements of the visa liberalisation action plan. the reforms carried out by the country's administration are considerable and to be commended. the second reason for my vote in favour is the tangible benefits that the moldovan people will derive from this regulation. the costs and expectations of travel within the schengen area will be reduced, as will the principle of free movement of the european union. i shall also vote in favour of the way in which this proposal has been put forward, namely without any amendments, in order to facilitate, as the rapporteur has said, 'a swift and smooth adoption process within parliament'. finally, i very much hope that gradual economic and trade integration will develop and bring the republic of moldova and the european union ever closer together.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the control of persons at the external borders in line with the rapporteur and the vote in the libe committee. the proposal for a european parliament and council decision aims to introduce a simplified regime for the control of persons at the external borders based on the unilateral recognition by croatia and cyprus of certain documents which can be considered equivalent to their national transit visas or for intended stays of no more than 90 days over a period of 180 days in their territory. at the same time, by voting in favour of this report, we are going to repeal european parliament and council decisions no 895/2006/ec and no 582/2008/ec. the amendments proposed and approved are aimed at clarifying cyprus' status as a member state which has not yet fully implemented the schengen agreement.
in writing. - i welcome the report by mr fajon on the introduction of a simplified regime for the control of persons at the external borders in relation to the unilateral adoption by croatia and cyprus of certain documents considered equivalent to national visas for transit or stay not exceeding 90 days over a period of 180 days on their territory. i say this because i believe that any barrier to the free movement of persons within the european territory must be removed, always keeping in mind the rules governing the proper functioning of the free movement of persons and respecting the wishes of the citizens of the european union. at the same time, i welcome any developments in terms of integration, especially in the case of croatia and cyprus, two countries which are part of the union but which, as far as the schengen area is concerned, have not yet put into practice the technical measures necessary to join it. i believe that a union in which the borders of these two countries are also free from controls can only bring benefits to the two countries themselves, in particular in terms of reducing the waiting time for visas, as they are more united and cohesive.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs fajon's report. the text deals with a simplified regime for the control of persons at the external borders based on the unilateral recognition by cyprus and croatia of certain documents as equivalent to their national transit visas or for intended stays of no more than 90 days over a period of 180 days in their territory.

in writing. - the european arrest warrant is a key instrument for prosecuting crimes across national borders, such as terrorism, drug trafficking, corruption. however, practical problems of application risk rendering its effectiveness in vain. in order not to undermine the credibility of the european arrest warrant and of union initiatives in the field of criminal justice in general, a number of problems need to be addressed: incomplete and inconsistent implementation of the framework decision, in particular the failure to respect the deadlines, the deficiencies in the framework decision and the incomplete and unbalanced nature of the union criminal justice area. i therefore agree with the need for revision, also to better protect the procedural rights of suspects and accused persons, to improve conditions of detention and to prevent any abuse of the mandate itself.

in writing. - as a woman, i believe that our role and our rights should never be questioned, even in what are traditionally considered "second-rate" areas. the scant and sometimes missing statistics show us that 100 000 women are currently employed in the fisheries sector, but it was only in 2010 when the hearing on 'women and sustainable development in the fisheries sector' was held that the real conditions of hardship faced by women in the sector were revealed and the need to promote greater participation and better protection of women was therefore evident, so i voted in favour of this measure. for many women, and i am thinking particularly of mothers, fishing is the only means of economic support for them and their families, so disciplining their working conditions, making them equal to those of men, could be a solution. women, as well as young people, are a category which, in a historical period such as the present one, is most affected by the effects of the economic recession, and i therefore believe that strengthening the associations and networks already existing in europe can ensure them greater visibility and support in any difficult situation through better coordination of the various actions.

in writing. - the report rightly emphasises the contribution of women workers in the artisanal fisheries sector, also considering that women and young people are the most affected categories in times of economic crisis. i agree that the new regulation underlying the common fisheries policy will have to define its objectives clearly and give value to the work of women in the sector. in doing so, the new policy will have to pursue the objectives of the principle of equality, historical recognition of the socioeconomic role of women in the fisheries sector, non-discrimination on grounds of sex, social measures and the necessary aid for unemployment, promotion of their inclusion in committees and advisory councils and the search for financial instruments and the necessary social measures and aid for women workers during periods of biological detention.

the agenda includes the report by mr sven giegold, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, with recommendations to the commission on the review of the european system of financial supervision (esfs) (2013/2166 ((inl)) (a7-0133/2014).
member of the commission. - mr[nbsp ]president, on behalf of the commission i would like to thank the rapporteur, sven giegold, the committee on economic and monetary affairs and the european parliament as a whole for the work done on this report on the review of the european system of financial supervision (esfs). the report underlines the important contribution the esfs has made to enhancing the quality and consistency of financial supervision in the internal market. the esfs was established to address the inefficient, uneven and fragmented regulation and supervision of financial institutions and markets, as revealed by the crisis, and the lack of coordination among supervisors. the report confirms that, overall, the authorities have lived up to the expectations we had of them. the report also points to some areas for improvement, particularly with regard to the governance of the authorities, which would benefit from a stronger focus on union values and interests. we very much welcome the contribution this report makes to the review. based on our own assessment and consultations, we agree that the authorities are cornerstones of the comprehensive reform process that has been initiated since the outbreak of the financial crisis. they have successfully built functioning organisations, started to deliver on their mandates and developed their own profiles. their roles should therefore be preserved and further strengthened. we acknowledge that the establishment of a banking union will impact on the functioning of the esfs, but it does not call into question its existence or the need for it. on the contrary, the european supervision authorities may have an even more crucial role to play than they do today in ensuring consistent application of eu law throughout the internal market. the recently-reviewed system of governance of the european banking authority (eba) reflects that role. the european systemic risk board (esrb) will remain the macro-supervisor for the union as a whole, with a mandate unique in geographical scope and in the variety of sectors covered. an assessment of the interaction between the esfs and the banking union would be premature at this stage, but this aspect will be closely monitored in the future. we appreciate the report’s consideration of some of the key issues concerning the functioning of the authorities. for example, we agree that due consideration should be given to how best to ensure that relevant decisions are taken in the european interest. we also concur that further streamlining of the funding arrangements should be considered, in order to ensure that the authorities can fulfil their mandates while taking into account the existing budgetary constraints at both national and european level. moreover, we agree that the decision-making process in the esrb general board could be streamlined. the commission takes note of the recommendations addressed to it in the report and will carefully consider them when preparing its policy response in this area.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday, 11 march, at 12 noon.
the agenda includes the report by sophia in 't veld, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, on public access to documents (article 104 (7) of the regulation) between 2011 and 2013 (2013/2155 ((ini)) (a7-0148/2014).
member of the commission. - mr president, i wish to thank the rapporteur, ms sophia in ’t veld, for underlining again the crucial importance of the principle of transparency in enabling democratic participation and fostering public trust in the european institutions. it is certainly the joint responsibility of the council, parliament and the commission to ensure the appropriate transparency in these institutions. this joint responsibility of the institutions also applies to one of the most significant instruments in the field of transparency – the right of access to documents implemented by the so-called ‘access to documents’ regulation. an ever-increasing number of documents are being disclosed following requests from citizens under this regulation. the commission, for instance, handles more than 6[nbsp ]000 access requests per year. this illustrates that citizens are increasingly aware of their rights in this area. the commission remains the institution handling by far the largest number of requests for access to documents. for instance, more than four out of five requests are granted at the first stage, and there is a relatively low average number of confirmatory applications – approximately 200 per year. the commission remains clearly committed to implementing access to documents legislation as fully, effectively and positively as ever. in doing so, the commission takes full account of the comprehensive case law of the court of justice of the european union, which has developed over time and to which the rapporteur herself has made reference. the rapporteur is putting much emphasis on the issue of trilogues, and given the role of trilogues in legislative procedures, it is clearly the primary responsibility of the co-legislator to define the appropriate level of transparency in this area. the commission supports the general aim to make the legislative process transparent and easily understandable. the right balance must be struck between transparency and the efficiency of the legislative process. as suggested by ms sophia in ’t veld, the commission is ready to re-examine, together with the council and parliament, the format of our annual reports on access to documents, with a view to making them more comparative. finally, as far as the review of the access to documents regulation is concerned, the commission remains open to a genuine discussion with the two branches of the legislature on the basis of the existing commission proposals.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday, 11 march, at 12 noon.

in writing. - the present report aims, on the one hand, to support the commission's desire to align the existing provisions on comitology with the delegated and implementing acts and, on the other hand, to simplify the powers delegated to the commission in order to safeguard parliament's prerogatives. in my view, the need to optimise the collection processes for statistics on inland waterway transport is now clear. moreover, in order to further consolidate the importance of inland waterway navigation, decisions must be based on objective, comparable and reliable statistics which produce verifiable data on the actual results achieved in this area. the naiades ii programme was adopted with the aim of making structural changes in terms of infrastructure, jobs and skills in inland waterway transport so that the sector can make a substantial contribution to the eu 2020 strategy. i agree with the rapporteur that water transport should be given the same importance as air, rail, etc. by introducing statistical data collection covering several parameters and making compulsory the collection of some data which has been carried out on an optional basis.
in writing. - the lichtenberger report does not make any particularly critical points and is intended to support the development of trade in goods transport by waterways which could also have a positive impact on our territory, and for these reasons i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. - in order to make the work of collecting statistics on inland waterway transport really useful and comprehensive, i welcome the proposal put forward by the committee on transport which raises some criticisms of the methodology of data collection and proposes some amendments to the text to remedy them. in particular, also in view of the greater completeness of the data collection for statistical purposes foreseen for the other transport sectors (maritime, air, rail, road), it is considered necessary that statistics also include passenger vessels. the purpose of collecting such data is to make inland waterway transport increasingly efficient, seeing in it a very high potential also in terms of environmental protection, and to implement actions aimed at achieving the objectives set out in the eu 2020 strategy, therefore it is appropriate to make the collection of some of the most relevant data mandatory and no longer only optional.
in writing. - the collection of data on passengers and goods carried is necessary above all to develop an appropriate inland waterway transport policy and to ensure consistency in the collection of statistical data for all modes of transport. i therefore believe that this opportunity should be seized to optimise the collection of statistics which must be objective, comparable and reliable. i also agree with the rapporteur that inland waterway transport should play an important role in passenger transport as well as in freight transport, since it is a cleaner mode of transport and also helps to reduce traffic congestion. however , it should also be noted that fleet renewal and the construction of more appropriate infrastructure are necessary to be able to relaunch this type of transport .
in writing. - whereas regulation (ec) no 1365/2006 lays down common rules for the production of community statistics on inland waterway transport, the commission stressed the need to align the existing provisions on comitology with the delegated and implementing acts with a view to adopting certain measures in order to preserve the prerogatives of parliament. i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that inland waterway transport plays an important role, not only for freight but also for passenger transport, and that the renewal or adaptation of the fleet would bring environmental benefits.
in writing. - common rules for the collection of data for statistical purposes on inland waterway transport will allow the structural changes needed to achieve the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. the priority now is to improve the infrastructure of the sector, in full compliance with environmental standards and to boost employment in the whole sector.
in writing. - the commission's intention to align the existing provisions on comitology with the delegated and implementing acts is commendable, but the powers delegated to the commission should be simplified and parliament's prerogatives preserved. statistics should be objective and comparable, but they are not sufficient at present to guide and evaluate eu policy in this area. in addition, inland waterways must also be seen as a means of transport for passengers, not just for freight, because it is a cleaner mode of transport, as it is not hampered by traffic congestion. a problem highlighted in the report is the lack of adequate infrastructure.
in writing. - in order to strengthen the eu's economic governance, it is necessary to focus on improving the statistical control system for data relevant to the macroeconomic imbalances procedure (mip). this is a strategy aimed at the rapid identification and monitoring of macroeconomic imbalances, while ensuring the quality of the statistical data collected. in addition to welcoming the proposal for a regulation, i welcome the amendments proposed by the rapporteur in terms of alignment with the strengthened economic governance framework and the existing legislation on european statistics, the transmission of data to the commission, providing deadlines for the notification and reporting of data, dialogue visits aimed at assessing the quality of statistics and the strengthening of the role of the european parliament by involving it more in the process of monitoring and verifying the data collected.
in writing. - i found the eppink report analysing the proposal for a regulation on the provision and quality of statistics on macroeconomic imbalances to be balanced and to be shared, and for these reasons i supported it by voting in favour of it.
in writing. - the report deals with a highly sensitive political issue: building the factual basis on which european governance decision-making processes are based. in this area, there have been major events, such as the bailout of greece, and small daily controversies, such as those which arise after each statement by the commissioners on the objectives assigned to the states. the report touches the raw nerve of a union which is still largely imperfect, marked by processes of renationalisation of the economies and by recurrent temptations to return to a traditional policy of influence by the individual states. on the other hand, it would be unfair not to recognise the efforts of those who are working for effective integration, which is guided by the values of solidarity and subsidiarity. i think that this is a characteristic of the report's forecasts, particularly where it envisages a greater role for parliaments in economic governance, effective independence from eurostat, a comprehensive and plural monitoring system which prevents instrumental and tendentious interpretations and which favours a government based on the values of equity, realism and genuine europeanism. i would also say with equal honesty that we should keep a close eye on the actual independence of the national statistical offices. one of the most serious problems is that european governance is too much affected by internal political dynamics.
in writing. - having very reliable and detailed statistics can always determine the success of one policy rather than another, which is why i think it is very important to adopt this resolution whose objective is to increase the quality of statistics which are used to assess any macroeconomic imbalances. the two-step approach advocated by the european parliament is adopted, first with a deposit of interest (0.05% of gdp) and then with fines in favour of the european stability mechanism. moreover, the geographical scope is not limited to the euro area but applies to all 28 member states, so that all states will be subject to the same rules.
in writing. - whereas the proposal aims to ensure the quality and timeliness of the production, supply and quality monitoring of statistical data produced or transmitted for the purposes of the procedures for the detection of macroeconomic imbalances, as well as the prevention and correlation of excessive imbalances within the union; whereas the proposal for a regulation aims to align the economic governance framework with the existing european statistics legislation and to clarify the transmission of data to the commission by improving the efficiency of the proposed procedures ('dialogue visits'). in view of the opinion of the econ committee, the committee responsible for the substance of the proposal and the suggestions received from the regi and empl committees, i have voted in favour of the proposal.

in writing. - i supported the report on genetic resources because i am aware of the scale of the phenomenon of biodiversity loss. this is not a position dictated solely by ethical and/or moral convictions, but rather by the desire to reduce the impact of biodiversity loss in economic and social terms. preserving biodiversity therefore becomes a shared mission to safeguard europe's socioeconomic dynamism by directly benefiting from the use of genetic resources. this report, together with the report on the nagoya protocol, forms part of the international strategy for the conservation of biodiversity. the eu has decided to challenge the member states on the issue of access to genetic resources, but believes that clear and unequivocal provisions should be provided on the fair sharing of benefits (not just financial) from the use of these resources and also on compliance with international legal obligations. this allocation mechanism will allow for the protection of the environment, social progress and the sustainable use of in situ resources. i welcome the rapporteur's proposals on the chain of use of energy resources and the associated traditional knowledge, as well as on strengthening transparency and legal certainty.
