in writing. - i am wary of any economic evaluation of biodiversity as a tool for political discussion and note that this approach has been the focus of a heated debate for years, not limited to academic circles. i prefer to focus on the clear implications of protecting biodiversity as the foundation of a future that can be built on the christian and liberal values of intelligent stewardship of natural resources. in this context, i also support the report because of the many references to human rights in the context of natural resource management: it is essential to agree on an approach which recognises fair and forward-looking management as an element of a society based on free markets, accountability and legality. the nagoya protocol clearly links benefit-sharing with a vision of sustainability and biodiversity conservation. finally, i would like to join the suggestions for greater transparency and legality and for combating bio-piracy, which is a scourge specifically linked to those dangerous currents of thought and utopian movements whose common final destination is invariably the denial of the value of the person and of man.
in writing. - the main objective of this regulation, which is the same as the nagoya protocol itself, is to preserve and protect biological diversity. other secondary objectives, such as the transfer of technology to developing countries, complement and reinforce the first objective. i therefore believe that, in a context where the loss of biodiversity continues to worsen and accelerate, it is right to vote in favour of this commission regulation and to approve the amendments proposed by the rapporteur. i appreciate the aims of the proposed amendments, in particular that of benefiting european citizens by guaranteeing traceability and ethics, respect for international legal obligations and fair and equitable sharing of benefits. i also believe that the desire to strengthen international equity and the confidence of third countries suppliers is something that can be shared and that this can contribute to the preservation of the environment, social progress and a sustainable use of resources. i also agree with the need to combat 'biopiracy', i.e. the illegal acquisition and use of genetic resources, and i believe that by defining the crime of 'biopiracy' in law and by laying down appropriate sanctions, we can effectively combat this phenomenon.
in writing. - sharing the benefits of greater use of genetic resources and a deeper sharing of good practices and technologies can only be welcomed. i vote in favour of this.
in writing. - the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council aims to ensure that biodiversity, its peoples and their knowledge are preserved and that the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge are distributed in a fair and equitable manner. this is the spirit in which the nagoya protocol on access and benefit-sharing was signed in 2010 in the context of the 10th conference of the parties to the convention on biological diversity, and it is time for the european union to transpose and reflect that protocol. i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - one of the eu's objectives must be to ensure the integrity of the chain of use, to allow traceability and legal certainty for users, which is why i support the proposal to maintain control points when a marketing authorisation is applied for and when public or private research funding is granted. legal certainty is a key element in creating a simple and immediate legislative framework, which is why the term 'biopiracy' needs to be clarified and transparency in the management of genetic resources ensured. i also welcome the rapporteur's proposal to create a union fund for benefit sharing, funded by the users of genetic resources with a view to preserving the world's biodiversity, which could contribute to a multilateral worldwide benefit sharing mechanism, as provided for in article 10 of the nagoya protocol.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, over 38 000 people die on european roads every year, and 5 of those people die every day because of technical defects in the vehicles they drive. a recent study even found that about 10% of cars and motor vehicles in circulation have a defect that would prevent them from passing technical inspections. for these reasons i support the report by mr werner kuhn, which makes the checks on motor vehicles more stringent and rigorous, thus helping to make european roads safer. the text we have worked on in committee is designed to extend these checks to scooters, motorcycles and light vehicles, with an increase in the frequency of checks also on cars and light vehicles: four years from the date of first registration and two years thereafter. it is important to stress, mr president, and i conclude, that this regulation does not affect the possibility for the member states to introduce stricter rules, but always in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. - i have decided today to approve the report on the technical inspections of vehicles and their trailers because i believe that it is appropriate to assess carefully and precisely the impact that the proposals put forward could have on citizens and businesses, especially in financial and administrative terms, avoiding creating additional complications, burdens and inefficient bureaucratic procedures. i welcome the commission's proposals as amended by the rapporteur on the following points: frequency of inspections and vehicle categories, technical requirements and test methods, qualification of independent inspectors to carry out technical inspections, exemptions for historic passenger cars, cross-border re-registration of a vehicle and consolidation of delegated acts. i think it is good to focus on the education and training of inspectors not only to ensure efficient control and optimum safety, but also to avoid any potential conflict of interest. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very important one.
in writing. - i think that the kuhn report contains contradictory and unclear points, which is why i abstained.
in writing. - although the so-called peltzmann effect has been codified for almost 40 years, it has been less than ten years since the european legislator began to assess this phenomenon (in which the increase in physical and technical safety measures can increase the risks arising from human behaviour). in other words, the regulation of vehicle inspections should be periodically reviewed as a tool linked to the general objectives of reducing emissions and protecting the health and safety of citizens, without unduly emphasising the benefits and in accordance with the principle of proportionality, especially as vehicles are often the capital goods of smes or are modes of urban transport with no viable alternative for consumers. to impose additional burdens on them in a time of crisis would be harmful and wrong. the data in our possession show that the vast majority of road accidents are due to dangerous behaviour rather than to the technical inadequacy of the vehicles, and a significant proportion is due to improper configuration of the seat and intersections in relation to the weak user (pedestrians, cyclists). that said, i support the extension of checks to motorcycles and i support the rapporteur's position, which intends to moderate the commission's forecasts somewhat.
in writing. - the increasing mobility of people across the european union requires more harmonised legislation on roadworthiness tests. this legislation is necessary to improve road safety. i have chosen to support the proposal because it provides for new rules on roadworthiness tests, with the aim of further improving road safety and ensuring a high level of environmental protection. the proposal is based on the establishment of common minimum standards at eu level for vehicle inspections but allows member states to introduce more stringent standards. the proposal provides for: a mandatory eu-wide roadworthiness test for scooters and motorcycles; an increase in the frequency of periodic roadworthiness tests for certain categories of vehicles; a minimum level of competence and training requirements for inspectors; and an improvement in the quality of vehicle checks by defining common minimum standards for deficiencies and instruments. it also provides for the introduction of mandatory checks on electronic security components.
in writing. - i am in favour of the proposal for a regulation as a whole, which i consider to be considerably improved by the addition of the necessary amendments. this regulation is part of the continuing process of unification between all the member states, which necessarily must also provide for transport safety. with the free movement of persons between community countries, there is a growing need to standardize safety checks on the condition of motor vehicles on public roads. this regulation, which does not preclude member states from introducing stricter rules in their national legislation, aims to ensure minimum safety standards for all vehicles registered in the eu by reducing road accidents and by further protecting the rights of consumers, who will be able to consult a detailed list of the use of each vehicle, including the actual mileage, by means of a register, thereby limiting fraud in the sale of used vehicles. the need for serious and professional checks by qualified staff is emphasised and the aim is to reduce the burden of such checks on the public.

in writing. - the proposal to introduce common european standards for vehicle inspection is a step forward in improving road safety. the possibility for member states to apply stricter rules is itself a means of protecting citizens and reducing road casualties. finally, the introduction of tachograph control and, above all, the increase in penalties for tampering will make it possible to develop trade in vehicles between the different member states.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the united nations and the european union define torture as an act against fundamental human rights. it is anachronistic that they should still be forced to talk about it today. yet too many states still practise it, along with the death penalty. torture is practiced by institutional actors such as the police and in some cases by independent actors, and these are the most difficult cases to counter. today we want to say no to any practice that brings pain and suffering to all human beings, especially the most vulnerable, that is, children, and we will continue to fight so that child pornography is just a bad dream. this report on the eradication of torture in the world is a very important step forward in the work of this parliament.
in writing. - i strongly support this report, which denounces the continued occurrence of torture and other forms of ill-treatment throughout the world. we have the duty to reiterate at every opportunity the absolute condemnation of such acts, which are and must remain prohibited at any time and in any place whatsoever and can thus never be justified. with this text we underline that the implementation of the eu guidelines on torture remains insufficient, and therefore we urge the european external action service and the member states to give renewed impetus to the application of those guidelines.
in writing. - i support the report, convinced that the eu must be a contemporary reference in the field of civil and human rights. without taking anything away from the united nations, the fruit of the intuition of an american president of a positivist culture, after the bloodbath of the great war, i would point out that the first elaborations can be traced back to our ancient classical and especially christian cultural matrices and to the concept of the rule of law, which was widely codified in the middle ages. i agree with the points in paragraphs 2 and 5, 6 and 19 to 22 and 83, and with the sections on the protection of vulnerable persons. the eeas must act with courage and not be afraid to raise the problem openly in the face of the most hostile interlocutors, nor can we give in to the recurrent pressures exerted on trade relations. i believe it is our moral duty to bring about results, also against the shameful speculations in this field, which sometimes pollute a common struggle with elements of extreme and minority political agendas, such as the attempt to extend the concept of torture to an extreme extent to make it an instrument of criticism in western countries, where the rule of law prevails, while ignoring the barbarity and enormity of theocratic or totalitarian states or warlords.
in writing. - "torture constitutes one of the gravest violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms, has grave repercussions for millions of individuals and their families and cannot be justified under any circumstances": i fully share the words of the report on the elimination of torture in the world, because i believe that not enough is being done to eradicate violence, especially that perpetrated against human rights defenders, defenceless people such as women and children, or anyone who is tortured and unjustly imprisoned. i particularly appreciate certain parts of the report, including the one on the gaps in the report on torture of children and the one on women's rights. i believe that phenomena such as cyberbullying, child trafficking, child pornography, child soldiers, child labour, as well as rape, sexual slavery, forced prostitution and female genital mutilation, must be combated with strength and determination, through all possible channels and by providing those who deal with them with the appropriate resources. in conclusion, i think that any reference to awareness-raising, prevention and the social and psychological rehabilitation of victims is important: we must eliminate torture, but we must also witness and remember those who have been tortured.
in writing. - we welcome this report because it highlights the need to establish an integrated and comprehensive strategy to combat torture in the world, acting on its root causes. we believe it is essential to adopt general institutional transparency and a stronger political will to combat ill-treatment at the level of states, by developing development cooperation and the european union's human rights mechanism. we also believe that it is important for the european parliament's delegations to visit prisons and other places of detention where there is reason to believe that the accused may have been subjected to torture or ill-treatment and to request information and independent investigations into individual cases. the strengthening of the principle of zero tolerance for torture must remain at the heart of the union's policies and strategies in promoting human rights and fundamental freedoms, both outside and within the union.
in writing. - the use of torture can never be justified and justified: the european parliament has always been a party to the treaty of rome, and it has always been a party to the treaty of rome. unfortunately, however, torture is still used systematically in many countries of the world, both in the context of conflicts and as a weapon used by the various police forces to extract confessions or revelations. i 've always been very clear and sharp in my thinking: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i find it really hateful when the victims of torture are women or even children: it would seem so unheard of that it's not even imaginable, but unfortunately it's not, and especially in africa and asia we have had many such encounters of such naughtiness. europe must be a bulwark of civilization in this field, making an effective contribution to the eradication of this phenomenon, which we too have experienced and which we have fortunately overcome almost definitively.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the motion for a resolution on the elimination of torture in the world. torture is one of the most serious violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms and has a serious impact on millions of individuals and their families. for this reason, the prohibition of torture has become absolute under international and humanitarian law, the un convention against torture (cat) and is a cornerstone of eu human rights policy. by voting in favour of this proposal, i therefore reaffirm the european union's commitment to eradicating all forms of torture in the world and i call on those countries which have not yet done so to ratify and implement the united nations convention against torture and to incorporate the provisions concerning the prohibition of all forms of violence and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment into their national legislation.

president-in-office of the council. - madam president, tomorrow this house will be voting on the reports by mr albrecht and mr droutsas on the comprehensive data protection package, which was proposed by the commission in january[nbsp ]2012. this package comprises two legislative proposals. the first is a general data protection regulation, which is intended to replace the 1995 directive. the second is a directive on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties and the free movement of such data. this is intended to replace the 2008 data protection framework decision. the council has welcomed these two proposals and has, on several occasions, publicly pledged its broad support for them. like parliament, the council is entirely convinced of the need to update and modernise the union’s data protection legislation in light of the significant technological changes that have occurred since the adoption of the 1995 directive. over the past two years, no other legislative file in the area of justice and home affairs has been the subject of such intense discussion in the council. in 2013 alone, almost 50 days of meetings of the relevant working groups were devoted to the discussion of these two proposals, and the greek presidency had already devoted over 10 days of meetings of the working party to this package. however, there is no hiding the fact that the council has not been able to make as much progress as you have done, and i am aware that this is a source of some frustration, as the honourable member mr droutsas has just mentioned. the commission chose to propose a regulation, rather than a directive, to replace the current 1995 directive. the commission had good reasons for making this choice. i am well aware that parliament is also in favour of the increased harmonisation which could be brought about by the regulation. the discussion of the regulation is very work-intensive. this is the biggest, most ambitious piece of draft legislation in the area of justice during the term of this parliament, covering all companies, public authorities and individuals in the eu. this implies detailed scrutiny by 28 member states. this shows the great interest of member states, which have held detailed consultations at home, with several ministries involved. experts from all 28 member states are working to ensure that the result of the negotiation is a high-quality legislative instrument. furthermore, data protection is a cross-cutting issue which touches on almost every area of life and society. this means that the implementation of the 1995 directive affects almost every area of society and a large number of different legislative acts at national level. the greek presidency is committed to progress on this file which is, as you know, a key element for both individual rights and growth in the eu. this file is of crucial importance for the digital internal market, as highlighted by the european council. i would like also to remind you of the conclusions of the october 2013 european council on the digital economy, which saw the timely adoption of a strong eu general data protection framework and the cybersecurity directive as essential for the completion of the digital single market by 2015. during the justice and home affairs council of last week, the member states confirmed their broad support for the territorial scope and the understanding of the key principles of international transfers – this is chapter 5 – in line with the position already expressed in the informal january meeting of ministers in athens. progress was also made on key provisions of chapters 1 to 4, namely pseudonymisation, portability of personal data, obligations of controllers and processors, and profiling. these are essential for the digital internal market. if, on top of this, you take into account some very specific provisions on data protection in the public sector, such as legislation and social benefits, pensions, youth welfare and public health, you will appreciate that this is an area of very great complexity. furthermore, these provisions are often intrinsically tied up with the institutional, administrative and even constitutional arrangements within each member state. our aim is to have a high-quality legislative instrument which is able to protect the personal data of our citizens and which can be applied in all member states. i am confident that, once our internal negotiation process is over, it will be possible for both our institutions to find common ground on these proposals and to have the two instruments adopted. i would like to take this opportunity to support this parliament’s view that the data protection reform should also apply in the future to the eu institutions. last june, vice-president reding made a commitment that the commission would put forward such a proposal. i would like to assure you that the council, like parliament, attaches considerable importance to these reforms. i would like also to thank the commission and, personally, vice-president reding for her dedication and engagement in this file. the hellenic presidency will make every effort to contribute to finalising the negotiations between the member states as soon as possible, so that we can begin discussions with parliament.
vice-president of the commission. - madam president, i would like first to say a personal word to the rapporteurs, to the shadow rapporteurs and to all their collaborators. you have been extraordinary during the last two years and in the preparatory years before, and i think that through your work you have really shown that the european parliament is a strong voice for citizens and for economic development and the preservation of our common values. so thank you for having done that, and vous avez bien mérité de notre europe. madam president, in may[nbsp ]2011 this house called for a reform of the european data protection rules. the commission delivered the proposals requested by parliament in january[nbsp ]2012: a package, as had been asked for in parliament’s resolution by your colleague, mr[nbsp ]voss. now it is again time for this house to act. now is the moment when this parliament has the possibility to make the reform irreversible; to show to the world outside that european citizens’ concerns have been heard; to give european businesses a single market in personal data protection so that there are no more barriers and there is legal certainty. so this vote will be an important part of the legacy of this legislature – a test of its willingness to fight for europe’s values. i welcome the level of ambition of the report which matches, and sometimes exceeds, what the commission has proposed. i welcome the fact that parliament has managed to work on the two reports in parallel and is putting this to the vote tomorrow as a package of revised rules. this is very important and responds very clearly to the voss resolution. the commission and parliament agree on the pillars of this reform. there has been a strong endorsement of the choice of legal instrument: the regulation, a single law for the whole of europe. we must do away with the current directive, which has resulted in a patchwork: 28 national rules that make life complicated and are costly for companies. the savings for companies by doing away with this patchwork come to eur[nbsp ]2.3 billion per year. so this alone is really an action for sme preservation. the level playing field will also allow europeʼs digital industry to compete globally. when offering services to europeans, non-european companies will have to apply european rules and adhere to the same levels of protection of personal data. this is about creating a level playing field between european and non-european businesses. this is about fair competition in a globalised world. parliamentʼs proposals will also put individuals back in control of their own personal data by updating their rights. explicit consent, the right to be forgotten, the right to data portability, and the right to be informed of personal data breaches are all important elements. these important elements will help to close the rift which exists today between citizens and the companies with which they share their data, willingly or otherwise. they will bring back the trust which has been lost. the benefits for businesses and citizens alike, as regards the one-stop-shop mechanism, are also confirmed. companies will only have to deal with one single supervisory authority, which will be the one in the country of the main establishment of the business, rather than with 28 different authorities. this will make it easier, simpler and cheaper for companies to do business in the eu and to build this digital economy, which everybody agrees that we need. this consistent application of eu law will also make it easier, swifter and more efficient for individuals to defend themselves, to be protected, and to have their complaints dealt with swiftly and on the basis of a coherent and strong protection mechanism. finally, if companies do not play by the rules, as is very often the case today, european regulators will be equipped with strong enforcement powers. the rules will give them teeth. they will be able to fine the companies which do not comply with eu rules up to 5[nbsp ]% of global annual turnover. the commission proposed 2[nbsp ]%. well, let us go for 5[nbsp ]% if parliament wants to do so. it will be a deterrent. it will allow our regulators to apply the law, which unfortunately they cannot really do today. these are the very practical and concrete ways in which the reform will help rebuild citizens’ trust in the digital economy and help european businesses to exploit the full potential of the digital single market. europe must act decisively to establish a robust data protection framework. i am impressed by the way the greek presidency has taken this dossier in hand. finally, somebody is leading this dossier. after the irish presidency had done some very good work we went into hibernation. now that spring is back, let us hope that in the council this spring will lead us to a summer decision. tomorrow’s vote is a crucial step along the way. parliament will make this reform irreversible. our citizens will say thank you to parliament. the rapporteur. - madam president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the possibility of creating a european public prosecutor's office has been discussed for many years. the commission's initiative in sending a strong signal for the creation of a common area of criminal justice by publishing a legislative package bringing together eurojust and the european public prosecutor's office, which is of course looking at an audit of olaf, can only be applauded. however, the european parliament must be recognised for its unremitting work, including within the crim special committee, in which i was the sole rapporteur, when we identified a list of priorities, a timetable and a timetable with recommendations to the commission and the member states for the period 2014-2019 and for the fight against criminal phenomena, including through the establishment of a union body that can prosecute such crimes, with particular reference to those that cause damage to the financial interests of the european union. strong opposition to community fraud, through strengthened judicial and police cooperation, huge resources being taken away and hundreds of millions of euros each year being taken away from welfare, cultural offerings, jobs that could have an employment impact on the many talents that the european union has: i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the problems of the poor. the european public prosecutor's office must be a structure, mrs reding, which is agile and lean, and it will have to work in synergy with eurojust, olaf and europol. the fruitful cooperation with the commission, as well as with the shadow members, whom i thank, the advisers, has enabled compromise amendments to be adopted in line with our expectations. the persons concerned are protected by judicial remedies, and the natural judge has been clearly identified. we have also expressed our views, sometimes in a critical manner, on the investigative measures, the admissibility of the evidence, as well as the closure of the investigations. we need greater procedural guarantees to protect the accused without weakening the institutional architecture of the system, further strengthening the judicial control entrusted to the national courts and strengthening the role of the court of justice, including with regard to the possibility of appeal. the council's half is now in the field, madam commissioner, and we shall be voting tomorrow. we welcome this interlocutory report which represents the genuine view of the european parliament. we want a european public prosecutor who can work well, who can make the best use of the european arrest warrant, the european search warrant and the seizure and confiscation, when it is in place to strengthen a common area of criminal justice in europe. the anti-money laundering package adopted today in plenary defines additional transparency rules which will allow the prosecutor to more easily trace suspicious financial transactions which could represent community fraud or corruption. the work carried out in this parliament is continuing, and has produced encouraging results, while respecting the principle of proportionality and subsidiarity, which we must also take into account in criminal justice. i conclude by saying that the confidence of the citizens in the institutions will certainly be strengthened by an increasingly strong fight against community fraud and so that the resources of the european union can be used ever more effectively to provide services to the citizens of the european union.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in taking the floor on this interlocutory report, for which i thank mr iacolino for his work, assisted by the other rapporteurs, i would like to state that i fully agree that the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office represents an added value to the area of freedom, security and justice. so i am more than in favour of the council involving parliament so that we can reach a common result. the need to combat fraud to the detriment of the european union, which unfortunately represents a scourge of serious damage to the functioning and development of the eurozone, justifies the insistence on the intention of establishing a european public prosecutor's office, to which all the member states will adhere, although the attitudes of the national parliaments suggest that unanimity in the council, as required by the treaty on the functioning of the european union, will be difficult to achieve. the centrality of the union's economic interests cannot, however, make us forget that the powers and procedure of the european public prosecutor are intended to affect the fundamental rights of citizens. in this context, i think it is extremely appropriate that the report under consideration should not only recommend to the council that the european public prosecutor's office should ensure the independence of both national governments and the eu institutions, but also make reference to the need to lay down rules to ensure that the european public prosecutor's office is protected from any political pressure.

vice-president of the commission. - madam president, i would just like to underline that the public prosecutor’s office is based on article 86 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. this article specifically says how this very unusual way of law-making should be handled. i would like to thank parliament for its constructive support of this initiative and look forward to the adoption of the interim report. i absolutely agree with parliament that you cannot have a public prosecutor’s office without having the rights of the accused being firmly anchored in a horizontal way. i absolutely agree, and that is one of the reasons why the commission has strongly underlined these rights. i would like to thank parliament for its continuous support in order to get the procedural rights adopted, and i call on the council also to adopt the still outstanding procedural rights.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we have heard contributions, criticisms, observations and comments on a subject which is of the utmost interest to the citizens. we need to put into practice a principle and a value enshrined in the treaty establishing the european union: the european court of justice. but at the same time we must remind all our colleagues that this is an interlocutory, preliminary report in which we have tried to express some criticisms, some specific points of view on the commission's proposal, which we nevertheless welcome in its complexity: procedural rights and protection of the accused, guarantees, concrete assessment of costs by eliminating inappropriate ones, clear definition of the natural judge, clarity on institutions such as archiving and compromise, as well as on the powers of the public prosecutor's office. of course, this dossier will have to be accompanied by an olaf audit once the office is set up, activated and operational. we need a power of attorney which will best combat fraud in the community, which will guarantee cooperation and speed of decision. we need a flexible and streamlined structure that makes justice efficient, protects the citizen, protects and guarantees the rights of the accused, and ensures quick decisions. in this way, citizens will certainly be able to regain their trust in the european institutions, and the european public prosecutor will be able to secure a number of resources which would otherwise be withdrawn from the common use and instead allocated to criminal or corrupt systems. i therefore naturally continue to encourage my colleagues, recalling the substantial agreement that was reached during the libe committee's work, and i am sure that there will be support again tomorrow morning and that the european public prosecutor will have taken a decisive step towards the adoption of a final text.
member of the commission. - madam president, i always have good concluding statements prepared on turkey, but i rarely use them because the debate always makes me think about how to react in the best way to the wide spectrum of other views. so let me offer you – as these will be my last comments on a report on turkey in this european parliament with me in this position – three more personal points. the first is that there is only one way to become a european union member state: to deliver fully on all chapters of the accession process. there is no derogation from the fundamental freedoms, rule of law, accountability and separation of powers. there are no interim periods. there is no shortcut which would ignore this value-based accession process where conditionality is our main instrument. what i have always expected from this house is that it will put the right questions to me and help me to find the right answers. but you will not help me or my successor if you keep saying that we should be more demanding on the one hand but also more restrictive as far as the opening of accession negotiations is concerned. it is through those accession negotiations and the opening of chapters that i am really able to answer the most relevant question. i have heard it a couple of times before – not really today – and it is this: do we want the european union to continue to be the benchmark for the turkish reforms or not? this is the question. secondly, there is no other way to find a comprehensive settlement to the cyprus issue than one which is in line with the principles on which the european union is based. i am happy to see that, with turkish involvement, we have been able to see progress there. just today, two negotiators met in the united nations protected area. they will continue the discussion on friday, 14[nbsp ]march. they confirmed today that the leaders’ meeting will take place on 31[nbsp ]march[nbsp ]2014. there is a third element. a young boy, who was 15 years old, died today. many of you have referred to him. he died after 260 days in a coma after being injured by a tear-gas canister shot by police during the gezi park protests. it is extremely sad, but it is also an important reminder of the turkish people’s aspirations. i have held those aspirations as the leading light in my efforts, and i will always do so. the agenda includes, for joint debate, the report by marian-jean marinescu, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the establishment of the single european sky (recast) (com (2013) 0410 - c7-0171/2013 - 2013/0186 (cod)) (a7-0095/2014) and the report by david-maria sassoli, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 216/2008 as regards airports, air traffic management and air navigation services (com (2013) 0409 - c7-0169/2013 - 2013/0187 (cod)) (a7-0098/2014).
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking my shadow colleagues for their very constructive collaboration in the drafting of this text. the regulation on airports, air traffic management and air navigation services and the single european sky are, as you know, part of a package presented by the european commission in june. the aim is to improve the overall efficiency of airspace organisation and management through a reform of the provision of navigation services. the text on the single european sky, which is very complex in view of the impact it will have on the various member states, is very broad and deals with the most controversial issues, in particular, first, the inefficiency in the provision of air navigation services; secondly, the fragmentation of air traffic management systems. the regulation on which i am rapporteur deals with the question of aviation safety and the responsibilities of the european safety agency. the objective is to establish and maintain a high and uniform level of civil aviation safety in europe. it is a regulation which is very technical in some ways, but which also deals with the question of the governance of the agency. the first part of the text deals with adaptation to the new rules of the single european sky, including air navigation services and air traffic management; the second part, on the other hand, deals with the reform of the governance of the agency. on the technical aspects of the regulation, after hearing various speakers, the european commission, interested parties, i found unanimous agreement on the text presented. the regulation in its technical specifications applies to the design, manufacture, operational aspects of aeronautical products, including air navigation and air traffic management services, and pilot certificates. the aim here too is to establish and maintain a high and uniform level of security. the question of the governance of the agency is different and is dealt with in the second part of the regulation. the commission has put forward an innovative proposal, which provides for a reform of the agency itself, including a redistribution of responsibilities, by providing for easa to focus on the drafting and supervision of technical and safety regulations; the european commission for economic regulation; eurocontrol on operational tasks. this reform was evident from the outset, given the commission's willingness to change the name of the agency itself from european aviation safety agency to european aviation agency, it immediately showed that it wanted to bet on an agency like the us federal aviation administration. the european commission also wanted to implement the new interinstitutional agreement of july 2012, whereby the commission, parliament and council agreed on a common approach on european agencies, which, while not legally binding, is based on a case-by-case approach and contains progress on many aspects: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of the agency, the choice of its seat, its governance, its operation and the use of its resources. the agency for aviation safety is one of the largest and most important agencies of the european commission and given its powers it is essential that parliament is its interlocutor and that is why the director of the agency will have to make a statement before the transport committee of the european parliament to inform about the activities and programming of the agency. the european aviation industry is constantly evolving. as you know, the primary objectives are efficiency, safety and in a world where the number of flights is naturally constantly increasing. it will be important to understand the role of europe, because the european countries can no longer compete with the big countries of other continents and only increasingly centralised management will allow us to maintain high standards of services, competitiveness and greater security. the results would be immediate, lowering ticket costs, enhancing safety, reducing the fragmentation of air traffic control, reducing fuel consumption and therefore less pollution, fewer delays on airplanes. it is of vital importance that we meet this challenge, which could also be of fundamental interest to our economy. i would like to conclude, madam president, with a small technical clarification, because of an error in communication by the secretariat of the committee on transport, two amendments, nos 43 and 44, which were already voted on in committee on 30 january, were not included in the text for tomorrow morning's vote. since it will not be possible to amend the text presented in the house for technical reasons, the two amendments will be put to the vote tomorrow.

in writing. - the importance of the pericles project for european integration and security policies cannot be underestimated: the commission is also proposing to develop a new approach to the problem of the environment. significantly, the programme is focusing on border regions, which according to some studies absorb about 5% of the workforce, and which, together with dual-regime countries, constitute the ideal habitat for forgers. it will be noted, inter alia, that while the value of seizures of counterfeit national currency is decreasing (e.g. in the czech republic, 2013 on 2012), the value of seizures of euro currency in core countries (e.g. the netherlands) is increasing; national authorities seem to converge in identifying two or three member states which, mainly because of their proximity to logistical hubs and/or areas with a high crime rate, are prime counterfeiting hubs, able to seize any useful opportunity (such as the introduction of new currency, the orientation of consumers towards the use of smaller denominations, etc.). it is therefore possible that the fiscal impact of counterfeiting, which the commission has estimated at 676 million, should be revised upwards. in this context, the extension of the programme is essential and i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this text, which contains recommendations for the future extension of the pericles 2020 programme to third countries, since the programme has been a partial success, and i therefore think it is right that it should be continued and extended to new actors, also in view of the increased use of the euro on global markets. the pericle2020 programme, which has been in place for several years, provides high-level training not only for the police authorities responsible for combating counterfeiting but also for those who operate in the sector without being directly responsible for supervision. this ensures a continuous fight against counterfeiting that affects a multitude of individuals and areas that go far beyond simple police checks and consequently achieve very encouraging results that encourage ever greater future use.
in writing. - pericles 2020 is a programme designed to take measures to protect the euro against counterfeiting. it is part of the eu's anti-fraud policy which makes a significant annual contribution to the protection of the financial interests of the eu and member states' budgets. it ensures that eu and national budgets are well protected, that money is used as intended, and that it reaches the beneficiaries. i could not help but vote in favour of this programme which, according to the evaluations carried out in 2004 and 2011, has proved to be very effective. moreover, it should continue to achieve its objectives in the future, increasing its effectiveness in protecting the currency and suppressing counterfeiting of the euro.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there are 27 000 flights crossing european skies every day and a 50% increase is expected over the next 20 years. without an integrated and efficient airspace management system, there is a risk that europe's skies will become saturated to the detriment of safety and environmental sustainability. the single european sky project envisages the gradual elimination of national air borders through the implementation of 9 regional airspace blocks, which will make the traffic in our skies more efficient, competitive, safe and less dangerous for the environment. flights often cannot now fly direct routes with increasing flight times and fuel consumption; the cost of this inefficiency is about eur 5 billion per year for passengers alone. the regulation we are approving today will, on the other hand, allow us to create shorter routes, reducing fuel consumption and minimising the environmental impact of air transport.
in writing. - in 2000, the commission launched the 'single european sky' initiative, which brought air traffic management and navigation services into the framework of the common transport policy. the initiative, however, did not produce the expected results: no progress has been made in either the overall efficiency of the design or the use of the european route network. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question were necessary to achieve the objective of common interest. the recast of the regulation establishing the 'single european sky' is intended to accelerate the implementation of the reform of air transport services while remaining faithful to the original objectives. i therefore welcome the new proposal, which i believe represents an opportunity to speed up the implementation of the european union's flagship initiative, which has been delayed for too long. i also welcome the twofold objective of strengthening the independence of national supervisory authorities by strengthening the role of the network operator and redefining the concept of functional airspace blocks, which give the industry a more prominent role.
in writing. - the single european sky (ses) initiative was launched in 2000: since then, much has been done to achieve the ambitious goal of creating a true airspace. however, i believe that the single european sky project should be brought more into line with existing eu legislation, i.e. more precise definitions of union-wide performance targets and sectoral partnerships, which are crucial to the structuring and smooth functioning of airspace. i also think it is right to encourage greater coordination between airspace members in order to promote cooperation between them beyond the borders within which they operate. this process of harmonisation must also be put into practice by adopting a uniform procedure for the certification of air navigation service providers in the future and for the accreditation of national aviation authorities. this could provide a single authorisation gateway at union level for the performance of the various tasks. in addition, the european union aviation agency (eaa) would be responsible for issuing such certificates which are recognised and acceptable in all member states. in conclusion, i believe that the proposed amendments strike the right strategic balance between industrial and commercial needs and social needs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the marinescu report on the establishment of the single european sky. the implementation of the so-called 'single sky' would have a cumulative effect on eu gdp of eur 419 billion, with the creation of 328 000 jobs. at this time of deep economic crisis, i believe that this transition is necessary to maintain the competitiveness of european industry at a high level worldwide.
in writing. - the report takes the task of bringing the reform to a successful conclusion, while maintaining a balanced approach to the issues at the heart of the debate on the single european sky: the scope of the services to be tendered, linked to precise guarantees for the skills wisely declined in the broader sense of human factor - the synergies between the commission, the eaa and the national authorities with their respective tasks, the various instruments for financing joint projects, the implementation of sesar, management by functional blocks, the meaning of the atm master plan. the system of declarations is well calibrated, with attention to the necessary flexibility at the entry into force stage, and appropriate to such a profound and demanding regulatory reform. the architecture of the transparency systems is convincing, as regards monitoring activities, management of information flows, the role of the ovp, conflicts of interest (including the cool-off period to avoid revolving doors contrary to the correct market dynamics). as well as developments, impact assessment of measures and verification of implementation (legal/organisational and material plan with sesar application). i support the report with a strong vote in favour.
in writing. - the single european sky (ses) initiative was launched in 2000 and brought air traffic management and navigation services into the framework of the common transport policy. since the implementation of the ems, enlargement policy coupled with an active neighbourhood policy have extended the european air transport market to 38 countries, making eu air transport a global player. however, the ses has not produced the expected results. i supported the recasting of the regulation on the establishment of the single european sky as it is intended to speed up the implementation of the reform of air transport services while remaining faithful to the original objectives and principles. it aims to strengthen the independence of national supervisory authorities, strengthen the role of the network operator, redefine the concept of functional airspace blocks by giving industry a more prominent role and provide for open tendering procedures for the selection of air transport support services.
in writing. - the first time that the single european sky was mentioned was at the end of the 1990s, while the first ess regulation was 10 years ago. today i approved the proposal for the essii+ regulation, hoping that it will have more success than the previous two and that the further corrections made to the text will make it easier to implement. the creation of a single european sky is of the utmost importance in order to optimise a resource which, contrary to what is commonly thought, is not unlimited, namely the sky. every day, 27,000 flights cross european skies, which requires a streamlining of routes that is only possible with greater cooperation of national authorities, which can be achieved through sesii+. the european airspace is currently based on national borders, there are 28 national air traffic control authorities managing some 60 air traffic control bodies divided into 650 sectors, this proposal aims to eliminate national borders and reduce the 28 authorities to 9 on a regional basis, with clear improvements in safety and costs as well as more efficient route management ensuring less pollution and benefits for passengers in terms of time and money.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the establishment of the single european sky, an initiative which aims to bring together air traffic management and navigation services within the framework of the common transport policy. enlargement policy has made the eu a global player. however, the desired results have not yet been achieved: the reform did not lead to a reduction in air navigation charges, ticket prices, average flight duration or fuel consumption. the ses is intended to accelerate the implementation of the reform of air transport services while remaining faithful to the original objectives, by strengthening the independence of the national supervisory authorities, by enhancing the role of the network operator, by redefining the concept of functional airspace blocks, by giving more importance to industry and by providing for procurement procedures for the selection of assistance services. i believe that airspace should be used more flexibly and that member states should establish enhanced cooperation across borders.
in writing. - the single european sky (ses) initiative was launched in 2000 and brought air traffic management and navigation services into the framework of the common transport policy. this is a very important regulation for two reasons: on the one hand, adaptation to the new rules of the single european sky, and on the other hand, governance reform, aimed at implementing the interinstitutional agreement on european agencies signed in july 2012. the main objective of this regulation is to establish and maintain a high and uniform level of civil aviation safety in europe and to establish the governance structure of the european aviation agency.
