in writing. - i agree with the positions of the sassoli report which analyses the changes to be made to air traffic management and air navigation services. i believe that it is necessary to simplify and clarify the current legislation, separating the current overlaps between the single european sky and the european aviation safety agency regulations, and thus achieve a better management of air navigation and management services.
in writing. - the regulation covers airports, air traffic management and air navigation services and is part of the single european sky package. it addresses the issue of aviation safety and the competence of the european aviation safety agency (easa). this is a very important regulation for two reasons: on the one hand, adaptation to the new rules of the single european sky, and on the other hand, governance reform, aimed at implementing the interinstitutional agreement on european agencies signed in july 2012. the main objective of this regulation is to establish and maintain a high and uniform level of civil aviation safety in europe and to establish the governance structure of the european aviation agency. the text can be divided into two parts: the first part, technical, identifies a whole series of definitions, principles, standards and categories of organisations competent in the field of aviation safety, aimed at establishing european standard safety criteria. part two, dedicated to the aviation safety agency (easa), sets out rules governing the governance of the agency and its responsibilities.
in writing. - this is part of the measures to be taken for the increasingly necessary establishment of the single european sky. i voted in favour of this report, which is based on the need for common and extremely high safety standards throughout the european aviation sector. it applies to the design, manufacture, maintenance and operation of aeronautical products, to personnel and organisations involved in design and maintenance, to personnel involved in flight operations, to the design and maintenance of airports and to personnel involved, as well as to air traffic management and air navigation services atm/ans (air traffic services, aeronautical meteorological services, aeronautical information services, communication, navigation and surveillance services). the second part of the proposal, however, deals more with the organisational aspects of the european aviation safety agency (easa) and, in addition to the technical aspects, rejects the commission's proposal to change its name, in order to maintain the 'safety' aspect in the name of the agency. the report concludes by stressing that the creation of an agency with such extensive powers could ensure the more efficient operation of the aviation system not only in europe but also abroad, by ensuring the exchange of useful information with non-european agencies.
in writing. - the commission will be presenting a report on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment in the context of the single european sky. thanks to the work of the committee on transport, we have reached a good compromise which allows us to maintain a high level of civil aviation safety in europe, to establish the governance of the european aviation agency and the competences of the european aviation safety agency (easa). the safety issue is very important, as it concerns the control of certifications of components, aircraft and technical parts which must be issued by qualified bodies, and the training of pilots and flight personnel. in this respect, the member states play a key role, being able to intervene in the event of safety problems concerning these very items subject to regulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation on airports, air traffic management and air navigation services because europe is finally taking a step forward on the issue of aviation safety in europe. the aim of the text is to establish and maintain a high and uniform level of civil aviation safety in europe. the new rules laid down by the committee provide for a redistribution of responsibilities by focusing the european aviation agency on the drafting and supervision of technical and safety regulations, the commission on economic regulation and eurocontrol on operational tasks. the commission's intention to reform the agency was evident from the outset, as it proposed, among other things, that the name of the agency be changed from the european aviation safety agency (easa) to the european aviation agency, showing its interest in having a global partner in the aviation sector, following the example of the us federal aviation administration. the european aviation sector is constantly evolving in europe and worldwide, the primary objectives are always those of efficiency and safety of the service, in a world where the number of air flights is constantly growing. it will be important to understand the role that europe will play at the end of this journey on the single european sky package.
in writing. - the question of aviation safety and the competence of the european aviation safety agency (easa) is very important. this importance derives from the fact that maintaining a high level of civil aviation safety in europe is a common and primary objective. i think it is necessary to support this proposal because it is essential to strengthen the agency's powers and effectiveness. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of passengers is not compromised. however, these objectives should be achieved by means of new powers without entailing an increase in the budget of the agency itself.
in writing. - the single european sky (ses) initiative was launched in 2000 and brought air traffic management and navigation services into the framework of the common transport policy. this is a very important regulation for two reasons: on the one hand, adaptation to the new rules of the single european sky, and on the other hand, governance reform, aimed at implementing the interinstitutional agreement on european agencies signed in july 2012. the main objective of this regulation is to establish and maintain a high and uniform level of civil aviation safety in europe and to establish the governance structure of the european aviation agency.
in writing. - the proposal finally addresses the question of the competence of the european aviation safety agency (easa). the agreement reached by the european commission, the european parliament and the european council seems to be sound and geared to the proper functioning of air navigation and management services. i think that the rapporteur has interpreted the safety issue well, in particular by maintaining high standards of care for the certification of components, aircraft and technical parts, as well as for the training of pilots and flight personnel. they also agree on the need to strengthen the agency's competence, especially in the field of air safety.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the tourism market is constantly evolving, especially the online market, where there are always new ideas and business proposals. many types of holiday are not covered by existing community legislation, which is why the package travel legislation needs to be revised to ensure that all travellers have uniform protection and clear and equal rights in all member states. more guarantees are needed in the conditions offered to consumers, especially when there are extraordinary and unforeseeable circumstances that prevent re-entry. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, consumer protection has always been a priority for the political action of my party, which has always fought to defend the position of the weaker party. that is why i voted - also in disagreement with my group, with alde - on some amendments in favour of the proposal for a directive on package holidays and assisted tourism services, because this will give greater protection to the consumer who will finally have uniform protection and clear and precise rights in all the member states in pursuit of one of the objectives of the european union: the common internal market. it was important to update the directive by extending its scope to online commerce, which has now become the main tool used also for the tourism sector. it is also to be welcomed that the directive was intended to ensure compliance, effectiveness and an adequate degree of protection in the event of the insolvency of operators.
in writing. - the mayer report is balanced and acceptable, and i have therefore decided to support it with my vote.
in writing. - as this is a subject which is very dear to me, i have followed the drafting of this proposal with particular attention and i fully endorse it. the tourism sector, in addition to continuing to increase its turnover, is one of the sectors where change is taking place most rapidly. this, in addition to being an advantage for travellers, who are presented with an increasingly wide and diversified tourist offer, can be a threat to consumer protection guarantees. the proposal seeks to update the rules for the protection of travellers, considering that the rules contained in the previous regulation are no longer sufficient. one of the main issues raised concerns the definition of an autonomous tourist service. the directive, which considers the concept of 'all-inclusive package' to be obsolete, is intended to guarantee travellers who intend to purchase tourist services separately in an autonomous manner. it is also considered one of the fundamental prerogatives for the protection of travellers, that travellers should be aware of the degree of protection offered by each service before proceeding with any form of purchase. however, the protection of travellers must not impose obligations which are too onerous for tour operators, but must be a fair compromise which does not penalise anyone.
in writing. - the revision of directive 90/314/eec on all-inclusive travel is necessary both because of the need to include online trade and to meet the prospect of a large development of tourist flows, in particular the chinese one. the scope of the directive should therefore not be too narrow and too specific, so as to avoid the directive being obsolete at the time of its adoption. it is essential to avoid the development of business models which seek to circumvent the scope of application. the essential aspect of the directive, in addition to the duty of the member states, must therefore be to ensure compliance, effectiveness and an adequate level of protection in the event of insolvency, and to lay down penalties, even of considerable amounts, in the event of breaches of obligations by undertakings. mutual recognition of insolvency protection and administrative cooperation between member states are important. it is also necessary to ensure that the new directive does not overlap with the existing regulations on passenger rights. the basic principle is that rights can be cumulated only if they do not relate to the same facts.
in writing. - the tourism market is constantly evolving, especially the online market, and new business ideas are constantly being developed. i have welcomed this directive because its primary objective is to ensure that the level of protection is respected and effective and increased in all types of travel. it is of particular importance that all the specific details of the journey are included in the pre-contractual information or in the contract itself. in the pre-contractual information, it is important to introduce a clear distinction between 'package travel' and 'linked travel services'. price changes must always be justified in writing and, in the event of insolvency, it would be appropriate to have the utmost protection for the traveller. in the event that the traveller encounters difficulties, even if not attributable to the organiser, the organiser should nevertheless be required to act with the utmost diligence to provide the traveller with adequate assistance and alternative travel services.
in writing. - the directive governing all-inclusive travel packages is now obsolete and largely outdated. the change in consumer habits, the liberalisation of the air transport sector, together with the increasing availability of online offers, have made it necessary to initiate a process of revision of the existing legislation. i agree with mr mayer's proposal to strengthen the rights of those consumers who, through a more active role in planning their holidays, prefer to combine different tourist services independently rather than choosing ready-made packages. the proposal also aims to harmonise legislation in the various member states, to make rules more transparent for operators in the sector and to increase consumer protection irrespective of the way the holiday is booked.
in writing. - the tourism market is constantly evolving, especially online. travellers should enjoy uniform protection and clear and precise rights which should not differ depending on the member state in which they live. i am voting in favour of full harmonization in the interests of european consumers and, for reasons of competition, also of european businesses. in particular, i supported provisions allowing the traveller to terminate a contract for a package in the event of proven extraordinary and unforeseeable circumstances and those aimed at ensuring that certain basic information is provided to travellers also for individual travel services.
in writing. - the revision of directive 90/314/eec to include online commerce in its scope is a necessary step dictated by the evolution of technology and the digital market. i would appreciate a specific clarification of the distinction between pure advertising and real proposals in the digital market, so as not to penalise economic operators and at the same time to protect consumers from overly aggressive marketing strategies. the right of consumers to information and the right of withdrawal are also important: i consider it essential that pre-contractual information or the contract contains information on all relevant contact details, including information on the right of withdrawal, which should be possible at any time, in exchange for appropriate compensation. i think that the measures to support travellers in difficulty (even if not caused by the organiser) and the measures to protect them in the event of insolvency are proportionate.
in writing. - the european commission's proposal for a regulation introduces new provisions at european level for the phasing out of the marketing and use of hfcs, which are widely used in the air conditioning and commercial refrigeration sectors. the agreement reached between the council and the european parliament confirms the objective of a gradual reduction of 79% of hfcs so that the volume of products placed on the european market in 2030 does not exceed 21% of current levels. the proposal initially provided for an ambitious roadmap for certain industrial sectors, thereby risking undermining both the competitiveness of these sectors and that of the industrial chains concerned. after a long negotiation process initiated in the envi parliamentary committee, of which i am a full member, i am pleased that this agreement has been reached, which allows for the alternative technologies available to the various sectors to be taken into account, the economic sustainability of the technologies themselves, and the timing of adaptation to new standards, all the while maintaining the objective of keeping these sectors competitive on the international market.
in writing. - the eickhout report on fluorinated gases and the greenhouse effect is acceptable. i think it is remarkable that the alternative technologies already available to the various sectors and their economic viability have been taken into account, as well as the timing of adaptation to the new standards, with the aim of keeping these sectors on the market. for all these reasons i voted in favour of the text.
in writing. - the european union, following the montreal protocol, set the ambitious but necessary target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels. the progressive reduction of chlorofluorocarbons (cfcs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (hcfcs) has been a major step forward in this respect, but environmental legislation must always keep pace with the times and with technological and scientific progress in order to steer human behaviour towards a more sustainable lifestyle. the commission proposal represents a major step towards replacing the currently widely used high global warming potential (hfc) (pfc) (sf6) substances with new, less climate-damaging systems, but it does not take account of some very important factors, which is why i am voting in favour of the amendments tabled by the envi committee. the new proposal takes greater account of the cost-effectiveness of such levies, creates a clearer and more feasible agenda, does not ignore the risks of existing schemes and finally proposes the concept of an emission allowance use tax that compensates for the higher costs of more sustainable alternatives, thus encouraging their development and marketing.
in writing. - the regulation introduces new provisions at european level for the phasing out of the placing on the market and use of hfcs, which are widely used in the air conditioning and commercial refrigeration sectors. the agreement reached confirms the european commission's proposed target of a gradual reduction of 79% of hfcs, so that the volume of products placed on the european market in 2030 does not exceed 21% of current levels. i supported the text of the agreement with the council which allowed for greater realism than some of the rapporteur's requests and took account of the alternative technologies available to the various sectors of their economic viability, as well as the timing of adaptation to the new standards, with the aim of keeping these sectors on the market. in particular, i supported and welcomed the fact that the system of allocation of emission allowances does not provide for the imposition of a tariff and that the prohibitions of use introduced for certain specific equipment and products have been circumscribed. i also think it is right that in the negotiations with the member states the ban on charging equipment before it is placed on the market has been removed and that a system of tracing hfcs placed on the market has been opted for instead.
in writing. - i think that the commission proposal provides good information, particularly on the provisions relating to the limits of hfcs which cannot be placed on the market or the prohibitions on hermetically sealed equipment. i think that some of the measures proposed by the rapporteur on the gradual reduction of production and consumption of hydrofluorocarbons are particularly welcome, as is the intention to increase compliance by producers. last but not least, i believe that the problem of by-products, as highlighted in the report, is a focal point, which, if not fully addressed, risks undermining the european union's efforts to achieve its environmental policy objectives.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is true that freedom of movement is a fundamental freedom and it is right that the member states should do their utmost to remove unnecessary bureaucratic obstacles for those who study and especially for those who work. but it is not acceptable for community citizens to move from one country to another without studying or working, only to burden the host country's government, which may have a more favourable social protection system than the country of origin. how many people move just to get free social assistance and various benefits! this is not fair, especially in a time of crisis, because all these services are very expensive and they are resources that we are taking from citizens, especially the poorest and most vulnerable.
in writing. - i did not intend to support the bauer report because i believe that it aims to facilitate immigration to europe of third country nationals through a series of deliberately hidden references in the folds of the text under vote.
in writing. - i commend the rapporteur for taking a realistic approach to such a sensitive subject, upholding the essential value of free movement, without ever falling into the temptation of the rhetoric of pure principle which often exacerbates open political problems. i was born in a region of emigration in a country that today, with the third largest economy in the eurozone, is once again a region of emigration: i am not unaware, however, that certain difficulties may be a cause for concern and, unfortunately, open to exploitation for reasons of internal policy. so while i am sad to see so many young italians leaving their cities to move elsewhere in europe, i consider this to be a sign of growth for their generation, as finding a qualified job in a big city was for ours. it is still difficult to make it clear that full mobility will be a given in the near future: in the united states, states compete to attract citizens, who bring in income, revenue, production and strengthen communities even in the dialectic at the federal level. the rapporteur supports a reasonable solution based on the removal of obstacles through cooperation between national authorities and at european level. i certainly vote in favour.
in writing. - i agree with all the arguments put forward by the committee on employment and social affairs in that they seek to improve the freedom of movement within the european union for community workers, which, although long recognised as one of the fundamental freedoms of citizens (article 45 tfeu), still has some limits in its application. the possibility of creating genuine flows of workers across the member states must be seen as an opportunity for the different economies and therefore encouraged as much as possible both by projects aimed at making citizens aware of the different labour markets and by guaranteeing those who decide to undertake this work path the same conditions valid for all workers, avoiding any form of national and gender discrimination. the free movement of workers contributes to closing labour market imbalances and to developing a healthy spillover of knowledge and cultures between countries, contributing to the process of european integration. it seems absurd to have regulations where equal treatment of european citizens is required but since integration is a slow and complicated process, this is still considered necessary and it is good that the rules are as clear as possible.
in writing. - the effective exercise of freedom of movement for workers is not yet a reality and many workers are often unaware of their rights in this area. they still face discrimination on the grounds of nationality when moving within the european union. these are some of the reasons why i voted in favour of the report. the free movement of workers needs to be a key element in the development of a genuine labour market in the union. every citizen should have the right to move freely from an area of high unemployment to another with a shortage of labour, in order to work and reside there. for their part, member states should make all necessary information on working conditions available and also establish the modalities under which this information may be made accessible to employers, workers and other interested parties.
in writing. - the free movement of workers was one of the pillars on which the single market and the european union itself were built, and the idea itself would also be acceptable, insofar as it facilitates a citizen who wishes to work in a country other than his own. the point is that this mechanism could have worked in a europe different from the present one, with a few member states and not too dissimilar labour, social and welfare systems. the problems arise from the fact that the european union is made up of too many different economic, social and cultural realities. the great eastward enlargement in 2004 created a situation which is now difficult to manage, with hundreds of thousands of workers from these countries deciding to move elsewhere where conditions were much better for them. but all this has led to a number of problems, which are obvious to all of us: it is not out of mere selfishness, but out of pure realism, that i believe that this rule should be thoroughly revised before it is too late and the situation becomes really unmanageable.
in writing. - article 45 of the treaty guarantees the right of eu citizens to move freely within the union for work purposes, without being discriminated against on grounds of nationality or working conditions. the directive aims to strengthen the implementation of regulation no 492/2011 concerning the rights deriving from the freedom of movement of workers and defines specific areas where discrimination on grounds of nationality is prohibited.

in writing. - the environmental impact assessment (eia) directive sets out and harmonises at european level the conditions for the design and construction of industrial plants and infrastructure in various sectors in compliance with strict environmental criteria. it therefore affects a wide range of industrial sectors (energy, transport, construction, waste disposal, agriculture). i supported the final agreement with the council, reached after particularly difficult negotiations, which managed to strike a balance between the needs of the various member states and the objective of simplifying and improving the quality of the legislation in force. i voted in favour of the final text which resolves some of the criticisms raised by italian companies concerning the need for greater clarity in the interpretation of the clauses and a general reduction in bureaucratic and administrative burdens in order to streamline and shorten the time taken for procedures. i appreciated the choice to limit the scope of application in order to avoid overlaps with existing legislation, clear provisions on deadlines and timing at different stages of the procedure, the elimination of the requirement for accredited experts, the provision for coordinated and common procedures (one stop shop), the non-retroactive application of the new rules on ongoing procedures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on statistics on external trade with third countries because i welcome the amendments tabled by the rapporteur to amend the commission proposal, given that the commission's objective is to bring regulation (ec) no 471/2009 into line with the system of implementing and delegated acts introduced by the treaty of lisbon. in order to ensure greater legal certainty and transparency of this legislation, the rapporteur proposes to transform those implementing acts concerning measures on codes to be used for statistical data and on the link between import and export data and business data into delegated acts. in my view, individual rules should always be adopted by means of delegated acts in order to respect parliament's legislative competence: if it were to accept implementing acts of general application, the commission would have the power to lay down rules which, although introduced under the control of the member states, do not provide for any role for parliament. it is clear from this that the aim is to limit the commission's scope for action by allowing parliament to monitor and supervise the decisions taken by the commission.
in writing. - the moreira report on statistics of external trade with third countries (delegated and implementing acts) is a mere adaptation of the legislation on delegated acts to be conferred on the european commission, it is not critical, and i therefore intend to support it with my vote.
in writing. - no, i'm very pleased with the report. the subject is rather technical, and i do not see why parliament should go into these details, which the european commission can decide. we are talking about what legal basis to adopt in order to be able to change the statistical classifications for foreign trade and i think that parliament should be devoting itself to higher, more political tasks, instead of these details which should be worked out by the technicians, with the support of those who use these standards on a daily basis. moreover, when politics changes statistical classifications, there is always the risk that it does so to embellish the results. i therefore voted in favour of the commission's proposal, against the rapporteur's recommendations.
in writing. - in its proposal, the commission proposes to use delegated acts in a number of cases, almost all of which have been covered by the regulatory procedure with scrutiny in the past, while implementing acts are proposed for measures relating to codes to be used for statistical data and measures relating to the link between import and export data and business data. i share the rapporteur's view that parliament should be more demanding in the separation of delegated and implementing acts, the real difference being in the setting of rules or measures for specific and concrete situations. i also agree with the reduction of the commission's powers to five years, so as to ensure greater parliamentary control.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the asylum, migration and integration package is very important and ambitious and i congratulate the rapporteurs on the excellent work they have done. but i really hope that the financial resources are actually allocated to the main priorities. 1) a clear entry policy without derogations. yes to legal immigrants, who have a legal study or residence permit, also for work reasons. yes to asylum seekers, with an eye to the most vulnerable, especially minors, but mandatory returns for irregular migrants. 2) a european policy of sharing humanitarian emergencies to work towards the objective of a system of compulsory relocation of refugees within the european union. 3) the establishment of humanitarian corridors when there are serious humanitarian crises. 4) bilateral agreements between the eu and the countries of origin and transit of migrants to prevent irregular immigration, ensure effective return policies and effectively combat trafficking in human beings by criminal organisations. 5) strengthen frontex for effective border control with coordinated patrolling actions. a thought on frontex: the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the creation of a european research area. finally, some questions on the general financial provisions. accessibility to a wide range of public and private actors who can benefit from resources risks fragmenting the resources themselves and reducing the concrete impact of actions.

in writing. - this morning, speaking about the european budget for next year, i wanted to stress the uselessness of several decentralised agencies of the union, citing as examples enisa, the european agency for network and information security, which is based in greece, in crete to be precise. we have voted today on this text, which deals with a directive aimed at ensuring a high common level of network and information security in the union: i have found no reference in the report, if not a marginal reference, to the work of the european agency in crete to prove the correctness of my statements this morning. the subject of the proposal is, however, too important to be the subject of sterile debate, which is why i wanted to support this text, which calls on the member states to increase their level of preparedness and to improve cooperation with each other, while operators of critical infrastructures such as energy, transport and the main providers of information society services (e-commerce platforms, social networks) are asked to take appropriate measures to manage security risks and to report serious incidents to the competent authorities, thus creating an essential condition for a safe and reliable information environment.
in writing. - the digitalisation of markets and services, together with the increase in spending by european citizens online, have led the european digital agency to call for the introduction of network and information protection measures as early as 2010. the objective of the proposal is well received in this respect, aiming to strengthen a high common level of security in europe. it is important, however, that the principles of proportionality are respected and are well balanced with the outstanding obligations of the member states in the field of safety and accident reporting. a very interesting point is the one concerning penalties, which must be well proportioned so as not to risk discouraging the reporting of incidents.
in writing. - while i share the importance of transparency in financial reporting, i believe that the request for over eur 43 million for the union's financial reporting and auditing programme for the period 2014-2020 is excessive, which is why i have decided to abstain in this vote.
in writing. - i am in favour of such an important programme to facilitate the correct and transparent drawing up of budgets and to ensure simple auditing by the responsible bodies, overcoming the barriers still existing between the different national legislation of the member states. i believe it is in europe's interest to pursue such programmes, whose public utility is indisputable, also in view of the ever-increasing and natural integration of markets. the reasons put forward by the rapporteur are very much in line with the objectives underlying the european union's institution, namely to ensure and help citizens and businesses to deal with each other in a simple and fair manner, overcoming the limitations imposed by nationality, which still exist in the drafting and revision of budgets.
in writing. - today i voted in favour of the report on radio equipment amending the commission proposal for a revision of directive 1999/5/ec of the european parliament and of the council. the amended directive provides a regulatory framework for the placing on the market, circulation and entry into service in the eu of radio equipment and telecommunications terminal equipment with a view to creating uniform rules aimed at completing the internal market. in this connection, the directive also contains provisions on health and safety protection, electromagnetic compatibility and the prevention of harmful interference. i welcome the rapporteur's proposals for some changes at vertical level (definition of radio equipment, registration of certain equipment, traceability, etc.) and horizontal level (improvements in wording) which will reduce the impact of administrative burdens on smes and at the same time ensure adequate consumer protection by increasing market surveillance. the amendments also aim to eliminate any inconsistencies in the legislation that could be the source of a lack of legal transparency.
in writing. - in view of the technological developments of recent years, particularly the massive development of wi-fi equipment, i believe that the harmonized standards for radio equipment need to be updated to improve the safety of networks, and for these reasons i voted in favour of the weiler report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal, which i believe contains the necessary changes to the already good text presented by the commission. in particular, i am in favour of greater regulation of radio equipment, including both generating and receiving equipment, as this would ensure greater harmonisation in the management of radio spectrum in view of their ever-growing range of uses. i also think it is important that this regulation does not place an undue burden on the industry and smes, as there are now advanced, easy-to-use and low-cost systems to connect producers, consumers and the regulatory bodies in the sector. in this context, the call for the use of electronic labels and manufacturers' websites wherever possible seems to me to be extremely appropriate. the directive and the proposal put forward by mrs weiler also seek to strengthen the eu's fight to eliminate waste and simplify the use of electronic devices, in particular the desire to extend to all radio equipment the need to use a universal charger and accessories. i think this is really sensible and right.

in writing. - this report is intended as an evaluation of the implementation of the lisbon treaty with a specific focus on the changes introduced in the interinstitutional relations between parliament and the commission. in the light of the democratic evolution of the eu since the introduction of the lisbon treaty, the commission, while still the eu's executive organ par excellence, seems to have lost some of its capacity to influence the union's institutional architecture as a result of the economic and financial crisis, which has undoubtedly highlighted the still strong presence of an intergovernmental approach dictated by the national interests of the member states, represented by the council, to the detriment of a community macro-strategy. however, in the light of the role which the european commission has played and should play at international level, it is essential to restore to it the political legitimacy which it has as a body which ensures that the acquis communautaire is properly applied. in view of the european elections in may 2014 and the future of the eu, i therefore agree with the rapporteur that parliament should continue to monitor the commission's activities. this must not mean, however, that there is a phenomenon of parliamentarisation due to the consolidation of parliament's powers of control over the commission itself, which, although monitored, should enjoy the autonomy that is its due.

in writing. - i think the report by my colleague is acceptable and i am voting in favour of parliament's adoption of the text. the implications of the major changes introduced in the interinstitutional relations between the european parliament and the european commission are the focus of the analysis, and i think the rapporteur's calibrated and neutral style is to be appreciated. i support the proposal for the nomination of candidates for the presidency of the commission by european political parties, and i believe it is important to strengthen its democratic legitimacy, political influence and efficiency in every possible way within the framework of the existing treaties or in the context of a future revision of the treaties. i agree with the rapporteur that we must avoid excessive parliamentarisation of the system and that the principle of separation of powers must be borne in mind. i think that the proposal to reduce the majority currently required for a motion of censure against the commission is sensible, as is the proposal to invite the candidate for president of the commission to present his programme to parliament. finally, i think it is important to ensure that the president of the commission has greater autonomy in the choice of commissioners.
in writing. - i think that perhaps the only useful thing that the treaty of lisbon has done is to give the european parliament a greater role and power, which until then had been reduced to almost a mere 'institutional presence'. we must never forget that we have here the representatives elected by the european citizens, the only ones with popular legitimacy, and our scope for action is still very limited, compared, for example, with that of our national counterparts. there is an important point in this report which i would like to stress, namely that 'it calls for the parliament's right of legislative initiative to be fully recognised at the time of the next revision of the treaties by requiring the commission to act on all requests made by parliament under article 225 of the tfeu by submitting a legislative proposal within an appropriate time limit': i would like to see the commission's proposals on the subject of the internal market adopted.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as announced in this resolution, there are three rapporteurs because three committees have been involved in a long and arduous process of examining the commission's proposal for the mid-term review of the stockholm programme. some time has been spent and we wanted to examine the first results of this initiative, which was initiated by the commission. i think that this attitude should be emphasized, because we in the union, and in particular in this parliament, must not only propose and decide but also verify and monitor what is happening in practice and what are the tangible results of the initiatives for the progressive integration of legal and judicial systems in europe. the results we have obtained can be summed up as follows. the first point i would like to raise, because it seems to me to be a bit new in our debates, is that we must check how many citizens are benefiting from the now extensive elaboration of regulatory monuments, a set of rules which increasingly regulates our legislation at european level. the results are disappointing. the rules adopted are very important - they have been listed in our results - it is very important that the subsidiarity of the rules as a whole with respect to the national states is always faithfully integrated, but an actual result of implementation on the citizens is disappointing, because the percentages of citizens involved in the use of the benefits that we, with our standardisation, want to provide them are very low. the first point to be made in the mid-term evaluation of the stockholm outcome is that implementation is becoming a categorical imperative for the union's legislative work as well. i shall therefore focus on two aspects in order to keep to the present time. the first is that we need to take the commission's initiative on the justice scoreboard to the end and therefore prepare the instruments for monitoring implementation and enforcement and that this must extend to the entire legal and judicial horizon, and therefore to private, civil, commercial and so on and also to criminal law, that is to say to all those aspects of the civil and everyday life of citizens and the protection of their security which is represented by these rules. we must have a greater say in this. the second aspect concerns the progressive creation in europe of a common legal and judicial culture, that is, something which forms the basis of the behaviour of legal practitioners, and this too has been included in our proposal.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president of the council, madam commissioner, a few days before the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, this parliament adopted a report entitled 'an area of freedom, security and justice serving the citizens'. the aim was to bring the treaty of lisbon forward so that this parliament could be immediately engaged in a reflection on a large number of issues, all of them of extraordinary importance. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it must be said, then, that the procedure of the associated committees juri, libe and afco has given a positive result, so much so that this procedure has been repeated for the report which i am now presenting and which uses, in fact, the same rapporteurs as five years ago. the debate on the question of freedom, security and justice in the service of the citizen has almost symbolically opened this parliament and is now closing it. as chairman of the committee on constitutional affairs, i would simply like to highlight some of the points made in the report: the need to respect the standards of the codecision procedure and to adapt the internal justice sector to the lisbon treaty for those aspects that have not yet been sufficiently addressed; the crucial role of national parliaments; the need to adopt a uniform electoral law for the european elections; the need to improve the discipline of the citizens' initiative. from the institutional point of view, the coming legislature has allowed the european parliament to play a full part in the development of the area of freedom, security and justice, following the transformation of what was formerly called the 'third pillar' in political matters, which is now almost entirely subject to the community method, that is to say, the ordinary legislative procedure. the commission should therefore be encouraged to make full use of its right of initiative in this area, while at the same time responding to the questions raised by the co-legislators. any new multiannual programming will therefore have to be established by common agreement between the three institutions in accordance with article 17 (1) of the treaty on european union. in this connection, it is regrettable that the european council has decided unilaterally to give its opinion on the strategic guidelines for this programming at its meeting on 26 and 27 june next, just when the current parliament is not meeting and before the new parliament is set up. this seems to me to be contrary to the principle of loyal cooperation between the institutions, as laid down in article 4 of the treaty on european union. apart from this observation, which i make in my capacity as chairman of the committee on constitutional affairs and as rapporteur, i must nevertheless express my support for the report and hope that it will be adopted by a very large majority. there are of course some aspects which remain open and some votes from my group will perhaps indicate some distinctions but these are secondary aspects for a report which is very positive on the whole.
the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one. in this task, parliament - this and the next - is determined to play a leading role, in a strategic dialogue respectful of the european council, but in the demanding exercise of its institutional prerogatives and its role as co-legislator. the strategic planning can be unfortunately placed in time by the european council, but we remind you that without parliament no legislation, however planned, can be implemented. the report is full of practical points. parliament called on the council to continue the process of eu accession to the european convention on human rights, to unblock the negotiations on access to documents of the institutions and to adopt the proposal for an anti-discrimination directive as soon as possible. i would like to focus on a fundamental question here: the european union is not a party to the schengen agreement. the mediterranean must be recognised as a frontier for all and a political partnership with the countries of the southern shore must be re-launched. common standards for legal entry and residence are needed; active inclusion policies based on the hard core of social citizenship rights for migrants are needed; in the event of a humanitarian crisis, a mandatory internal solidarity mechanism should be established, thus alleviating the rigidity of the dublin mechanisms. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the european union. we will be demanding on these points and we will play our full part as representatives of the european citizens.

vice-president of the commission. - madam president, this is the moment to look back to the very beginning of the term of this parliament. remember: five years ago europe was not fully equipped to act in the interests of the citizens in the area of justice and fundamental rights and citizenship. five years ago, decisions taken by justice and home affairs ministers were not transparent. decisions were taken by the council, acting mostly alone and always behind closed doors. parliament had little say in the so-called third pillar. the opinions of the representatives of eu citizens were given little importance and were quickly dismissed. international agreements were negotiated and signed in closed chambers. parliament’s voice was ignored. legislation and international agreements were based on emotional responses to the latest scare rather than on evidence. the focus was on security, and the rights of the citizen played second or third fiddle. justice was neglected, and europe often disappointed the expectations of citizens. five years on, things have changed dramatically. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty brought a much-needed change to justice and home affairs, with the use of the ordinary legislative codecision procedure and qualified majority decisions in the council. thanks to the work of parliament, we have brought tangible benefits to our citizens. together we have re-oriented european policies, putting justice first. together we have delivered in protecting the personal data of eu citizens; in strengthening the right to free movement; in ensuring that suspected persons have a clear set of rights all over europe; in ensuring that victims are protected from offenders; in facilitating the life of european businesses, with efficient and simple rules in civil and commercial justice – our justice for growth agenda. i think we can be proud of what we have achieved together in these past five years. over the last years we have taken a number of small steps that, seen together today, constitute a giant leap forward on the road towards a true european area of justice. but the journey is not over. we need to build more trust, promote more mobility and contribute better to growth. and so for the next parliamentary term, i look forward to seeing the consolidation of an eu system of justice built on trust; the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the debate this afternoon has revealed an important fact, namely that the issue of justice, although it does not interest the media and many of our colleagues - but this seems almost natural to me - has become an important issue in the european union. the lisbon treaty opened this way and the identification of the stockholm programme has made it possible to continue. i very much agree with commissioner reding when she tells us that important measures have been adopted which affect the daily lives of european citizens, which do not make the headlines and which are not often the subject of political interest, but which are the basis of european citizenship, whereby citizens feel european because a part of their lives is supported, promoted and regulated in a positive way. this was the stockholm programme. we have added an additional consideration: it is not enough to produce rules if they are not sufficiently implemented. there is a season now about the implementation of the rules that are produced, the implementation, the citizens having the concrete benefits of what is defined by the legal framework. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president-in-office of the council, commissioners, i have already said in my opening remarks why this report deserves a broad consensus. i now reply to some of the objections raised during the debate, particularly on the question of the european public prosecutor, which is already provided for in the treaty of lisbon. the lisbon treaty should also be implemented in this area, at a time when the globalisation of everything, including the difficulty of research, requires a concentration of research in one area. it is not a question of judging, but of gathering evidence, which is often very difficult to gather because the world has become global. secondly, as regards the other issues of justice - and i am speaking not only as chairman of the afco committee and rapporteur but also as an expert on justice in my judicial profession - i must say that the main problem today is the speed of the process. hamlet already complained, as a great hand that could push him to suicide, the length of the trials. this applies to criminal proceedings as well, but above all to civil proceedings. we must also speed up trade processes precisely in order to achieve the internal market better, to increase the possibility of trade and thus, ultimately, also to boost growth. of course, in this respect, it is not the substantive law that has primacy but procedural law. so by saying that commercial law is above criminal law and procedural law above substantive law, i am once again giving my consent to this important report.

member of the commission. - madam president, i would like to thank all the members who spoke in this debate. let me say a couple of things very clearly. i have sympathy for the amendment introduced by the socialist group. however, the problem is that, if this amendment were to be adopted, we would be forced to have a trilogue and would not be able to finalise the procedure before the end of the mandate of this parliament, which is in fact going to be dissolved within a little less than two weeks – not next week, but the week after in strasbourg. that is the reason why i cannot support the amendment. when you read in the amendment that they are giving you, as the commissioner, unlimited powers, that is very attractive, but the problem is that, given the time constraints, it would not be a good solution. on the other hand, the dcfta is part of the association agreement so, together with the political provisions – the so-called association agreement – this makes one single instrument. so there is very clearly a link between the chapters that have already been signed and those that will have to be signed once the elections have taken place and a new government is being constituted. there is very clearly a political link; whether there is a legal link is open to dispute because, in answer to mr scholz, there is not yet a treaty that has been ratified. we can only resolve that with a temporary instrument such as this one which is in fact – how i can i put this – a forecast of what the dcfta will mean for ukraine. therefore, i must insist that parliament does not adopt this argument so that we can proceed; so that after parliament has voted tomorrow, the council can adopt the provisions as soon as possible and they can then be put into practice, hopefully in may. that is also my answer to mr demesmaeker. i have a lot of sympathy for the argument but, given the time constraints, we cannot take any other route than to adopt the commission proposal without amendment. mr scholz asked why this was not done in october. i would have to say that this is an argument that i do not really understand because what happened in october was that the association agreement, together with the dcfta, were ready to be signed and at the very last moment – all of a sudden – the ukrainian government said that it was no longer going to sign it. this was rather surprising because the commission had been negotiating the dcfta with the government led by mr azarov and president yanukovych. we were not negotiating with the current government. we negotiated with the previous government and it was that government that in fact refused to sign the agreement. so i do not see how we could, at that time, unilaterally have decided to put into place these trade preferences. we had no counterpart. we are doing it unilaterally now but we have a counterpart that is ready to sign the association agreement and has already done so, with its political chapters. so this is a completely new situation. as soon as there was a new situation, the commission took the initiative of proposing to the european council that it go that way. that is why we are having this discussion tonight and why we are asking you to give your wholehearted support to this proposal.

in writing. - mr president, it is essential for the european union to have a regulatory framework and adequate instruments to ensure the effective exercise of the union's rights in international trade agreements, in order to safeguard its economic interests quickly and effectively and to discourage infringements, otherwise temporary measures of defensive retaliation will be implemented as an extreme solution. this will also help to build the eu's credibility in the wto and other international trade agreements and to convince trading partners to play by the rules. it is also appropriate for the commission and the european parliament to establish a structured and systematic exchange of information on the handling of commercial disputes, including the countermeasures to be taken and the reasons underlying them, as they could have significant repercussions on specific european industries.
in writing. - the european union currently lacks a horizontal legislative framework to enforce its rights under other international trade agreements. the instrument proposed by the commission is therefore designed to assert the legitimate trade rights of the european union, to strengthen its credibility and, last but not least, to draw the attention of our trading partners to the need to comply with the rules laid down in international trade agreements, in particular for those countries which have been responsible for infringements. this does not mean that the european union should resort more frequently to rebalancing measures, but that this proposal will help to present a credible and concrete threat to international partners, thereby dissuading them from taking action which does not respect the rules and is detrimental to fair competition in the internal market. in my view, the proposal for a regulation will make a positive contribution to the opening up of new markets for the european union. finally, i agree with the rapporteur that it is appropriate to ask that this proposal should contain a structured and systematic exchange of information between the commission and the european parliament, without this entailing delays in the decision-making process.

in writing. - the sst programme, although not one of the most ambitious and hence notorious european space programmes, is crucial to the success of all esa's present and future space missions. it is estimated that more than 700,000 hazardous debris is in orbit around the earth and that their potential to damage or destroy operational satellites is extremely high. the possibility of losing a mission due to the impact of space debris is considered the third highest risk, after the hazards arising from launch and distribution operations. the sst system allows the movement of these debris to be traced and thus predicted, limiting the risks to satellites and space missions. in this context, it is clear how important it is for the proper performance of the most important missions such as copernicus, galileo, etc. i voted in favour, as did the rapporteur, because i believe that increased participation by esa in the copernicus and egnos/galileo projects, including in economic terms, can ensure the smooth running of the programme without burdening the union budget.

in writing. - directive 2001/20/ec marked a major breakthrough in the development of the standards for conducting clinical trials in the union and internationally. however, it appears that this directive has created difficulties in promoting clinical trials in several member states. the proposal for a regulation aims to ensure harmonisation of the existing legal framework, a reduction in approval times (tacit approval) and a reduction in red tape, while at the same time promoting scientific research and innovation. in addition, as the commission proposes the establishment of a publicly accessible eu clinical trial database (transparency of results), with the clinical trial report, penalties for late submission and the indefinite retention of the permanent file, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i generally agree with the oecd's recommendation to divide clinical trials into three categories: the commission shall, by means of implementing acts, lay down the rules on the format and content of the information to be provided to the public. i voted in favour of the text, which is the result of an agreement which i particularly support, in particular, the provision for clinical trials in emergency situations to be authorized when it is impossible to obtain the consent of the subject or his representatives within the period of the therapy and, moreover, when the trial is specifically designed for the emergency situation. the trial must present a proportionate risk to a patient in the situation being tested compared to a standard treatment; in addition, it must have the potential to generate a direct clinical benefit. i also believe that it is essential to defend the rights of patients and vulnerable people to informed consent. the participation of certain groups of patients, such as minors or pregnant women, in a clinical trial should be subject to strict conditions in order to ensure a high level of protection.
in writing. - there is a broad consensus on the need to reform existing legislation on clinical trials, which has declined due to some of the provisions of the clinical trials directive. i agree that one of the main problems with the directive is its legal form, which should be replaced by a regulation in order to ensure greater consistency in its application. in addition, the simplification of bureaucratic procedures can play a key role in promoting experimentation in europe. i also believe that the question of ethics committees is of fundamental importance, as they have an important role to play in authorizing trials and ensuring the safety and well-being of patients. the establishment of a common european platform where ethics committees can discuss the modalities of authorization of clinical trials is therefore very welcome. finally, i believe that the lack of transparency in the results of clinical trials is at the root of the loss of public confidence in them. in this regard, improvements are therefore needed in this regard by encouraging the publication of the results of the trials and the publication of a full clinical trial report in the eu database.
in writing. - the concrete and balanced text addresses a number of issues such as the importance of coordination in the event of accidents, the independence of the regulatory authorities in the member states, periodic self-assessments with peer review and the review of the euratom treaty. that is why i have voted for it.
in writing. - following the very serious accident at fukushima, which raised serious doubts about the safety of energy from nuclear sources, the european union, which is probably the first in the world in terms of safety, also decided to review the regulations in this field. i voted in favour of this report because i welcome any effort to improve the already high european standards of safety in health and environmental matters. i also believe that ensuring more comprehensive legislation is also a duty towards the countries of the union which have decided to abandon the nuclear road because they are not convinced of its safety. nuclear energy, however, is one of the main sources of energy available to the union. so while the debate within countries remains the focus of attention, i am extremely positive about the willingness of the commission and parliament to make some changes to the legislation to ensure greater safety and greater participation of the populations concerned in nuclear decisions. however, i agree with the legal affairs committee that there should be no major changes to the case law on this subject, which appears to be dealt with in a more than satisfactory manner by the euratom treaty.
in writing. - the purpose of this directive is to maintain and promote the improvement of nuclear safety, leaving the member states with the necessary powers to define appropriate national regimes in this respect. it also covers vital questions of staff responsibility and training. i think it is very constructive and therefore i vote in favour.

in writing. - i think that the transversal report proposed by my colleagues is acceptable and i therefore support its approval by parliament. the stockholm programme aimed to strengthen european citizenship and its rights, to build a secure europe through cooperation in criminal matters and between the police forces of the member states against transnational crime, to strengthen borders and to develop a migration policy based on solidarity with migrants and respect for the needs of the member states. i believe that this was a great step forward, but at the same time, as the rapporteurs have pointed out, much remains to be done to develop the great potential of this programme to its full potential. i therefore share the rapporteur's various and well-reasoned observations and proposals so that we can start 2015 off with a new leaf in the fields of internal security, judicial cooperation, borders and visas, and asylum and migration. i believe that the qualitative leap can be made through greater cooperation between the union's institutions, in order to create a fully-fledged and well-functioning area of freedom, security and justice.

in writing. - when i first entered the european parliament, i strongly supported the stockholm programme, which set out the european union's priorities in the areas of justice, freedom and security for the period 2010-2014. there have been many successes, but in many areas there is still much to be done. i am thinking in particular of the promotion and protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and of judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters, areas for which adequate planning is urgently needed in the near future. until we achieve full harmonization in these areas, the fundamental freedoms of european citizens will always be confronted with insurmountable obstacles.

in writing. - i find the report acceptable and i announce a vote in favour. in global economies increasingly influenced by the ict sector, which is pervasive to the point of being the architecture on which all essential functions of not only the public sector but also the private sector (credit, logistics, trade, etc.) are based, it was inevitable that the dual use problem of these technologies would have a major impact. recent developments confirm the position of parliament and the union. from the nsa scandal to civil rights abuses in the middle east to forms of police surveillance in the people's republic of china, we are facing a scenario where such technologies can be used in contravention of international conventions and the common sense of our fellow citizens. in the meantime, we note that agreements are increasingly being made between multinational companies and governments using such technologies in the sense indicated above. the community regime solution can be an effective response, especially where parliament, the commission and the council are committed to developing legislative mechanisms and automata capable of overcoming the problem of 'delay' associated with updates of annexes containing products and technologies subject to the control system.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr liese on the amendment of directive 2003/87/ec establishing a system for the trading of greenhouse gas emission allowances in the field of international air transport. the proposal adopted today is a temporary solution, pending international agreement on the delicate issue of reducing co2 emissions from aviation at icao on a single global measure to be applied from 2020. only internationally agreed solutions implemented collectively will be able to contribute to an effective reduction of carbon dioxide emissions in our skies and remove the threat of unnecessary trade disputes between regional blocs and global aviation giants, as threatened by several parties. the eu is once again confirming its leadership role in the fight against climate change, but it is now necessary that our third country partners and the major economic operators in the aviation sector also contribute to this common objective to defend the future of the planet. it is therefore hoped that the icao negotiations will, after this vote by the european parliament, find new impetus for the definition of common solutions.
in writing. - i supported the proposal because its objective is to promote the icao negotiation towards an agreement on a single global measure to reduce aviation emissions that should apply from 2020. the ets-aviation proposal aims to apply the ets to european regional airspace rather than to all flights arriving at and departing from airports located there. this is a temporary solution pending the adoption of a global measure. the icao general assembly adopted a resolution on climate change, which commits to a single global market measure for international aviation emissions by 2016 and to its operationalization by 2020. in the absence of agreement, the ets would be re-implemented for all flights and operators would have to surrender their allowances by 30 april 2014. this outcome would have been likely to be seriously counterproductive to the success of the icao negotiations. this compromise is directed at the industries concerned as well as at consumers. this is an important step towards the future implementation of an international agreement for the application of a global measure for the whole aviation sector.
in writing. - europe has always paid close attention to the protection of the environment. the aviation sector, because of its complexity, is the least regulated sector in this field to date. as a result, its emissions risk undermining all efforts in other areas. the need to impose an emissions trading system has been known for a long time, but it often clashes with the interests of airlines and the unfair behaviour of third countries. i therefore vote in favour of this report, which, by introducing the system at the level of 'european airspace', guarantees greater coverage of emission allowances and a fairer redistribution of burdens between european and non-european carriers. finally, i agree with the rapporteur that it is not appropriate to consider an extension of the suspension of time limits as a solution. i accept that regional (european) legislation alone is not the final solution but, pending a global approach to the issue (we hope to have answers from icao in 2016), this project is demonstrative as well as practical.

in writing. - while i fully support the commission's proposal, a number of amendments were necessary, particularly to strengthen european ambition in the field of the environment and equal treatment with regard to other areas. it was also important to point out that some member states are reluctant to implement the legislation, while third countries refuse to surrender allowances for flights within europe, which is unacceptable.
in writing. - i have always been a strong supporter of electronic money and i can see myself in mr zalba's report, for which i am voting in favour. there is broad agreement on the value of electronic payments in relation to the single market and the fight against tax evasion and the black economy. among the wide range of studies on the subject, i point to a 2013 european-wide benchmarking analysis by bankitalia, which reveals how income and the spread of card payment access points are actually the factors reducing the demand for cash. the zalba report is therefore focused when it addresses the issue of rentals from pos, operator or credit institutions in three- and four-channel schemes, which impose excessive fees on consumers and unsustainable charges on retailers for the use of pos services, in effect encouraging a return to cash. the use of electronic payment also presupposes a reasonable degree of fraud protection on the part of the consumer and certain levels of income and financial literacy. if it is more difficult to intervene on income, certainly the innovations in the regulation are a powerful incentive to a more lively and therefore wider and safer market.
in writing. - the limitation of credit and debit card costs will benefit consumers and retailers. i have chosen to support the proposal because it provides for more favourable rates for european citizens when paying by credit or debit card and standardisation of the rules for online transactions. this is an important step towards the harmonisation of payment services, which creates a level playing field for this market in the european union, promoting its competitiveness and innovation. today, each member state has different and unclear laws governing online card payments, thus creating a fragmented payments market costing €130 billion a year. the new legislation aims instead to establish a level playing field which will help to defragment this market, bringing great benefits to both consumers and retailers. the payment services directive also aims to make it easier and safer to use online payment services. the booming world of e-commerce will finally be subject to strict european supervision rules to protect consumers from fraud and other possible abuses.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i consider this proposal for a regulation to be a genuinely necessary one in order to improve the situation of the internal market and consumers and to allow for a greater spread of electronic payments as envisaged in the europe 2020 strategy and the green paper. interbank fees which are charged to merchants as a fair cost which they must pay for a service which is safer than cash and which guarantees a larger user base, are in reality often passed on to the final consumer who is thus forced to pay for a service from which another person benefits. the european commission has already proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states on the use of credit cards and debit cards.
in writing. - among the many things the report deals with, i welcome the first amendment. national measures risk creating significant obstacles to the completion of the internal market in the area of payments by card, internet or mobile card-based devices. there would be a risk of hindering the freedom to provide services. these measures are a burden on business and are unfairly imposed on citizens. i therefore think i must vote in favour.
in writing. - cashless transactions play a crucial role in the functioning of economies as they are fast, secure and innovative, but the achievement of an integrated eu market is hampered by the existence of multilateral interbank fees. i have supported this proposal for a regulation because i believe that it is necessary to limit the fees that banks charge retailers for processing credit and debit card payments. this taxation costs european retailers around eur 10 billion each year and retailers raise the prices of the goods or services they sell to support these costs. but by limiting the fees banks charge for transitions over time, users will benefit from lower prices.
in writing. - the improvement of the internal market for payments is an important step towards the overall completion of the european internal market. the development of a card acceptance network should therefore be promoted, with ceilings on interbank fees for domestic and cross-border transactions. at the same time, i agree that it is essential to create the appropriate instruments to ensure the proper functioning of the market.
in writing. - according to data released by the ecb in 2012, the number of credit card payments has quadrupled since 2000. the growth rate, although less spectacular, was recorded for electronic transactions (e.g. payments by bank transfer), the expansion of the pos and atm networks. the old paper bank cheque is being used less and less. these figures have been included in the extensive consultations and impact assessments underlying the proposal for a directive which is the subject of today's report, and which i shall be voting in favour of. the text analyses a number of developments by correcting distortions and legislative gaps which have left room for unfair practices to the detriment of consumers. i refer to forecasts such as those in articles 3, on the abuse of the exemption for limited networks, 55 on tariffs, 92) on the effectiveness of sanctions, and the repeal of the old article 3), which has led to the proliferation of fake spin-offs aimed at applying exorbitant user fees, with the aggravating factor in some cases of explicitly targeting a vulnerable user, identified through specific profiling activities on a detailed geographical basis. this ambitious reform removes serious obstacles to innovation in a particularly dynamic sector with a high potential for the application of new technologies, which is the subject of eu policy papers.
in writing. - strongly supporting the need to encourage the use of electronic money, i voted in favour of this report which introduces indications in favour of an increasingly competitive and secure electronic payments market. the need to increase the use of payments with new technological tools provides significant benefits for consumers, merchants and public funds by effectively combating counterfeiting and evasion. the objective of this report is to create an internal market for electronic payments which does not discriminate between credit/debit circuits in order to ensure the entry of new players into the market. with the consequent increase in user convenience, it is also hoped that these payment methods will be progressively used more by consumers with the associated benefits. the key aspects of the text are to ensure a level playing field between all categories of payment service providers and to ensure an increasingly secure system, and i therefore fully agree with the rapporteur's position.

in writing. - today's vote is a significant step forward towards the single telecommunications market and a further step towards the practical realisation of the free movement of european citizens who will finally be free to use their mobile phones without changing operator and tariff in any country of the european union. all additional charges for international roaming within the eu will be zeroed by december 2015. telephone calls, text messages and internet browsing will be free of charge for all european citizens within any other member state of the union. in addition, electronic signatures and certificates will be better protected by a more secure online environment through the mutual recognition of electronic identification systems by member states.
