in writing. this year marks the 100th anniversary of the outbreak of world war i, in which over 20 million military and civilian casualties were lost, and even more horrifying was the number of wounded. it was a real tragedy, fought on european soil between nations and peoples who were never friends, who over the centuries often fought for dominance over each other. today, fortunately, we have lived for almost 70 years without conflicts between european states, and this is certainly a merit that must be attributed to the idea of europe conceived by people like schuman, de gasperi or adenauer: when i criticise the european union, it is also because i am thinking of those people who believed in a dream at the time, and i do not want it to be burned to the ground now because of wrong decisions that risk stirring up resentment among the people. peace is an absolute value, even for people like me who have never had war in their home: but our grandparents who are still alive know what this means, and we must fight to prevent this from happening again, even by criticizing the measures taken from above, which can bring anger and tension.

in writing. - today, community workers moving between member states risk losing their acquired rights if the length of their residence is not considered to be long enough by the state to which they move. i voted in favour of the proposal which has emerged from the negotiations between the ep and the council, with the participation of the commission, to ensure legal certainty on supplementary pension rights. under these new rules, the period of active membership of a pension scheme required for a person to maintain supplementary pension rights will not exceed three years. i believe that this is a great step forward for the free movement of workers and a push towards a social europe.
in writing. - i give a favourable opinion on the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the minimum requirements for increasing the mobility of workers between member states by improving the acquisition and maintenance of supplementary pension rights. the proposal under consideration is a further step in the direction indicated by the community lisbon programme, since it aims to facilitate the cross-border mobility of european workers. the text deals in particular with supplementary pension rights and aims to enact a coherent community directive to ensure that they are safeguarded despite the differences in the social protection systems in force in the individual member states. the recognition at community level of workers' pension rights is an essential measure for enhancing the flexibility of the european labour market. for these reasons, i regard this motion for a resolution as a valuable instrument for removing an obstacle to the free movement of workers within the union.
in writing. - food safety has always been at the heart of community action. the eu's agri-food industry is the second largest sector, with a total output of the food chain of around eur 750 billion per year, employing over 48 million people: from primary production to retail to catering. i believe strongly in the need to simplify the general legal framework, which is fragmented and overlapping and which leads to divergent interpretations and application at national level. i therefore voted in favour of the text calling for greater consistency throughout the system of controls.
in writing. - i support the report by my colleague and friend mr pirillo, which aims to modernise european legislation on official controls to ensure compliance with european legislation on food and feed, animal welfare and plant health and plant reproductive material. the report focuses on the need to have a food chain effectively controlled at all stages and integrates well with other sectoral regulations (animal health, plant disease measures, expenditure management) as part of an overall package on the food and plant chain. among the most positive elements of the text: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive. it is also important to have increased the degree of flexibility in the system of payment of the costs of the checks carried out: one of the important lines of the report allows member states to limit the burden of mandatory fees for controls on operators in the primary production sector. it is therefore a positive regulation which will contribute to the objective of a safer and more transparent food chain, and which i have therefore supported by voting in favour of it.
in writing. - the compromise reached by my colleague pirillo is good; the amendments are extremely positive: lower costs contributing to the formation of mandatory tariffs (in fact only staff salaries excluding social charges , travel expenses and costs of laboratory analyses remain); and discounts for operators who are consistently compliant, to name just a few. however, i am concerned that any exemptions from the payment of the mandatory fees may make the system economically unsustainable and that there may be implications for the control activity at the expense of the level of safety.
in writing. - the report by mr pirillo on food safety, which has always played a central role in community action, was voted on today in the plenary. in the food chain, official controls are an essential element for ensuring a high level of health protection and the correct implementation of complex legislation throughout the agri-food chain and for building consumer confidence. for the feed and food, animal health and animal welfare sectors, controls are currently governed by regulation (ec) no 882/2004, while those in other sectors, such as plant health controls, are governed by specific legislation. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to take a more active role in the fight against fraud. the rapporteur also believes that the threshold for surveillance in border controls and in the meat sector cannot and should not be lowered and that for these reasons controls should be entrusted to highly qualified staff who are able to detect the emergence of possible risks and dangers to human health.
in writing. - food safety has always been at the heart of community action. ensuring a high level of human, animal and plant health throughout the food chain is a key objective of the union, which requires a harmonised and comprehensive framework to be achieved. i agree with the rapporteur that the legal framework that the eu has developed so far has proved, on the whole, to be effective in preventing and combating risks, as eu products remain among the safest in the world precisely because of the controls they are subjected to. nevertheless, the increasingly long and complex agri-food chain exposes the european union to new risks and requires constantly improved controls along this chain. i therefore support the harmonisation of the minimum frequency of checks proposed by the rapporteur, as well as the creation of european reference centres, which will have the specific task of developing and validating methods to be used in the event of intentional breaches of the rules. finally, i also welcome the rapporteur's attention to micro-enterprises.
in writing. - i voted against this measure, which has possible negative effects on livestock farming and in italy the rules on the management of domestic animals already provide for the control systems referred to in the text.
in writing. - a european law on animal welfare, containing the general principles on duty of care, division of responsibilities and training requirements, would be of great value to animals and farmers in europe. however, the right balance between predictability and flexibility must be ensured. i also appreciate that the commission proposal focuses on rapid and effective measures to control and eradicate certain diseases, but we must not forget that the greatest costs to society are actually caused by endemic diseases which will not be listed in this regulation. finally, it should not be forgotten that a functioning internal market also requires good control of animals living in a country bordering the union, which makes strict buffer zones necessary to prevent the spread of diseases into the eu from neighbouring countries.
in writing. - the aim of the current eu regulatory framework in the field of plant health is to protect european agriculture and forestry by preventing the entry and spread of harmful organisms. the main instrument for this is council directive 2000/29/ec. this is a regulatory framework that has been criticised for some time for failing to stop the increasingly frequent entry of new pests into the territory of the european union as a result of the expansion of international trade. the experience of other countries suggests that a completely closed system does not prevent the spread of diseases but only adds unnecessary burdens to operators. the proposals in the text are exactly in that direction, and i have therefore decided to abstain.
in writing. - the commission proposes to extend the scope of regulation (ec) no 718/1999, to allow the reserve funds to be used to support the inland waterway sector more effectively and to create a favourable environment for innovation and improvement of safety and environmental performance. in my view, inland navigation offers many benefits: the commission will be able to assess the impact of the proposed measures on the environment and the environment in the light of the experience gained in the past. i therefore believe that we must make better use of its benefits by supporting investment in measures to promote 'greening' and innovation. however, the funds available under this regulation are rather limited, and i therefore call on the commission to optimise the financial instruments for the sector.
in writing. - the current eu regulatory framework in the field of plant health is intended to protect european agriculture and forestry by preventing the entry and spread of harmful organisms, however, in recent years the increase in imports has led to the emergence of significant outbreaks of dangerous pests, with particularly negative consequences for european forestry. for these reasons, the package proposed by the commission has an important objective which cannot be put on the back burner. in this respect, i share the view that all professional operators should be included in the protection regime against plant pests. furthermore, as regards the entry into force of the legislation, i believe it is useful to give national supervisory authorities and professional operators sufficient time to prepare for the new regime.
in writing. - the report on the proposal for a regulation on the safety of consumer products is of substantial importance for the italian industry, especially in connection with the proposal to include the indication of the country of origin among the information to be provided to consumers for all non-food products intended for them. this obligation to indicate origin, or the so-called 'made in' clause, was contained in the original proposal of the european commission, the text of which was confirmed by a vote in the relevant parliamentary committees. this provision, if approved, would achieve a twofold objective: the commission has also proposed that the eu should make the product more traceable on the european market and align the conditions under which european companies operate with those of the eu's main trading partners, which have already introduced similar provisions. i therefore welcome the european commission's proposal and, in particular, i support the wording of article 7 of the proposal containing the 'made in' clause. i believe that the positive outcome of the vote on this key point of the report represents the necessary incentive for the finalisation of an interinstitutional agreement on the initiative, helping to overcome the differences between member states which, until now, have precluded the possibility of reaching an ambitious agreement in the council.
in writing. - i voted today in favour of this report, in line with the ppe. finally, parliament has approved the regulation governing 'made in', with a whole series of standards which will have to be followed carefully by each individual state. as we all know, "made in italy" is the most imitated brand in the world: the commission's proposal for a regulation is therefore another step towards a greater defence of our excellences and towards official recognition of our products. with this report we have made a major breakthrough in the battle that has been going on for many years now and which has involved the council and the commission in lengthy negotiations with parliament. italy will thus be able to protect itself more effectively also in relation to exports by preserving the prestige of the 'made in italy' brand which it is entitled to and by safeguarding the expertise and know-how which have always characterized italian production.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the measure, and in this case article 7 which introduces the concept of product traceability and 'made in' which could have a considerable impact on the italian business system, which is made up for the most part of micro and small and medium-sized enterprises which make the marking of origin one of their strengths.
in writing. - the report on the safety of consumer products plays a key role in the effective completion of a european internal market which instills confidence in consumers and european citizens. in this context, the provision in article 7 of the regulation on the obligation to indicate origin, the so-called 'made in', can symbolically represent the european union's willingness to bet on its ability to emerge definitively from the economic crisis using one of the best weapons we have: quality manufacturing. it is not a question of erecting protectionist barriers to protect european production, but of ensuring information, transparency and traceability throughout the production chain, as is being done with great difficulty in the food chain: we must allow the european consumer to make informed choices about the products he buys. the approval of 'made in' would also remedy the current lack of reciprocity between the european union and many other countries in the world and help the fight against counterfeiting. a zero-cost measure will therefore have a number of positive effects: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. for these reasons, i strongly supported the schaldemose report.
in writing. - in the last few days alone, the financial guard has seized over a million dangerous consumer items, mostly toys intended for children for the easter holidays. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i not only note a healthy effort to systematize and update the legislation, but i also stress the value of the regulation as a safeguard for consumer protection in a globalised world, which has changed profoundly in its market, consumption and distribution aspects. the introduction of the precautionary principle, full traceability and the introduction of the ce+ mark are therefore welcome. i would like to stress two points in particular. as regards costs, the pia assesses them as being borne by firms, in comparison with the direct benefits of increased consumer confidence and the documented increase in trade in the european market. on a principle level, i also find it commendable that the costs of supporting control systems are being shifted from the taxpayer, who is himself a victim of unfair commercial practices, to those who engage in such practices, by increasing the sanctions regime, which will also have a deterrent effect.
in writing. - i strongly supported this report because the health of consumers must be absolutely protected against the danger of any counterfeiting. the counterfeit is not only chinese but also turkish, that is, the country which the european union is determined to defend and which it hopes will soon become a member of the eu. in-depth studies show that the most counterfeited products in turkey are italian products. moreover, italian companies in particular rarely take legal action, as they have no confidence in the objectivity of turkish courts. in turkey, counterfeit goods are particularly prevalent in the fashion sector, with particular emphasis on leather accessories such as bags and belts, footwear, sunglasses, jewellery, watches, cosmetics and perfumery. and let us not forget toys and gadgets that in most cases do not meet the health requirements. it is therefore pointless to mention the extent of the damage which is being caused to our production by the inaction of the turkish authorities and customs in the matter of controls. another reason, along with others, to support the no to turkey in europe!
in writing. - i voted in favour of the package on product safety and market surveillance. the battle won today ensures that all products are marked with the 'origin of origin'. italian excellence will thus be protected and easily recognised by consumers. the new rules, including electronic traceability and increased security in trade within the european union, send a strong signal against the black market for counterfeits. we have fought to protect the interests of small and mediumsized enterprises and to preserve the 'made in italy' from often unfair competition.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mandatory introduction of the 'made in' label for non-food products sold on the community market. i believe that product safety is the key to ensuring a well-functioning single market and facilitating the growth of european businesses and the prosperity of the union through it. however, 27% of european consumers do not feel safe when operating in the single market, as revealed by a commission survey conducted in 2012 by eurobarometer. by making the 'made in' mark compulsory and imposing stricter penalties on fraudulent companies, a major step forward is made in the transparency of the supply chain of a product and greater security is given to consumers, thereby encouraging them to buy more products in the single market.
in writing. - parliament votes in favour of the regulation on the safety of consumer products, including its chapter 7 on the mandatory 'made in' mark, and rejects the council which has for years tried to block the implementation of rules and regulations to ensure the safety of european consumers and fair competition on the market. once again, governments that protect only retail against manufacturing have been defeated by their own representatives who are answerable to their own citizens. i leave the european parliament after 25 years of work for italy and europe, with the satisfaction of having seen the house vote twice for the 'made in' in defence of european consumers and producers and against those governments which are unable to defend the rights of their citizens. we now rely on the italian presidency to finally bring about a favourable vote in the council during its six-month term of office so that the rights of consumers and producers are recognised and production and therefore growth can finally be redistributed.
in writing. - pier antonio panzeri (s&d), mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am voting in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the safety of consumer products and repealing council directive 87/357/eec and directive 2001/95/ec. the simplification and harmonisation of the rules governing the internal market and the strengthening of consumer protection legislation are key objectives of community policies. in view of the intensification of international trade relations, the proposal aims at creating an effective european legislative framework which will act as a 'safety net' for product safety. first, the introduction of the ce+ mark, which is complementary to the existing ce marking, allows for the immediate identification of goods tested by qualified third parties. in addition, the compulsory indication of the country of origin of products ensures better traceability of goods and greater transparency in the marketing process. finally, the proposed regulation provides for a substantial strengthening of the internal market surveillance system by establishing contact points to optimise communication and cooperation between member states. i therefore welcome this proposal and hope that it will establish a relationship of trust between the european citizens and the single market.
in writing. - consumer product safety is a key aspect of the internal market, which the eu must take into account if the market is to be safe for consumers. some aspects are particularly relevant: i am referring in particular to measures relating to the traceability of products and the principle of origin, which i consider essential if the consumer is to be able to make informed and fully informed economic choices. traceability makes it possible to understand where a product comes from, so that the buyer can actually understand whether the country of origin is one of those that register the largest number of products that do not meet european safety criteria.
in writing. - more stringent rules on the control of products circulating on the union market have long been needed and desired. the text under voting succeeds in maintaining the right balance between the safety requirements for consumers and certain and functional standards for businesses, and finally facilitates cooperation between the authorities of the member states. for these reasons i have decided to support it.
in writing. - the commission proposal aims to establish a common european framework for market surveillance covering all products circulating in the internal market, including those imported from the union. the commission's analysis has shown that only 0,3% of goods imported or placed on the union market are controlled by the authorities, and this is an alarming figure. to ensure that crime does not pay, i voted in favour of stricter, more proportionate and more dissuasive penalties for companies that violate the rules of the market. i also think it is useful for the commission to draw up an eu-wide blacklist of companies which have intentionally and repeatedly breached product safety rules. this will increase the level of coordination, cooperation and exchange of information between the market surveillance and product safety authorities of the different member states.
in writing. - at the end of march, the european commission published the data on the annual activity of rapex, the rapid information system on dangerous products, which has been designed for ten years to identify and block non-compliant goods and products (other than foodstuffs) placed on the european market in a timely manner. the reports for 2013 were over 2,300, mainly concerning clothing, textiles, fashion items and toys, which together cover half of the total complaints. more than 64% of the irregularity reports come from one source, which i think is easy to guess, but which is worth mentioning again, because i will never tire of pointing out all the problems that originate in china. these are non-compliant products, which can also have serious health implications, and i am appalled that 25 percent of the reports concern toys and therefore the safety of our children. since its introduction in 2003, the number of reports to rapex has steadily increased, demonstrating an increasing risk: i hope that the report we have voted today will serve to establish and enforce stricter standards, because the invasion of highly dangerous chinese products must be stopped immediately.
in writing. - member states' market surveillance is still far from meeting the challenge posed by the increase in imports into the eu and the increased number of products circulating in the single market, which is also weakened by a highly cumbersome and inconsistent legal structure. it is therefore necessary to step up and strengthen cooperation between the supervisory authorities of the member states and the exchange of information, which currently relies mainly on rapex and icsms. as regards sanctions, they should in any case be dissuasive, but at the same time proportionate.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the auken report on the amendment of the packaging directive which contains important provisions for reducing the consumption of plastic bags in europe. the consequences of plastic bag pollution are plain to see, and one fact alone illustrates the extent of the environmental damage: in 2010, over 8 billion plastic bags became waste, with serious impacts on protected areas, fragile ecosystems and marine ecosystems. i welcome the european commission's proposal and the compromise amendments adopted last month by the committee on the environment. on the basis of this directive, italy, which is now at the forefront of europe in the production of biodegradable and compostable plastic bags, will be able to maintain this virtuous system, thus cancelling an unjust infringement procedure which the eu had initiated against our country. it will thus be possible to demonstrate to the whole of the european union how it is possible to combine development, research and entrepreneurship in a balanced way with the principles of respect for the environment and of reducing pollution and to find a virtuous way to reduce and recycle waste and plastic.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the report, with an underlining and a caveat. i would stress the important principle that member states can go beyond the objectives set out in the directive by means of disincentive measures. the case of italy is illuminating: a series of measures since 2011 has resulted in a 50 percent reduction in the use of traditional single-use bags (including through the encouraged spread of reusable shopper bags), an increase in organic recycling rates of plastic waste, an improvement in the quality of the organic fraction through less plastic contamination. measures which have at the same time produced effects of environmental awareness, concretely reduced the impact of pollution (especially of the coasts), encouraged the growth of new markets for bioindustries. in this respect, my caveat can be translated into an invitation to the rapporteur to reconsider, in the light of the italian case, the multiple economic opportunities and environmental values of a greater spread of biodegradable and compostable plastics. i see no risk of perpetuating a consumerist mindset from the 1960s production system. on the contrary, i see clear potential on the side of environmental awareness in the direction of circular economies that emphasize sustainability values and can be a driver of innovation and economic and cultural growth.

in writing. honey is not a compound product. for this reason, it is expressly forbidden to add food ingredients, additives and any other substances to honey. it follows that pollen is not an ingredient of honey, as it is not intentionally added to honey, but is, on the contrary, a natural constituent. classifying pollen as an ingredient means first of all affecting the reputation and true identity of this all-natural product, with repercussions in economic and employment terms on the beekeeping sector: increased production costs due to additional testing requirements and labelling charges; the commission has therefore decided to initiate the procedure provided for in article 93 (2) of the treaty in respect of the aid scheme for the production of olive oil.
in writing. - the proposal will enable the commission to amend the technical specifications relating to the names, descriptions and definitions of the products listed in annex i and to the criteria for the composition of honey listed in annex ii to this directive. as the rapporteur considers that these are all essential elements of the directive and has therefore removed these references from the commission's proposal, i intend to support this text with my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs girling's report on a particularly controversial subject, the honey directive. a subject that has been controversial since a debate on the constituent elements of honey was triggered by a ruling by the court of justice that the pollen in honey should be considered an artificially added ingredient and therefore regulated under the directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs. however, it is clear that pollen enters the hive only through the activity of the bees and is therefore naturally present in the honey, regardless of whether or not the beekeeper extracts it by centrifugation. the text adopted therefore clearly states that pollen should be classified as a natural constituent of honey and treated as such, both for the sake of correct legislation on the subject and for greater clarity for producers. however, in line with the eu's policy of greater transparency for consumers, i believe that if the presence of gm pollen is found to be above the natural limits allowed, established by appropriate controls, this should be adequately highlighted on the product labelling.
in writing. - attempts to treat pollen as an ingredient rather than a natural component of honey have been repeatedly thwarted. this approach is scientifically flawed and would lead to problems which could lead to a sharp decline in italian honey consumption, with a strong impact on employment. the result achieved with the current wording of the directive, as proposed by the european commission, is therefore very good. the commission has also proposed that the eu should be able to provide the eu with a comprehensive list of the products it intends to import from third countries.
in writing. - i support the proposal to ensure that honey is also covered by a set of rules which define pollen as a natural component of honey rather than as an ingredient. the ingredient/constituent dilemma arose because of the labelling implications for each option. if pollen is still considered a 'constituent', the genetically modified pollen present would not need any labelling. this is because, according to the gmo rule, only the genetically modified content in quantities above 0.9% must be indicated on the label of the finished product. since natural pollen reaches a threshold of around 0.5% for each consignment of honey, it could never exceed the labelling threshold. i fully share the parliament's position on this issue, since it has decided to take a stand against gmos, in favour of quality agricultural products which are characteristic of the european market and of certain european regions in particular, promoting high quality standards, with an eye to the vast agricultural component of the european economy.

in writing. - the commission's proposal is very well received, as it can bring great benefits to consumers and smes in exercising their right to compensation for damage caused by infringements of competition law. the absence of adequate national rules is a very serious shortcoming for several member states and the difference between the various national laws further exacerbates this situation. the instruments provided for in the text in question can make a major contribution to reducing legal uncertainty and gaps, ensuring the rights of operators on the european market and strengthening their confidence.
in writing. - i think that the report analysing the regulation on shipments of waste is acceptable and does not present any particular criticisms, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - i appreciate the balanced approach of the report, which avoids easy ideological exploitation and implicitly recognises waste production as an aspect of the global production system. the illegal export of waste to politically weak or corrupt areas from somalia to west africa is a well-documented scourge whose origins date back to the blockade era. it is a moral scourge, because of the environmental and health risks in the regions concerned, but above all from an economic point of view, because it is the main obstacle to the widespread development of an adequate industrial base which could, within a legal framework, express an important economic potential also for the emerging countries, in a perspective of comparative advantage. the effects of slowing down development and innovation are even more visible in the european industrial system, again with significant moral implications not only in terms of corporate social responsibility but also in relation to the overall high amount of funds allocated by both the fp and horizon 2020 to the development of environmentally sustainable economies. an appropriate control system, such as that suggested by the protocols provided for in the regulation, seems likely to make important progress. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - in the text, the commission identifies a number of specific costs and causes of illegal waste shipment, which are borne by the member states and, ultimately, by european citizens, both in economic terms and in terms of well-being and health. it therefore proposes a series of measures to overcome several shortcomings in the implementation of the relevant legislation in the member states. i support the report also because it aims to strengthen these measures by improving knowledge of illegal shipments and giving greater powers to the authorities, as well as by strengthening cooperation between member states, while not putting an undue burden on honest economic operators working in the sector.
in writing. - analysis of recent data on the use of psychoactive substances has shown the need for more effective and better coordinated action between member states and eu agencies in relation to the use of such substances. this proposal for a regulation is welcomed as it establishes a system for the rapid exchange of information on new psychoactive substances appearing on the market, including their commercial and industrial use, in order to assess the risks of those of concern at eu level and to withdraw those of concern from the market. we must prevent the social, health and safety risks that these substances can cause, and through this regulation we can ensure an effective and structural response to the problem in question.
in writing. - i share the views expressed in the report analysing the regulation on new psychoactive substances, and i believe that the harmonization of legislation at european level and the creation of a single register will facilitate the management of these substances in all the member states.
in writing. - over 200 substances with dangerous psychoactive effects are readily available in european cities, not to mention international trade, fuelled by a vibrant blogosphere of enthusiastic regular users, unlikely rebel theorists, and real brokerage businesses. in addition to plant extracts, which are widely available to consumers, the immediate and obvious threat is the abuse of medicines (especially analgesics of certain categories) and the spread of precursors. the eu has long adopted a philosophy of not criminalising the use of individual substances by individuals, but of assessing their impact on society on the basis of objective scientific and epidemiological findings, in order to protect the safety of citizens, which is one of the values enshrined in the european charter. the trivialization of the social risks of unconscious use of such substances must also be combated. the eu has the merit of responding in a timely manner to this new challenge to the health of europeans through a balanced and flexible regulation, strongly anchored in the principles of proportionality and subsidiarity, which provides the tools for an effective and immediate response, while at the same time establishing important mechanisms for the exchange of information between the authorities concerned by scientific research, regulatory categorisation and enforcement.
in writing. - the report aims to regulate the increasingly widespread misuse of what are termed 'new psychoactive substances', i.e. new generation chemicals for commercial and industrial use. they reproduce the effects of certain drugs, their consumption is highly harmful to the health of individuals and their marketing under the guise of environmental perfumes and fertilizers is a danger to public health and society. for the reasons stated above, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - the rapid spread of psychoactive substances has led to a variety of control measures in the member states, with the application of state-specific methods which may create obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market. the commission's communication on this subject is therefore welcome, as it calls for a more decisive and coherent response from the eu and the member states, through more active exchange of information and withdrawal and temporary restrictions for certain substances. the fight against these new substances will be better tackled by means of these new instruments, allowing for more coordinated action, which is essential in the fight against organised crime in this sector, which often exploits transnational criminal networks.
in writing. - i am in favour of this proposal because it aims to bring the new psychoactive substances under the same criminal law provisions as other substances controlled under the un conventions. psychoactive substances, like many other drugs, are a threat to society, affecting the functioning of the brain which creates symptoms such as changes in consciousness, behaviour and cognition. tackling the distribution of psychoactive substances is not to be underestimated. though member states do have their own policies on tackling illicit drugs, when psychoactive substances are being distributed from one member state to another efficient cooperation between member states is indispensable, especially in an era when commerce and communication are no longer limited by physical and geographical boundaries.
in writing. - i consider the report to be balanced and acceptable, and for these reasons i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. - a recent epidemiological study published by a leading american university indicates a 30% increase in a component linked to the use of psychoactive substances in the statistics of fatal road accidents. in addition, there is a growing tendency to combine different psychotropic substances, both legal and illegal, in a mixture extremely harmful to the health of the person concerned at the liver and kidney level, as well as being likely to trigger genuine psychotic episodes. in some member states, recent case law is moving towards the case of voluntary manslaughter in the event of a fatal accident caused by the use of substances capable of altering an individual's capabilities. studies accompanying the european road safety plan indicate that, in the face of a steady improvement in the safety conditions of the network, there is a corresponding increase in dangerous behaviour. a driver who is intoxicated by alcohol is 13 times more likely to cause a fatal accident. in the case of alcohol and psychotropic substances, the odds are 24 to 1 compared to a compos sui driver. there is no room for any indulgence. i shall be forgiven for giving a simple but emblematic example of detail in support of my declaration of vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - the following proposal is part of the regulatory package on new psychoactive substances. it aims to include them in the list of drugs, thus making applicable the package of rules and sanctions already in place for the protection of union citizens in this area. i am voting in favour of the initiative as i consider it to be correct and proportionate.
in writing. - i agree with the decision to subject new psychoactive substances to the same criminal law provisions as other controlled substances under the un conventions. although member states have their own policies to combat illicit drugs on the national market, more efficient cooperation is needed in order to fight a transnational organised criminal system on an equal footing.
in writing. - i voted for the report to continue to elevate eu-japan relations by the timely conclusion of the negotiations for a comprehensive strategic partnership agreement.
in writing. - the political and commercial link between the eu and japan is now an established reality and one of the eu's major international successes, which is why its further deepening can only ensure a rise in mutual friendship and trust. the political dialogue must continue to emphasise a range of shared values, objectives and responsibilities for the promotion of peace, stability and democracy at global level, while also aiming to strengthen the promotion of peace in the regional area in which japan is located and to promote respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms there. in economic matters, a framework on cooperation in science, technology, trade and research is needed to increase the eu's innovation potential, but also to cooperate in defining a sustainable common agenda for combating climate change.

in writing. - smart regulation for smes is essential to ensure their competitiveness, avoiding excessive bureaucratic burdens and discriminatory measures. for this reason, i fully support the principle of 'think small', which takes full account of the role that smes play in the european economy and thus protects them from unfair competition. this approach therefore also includes the responsibility of the eu and the member states to ensure administrative simplification - which normally burdens smes much more heavily than large enterprises, due to their smaller economic capacities - as well as measures to enhance the transparency of procurement and relations between enterprises and public institutions, so as to ensure a level playing field between smes and larger competitors.

in writing. the economic formula proposed by president juncker does not meet the real needs of the european people and does not allow for a sustainable recovery. the austerity policies have proved to be utterly ineffective, especially in the long term. europe lost trading ground to other major economic players like the united states, which rightly reversed the crisis by injecting liquidity into the economic system. europe continues to strangle its peoples with suicidal economic policies which do not allow growth. the formal perfection of public accounts is still sought, at the expense of the incomes of the less well-off. in fact, it is the low-income groups that suffer the heaviest tax levies, holding back gdp growth, which would receive a huge boost if the heavy tax burden on low-income earners were eased. many economists have come out in favour of theories developed by john maynard keynes and i refer to the "principle of effective demand": a nation's level of production, its income and consequently its employment are determined by consumer demand. when the income of most of them is reduced, then countries fall into a destructive spiral.

president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, as you said, the high representative and vice-president ashton is in vienna for negotiations on iran and i am therefore pleased to speak on behalf of the council on this subject. the destruction of syria's chemical weapons stockpile has already produced results. results that have been materialized in the removal of chemical weapons components from syria. we, as the presidency of the european union, are speaking for information only, because the union has contributed at budgetary level, but this is an operation carried out by 28 european states, which are also members of the european union, and not, as regards the majority of decisions on operations, by the european union as such. but it is certainly very important to discuss and inform you this evening on this subject. it is certainly important also because it is a fundamental objective to ensure security in our neighbourhood as the european union. the plan for the destruction of the syrian chemical weapons we are talking about was designed, it was intended, it was outlined under the control of the organization for the prohibition of chemical weapons and the united nations and the world health organization and the united nations environment programme also contributed to the operation. of course, in this organization the 28 member states of the european union have actively participated in the decisions of the operations. joint planning by the organization for the prohibition of chemical weapons and the united nations concluded that hydrolysis of the chemical weapons aboard the american ship cape ray was the best solution under the circumstances. the american ship is simply used as a platform, where the hydrolysis operations have to take place. it is a process that basically consists of dissolving chemical components through various salts, and it is a method that has been used by the united states for many years to destroy its stockpiles of chemical weapons. the planning was made public, as were the decisions of the organisation for the prohibition of chemical weapons through its executive committee. a mission between the opcw and the united nations also organised two major briefing events, one on board the cape ray ship, to explain to leading environmental ngos and the international media how the operations to remove first syria's chemical weapons and then destroy them were conducted in full compliance with national laws and international regulations. it's a process that has been used successfully in the case of libya before. all measures taken by the two organisations to ensure the safety of operations and to ensure environmental safety were also indicated. the european union, for its part, is aware of the international importance of this effort. it has been at the forefront of this operation from the very beginning, as far as it could contribute, and did so in the initial stages through a contribution of eur 5 million to start the activities of the joint mission and later also contributed to the special trust fund of the organisation for the prohibition of chemical weapons with another eur 12 million, precisely intended to finance the destruction of weapons. these are the only contributions legally made by the european union as such. of course, many other member states of the european union have also made important financial contributions and also important contributions in kind, which i would like to mention. the presidency of the council would like to express its particular appreciation to denmark, which together with norway has contributed commercial vessels to the operations, and also to denmark and the united kingdom for also having provided the military supplies needed for the arms-removal operations. italy has made the port of gioia tauro available for the transport of a part, the most important part of these chemicals, the so-called 'priority 1's, on board the american ship cape ray. this was an essential part of the destruction process. three other member states finland, germany and the united kingdom have also confirmed that they are willing and able to contribute to the destruction of further chemical weapons by making their civilian facilities available. we also want to express our thanks and appreciation to the director-general of the organisation for the prohibition of chemical weapons and the united nations special coordinator and their teams for the truly outstanding work and commitment they have shown throughout this operation. we believe it was only natural that the organisation for the prohibition of chemical weapons should receive the nobel peace prize in 2013 precisely for its contribution to this operation and to world peace and security. the operations will soon be completed and so the member states of the union and also, at least in part, the union itself will have made an important and practical contribution to reducing some of the suffering in syria and to contributing to a potential peace on which we certainly still have a great deal to do in the days and weeks ahead.

member of the commission. - mr president, honourable members, i would like to thank everyone who contributed to this discussion and especially those who were speaking for the first time in this house. because the time is short and the discussion itself was quite long, i will try to be brief but also concrete. i agree with everyone who stressed that the european union needs to do more for economic growth and job creation overall, not only focusing on the young generation but on the entire labour market. however, we have reasons, strong reasons, to develop measures and reforms targeted at the young generation, improving school-to-work transitions in the european union, because young people have been disproportionately hit by the consequences of the financial and economic crisis, and as is well known the youth unemployment rate is more than twice as high as the overall unemployment rate in the european union. but our starting point is that europe indeed is quite diverse. it is also very imbalanced. there are some countries which have been performing quite well and we have to help others learn from the good performers – this expression has been used widely in this discussion, including by mr arnott. indeed the good examples of austria, germany and other countries where there is not such a great gap between the overall unemployment level and the youth unemployment rate need to be studied and if possible taken over. this applies to the various forms of dual training, apprenticeship models, but also how the public employment services function in these countries, and i strongly believe that good social dialogue and social partnership also contribute to finding the right solutions and the right ways forward. the youth guarantee is not a one-size-fits-all policy. the eu agreed on some key principles and parameters which can be delivered if the financial backing is also provided. but the member states themselves are developing their own national youth guarantee schemes in close cooperation with the commission, and also paying attention to each other. questions have been raised concerning specific countries, such as spain or italy where the situation is indeed much more serious than in some other cases. the commission is paying close attention to these countries. i myself before the end of this week will be going to italy to attend the informal council and next week once more to spain, and these missions allow for comparing notes with the governments about progress with the implementation of the youth guarantee. this implementation does not entirely depend on the eur 6 billion financial instrument, because this is a top-up fund to supplement the european social fund resources and the national resources that also have to be used. almost all countries are still spending the esf allocations of the previous period that ended last december. so because of the financial factor there are no delays. in fact those who have any kind of questions were given a good explanation of how to use these financial resources in march, which all the ministers received, and some countries take advantage of the european investment bank bridging finance facility to accelerate funding to youth-related measures. this is of course not sufficient if we look at the very severe imbalances inside the eurozone. i agree with those who stressed that there is indeed a link between the emu imbalances, and that is why we do not just have to monitor these imbalances through a scoreboard which includes youth unemployment and inactivity, but also to continue working on emu reform and consider options for counter-cyclical fiscal capacity. this is what the council will also discuss later this week in an informal setting in milan – what options exist. the age limit has been discussed. member states – and this needs to be known – member states are allowed to go to 30 years if they opt for this. however, the commission has been encouraging all these member states first of all to focus on the generational cohorts under 25, to introduce the measures – very important reform measures – to support and improve school-to-work transitions, whether on the education and training side or on the labour market side. and once this is successful for under-25s obviously there should be no reason to refrain from going to a higher age bracket. this is not only a supply-side question – this is my answer to mr schwab. skills are very important. supply-side measures are important but the youth guarantee also has to be able to intervene on the side of the demand for labour and supplement the missing demand in many cases, especially at a time of recession. the commission has been working very closely with the member states and also checking how the funds are used and how the reforms are prepared. it is not only a matter of personal visits which i made in pilot cases in the city of évora in portugal, or ballymun in ireland, or the extremadura region in spain where there is a regional youth guarantee scheme already in place. we also use the european semester to assess and provide feedback to the member states and we cooperate with the ilo and the oecd which are also involved in technical advice. it is true that the turin meeting of heads of state and government has been postponed but the italian presidency keeps youth employment and the youth guarantee among its priorities and the attention of the heads of state and government remains very important. so the youth guarantee is a major flagship initiative. the commission is working with the member states and other stakeholders to implement it, but this is of course not a substitute for the right macroeconomic policies or industrial policies which will help generate economic growth and jobs in the eu.

in writing. the 'youth guarantee' introduced by the european parliament is certainly an important step forward in the fight against youth unemployment, but it is aimed at unemployed young people under the age of 25. as an italian mep i cannot help but point out the terrible emergency my country is experiencing with regard to unemployment among young people up to 30 years of age and even beyond. but not only in italy, there are about 6.8 million young people aged 25 to 30 who are not in employment, education or training in europe. it is clear that the solution to the problem of unemployment cannot come from the 'youth guarantee' alone. the member states must take steps to reduce their own bureaucracy, which prevents the creativity of selfemployed workers and small and mediumsized enterprises from growing and developing. tax policy must be lightened. young people must be able to lead a life of dignity and autonomy, with work that provides them with stability and security, a decent wage and social protection. only then will they be able to leave the family of origin, which is now the last and only support for unemployed young people.
in writing. unemployment in europe is a major concern for most eu governments. it is not only very "heavy" from a social and economic point of view, but also frustrating and demeaning in that it places people in a position of inferiority and unfitness. the dramatic nature of the situation is shown by the figures repeatedly cited in the debate, in particular those relating to youth unemployment, which is 23% in europe and 43% in italy. three points to consider: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. at the moment, the recovery of youth unemployment seems far off. investment in schools, vocational training, universities and research is needed to facilitate the meeting of demand and supply of labour, particularly where innovation is required and, at the same time, dropout and absenteeism are to be tackled more effectively. if unemployment creates poverty and poverty is no longer a temporary and cyclical phenomenon, social inequalities will widen and the fundamental rights of citizens will be undermined, with the result that structural changes will take hold. this requires major political choices and the mobilization of all cultural, social and business forces.

in writing. - in its resolution adopted today, parliament voted in favour of lithuania joining the euro area on 1 january 2015. i welcomed the fact that lithuania fulfilled all the euro eligibility criteria: the recent average annual inflation of 0,6% (well below the reference value of 1,7%); a government deficit of 2,1% of gdp in 2013 (reference value of 3%) and a gross debt ratio of 39,4% of gdp (well below the 60% reference value). all this shows that intensive work has been carried out by lithuania since 2006. lithuania is about to become the 19th member of the euro area, following latvia (2014), estonia (2011), slovakia (2009), cyprus and malta (2008), slovenia (2007), greece (2001), and belgium, germany, france, ireland, spain, italy, luxembourg, the netherlands, austria, portugal and finland (1999). welcome to the euro area, lithuania!

member of the commission. - mr president, some members have asked how we reached this situation. i think the reason for today’s situation is clear: starting from a few years ago, it is a result of budgetary negotiations which provided payment appropriations at such an artificially low level, so low that it prevented us from being able to pay legitimate bills. this must be stopped and it can be stopped, provided that the commission proposals for the draft amending budget for 2014 and the draft budget for 2015 are adopted by the budgetary authority as proposed. what the commission asked for is observance of the agreement on the multiannual financial framework. that means the possibility to use payment appropriations at the level of agreed ceilings, and the possibility to make full use of flexibility mechanisms. if we do not stabilise the situation now in 2014 and 2015, then it is indeed going to be difficult to have a sustainable budget in later years. we cannot afford to kick the can down the road again and again. we cannot accumulate unpaid bills. this is why the commission proposed the three draft amending budgets for 2014, including a contingency margin, and a draft budget for 2015 at the ceiling level. this is the call for today: to stop the snowball effect. the commission is indeed concerned by the position that the council is taking in relation to payments, but it hopes that negotiations will allow for common ground to be found, to provide the financial means to fulfil the union’s legal obligations in 2014 and 2015. the commission will continue to monitor closely the overall situation, and budget implementation, and will provide all necessary information to parliament and the council. it stands, of course, ready to participate actively in any interinstitutional meeting to take stock with a view to addressing outstanding needs. the commission counts on the commitment of both the council and parliament to work constructively in a continuing dialogue on payments, with the objectives of addressing the 2014 payment shortages and avoiding the recurrence of artificial under-budgeting in 2015 and the following years. this is necessary. otherwise, we put the credibility of the eu at risk, and we have to avoid that.
president of the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i have listened carefully to your speeches and i hope that a solution can be found, as the italian presidency intends, without polarizing positions. we are not discussing whether the expenditure that has been planned is appropriate or not, and of course it has a legal basis, we are discussing how to avoid a phenomenon which is true in our country and which we have been trying to solve for some years, namely the problem of late payments. as i said in my introductory remarks, this is a different approach to the management of the annual budget. the creation of margins below the budgetary ceilings does not mean that we are trying to avoid the related expenditure. i agree with the commissioner that the new multiannual financial framework gives us room for manoeuvre and the tools to deal with unforeseen needs. however, these must be managed in such a way that the request for payment appropriations does not conflict with our excessive deficit procedures and the related constraints. we have also made proposals in this connection. the council is committed to achieving all the policy objectives linked to the old and new programmes of the multiannual financial framework. this commitment includes the objective of reducing the famous avalanche effect, which was also referred to in this debate, and of providing the financial resources needed to pay our bills. in this context, we will start examining draft amending budgets 3 and 4 as soon as possible, after adoption of the council's position on the draft budget for 2015. the italian presidency welcomes the invitation that has been made to start these new five years with a new spirit, also in relation to the subject we have dealt with today. thank you for your attention.

the agenda includes the discussion of the statement by the vice-president of the commission and high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the situation in iraq (2014/2716 ((rsp)).
acting president of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission and high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the situation in iraq - as is well known - is very serious. the conclusions of the june foreign affairs council expressed the european union's deep concern, condemning the attacks perpetrated by the islamic state of iraq and the levant (isil). a sunni insurgency has erupted in iraq, led not only by isil but also by several other sunni armed groups, including neo-ba'athists and tribal groups. isil, along with armed militants, now poses a more immediate threat in iraq than in syria. this organization, with its growing number of foreign fighters, is a real danger to iraq's neighbours, such as lebanon and jordan, and also to the european union. the current deterioration of the security situation in iraq is due to both internal and external factors. the crisis in syria has undoubtedly allowed isil to gain a foothold in the region and a starting point for the creation of the so-called "islamic state" in syrian and iraqi territory. however, the causes of the recent insurgency are not limited to the expression of a terrorist ideology. the motives of most of the armed militants are to be found in the discontent of the sunni community with the shiite-dominated iraqi government for over a decade. among the reasons for discontent are the iraqi government's arbitrary application of "deba'tization" policies, its inaction in providing for the basic needs of sunni communities and the human rights violations perpetrated by the security forces. we have seen these problems escalate this year in the cities of fallujah and ramadi in anbar province, where protests by local sunni populations against government policies have led to violent clashes between iraqi shiite-dominated security forces and local tribes. this situation provided an opportunity for isil to establish a foothold in the territory, as demonstrated by the full-scale offensive conducted in iraqi territory in june. the speed and effectiveness of that offensive, however, took the international community completely by surprise. all political and religious leaders in iraq share the responsibility to address the root causes of these tensions. the iraqi government in particular is called upon to play a moderating role, avoiding excesses in both rhetoric and action. the humanitarian implications of the security situation are a tragic corollary. today, a total of two million iraqis have been forced to flee their homes. the european union is gravely concerned about the evolution of this humanitarian crisis and the massive internal exodus of civilians fleeing the fighting. the european commission, through echo, has so far allocated eur 12 million for humanitarian assistance. this is money for syrian refugees and for iraqi nationals who are internally displaced. the european union is also coordinating its actions with additional donors and international agencies and i would like to commend the efforts of the european union services and international agencies in the very difficult local circumstances of the dispersion of displaced persons throughout iraq. the eu is constantly keeping up to date with the situation, adapting its relief operations to developments on the ground. another consequence of the terrible crisis affecting iraqi territory is the kurdistan region. in recent weeks iraqi kurdistan has unilaterally announced its intention to hold a referendum on independence in the autumn. let me stress that iraqi kurdistan is a model of stability throughout the region and has been an essential interlocutor of international actors, particularly in response to the humanitarian situation in iraq. this cooperation deserves to be rewarded. however, we believe that unilateral moves towards independence will not help to overcome the situation in iraq and may risk being a problem for kurdistan itself. we have called on all parties concerned to seek the solution of this and other disputes in the iraqi constitution, which, if fully implemented, can provide answers to many of the kurdish demands. the transition in iraq, which began more than a decade ago and has always enjoyed the support of the european union, is a difficult process. despite many setbacks over the years and although the prospects of iraq finally being put on a path to peace and stability are threatened today, there have also been positive signs recently. the april 30 elections saw a turnout of 60% of eligible voters, despite the difficult security conditions. the european union sent an electoral expert mission to iraq to monitor the electoral process and report on its findings. the experts concluded that despite some problems, which should not be hidden, in particular the exclusion of a significant number of sunni voters in anbar province due to violence, the elections were conducted satisfactorily. the turnout in these elections, which took place a few weeks before the sunni insurrection, demonstrates the commitment of the iraqi people to democracy and the unity of iraq. beyond security, the most immediate challenge in iraq today is the ability of moderate political leaders to drive the political process. that's the message we've been sending to those leaders over the last few weeks. the rapid formation of a new government following the legislative elections on 30 april is a matter of priority. the appointment of the new president of the council of representatives yesterday, 15 july, was a step in the right direction. now a president of the republic must be appointed, so that a prime minister can be appointed and a government formed. the new government will have to seek dialogue with all the communities that make up iraq, including the sunni community currently excluded from the national political process that triggered the insurgency. without an inclusive approach and effective dialogue, iraqi society will not move forward on the path of reconciliation. as the high representative/vice-president catherine ashton has repeatedly stressed, the way out of the iraq crisis must first be a political solution, which must also lay the foundations for a security response. instead, it is very likely that overly harsh security measures will fuel sectarian discord and cause further suffering to the iraqi people. the european union stands ready to take any action it deems appropriate to facilitate political dialogue, in addition to the actions undertaken by our international partners. despite the gravity of the situation on the ground, the european union continues to provide assistance and support to iraq wherever possible, in particular in the planning and implementation of development assistance. this is a sign of the european union's continued commitment to iraq and is part of a set of actions to make iraq more stable by promoting governance capacity and supporting the delivery of basic services. such assistance shall include further support for measures to promote the rule of law to follow up the work of eujust lex. in the light of the new security situation in iraq, eu experts are also considering possible ways of supporting counter-terrorism operations. however, the fight against terrorism in iraq must respect the principles of human rights and international humanitarian law. the european union rejects the view that violations of human rights are an unavoidable or necessary price for security. the european union also works to promote cooperation between member states on the issue of foreign fighters, at their own request. finally, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the eu remains committed to the partnership and cooperation agreement with iraq and will continue to encourage such cooperation. in this connection, i take this opportunity to call on those member states which have not yet done so to complete the ratification process of the agreement as soon as possible. thank you for your attention.

i think it is perhaps appropriate to give a political dimension to this debate. mr della vedova reminded us that tomorrow is world day of international criminal justice. i believe that it is a symbolic day, which marks the anniversary of the adoption of the rome statute, the treaty which essentially established the international criminal court. i think it is also a day imagined as a moment to reflect and act on the suffering of those who are still victims of atrocities, genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression of one state against another, but also to spread the fight against impunity for these crimes and celebrate the progress in the field of international criminal justice. i think that kampala was a historic conference. the revision of the rome statute has opened a new road and we must be able to follow it all the way. at this conference, the member countries of the international criminal court, after nearly a decade of discussions, reached agreement on the shared definition of the "crime of aggression" as an offence of state, a source of disagreement in international law for years. after numerous reviews and high-level meetings, a great deal of progress has been made. but there is still a lot to be done, because the dramatic events in the international context of recent times - i am thinking of ukraine, as well as the debate we recently had on the israeli and palestinian issues - demonstrate with great force that much remains to be done in the area of the effectiveness of international criminal law. it was noted that several countries had already ratified the kampala amendments and that many had started their national procedures. although these are long and complex, i believe it is vital that a positive outcome is found as soon as possible. we now feel it is our duty to recall the historical importance of this compromise, and to re-launch european and international attention to the crime of aggression as an offence and to the kampala compromise, which defines it and provides for the jurisdiction of the international criminal court over this crime. the time has come to work with one voice to push for ratification by those states which have not yet done so. although the european union is not an integral part of the statute, we need to bring this important issue back into the political dimension.

on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we have seen that the value of agri-food products affected by the russian embargo is estimated by the european commission at five billion euros and affects the income of nine and a half million european producers, which is nine and a half million households. unfortunately, this assessment is optimistic. for italy alone, the figure of eur 160 million is less than the eur 200 million calculated by the trade associations. optimistic assessment because indirect consequences such as the one on triangular trade, which concerns european products sold to russia first via third countries, are not considered. optimistic assessment because it does not consider the loss of market shares in the long term, because the russian consumer could get used to other tastes and no longer take european products. optimistic assessment because imbalances in the internal market are not taken into account, due to the introduction of low-cost products which, if they no longer find an outlet on the russian market, will be dumped on the european market. it is therefore very likely that the aid granted, which is already below the level of needs, will not be sufficient. the five star movement calls on the european commission to ensure that the next steps are more carefully allocated and to work towards finally building a genuine harmonized european single market capable of absorbing shocks and emergencies, and managing internal trade flows in a forward-looking manner. either we all work together to create a true european system, or it means that if only emergencies dictate the guidelines, we can say that the european institutions are failing in their task.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the russian crisis is threatening the european agri-food sector in a dramatic way. the figures for eu exports to russia are impressive, but equally impressive are the negative effects of this embargo, both in terms of the losses already suffered by the sector and in closing the growth prospects so necessary for the revival of the agri-food sector. it is therefore clear that urgent incentive measures must be identified, particularly in the fruit and vegetables, milk and meat sectors, so that the companies in these sectors can recover from the effects of a political crisis and be helped to identify other markets for their products, and that action must be taken to change rapidly the methods of applying and distributing aid already granted between the various countries. i think that we must work to ensure that targeted compensation is provided, and, once the european commission has checked the budgetary availability, i hope that extraordinary measures will be adopted, as well as measures to advance the payment of cap funds to farmers, as already suggested by the minister for agriculture, maurizio martina. the commissioner cioloș's comments are certainly very welcome, but they are not enough. what i am asking for, however, is the timeliness of the european union's action. european farmers cannot wait, not least because, as they say in my area, while the doctor is studying, the patient is in danger of dying.
the russian embargo has blocked food imports from the united states, the european union, canada, australia and norway for 12 months. the risk is that we will bring our sectors, already battered by the crisis, to their knees. the value of agri-food products affected by the embargo is estimated by the european commission at eur 5 billion, affecting the income of 9 million europeans. these figures are quite optimistic as they do not take into account a number of factors such as triangular trade, long-term market loss and imbalances in the internal market. the aid granted will therefore not be sufficient. the european union must allocate resources more carefully and work to build a genuine harmonized european single market, able to absorb shocks and emergencies, by managing internal trade flows in a forward-looking way.
in writing. russia accounts for about 10% of the european union's agricultural exports, worth €12 billion a year, and has been banning imports of a number of agri-food products for more than a month. we would like to reassure our producers by asking the european commission what measures it intends to take both in the short term to mitigate the damage to the european agricultural sector and in the longer term to remedy this situation so that it is not the producers and small and mediumsized enterprises in the sector who bear the cost. it seems that russia is organizing itself, both by increasing its domestic production and by finding alternative trading partners, to no longer be dependent on european imports: it is therefore necessary to find a solution which will enable us to pursue our foreign policy without damaging our trade policy.
