member of the commission. - mr president, although there was a discussion on the political aspects of the relationship between ourselves and ukraine and the interference of russia, a lot of questions have been put about the dcfta and, more precisely, the agreements or proposal for an agreement on friday with respect to delaying the provisional application. what is it really about? it is a process; and i have to say that i am very surprised that you are surprised about this process, because it started on 11 july when there was a first trilateral meeting, asked for not by us but by the two other parties concerned, and the russians put on the table a number of remarks and questions and observations with respect to the dcfta. that resulted in technical consultations over the month of august, with the agreement to meet again on 12 september at ministerial level. then there was the summit meeting in minsk on 26 august, where catherine ashton, günther oettinger and myself represented the european commission. explicit reference was made to the meeting on 12 september and president poroshenko even said that he was going to postpone the ratification until that very date. that is why we met, mr auštrevičius, to make possible the ratification of this agreement by ukraine. that is why we have been doing this and when you look closely at the agreement that we reached on friday, what does it really say? on the one hand, it says that we are going to prolong the autonomous trade measures, which means that the advantages that we grant to ukraine can continue. i think this is very important, because what you really need in ukraine is economic growth and development. that is what you really need. if you want to find a lasting peace there, that is what you need. if you want to strengthen the position of the ukrainian people that is what you need, economic growth, and we continue that. on the other hand, the russians have been asking to cut out 2 400 lines from the agreement, that is about one fourth of the agreement on the tariffs. they are claiming that the technical barriers to trade are disadvantageous to them and they say that sps cannot go ahead as it stands at this moment in time. solutions exist for the sps, because we could very well have an equivalence on the ukrainian market between sps in russia – gost rules – and our own rules. you could have that. for technical barriers to date, it is a programme that still has to be put into practice. and the 2 400 tariff lines: yes, of course, if you make a dcfta that gives an advantage with respect to tariffs. but we are ready to do exactly the same with russia! we have been insisting with russia for years, about having a dcfta with them! it is not that we are doing anything against them, but that is what they want to do. to find the solution for that, we have postponed the provisional application for one year, leaving open the possibility for either party – either party meaning ukraine or the european union – to put possible changes on the table. just putting them on the table, you know: we have not agreed to any change. and, by the way, we could not do that. the only ones who could do that, honourable members, once you have ratified the agreement, is you; because it would mean that you would have to change the treaty with ukraine before you can change anything in it. i do not have the feeling that parliament is really ready to do that. so what we have been doing is creating the conditions for ratifying today. that is what we need today. once this ratification happens, this is a new fact. it is not only a political fact, it is a legal fact, it is a judicial fact. it means that you have an agreement, that you have a treaty, and that you can only change it by a new treaty. i have always understood that that is what you wanted, which is why i do not understand the remarks you have been making today. if you really want to put yourself in a difficult position with russia, if you really want to give them the upper hand, then you have to follow the line you have been voicing here, that this is a bad agreement, that in fact we should delay ratification of the agreement. allow me to say that to do so would be a historical mistake. what we have been doing is creating the conditions for ratification of this very, very important treaty. that does not concern only ukraine: it concerns the whole eastern neighbourhood. it is about whether or not we are in a position to continue this policy and make it a success.
, member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/ high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. - mr president, honourable members, there was a lot of wisdom, as always, during this debate – though rather more populist slogans than i have been used to hearing over the past five years, and some outrageous remarks too, from your side, such as the implication that the nationalities of our heads of delegation in our partner countries determine the policy of the european union. what a nonsense! i would like to make four points. the first, in response to your request that we should learn more about russia, is that we understand russia. the 1975 helsinki act clearly stipulates that borders may not be changed through military force. under the 1990 paris charter, it is reiterated that ‘within the framework of international law, all the participating states have equal rights and duties. they will respect each other’s right to define and conduct ... its relations with other states in accordance with international law and in the spirit of the present declaration’. the budapest memorandum of 1994 guarantees the ukrainians total integrity and sovereignty. all of that was violated and destroyed by one european country. in 2008, in the context of the nato-russia council in bucharest, vladimir putin said that ukraine was an artificial country – yet someone here is blaming eu policy for the problems there! i cannot follow that logic. my second point is in response to the call i heard for us to ‘grow up’ and to recognise a real threat. what is a real threat? i always thought it was when someone starts to violate the rule of law and international law, because those are the bases of our wellbeing. we have agreed that our commitments to law and to order will determine not only the way we treat each other but also how we treat our neighbours. this is predominantly what we base our security on. by the way, catherine ashton is not here not because she wants to avoid a debate with the european parliament but because she is also dealing with russian diplomats on the very complex iranian issue. she is doing everything possible to prevent the iranian issue becoming a hot topic for debate here. and she is moving in the right direction, in part thanks to constructive cooperation with the russian diplomats. so our insistence on russia living up to its commitments vis-à-vis international law and the rule of law does not prevent us from working with russians on other important hot topics around the world. my third point concerns self-deception. the problem is that the same people who have always called for us to respect the sovereignty of third countries’ decisions are now questioning our own policy, which is based on that. the thing which needs to be very clearly underlined is that there has been a ukrainian request to postpone the provisional application of the economic part of the association agreement – and that was also underlined in the discussion that president barroso had with president poroshenko and prime minister yatsenyuk. the reasoning was logical and understandable. the economy and financial system of ukraine face a huge test because of the events in the east, not to mention the impact of the illegal annexation of crimea. they expressed the wish to have more time to prepare the commitment of ukrainians to the text being negotiated. another thing needs to be underlined to which no one has really referred, and to all of you who spoke in favour of peace prevailing, i would like to make this point clear. the russians have their troops on ukrainian territory and they have also made it absolutely clear, repeatedly, on the record, that once the association agreement is ratified by the verkhovna rada, on that very day – rather than later when they might face economic or trade difficulties, although we do not share that opinion – they will not only repeal the commonwealth of independent states free trade agreement with ukraine, but will also adopt further restrictive economic measures against it. so, in addition to the military threat and possible escalation, we have also been facing the threat of a full-scale economic and trade war. we have the ratification of the agreement which, as described by my colleague, has been negotiated over four years. we will have the provisional application of the political part. we will have the continuation of reforms, because we asked that question and, in the discussion that president barroso had with prime minister yatsenyuk on saturday, we agreed on a number of elements: we will go ahead with the structure provided for in the association agreement; we will have the association council, the committee and various subcommittees; and we will start our work. the european agenda for reform, as agreed with the ukrainians, is very much about the implementation of the association agreement and it will go ahead. implementation of the action plan, which was also adopted today by the verkhovna rada, operationalising the association agreement, goes ahead. our preparations for the donors’ conference at the end of this year – to focus both on the implementation of the association agreement and on the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the east of ukraine – go ahead. the mandate and focus of the ukrainian support group, which has started its work already, remain the same, and the coordination mechanism provided for by the ukrainians for the implementation of the association agreement will go ahead. there is no a delay as a result of russian blackmail. now, the last point: a number of you spoke of dividing lines – we are being accused of creating dividing lines through the association agreement – and i believe the time has come to prove that the association agreement is actually one of the building components of what could, in future, be a european economic free very soon armenia too, will have their views on the association agreement with ukraine and its impact on those countries; it means that they too will have views on cooperation with the european union. not only do we all stand to benefit, but we will be able to eliminate the danger of creating a dividing line if we start to work together, because if we missed this aspect, thus undermining the importance of the regulatory framework, then by just ignoring the eurasian union we would be the ones contributing to the new dividing line in europe. i believe the agreement should be a part of this much bigger picture, in which all these important initiatives and steps are being put together.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the request, the ninth in the framework of the 2014 budget, for the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for a total amount of eur 700 000 for spain. the request was made by spain following redundancies in three woodworking enterprises in the region of castilla y leon. this excess may be linked to significant changes in the structure of world trade in woodwork and carpentry for construction.
in writing. - i strongly support the mobilisation of the globalisation adjustment fund in favour of certain spanish companies in the wood and cork industries and i welcome the commission's proposal to allocate eur 700 000 to help them. it is not at all pleasant to note that 587 workers have lost their jobs as a result of the sharp drop in the volume of exports of woodwork and carpentry for construction in europe. of course, at the moment we need to provide timely assistance to workers and also to businesses, but in the coming period we will also have to think about how to revive the timber market and the employment rate in spain, as well as in europe.
in writing. - i can only vote in favour of the egf following the redundancy of 587 workers in the wood and cork industries in the nuts ii region of castilla y león in spain. in this same area, the unemployment rate increased from 8,2% in the first quarter of 2008 to 22,70% in the first quarter of 2013 and the employment situation in the region concerned is particularly fragile due to the extremely low population density, as in the province of soria, and the high dependence on the wood sector, which due to such a population density leads to redundancies that also have a serious impact on the local economy.
in writing. - the measure covers 587 construction workers and amounts to € 700 000. my vote will be in favour of helping these workers, families and businesses in dire need.
in writing. - today we voted on five more requests to mobilise the globalisation adjustment fund. the one by mr esteban gonzález pons concerned the reintegration into the labour market of redundant workers in three enterprises operating in nace rev. 2 division 16 (wood and wood and cork products, except furniture; manufacture of straw and plaiting materials) in the region of castilla y león. these are concrete signals that the european parliament is sending to workers and businesses in difficulty because of the economic crisis.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the ebola virus epidemic in north africa is having a very serious impact on health and a very high cost in terms of human lives. more than 2,500 people have died and some 5,000 have been infected, but the african countries most affected by the virus have not yet received adequate attention and concrete interventions. the easily influenced western world has been enormously alarmed and rightly mobilized whenever a western contagion has occurred, but the same emotions, the same pathos, the same apprehension have not been expressed in the face of the hundreds of victims in africa, which generally comes back to interest when it comes to exploiting its resources. i've heard a lot about blending. what better opportunity than an emergency such as the one caused by the ebola virus to actually start holding accountable those multinational corporations that are making huge profits from the resources of the most affected countries? ebola is not just a health and humanitarian emergency, it is not just death and fear of contagion, it is also a social and political problem and it has a disastrous economic effect. the fao has recently announced the enormous risk to crops in west africa. the secondary effects of this crisis are becoming more and more evident. food insecurity is worsening the already fragile economies of these countries, which are now facing the imminent collapse of exports. the challenges for europe are immense. local institutions are very weak, public health systems ineffective, inconsistent, even in some cases non-existent. there is no basic infrastructure, no roads, no infrastructure to deal with the emergency. there is a distorted view of the disease among local communities because of the very low literacy rate that facilitates the spread of the virus. there are endless ethnic, political, religious divisions that spill blood on the territories and make only the merchants of death smile. my question, ladies and gentlemen, is this: europe is ready to take up this enormous challenge, and if so, how?
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are talking about thousands of deaths and europe is waking up again at the last moment, with a half-empty house. we are talking about a virus that has an incubation period of two to 21 days and we are talking about a moment when, with a dementia operation called mare nostrum, thousands of people are arriving in italy every day, even from countries where the virus is killing - i think nigeria, i think senegal and i think liberia. so, apart from the fact that obviously the more money is spent, the sooner we intervene in those countries, the better it is for everyone, especially for those who have no place in the italian and european news. but i ask myself and i ask you: if some countries in the world like south korea or saudi arabia are even thinking about closing their borders to immigrants from high-risk areas, what are we doing other than going to save those lives there, which is right and why are we already late, to avoid problems here? and i wonder, and i ask you, whether europe can still turn a blind eye to the arrival of thousands of people who, beyond the ebola virus, can, indeed are carriers - these are the figures from italian hospitals - of tuberculosis and scabies, which, however, do not stop in italy, i say to my european colleagues who do not care. the problem is not only italian, it is european, so i ask you if it makes sense to continue to go and collect these people in the middle of the sea without any kind of control, guarantee or even if the money we are throwing away for mare nostrum would not be better spent in africa, in north africa to avoid these people from death journeys and to avoid us and our children from possible and possible contagion.

author of the book. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, nelson mandela is a symbol of redemption for the whole of the african continent and beyond. pierre claver mbonimpa, like mandela, is a symbol of freedom, of struggle, of justice for a continent which is unfortunately still in the grip of corrupt leaders and local potentates who exploit the territory for their own personal enrichment. in burundi, for mbonimpa, history is repeating itself. exactly 20 years after his arrest and torture in prison, the journalist and human rights defender returned to his cell on 15 may. his fault? persevere in defending freedom of expression, a freedom that should be sacred. mbonimpa is a brave man. he defied the power and paid the price, and yet he decided to defy it again. his arrest is a political matter: there will be elections in burundi in 2015 and the current government seems intent on maintaining power by any means repressive and violent. his health condition has now deteriorated and he has been transferred under surveillance to the hospital. we call on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the situation in the former yugoslavia is resolved. the european parliament must condemn this new and unjustified detention of mbonimpa and use all diplomatic means to convince the local authorities to stop the use of violence against all civilians peacefully demonstrating in burundi for his release. fifty-two people are currently being held without due process in the country's prisons. we are helping the healthy civil society in burundi to change the course of history in that country.
the tragic situation in burundi requires europe to take a strong stand in its role as a global actor in defence of the rule of law and fundamental freedoms. the deprivation of liberty of a human rights defender, pierre mbonimpa, is an attack on the democracy of this country, which unfortunately still shows all the fragility that led it to a decade of civil war and to a tragic death toll of 300 000 people. we do not want to stand by and watch another genocide in central africa. the level of alert is high, especially in view of the upcoming elections, which must take place in a democratic and inclusive atmosphere, with the participation of the opposition. without full respect for the will of the people and their rights, the country risks being relegated to its own conditions of underdevelopment, with dramatic repercussions on the lives of hundreds of thousands of people. it needs a strong signal of hope, strength and courage for those who defend freedom and democracy. pierre mbonimpa must be released immediately.

in writing. - since the beginning of the ebola outbreak in africa, i have been campaigning for eu intervention to stem the spread of the virus. the resolution we are voting on, albeit belatedly, calls for more decisive action by europe with development policies aimed at greater prevention, improvement of medical and social infrastructure in africa and coordination of existing interventions to maximise results, and for all these reasons i voted in favour of it.

in writing. - the ebola virus epidemic, which broke out in west africa, has been underestimated by the international community and is now a challenge to global security. the countries affected are confronted with socioeconomic collapse. i voted in favour of this resolution to call for more resources and operational capacity, including qualified human resources and logistical equipment. i call on the member states to coordinate flights and establish dedicated air bridges and i invite the european commission to develop a needs assessment and specific plans for each affected country in order to determine and coordinate the request and the related deployment of medical personnel, mobile laboratories, protective clothing and treatment centres. in addition, the african union should be encouraged to consider a comprehensive plan of action, as the crisis has become complex and with political implications. as regards medical research, i would stress the importance of advancing clinical trials of proven treatments for the ebola virus.
in writing. - the ebola virus has already killed over 2,000 people in west africa and according to the world health organization, the contagion could spread to 20,000 people in the next 3 months. ngos such as médecins sans frontières have raised alarm about the inadequacy of the international community's response to the spread of the contagion (which has already affected, in addition to guinea, 4 other african states). europe must equip itself to prevent the spread of the virus within its borders and we therefore urge the commission to provide more funding for the affected areas but also to intensify its efforts to protect our southern borders by strengthening rescue operations and medical assistance for migrants. the institutions of the 28 member states must recognise that ebola is a global problem and requires a globally coordinated response. we also want to stress the need for a collective effort, not just an italian one, to provide relief to the tens of thousands of desperate people trying to cross to the schengen countries.
in writing. - this resolution is not just a dutiful signal of attention to what the who has called a 'public health emergency of international concern', which may have been underestimated at first. it urges the relevant institutions to take specific actions to try to address the serious shortcomings identified by the ngos most active on the ground in all aspects of the response: - the possibility of using military and civilian defence resources under the guidance of the un secretary-general; - coordination by the european commission of the dispatch of medical personnel, mobile laboratories, equipment, protective clothing, treatment centres with isolation wards; - the introduction of control systems to prevent misuse of resources; - the establishment by states of air bridges dedicated to the transfer of personnel and equipment to the affected countries. the resolution also stresses the need for action beyond health, given the dramatic implications of the epidemic in all areas of social life (with 4.5 million children under the age of 5 living in the affected areas). the resolution as a whole is therefore particularly welcome and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - as has been sadly known since march, the ebola virus has claimed thousands of lives at an ever-increasing rate. although the european commission has recently stepped up immediate support to contain the crisis, humanitarian workers face increasingly difficult conditions on the ground. this is the largest epidemic ever recorded in terms of cases, casualties and geographical extent and, as stated by the who, the crisis is a public health emergency of international concern and therefore requires a coordinated international response. i think it is right that parliament should state in this resolution that the international community must play a more decisive role, and that the african countries must assume their share of responsibility, and that it should therefore call on the commission to intensify its efforts and coordinate its actions with international partners to combat the epidemic. as the text of the resolution states, the international community has underestimated the crisis and has been slow to develop a proper coordination strategy, and i agree with this and other points, and i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution calling for the urgent deployment of funding, medical personnel and equipment to the countries affected by the ebola epidemic. this is an emergency situation that should not be underestimated in any way, especially since even the who has said that the number of people affected could exceed 20,000 cases in the coming months, spreading rapidly in the west african region. even the ngos currently active in the field feel that international efforts are totally inadequate and lacking. therefore, a coordination mechanism with all member states, the united states and all other international partners needs to be activated as soon as possible in order to mobilise a medical response capable of developing clinical, epidemiological and diagnostic infrastructures, including surveillance infrastructures and training of local staff. there is no time to lose, global security is at stake and not just the health of african citizens.
in writing. - in west africa, the number of ebola patients and victims continues to rise. riots are occurring and the isolation centers are unable to cope with emergencies. health-care workers are among the first to be infected and have a frightening number of deaths. ebola treatment centers are reduced to places where you go to die alone, and where you're offered palliative care and little else. it's impossible to cope with the huge number of infected people who are pouring into health facilities. for the reasons stated and to ensure that all international plans to help the affected countries to put an end to the contagion are put into effect, i could not but vote in favour of this resolution.

member of the commission. - mr president, on behalf of the commission and commissioner georgieva, i would like to make the following statement. the recent heavy floods which have hit northern italy and claimed at least three lives, causing several million euros' worth of damage, show once again the importance of sustainable investment in better preparedness against disasters. i would like to focus on three main points. first of all, natural disasters have become more frequent and more intense over recent decades, not only globally but also in europe. urbanisation, population growth and environmental degradation have very much contributed to this trend. it is estimated that average annual losses over the last decade have risen to eur 200 billion, with floods accounting for 35% of all losses. if we take last year’s floods in central europe alone, these are estimated to have cost eur 17 billion, topping the list of the costliest natural disasters in 2013. this spring, the floods in serbia and bosnia-herzegovina, croatia and bulgaria also caused widespread devastation and left more than one hundred people dead and half a million people homeless. fortunately, the damage caused by the current floods in northern italy and southern france is not on the same scale, but still reflects the same trend. this brings me to my second point. what is the european union doing to better manage natural disasters? natural hazards such as floods cannot be prevented, but the number of lives they take and the damage they cause can be greatly reduced through better preparation and protection. another major benefit, investment in prevention, is cost-effective. on average, for instance, every euro spent on prevention saves between four and seven euros that would have been spent once a disaster has hit. so the commission is implementing the approach across various policy areas, including civil protection, the environment and also regional policy and research and development. the most visible piece of eu legislation relating to flood management is certainly the floods directive, which has been in force since 2007 and which establishes a framework for the assessment and management of flood risks. flood risk management plans focusing on prevention, protection and preparedness should set the objectives and include the measures to achieve flood risk reduction. thanks to the support of parliament, we also have a new mechanism for disaster-proofing the major infrastructure projects covered under the environmental impact assessment directive. there are also provisions to disaster-proof new investments funded by the eu’s structural funds. flood prevention is actually receiving the bulk of available regional policy funds earmarked for risk prevention. for instance, for the 2007-2013 period, funding made available to member states to invest in risk prevention, including against floods – so this is risk prevention in its entirety but it includes floods as well – in risk management and in climate change adaptation amounted to around eur 60.5 billion. now the first estimates for the new 2014-2020 period show that this sum would increase to eur 78 billion. related projects include maintaining or developing flood plains such as along the tisza river in hungary; cross-border and transnational cooperation on flood prevention; the deployment of early warning systems, as well as support to civil protection. a concrete example of support is the eu strategy for the danube region, supporting projects to develop a common risk assessment methodology for the region. we have also come a very long way in the area of civil protection, which showed its benefits also during the recent italian floods – more about this in a moment. and, as of this year, we have our new civil protection legislation in place, with a very strong focus on preparedness and prevention, building up a voluntary pool of disaster response capacities, better response planning, a training network and reinforced cooperation among authorities in the field of training and exercises. of course, these are the things which have already been done. what else can be done? as regards the floods in northern italy, since i was referring to the civil protection mechanism, i must say that the italian authorities saw no need to activate the eu civil protection mechanism, but on 16 october requested activation of the eu copernicus emergency mapping system. what else can be done? i think, in conclusion, we also need to engage more closely with industry. we need to put disaster management firmly on the agenda of eu finance ministers because it is cost-effective. by investing euros in prevention, we save much more when disasters actually happen. let me conclude by stressing that we are now equipped with the tools not to completely prevent, but to mitigate and manage disasters, including floods.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the ebola virus is spreading with alarming speed in the central african countries, claiming victims whose numbers seem to be growing exponentially. the rest of the world is rightly committed to preventing the spread of the deadly disease that the virus brings, but it must be taken seriously that the international response in the countries really affected by this plague has been extremely late. despite early warnings from ngos, particularly doctors without borders, international institutions have wasted precious time in curbing the spread and saving thousands of lives. the imperative now is to save lives in the hardest-hit countries and prevent the development of a pandemic, but a separate reflection deserves an aspect that has been little discussed, namely the possible causes of the resurgence of the viral attack. fruit bats belonging to the pteroptida family are known to be healthy carriers of the virus. these harmless mammals usually live in the less accessible parts of the forests, but their deadly host can easily be passed on to other animals that feed on fruits already bitten by bats or by the animals themselves. yet another cause of the rapid spread of the virus is: the massive deforestation. these animals, like those of many other species, are increasingly being driven near human settlements as their natural habitat is destroyed by human greed.

member of the commission. - madam president, honourable members, i believe the milan summit of heads of state and government was a step forward, compared to berlin and paris, because prime ministers and leaders of public employment services spoke in much more concrete terms about the youth guarantee and its implementation in their respective countries than in previous cases. indeed, there were reports about the progress being made and the commission also keeps reporting about the results of pilot projects, as well as the actual youth guarantee implementation, on its own website. ms paunova and others who were asking about this can find information about it on the dg employment website, and i have also been reporting regularly to this house about the progress made. the youth guarantee is, as you know, an eu-wide initiative, but it is not a uniform model. it is tailor-made. countries themselves were designing their own youth guarantee implementation plans according to common guidelines which were provided at eu level. this is something to be emphasised, because mr mureșan as well as mr arnott were asking about this aspect. certainly, the youth guarantee is tailor-made in the case of each and every eu member state. we took inspiration from the pioneers, austria and finland, inside the eu and all countries have to apply the common principles – the four-month deadline, for example, and the importance of quality jobs, apprenticeships, training or learning according to their own needs and capacity. we have to clarify in such a broad discussion what the youth guarantee actually is and what it is not. the youth guarantee is primarily about the school-to-work transition. it is about improving school and training performance; improving labour market performance and the connection between the two, because this is where many young people, including the so called neets, have been lost – and not only at the time of the crisis. we are not only responding to the crisis with the youth guarantee, but also to the previous model of economic development, which was not inclusive enough and because of which europe was losing significant growth potential. the youth guarantee is certainly not a tool against deflation because, again, on deflation it is the european central bank which needs to act, and the surplus countries of the euro zone, by boosting investment and also wages. it is not a tool to generally promote industrial competitiveness, because innovation has to be promoted for that purpose, and it is certainly not a tool to respond to asymmetric shocks in the monetary union, because for that we would need a counter-cyclical fiscal capacity. the new financial instrument, the youth employment initiative, is in a way an embryonic fiscal capacity to respond also to the cyclical rise of youth unemployment in the european union, but it has to function according to the rules of the structural funds. the commission has to observe these rules and we have to be held accountable according to the regulations. i am sure that is also what the house would demand from the commission. nevertheless, the commission has been doing its utmost to help the member states to accelerate implementation of the youth guarantee and the financial instruments supporting it. we have been helping to design the programmes; we have been helping to exchange experiences and also accelerating the adoption when necessary. those who are still not satisfied with the speed, like ms steinruck and mr ropé, obviously would like to see a different type of fiscal capacity, for example in the form of automatic stabilisers, because that would indeed immediately provide financial support, but under the current design of the emu, such capacity does not exist. i think mr kósa is right. apart from the young generation, we also have to speak seriously and also act seriously about the unemployment in the european union. the youth, those under 25, represent about a fifth of total unemployment in the european union. total unemployment in the last one year has been falling, contrary to what some members of this house actually believe. the problem is that it has not been falling fast enough, it has not been falling everywhere, and very often the quality of the new jobs is not what we would like to see. indeed the quality of employment has also suffered during the crisis years and the commission’s initiatives have to respond to all these aspects: the speed of job creation, the balanced nature of economic growth and also the quality of employment. where the overall macroeconomic picture is concerned – and i agree with ms regner, this is very important – it is obviously true that the youth guarantee alone will not create a job-rich recovery. we outlined an employment package in 2012 with a host of measures that need to be taken: shifting taxation away from labour, for example, which member states are capable of doing just very, very slowly, but it also should be seen as a priority. boosting entrepreneurship and helping enterprises to employ more people is indeed an important part of this broader policy. but certainly, when we are facing the risk of another downturn it is also important that fiscal as well as monetary policies use their existing room for manoeuvre to stimulate the economy and to boost investment, which certainly should not remain just a buzz word of our time. i do not think it is helpful when some blame migrants for the level of unemployment in the eu, including for youth unemployment. in fact the two countries that receive the highest numbers of migrant workers in the europe union, germany and the uk, are doing relatively well. germany has had relatively low unemployment rates during the crisis as well and the uk is experiencing one of the fastest falls in unemployment, despite having received relatively large numbers of eu migrants. finally, on the question of decent work, because indeed this has been a priority for the commission, not only inside the eu but also internationally, just in the last one year we rolled out a number of initiatives: the quality framework on restructuring, the quality framework on traineeships, a new health and safety strategy for the next seven years and the european platform proposal against undeclared work. all these initiatives are supposed to help boost the quality of employment and improve industrial relations in the european union, but certainly they do not cover all aspects of the employment policy in the member states because a large part of it is dependent on national law, for example in the case which has been mentioned, about hungary. indeed, the commission finds it regrettable that some of these domestic measures have caused serious damage to the quality of employment, and the country operates with an inflated public scheme which is on the one hand quite costly and secondly does not help many of the participants reintegrate into the labour market at a later stage. but we have been promoting this as well inside the eu and we have been doing that also internationally, in the context of the g20. just yesterday we had a meeting with the representatives of bangladesh, involving the ilo as well, because we cannot allow unfair competition to continue internationally which does not respect the rights of workers and does not protect workers from risks to their health and safety at the workplace. i hope you find all these initiatives positive and helpful. we remain committed to boosting the quality of employment in general, but also specifically for young people in europe.
president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, very briefly because i do not think there are any conclusions to be drawn. i would like to thank all the members who have taken part in the debate with enthusiastic speeches which show the common interest and the common objective which i believe all of us europeans in different positions have, namely to tackle and possibly start to solve the issue of employment, youth employment in particular, employment in other categories with difficulties and possibly good employment. the start of the solution of structural problems such as those caused by unemployment cannot be achieved without a consistent commitment by the member states and the union institutions, which must be achieved through concrete and effective measures to be implemented quickly and without red tape. other high-level meetings that reinforce the momentum of those in berlin, paris and milan, which are obviously not places where solutions are found and implemented, but i believe they are places where open discussion and open discussion can make concrete policy progress. they will certainly help to accompany the measures already decided upon and to deepen the analysis of the conditions necessary for the recovery of employment initiated at the milan conference. i would like to thank all those who have spoken for their attention and contribution.
the third meeting on employment held in milan on 8 october did not produce the desired results: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the programme to include the following areas: as structural unemployment and disparities in national labour markets, especially in terms of the skills of jobseekers and the type of work available on the labour market, are increasing within the eu, reform is urgently needed. what went wrong, why no concrete and timely answers were provided on issues such as: wage bargaining models, adaptability to business cycle conditions; rebalancing of labour costs; design and adoption of unemployment benefits and insurance schemes; degree of flexibility in entering and leaving the labour market, labour mobility and rationalization of contract forms; and skills profile of unemployed workers? it is unacceptable that the heads of state or government have not been able to produce a joint document and have not formalised a programme of meetings aimed at solving the employment problems. expectations do not pay, especially during crises, and we risk finding ourselves in a subsequent analysis not only of poverty but also of the reasons for extremism in europe.
in writing. the risk that such important meetings, such as the one in milan on employment, may turn into a useless catwalk if concrete contents are not developed is well founded. the italian semester is almost over and we are still talking in a generic way without really addressing, and above all resolving, youth unemployment, the all-italian question of the expatriates and the wage gap between men and women in equal work. no more gateways that separate the european institutions from the citizens. the milan summit, among other things, took place in the wake of severe flooding which has affected economically very important regions of italy. there was no solidarity at the summit with regard to these events from the eu leaders.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report has not been watered down; it now reflects what i can call the political direction of the new commission. a political line is being formed, which is being defined with the help of the various groups supporting the new commission. i see four key elements in this resolution: the first is the need to launch the €300 billion investment plan announced by juncker as soon as possible. the second emphasises the importance of making the best use of the flexibility already provided for in the stability pact. thirdly, the role of structural reforms in strengthening medium- and long-term growth. fourthly, the need to strengthen the social dimension of european policies. and these four elements are closely linked. public and private investment is an essential ingredient for the rapid recovery of the european economy. at the same time, the flexibility provided for by the rules should be used in the event of exceptional circumstances, such as a prolonged recession or inflation expectations well below the european objectives. it is not only functional to get out of resignation but also to encourage and finance reforms. investment and flexibility can help to encourage, create mechanisms to make recommendations more binding and finally social cohesion, it is also a factor of competitiveness and growth. so there is emerging, and this is the political fact, a broad consensus on a new line of economic policy and it is to be hoped that the outgoing commission, in its assessment of national stability laws, will not wish to impede this new course.

in writing. - the financial regulations provide that the commission is obliged to present each year a draft amending budget which takes account of the result of the previous financial year. in this case, the current accounting is for the year 2013. if there is a surplus of some eur 1 005 million, it would mean that eur 30 billion of invoices remain unpaid, so the payment appropriations are not sufficient to cover all that has already been spent. the council has asked the member states to pay the invoices within 30 days, so if this type of practice continues, it will mean, for example, that erasmus students will not be able to receive the emoluments for their scholarships, some of the beneficiaries of the structural funds will not be paid and there could be many examples of a failure to serve the citizens. the 2015 budget is already under discussion but we want guarantees to close the 2014 budget.
in writing. - with the second amending budget for 2014, the commission took account of the surplus of the 2013 budget, the balances of which are in line with previous years. these surpluses are reimbursed to the member states by way of compensation for the monthly contributions paid by the member states to the european union. for our country this will be about 110 million euros. i voted in favour of the draft amending budget in question, because the measure essentially involves a return of funds from the eu treasury to the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this purely technical budget, which is part of a specific procedure codified in the financial regulation, which, once the result of the previous financial year has been established, requires that the budgetary changes noted be adopted and entered in the current year. the current situation is quite positive, with a surplus of eur 1 005 million from the 2013 budget forecast to be booked in 2014, meaning that the eu will have an additional amount of own resources at its disposal to reduce the need to request any additional contributions from the member states.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this measure which is an amending budget and refers to a surplus for the 2013 eu budget of around eur 1 billion, largely due to higher revenue from fines and interest on late payments. as a rule, this amount should be returned to the member states, but in view of various problems and the continuing shortage of funds, especially for payments, the committee on budgets of the european parliament has proposed that the adoption of this second amending budget be linked to the subsequent third and fourth budgets, in such a way as to compensate for unexpected revenue and expenditure and thus have a neutral impact. this, together with further amending budgets, should even lead to a final surplus for the eu coffers. it is therefore essential to consider this amending budget as linked to the subsequent ones and as a priority in relation to the discussions and adoption of the budget for the coming year 2015. all this because it is felt that it is absolutely necessary to settle the previous situations as soon as possible, before tackling everything else.

how many? if he had not deployed tanks, infamous minefields on the border, to prevent the turkish kurds from going to fight against an enemy that disdains all forms of humanity. how many? if he had not bloody repressed the demonstrations against these atrocities, more than 30 people would have died. the distracted and superficial eye of the west still should be ashamed of having forgotten for too long a drama of a region that in kurdish means the west, rojawa. were those men, women and children tortured, raped and beheaded by isis in recent weeks really an acceptable price for not having the courage to punch a big nato member's table? do they not even deserve a resolution in this parliament? the hypocritical eye of the entire international community...
the hypocritical eye of the entire international community, finally, an increasingly immobile and unfeeling eye on one of the many humanitarian catastrophes announced. hypocrisy, to deny it would be hypocrisy! burden on those countries that are more prone to the migration emergency. the dublin system leads asylum seekers to rely on illegal networks to reach their desired european destinations, even when they would qualify for international protection in any member state, since they cannot choose the state where to apply for international protection. semi-colonial exploitation and war industries that directly or indirectly contribute to conflict and misery, do the rest. the border states and the countries at the entrance to europe, such as italy or greece, are faced with a structural emergency which requires enormous expenditure of resources and which, we repeat, cannot be contained by an exceptional police operation such as 'mos maiorum'. this operation, however, risks unintentionally fuelling the business of immigrant reception and detention centres, which are increasingly the focus of the interests of organised crime and unscrupulous businessmen. i would like to stress that this is a business that must be kept under close watch, also because it feeds on the skin of human beings, migrants, who are often at risk of being victims of violations of their fundamental rights. in the the fight against trafficking in human beings? what if, with intellectual honesty, it is not more appropriate to provide for ex ante solutions, by revising the dublin regulation, filling the regulatory gap and providing for legal channels of access to the european union?

in writing. - regulation (eu) no 374/2014 on the reduction or elimination of customs duties on goods originating in ukraine was to apply until the entry into force or provisional application of the association agreement and no later than 1 november 2014. on 12 september 2014, the european union agreed to propose to the eu member states, as part of a comprehensive peace process in ukraine, to extend the provisional application of the comprehensive and deep free trade agreement until 31 december 2015, while maintaining autonomous eu trade measures in favour of ukraine during that period. since the regulation provides for unilateral preferences which will cost the community budget eur 487 million, and given the serious situation the ukrainians are in, i think the best vote is abstention.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the amendment to the regulation on customs duties on goods from ukraine which extends for a further year the trade preferences already in force with regard to kiev. the regulation has the important objective of ensuring continuity and certainty in our bilateral trade relations at a very delicate political stage and with a view to the full implementation of the dcfta, an important pillar of the wider association agreement with ukraine recently concluded. i think it is particularly significant that - also in this 'bridge' regulation - a clause on respect for human rights, the rule of law and the principle of sovereignty and territorial integrity is included, which is binding for the eu to grant trade preferences. it is also important that the regulation should pay particular attention to the most sensitive products, such as those of the eu agricultural and agro-industrial sector, through specific tariff quotas: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the conclusion of the agreement on the common fisheries policy. the adoption of this regulation will therefore enable us to take another step together in the difficult process of rapprochement between the european union and ukraine.

the european parliament has been a great help to the people of europe in the past, and it is a great help to the people of europe today. as president schulz said so well in his powerful speech, the fall of the berlin wall was an act of liberation: the victory of life over the sadness of oppression. celebrating the anniversary today means first of all remembering the victims of that wall - the political dissidents and the many citizens whose lives were upset - but it also means remembering those reformers who, before others, understood the true nature of real socialism. i would like to remember alexander dubček, whose death anniversary was celebrated in silence on friday. but today we also want to look to the future. the first lesson to be learned is that europe is the only antidote to the rise of new walls and conflicts. europe is a bridge that crosses over any wall. this european vocation for peace is now being called into question by the rise of new walls, such as the new imaginary wall dividing ukraine. we will never accept violations of fundamental principles of international law, such as territorial integrity, but we will not accept that some nostalgic for the cold war use the ukrainian tragedy as a wedge between europe and russia. the new walls are not just in europe. federica mogherini did well to make her first official visit to the middle east. europe, with its new activism, can become a protagonist in the peace process in the region. only by breaking down the wall in gaza, by rebuilding acceptable living conditions in that region, will we be able to bring peace and development. i understand the fascination of walls, also with regard to migrants, to non-eu citizens. the walls evoke closed universes, like the maginot line the french erected to protect themselves from the germans. but then we know how the french fortress ended: the historian marc bloch called it a strange defeat, because the collapse had occurred first in the souls. even today, the real european wall does not cross borders and maps. the real european front is in the minds. after the berlin wall, it was believed that history was over and that an alternative to the most unbridled capitalism was no longer possible. this has opened the way for unbridled neoliberalism and increased inequality. new, often parasitic, rent-based oligarchies have emerged, and too often europe has been unable to challenge the single mind and propose an ambitious agenda of market reforms. europe must continue to regulate finance if it does not want to fall victim to the financial lobby of this great power which threatens the democratic integrity of this great building which is europe. it is up to europe today to show that history is not over, but that the aspiration for equality, freedom and solidarity remains the northern star of our community.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, 25 years ago the fall of the berlin wall showed that no physical or ideological barrier could stop the will of a people, the will of a people to freedom, and gave us hope that a different europe would finally be born. but it didn't work out that way, unfortunately. since 1989 the european union and the european institutions have built a very high wall, which is getting higher and higher and more dangerous. on the other side of this wall are the citizens of europe. there are 122 million european citizens at risk of poverty, 25 million unemployed, businesses closing, young people without a future, old people who do not even have the money to live. the commission has already made a number of proposals. we must decide which side we are on, whether we are brave or cowardly, whether we are with the people or with the europe of banks, austerity, taxes and financial lobbies. we're at a crossroads. we can be the brave voice that interprets the needs of our citizens or we can stand with the economic dictatorship of this europe. we all have a great responsibility. we are fighting to change this europe. let us finally bring about a europe of the peoples.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr juncker, first of all, thank you for being here in parliament. your presence is an act of sensitivity and responsibility and we democratic socialists sincerely appreciate it. i would like to say at the outset that the first feeling one gets when reading about the schemes adopted by the multinationals to pay less tax is still one of indignation, even when one knows the facts. outrage at those companies that make billions in profits and don't pay taxes in the countries where those profits are made. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as president juncker has said, this is not a problem that affects just a few member states. it is a european and a world phenomenon. and it is shameful that while some countries - let us remember greece - were being given the horse-drawn carriage in the name of austerity, elsewhere, in europe too, multinational companies were evading billions of euros from public coffers by not paying taxes. and the worst, the most shameful thing, as president juncker himself has very honestly pointed out, is that the multinationals, in most cases, evaded taxes without breaking any european law or regulation. we must not allow this to happen again! if there is one thing that should unite this house, it is the tenacious and strong will to stop allowing a phenomenon to happen by changing the legislation, because the legislation must be changed to eradicate this phenomenon. many of the companies accused of tax evasion are the same ones that later line up to get funding and support from the member states. the philosophy is to draw on the state when it's convenient, but privatize the profits. this is the logic of rapacious capitalism, which has little to do with the thousands of small and mediumsized enterprises which are competing every day in the market without any tricks and which constitute the real backbone and salvation of the european economy. but the complaint is not enough, let's move on to the proposals. president juncker, when he took office as president of the european commission, when he won our confidence, he made commitments, which he reiterated this afternoon. we, as a group of socialists and democrats, are calling for a precise timetable for implementing these commitments and we are also adding some of our own proposals. tax harmonization is fine, but we need a stronger push for political, social and economic integration in europe. we also propose to the commission three measures which come from the report by a former colleague of ours, mojca kleva kekuš, which was approved by a large majority in this parliament. first proposal: the commission could and should adopt a clear definition of tax havens, which is broad and also takes into account dubious practices such as tax rulings. second proposal: the smart ones pay. the competent authorities must suspend or revoke the banking licenses of financial institutions that help to organise fraud. at the same time, companies that engage in such practices must be excluded from european funds, because it is not acceptable to try to evade taxation and then make a profit. proposal number three: we want financial information in the balance sheets of multinationals to be in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament decision rejecting the request by the deputy prosecutor-general of the portuguese republic to waive the immunity of ms ana gomes. application for criminal proceedings to be instituted against mr gomes and for him to be heard in the context of those proceedings, following alleged defamatory statements made during a television debate on the privatisation of important shipyards. it would not be right to waive immunity in this case, since mr gomes expressed those views in the course of his duties and on matters which he had personally dealt with at european level, as is clear from the questions addressed to the commission and the extensive correspondence on the subject with european commissioners tajani and almunia. the link between mr gomes's opinion and his duties as a member of parliament is clear, and this is a necessary condition for the application of immunity under the court of justice and european union law. moreover, the issue on which the member of parliament expressed her opinion is of great public interest, all the more important at european level since the portuguese government's decision had given rise to an investigation by the european commission for breach of union state aid rules.
in writing. - portuguese mep ana gomes has been sued for libel over statements she made criticising abuses by her country's defence minister in connection with the privatisation of a shipyard. given that the question was raised by mrs gomes herself on several occasions during her parliamentary activities, we do not think we should vote in favour of the waiver of immunity.
in writing. - mrs ana gomes has been sued for alleged defamation during a television broadcast in which she criticised the portuguese minister of defence over alleged abuses in connection with the privatisation of a shipyard in portugal. it is established practice in the european parliament that members may enjoy immunity for remarks made outside parliament if those remarks have a direct and obvious link with the duties performed in the context of the parliamentary mandate. furthermore, gomes had raised the issue on several occasions in several written questions to the commission and, subsequently, the facts she had complained of were the subject of a state aid investigation by the european commission. so i can only be in favor of not revoking your immunity.
in writing. - voting on parliamentary immunities is always very personal and sensitive and is aimed at verifying the effective exercise of the functions of a member of the european parliament, in order to protect our political action during the parliamentary term. in the specific case, concerning the request for the waiver of immunity from prosecution against ms ana gomes, i believe that it was correct not to waive her immunity, as her statements during the tv programme 'tvi24 cara a cara' were directly and obviously connected with the exercise of her duties as a member of parliament.
in writing. - the principle of parliamentary immunity provides that members are free to participate constructively in public debates by making their own comments without the risk of being sued by a court or other authority; this is the case with mr gomes, who has expressed an opinion in public which is directly related to the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. the existence of a clear link between the idea expressed by mr gomes and his duties as a member of the european parliament is therefore indisputable. i have given my consent to the report signed by mrs hautala, convinced that the initiation of legal proceedings against mrs gomes would send the wrong message, namely that a member of the european parliament cannot express his views freely.
in writing. - mrs ana gomes has been sued in connection with alleged defamatory statements made during a television debate in which she criticised the portuguese minister of defence on the issue of sub-concessioning the private use of the viana shipyards in portugal. the principle underlying parliamentary immunity is the freedom of members to participate constructively in debates and to represent their constituents on matters of public interest, freely expressing their views without risk of being sued before a court or other authority. given that mr gomes spoke on the television programme in question as a member of the european parliament, discussing matters of interest to him at european level, i cannot support the request for the waiver of parliamentary immunity.
in writing. - i have decided not to waive the immunity of my colleague, mrs ana gomes, because members of the european parliament, pursuant to articles 8 and 9 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union, may not be sought, detained or prosecuted for opinions or votes expressed in the exercise of their functions. in this case, my colleague had criticised the portuguese government on a television programme, in which she discussed issues of concern to her at european level. in particular, mr gomez objected to the privatisation of major shipyards, which had been the subject of two questions to the european commission for a written reply. the criticism was therefore directly and visibly connected with the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament and, as a result, i could only vote in favour of the decision.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i have voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted with absolute conviction and determination against the waiver of mr gomes's immunity because, as the court rightly pointed out in its interpretation of the articles of the case, a member of the european parliament can and must express his opinion outside the european parliament, because this too is an expression of the exercise of his parliamentary functions. it seems to me a basic principle of modern democracies that political debate should take place not only in parliament but also through the most varied media, from press releases to the internet. a member must be free to take part in debates and to represent his constituents on matters of public interest, freely expressing his views without fear of being sued in a court of law. a democratic society must guarantee the freedom of expression of its representatives, especially when they speak about the institutional task entrusted to them. if not, the concept of democracy should be revised. in this particular case, there is a clear link between the opinion expressed by mr gomes and his duties as a member of the european parliament. a legal action against her would prevent her from freely exercising the parliamentary mandate entrusted to her by the portuguese citizens.

in writing. - the irish authorities applied for financial assistance for 171 redundant workers at andersen ireland limited, which was operating in the economic sector of nace rev. 2 division 32 (manufacture of jewellery and related articles). the request is a derogation from the egf regulation (article 4 (1) (a)) which requires the mobilisation of the egf to be carried out by an additional 500 persons. i believe that the exceptional circumstances, given the influence of these redundancies on employment and the economy of the area of rathkeale, where the company is located, in economically difficult conditions, justify the derogation. the commission proposes to mobilise the egf in the amount of eur 1 501 200. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the commission's proposal, as i consider that the mobilisation of the egf is justified by the major changes in the structure of world trade in the field of cosmetics: third countries have increasingly gained a leading position in the sector, both in terms of volume and value, also thanks to online sales, replacing european producers. the derogation from the regulation was appropriate because the company was a major employer in the area, and also because the majority of the redundant workers are women, whose wages are the main source of livelihood for entire families.

in writing. - i welcome the signing of the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova, containing a trade pillar leading to the creation of a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta), as it constitutes one of the most ambitious free trade agreements the eu has ever concluded with a third country. the dcfta provides for liberalisation for most products from the eu side. this is one of the most significant mutual benefits of the agreement and is of major importance for trade and economic growth, job creation, prosperity and stability in the country. the association agreement also represents a step forward in eu-republic of moldova relations and a commitment to political association and economic integration. all this will have a long-term positive effect on the moldovan economy and will help improve the quality of life of its citizens.
in writing. - the commission considers that the association agreement will create trade opportunities in the eu and the republic of moldova and will foster real economic modernisation and progressive integration with the eu. the process should result in higher quality standards for products, better services for citizens and, above all, the ability of the republic of moldova to compete effectively on international markets. at the same time, an official from eubam, the european mission on the moldovan border, says that the transnistria region in moldova is a washing machine, importing goods of dubious origin and then repackaging them and reselling them to europe. that's why i decided to abstain.
in writing. - the conclusion of an association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova, following the recent developments in ukraine, is a further step towards achieving full political and commercial integration on our continent. i therefore thought i should vote in favour of this agreement, in the belief that the european union and the republic of moldova can mutually benefit from the creation of a deep free trade area (dcfta). the agreement also demonstrates the determination of the republic of moldova to strengthen its relations with the european union. finally, i consider the provisional application of that agreement as of september 2014 to be particularly important, as it could mitigate the consequences of the import restrictions decided by russia also in respect of the republic of moldova.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the report by mr petras auštrevičius, which will lead to the creation of a comprehensive and deepened free trade area (dcfta) between the republic of moldova and the eu. i would also add that the ratification of the eu-republic of moldova association agreement is a clear recognition of the success of the country's political and economic reform process, which testifies to its determination to eventual accession to the european union.
in writing. - my vote in favour of the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova reflects a genuine appreciation of the efforts made so far by the authorities of the country to implement a reform programme fully in line with european expectations. i welcome with great enthusiasm the progress that moldova has made so far in the area of justice and the fight against corruption, and i hope that responsible progress in the field of human rights will finally mark the process for its future welcome into the european family. i hope, therefore, that this agreement will only serve as a prelude to strengthening the european perspective of the republic of moldova, not only in economic terms but also in political and social terms. this document, which marks the beginning of cooperation between the two parties not only from an economic point of view, confirms that european soft power, as an alternative to a coercive approach, makes the alliance with europe highly attractive, the best possible one.
in writing. - i thought i would vote in favour of the eu-republic of moldova association agreement, confident that it will create new trade opportunities in the eu and in the republic of moldova. in addition, both parties will benefit from the creation of a deep free trade area (dcfta).
in writing. the republic of moldova has made significant progress in reforms and in strengthening its relations with the european union. furthermore, on the one hand, the conclusion of the association agreement is a function of a broader process of enhancing the european perspective of the republic of moldova at political, economic and social levels and, on the other hand, that agreement, which constitutes the precondition for the gradual integration of the republic of moldova into the eu policies linked to it, would determine, as an effect, the creation of conditions for the country to fully exploit its potential. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement marks an important milestone in relations between the european union and moldova, considering that the conclusion of this agreement is part of a wider process which will strengthen moldova's european perspective both politically and socially and economically. closer ties with the eu will benefit the country and will certainly bring stability and the independence of institutions that can guarantee democracy, the rule of law and good governance. in addition, the country's participation in eu agencies and programmes on common security and defence policy cooperation will ensure greater protection of its borders, especially at a sensitive time like the one moldova is experiencing with an unstable border situation. with the signing of the agreement with the entire territory of the republic of moldova, i hope that a workable solution can be found to resolve the worrying situation that has been created for some time in the secessionist territory of transnistria. the elections on 30 november will be an important test to see whether the pro-european parties will have a stable majority.
in writing. - i decided to vote against because the report is totally unbalanced against russia. the crisis in ukraine, the illegal annexation of crimea and the role played by russia are considered to be a serious threat to european security and have changed the geopolitical situation, which also has repercussions for eu-republic of moldova relations. the authorities are also called upon to continue the effective implementation of the national human rights action plan, with particular attention to the human rights of the roma.
