in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the peace process in northern ireland. since the good friday agreement of 1998 between the governments of the united kingdom and ireland, much progress has been made in terms of consolidating the peace balances. it is worrying that the implementation of the peace process has reached a deadlock and that the continued criminal activity of marginal elements risks jeopardising its continuation. over the past two decades, europe has offered its support for peacebuilding. in the light of the challenges that remain, i am convinced that europe must continue to play an active role in ensuring that the peace process in northern ireland is fully realised. in this process europe should play a leading role, coordinating the efforts of international partners such as the united states and canada, which have played an important role in supporting the implementation of the peace process. i believe that strengthening the progress made and promoting reconciliation in northern ireland and the regions around ireland is one of the priorities for europe.
in writing. - we welcome the progress made in the northern ireland peace process. in the current situation, there has already been an increase in foreign investment and a reduction in unemployment, although some important issues remain. we in the delegation hope very much that the process can be strengthened and continued, giving new impetus and momentum to the negotiations and guaranteeing equal rights to both communities.
in writing. - i voted unanimously in favour of this resolution. i think it is important that the eu intervenes wherever there are violent forms of protest within its territory, for whatever reason. at the same time, i believe that the eu must respect the principle of self-determination of peoples, without necessarily interfering in the internal affairs of the member states, but welcoming with open arms those european peoples who do not recognize themselves in their own state and respect, as a separate entity, the copenhagen criteria.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the peace process in northern ireland because i believe it is a priority for the european union to act as a promoter and mediator so that hostility and persecution of religious minorities in one of its member states is brought to a definitive end and a lasting peace is achieved between the opposing factions after a conflict that has been going on for almost a century. i hope that the european institutions, building on the many efforts already undertaken, such as the programme for peace and reconciliation in northern ireland known as 'peace iii', and taking into account the various agreements already concluded, such as the belfast agreement, reached in multilateral negotiations and signed on 10 april 1998, the weston park agreement of 2001, the agreement reached in the multilateral negotiations held in saint andrews, fife, scotland, from 11 to 13 october 2006, between the two governments and all the main parties in northern ireland, and the hillsborough agreement of 27 september 2008, will continue to encourage dialogue and reconciliation between nationalists and unionists to allow the start of a phase of development and reconciliation, as well as to promote the economic and social progress of northern ireland.
in writing. - today's vote is another positive step in the peace process. at this moment in northern ireland it is conceivable that the word peace is acquiring a lasting connotation. it took a great deal of effort and great mediation skills to get to this point. i remain of the opinion that we have a very good chance of replacing violence and terror with peace and democracy once and for all.
in writing. - twenty-five years after the signing of the good friday agreement, a decisive breakthrough is needed, without which the settlement of the conflict risks being jeopardised. the continuing economic crisis, with its devastating social effects, has given new life and motivation to those who believe that the only solution lies in violent, criminal and antisocial activities. it is our duty to prevent these minorities and marginal groups from undermining the peace process. to do so, we must recognize that they draw their strength and support from their inability to provide concrete and visible answers to the growing social distress caused by unemployment and low income levels. once again, and i almost regret having to stress and reiterate it, we are witnessing the effects of a reckless policy which has forgotten the needs and demands of so many women and men, who react with anger and become easy prey for exalted and unscrupulous minds, who bend this anger to criminal ends. this is no longer acceptable. we must prevent europe from becoming a hostage to dangerous subversions and we must give the people back the real hope of growth and jobs. otherwise our words will have little effect against populism and extremism.
in writing. - the current economic depression has been a major factor in the slowdown of the peace process in northern ireland, as it has swept away twenty years of prosperity like an earthquake. it is clear that the reduction in resources for development and détente projects is one of the main causes of the increase in criminal and violent actions we are facing today. today, with this resolution, we want to give further positive support to the peace process. certainly, more leadership will be needed to build lasting peace, but we have the best prospect ever seen in a generation to replace violence with peace and democracy. we cannot therefore refrain from urging all parties concerned to participate in the talks which began on 16 october to resolve the outstanding issues in order to support the functioning and stability of the democratic institutions of northern ireland. it is therefore a matter of course to ask that the eur 150 million provided for in the eu peace programme be used effectively to improve relations between communities and promote economic and social development in both the north and the south.

in writing. - it is essential that all violent conflicts within the european union be brought to an end. in this regard, the efforts of the peace programme to guide european countries towards a peaceful and stable society and to promote reconciliation between peoples, the support of the european regional development fund and, in particular, the eur 150 million allocated to the peace programme to address the priority issues in northern ireland and the surrounding counties of ireland, for the benefit of all the people living in those areas, should be acknowledged. in recent years there have been numerous political crises, including threats from opposition groups, which have led to a stalemate in the northern ireland peace process. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - in recent years the peace agreement has been jeopardized by problems between the parties sitting in the house, by tensions over issues of national identity and, lastly, by the result of the scottish referendum which has reignited the latent problems in northern ireland. the joint resolution of the european parliament, for which i voted in favour, is intended to ensure that the peace process, which is currently at a standstill, is resumed in a more decisive way so that agreement can be reached on the outstanding issues and with the aim of finding a lasting solution shared by all the parties involved. i regret that marginal elements, advocates of violent and sometimes criminal activity, can delay the reconciliation and dialogue of an entire community which, among other things, would bring benefits to northern ireland in terms of economic growth and reduction of unemployment, helping to reduce regional disparities.
in writing. - in pursuance of ankara's economic interests, the turkish oil exploration vessel barbaros entered the exclusive economic zone (eez) of the republic of cyprus on the morning of 20 october, in violation of international and european maritime law. turkish entry was preempted by the maritime directive (navtex) issued by turkey earlier this month, which prompted cypriot president anastasiades to suspend talks with his turkish cypriot counterpart for the reunification of the island. the directive authorizes the barbaros to commence exploration within the boundaries of the cyprus eez. the turkish directive comes into force on the same day that russian naval units armed with missiles begin exercises in the waters off the southern coast of the island as agreed with nicosia, before ankara issued its navtex. this unprecedented provocation by turkey can only be seen as a confirmation of the ambiguity of turkey's position, already highlighted by other contemporary behaviour which demonstrates the absolute unreliability of turkey for europe and, more generally, for the west.
in writing. - abstention from the vote: i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on turkey's actions creating tensions in the exclusive economic zone of cyprus. these unilateral actions by turkey are not to be underestimated and deserve a lot of attention, given that turkey is a candidate country for accession to the european union. these actions have already led to the suspension of peace talks between cyprus and the turkish-controlled north of the island. i therefore believe it is important that turkey withdraw its warships immediately, so as to create the conditions for the resumption of peace talks with cyprus. i also believe that turkey's actions cannot but lead this parliament to a wider reflection on turkey's own application to become a member of the eu. i hope, therefore, that this resolution will encourage the european parliament and the european commission to intensify their monitoring of turkey's activities in the exclusive economic zone of cyprus and to intensify their dialogue with turkey itself in order to achieve full normalization of relations with all the member states.
in writing. - turkey has failed to comply with its obligations under the law of the sea treaties and has openly violated the exclusive economic zone of the republic of cyprus. such behaviour does not favour a country which is a candidate for membership of the european union, which has a duty to pursue a foreign policy consistent with that of the union itself. we demand that the sovereignty of the republic of cyprus be respected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this urgent resolution, convinced that europe's peace-making action can serve as a stimulus to the already tense relations between cyprus and turkey. the ban on shipping imposed by turkey, which is disadvantaging cyprus and its exclusive economic zone by blocking state investments and major european companies, seems to be a pretext. both states must exercise restraint and act in accordance with international law, facilitating good neighbourly relations and seeking a peaceful settlement of all long-standing disputes. let cyprus, from the farthest corner of our union, be a bridge across the borders of the mediterranean!
in writing. - cyprus's sovereignty must be respected without conditions. i know that turkey is an important partner for the eu, although in recent years it has deviated a little from the path of eu accession that it had embarked on, and i know that it is now a strategic place in view of the threats coming from the middle east. at the same time, agreements must be respected and no exceptions must be granted. what i have in mind is peace, and my vote went in that direction.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on turkish actions in the cyprus economic zone, joining the conclusions of the european council of 24 october, which called on turkey to respect the sovereignty of cyprus over its territorial waters and the related rights in its exclusive economic zone. the navtex permit issued by the turkish authorities to allow an oil company to carry out seismic surveys has rightly caused great concern in nicosia and in all the member states, because ankara's behaviour, in addition to interfering with cypriot sovereignty, has not taken into account the cooperation agreements between cyprus and turkey for the equitable distribution of resources. the claims made by turkey appear to be in conflict with international law, including the un convention on the law of the sea (unclos), ratified by the eu, which sets out rules governing the uses of the oceans and their resources. i believe it is necessary and a priority for the eu to achieve a final peace between the island of cyprus and turkey, and i call on ankara to recognise the right of cyprus to exist. at the same time, it is strategically important for the eu to cultivate a good relationship with ankara and to protect cypriot sovereignty.
in writing. - i am firmly opposed to the exploitation of fossil fuels, and i have signed and voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on turkey's actions creating tensions in the exclusive economic zone of the republic of cyprus. turkey must act in accordance with international law, immediately revoke its maritime directive, refrain from any violation of the sovereign rights of the republic of cyprus and exercise restraint. the escalation of threats and unilateral actions by turkey against the republic of cyprus in relation to the eez is unacceptable. turkey shall respect and fully implement the declaration of the european community and its member states of 21 september 2005, including the provision that recognition by all member states is a necessary component of the accession process.
in writing. - turkey's accession to the union would be an important step forward and an essential part of the completion of the european geopolitical framework. this consideration, however, must not be allowed to slip from our minds, and above all it must not make the union itself weak in the face of the continuing provocations and unilateral acts, which sometimes take the form of real threats, which the turkish government repeats to the detriment of member states and international law (in addition, of course, to respect for human rights and minorities). in reality, what has happened is unacceptable, because the turkish government has deliberately sought to violate international law and, above all, to reiterate its utter contempt for a sovereign state. the union, for its part, must express its position and the right to express a foreign policy which, with authority, assert its interests, in full respect of all the requirements of international law. the turkish government must be aware that these actions may have negative consequences for the whole process of approximation and accession. on the other hand, it is legitimate for europe to demand that turkey immediately cease its acts of intimidation and return to the level of respect for international law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on turkey's actions creating tensions in the exclusive economic zone (eez) of cyprus. turkey has sent ships to the area off the southern coast of the island, with the aim of collecting data useful for hydrocarbon exploration until 30 december. i believe that turkey must withdraw its ships so that the infringement of cypriot sovereign rights can be brought to an end and peace talks can be facilitated.
in writing. - the republic of cyprus has the sovereign right to explore natural resources within its eez. at the same time, any turkish vessels detected within its vicinity should be withdrawn. any violation and/or threat to the republic of cyprus must necessarily be denounced, in the light of the fact that the claims and actions taken by turkey have no legal basis and are in direct conflict with international law. i am voting in favour of this because the continuation and/or repetition of these actions could also have a negative impact on turkey's relations with the union. in this context, turkey has a duty to ensure good neighbourly relations with the republic of cyprus.

in writing. - we are concerned about turkey's attitude towards cyprus, which is being implemented at a critical stage in the negotiating process. the entry of the turkish ship barbaros, which collects data useful for hydrocarbon exploration, into the exclusive economic zone (eez) off the southern coast of the island, announcing its stay until 30 december, violates nicosia's sovereignty over this part of the sea. the turkish government has not yet been able to reach a satisfactory agreement on the terms of the accession negotiations with the european union. finally, in order to resolve the difficult cyprus problem, we call on both communities in cyprus, greece and turkey itself to intensify their efforts to resume negotiations as soon as possible and to avoid potentially provocative actions.
in writing. - the european parliament resolution on turkey's actions in the exclusive economic zone of the republic of cyprus is of fundamental importance in order to ensure that turkey not only recognizes the existence of the republic of cyprus but also its legitimate right to explore and exploit the natural resources in the exclusive economic zone (eez). turkey must demonstrate that it is acting in accordance with international law and must cease its provocative actions within the eez as soon as possible. the resolution also supports the right of the republic of cyprus to complain to the united nations and the international maritime organisation about systematic violations on its territory and in its sovereign waters. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, with the navigational telex directive, turkey has reserved a very large area of the cypriot exclusive economic zone for seismic surveys. these seismic readings concern an area that the government of the republic of cyprus has allocated to korea gas corporation and eni for the exploration of possible hydrocarbon reserves. despite repeated calls from the eu, the turkish state continues to challenge the existence of the republic of cyprus and its legitimate right to explore and exploit the natural resources on its territory. the demands and actions of turkey have no legal basis and are in direct conflict with international law. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - the joint resolution of the european parliament was the result of a turkish maritime directive which identified blocks, under the exclusive jurisdiction of the republic of cyprus, where seismic surveys could be carried out on behalf of a turkish company. in that area, the italian energy company (eni) had begun drilling for possible hydrocarbon reserves in the seabed. it is clear that the presence of the turkish vessel patrolling that area has created quite a few problems and unjustified delays in the eni's search. we should also remember that there are already cooperation agreements for a fair distribution of resources between turkey and cyprus, and the one we are talking about is the exclusive economic zone of cyprus. the presence of the turkish vessel interferes with cypriot sovereignty and is also in conflict with the united nations convention on the law of the sea. i voted in favour of the resolution in the hope that it will make an effective contribution to the peaceful settlement of the problem and that everything will soon return to normal.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with this resolution parliament is making a strong appeal to the international community to find a firm solution to the conflict in south sudan. the region has been ravaged by war for too long. two decades of conflict and two million dead. the country's independence on july 9, 2011, gave hope to the south sudanese people, but it already contained the seeds of subsequent social divisions. we cannot stand by and watch another humanitarian emergency. we cannot allow thousands of children to be excluded from the education system and we cannot tolerate any more the repeated attacks and violence of all kinds against refugees, displaced persons, women and children. we therefore strongly urge the international community to commit itself to forcing all the actors to put an end to the conflict, a conflict which inevitably involves the whole region, the neighbouring countries and the militias already deployed. it is essential that all civil society, and in particular women, participate in the peace negotiations and develop post-conflict solutions that will allow the reconstruction of the country. we also call for an international arms embargo, which has been in force for years, and for respect for human rights. finally, mr president, we encourage the government of south sudan to ratify the cotonou agreement between the eu and the african, caribbean and pacific group of states.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the humanitarian situation in south sudan. i believe that the acts of cruelty and violence which have led to the deaths of over 10 000 people must be strongly condemned, as must the deportation of hundreds of thousands of people. in view of the gravity of the situation, humanitarian aid and food aid cannot be delayed and must be provided on the basis of primary needs, with neutrality, independence and impartiality. i also cannot help but join in the call for a transparent, detailed and comprehensive international investigation into the humanitarian and war crimes that have occurred in south sudan. i hope that the eu will support a long-term development strategy for the country's rebirth, helping it to support a transition to peace and stability that would allow people to recover a normal life, with the return to abandoned farms, the reopening of markets and the reconstruction of homes.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the humanitarian situation in south sudan. a political solution must be found to pave the way for democratically agreed institutions to build the new state formed after the independence referendum. despite the fact that the parties to the conflict began negotiations on 7 january 2014, agreeing to the cessation of hostilities, the opening of humanitarian corridors, the release of political prisoners and the protection of civilians, clashes continue. the eu, member states and the commission provided assistance worth over €254 million in 2014, and in september the commission announced an increase of €20 million for aid. since the outbreak of war in december 2013, some 1.4 million people have been displaced, and hundreds of thousands of children are at risk of dying from hunger and disease or being conscripted as soldiers. the food crisis, which affects some 1.5 million people, should not be underestimated either, and could be solved, or rather "alleviated", by sending basic necessities. it is therefore necessary to step up humanitarian aid to south sudan in order to ensure that the situation in the country is stabilised as soon as possible.

the agenda includes the report by mr davor ivo stier, on behalf of the committee on development, on the eu and the global development framework after 2015 (2014/2143(ini)) (a8-0037/2014).
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are very pleased to be able to present this report to the house today. with the rapporteur, mr stier, and the other shadows and all the colleagues who have contributed, we have done a tremendous amount of work in a very short time, in a spirit of collaboration and with an awareness of the importance of this report which will be the position of this parliament on the definition of the sustainable development goals which will be negotiated at the united nations next year. it is an ambitious and balanced report which has been supported by a very large majority in committee. it is essential that it should have an equally strong majority in this house so that it can present a united position of parliament and influence the conclusions of the council in mid-december. as an s&d group we have placed great emphasis on human rights, which must be at the heart of the new framework, insisting on the principle of non-discrimination and attention to the most vulnerable, as well as minorities, the lgbt community and people with disabilities. we wanted to emphasise the importance of a new global partnership, underlining the universality of the new objectives, the real novelty and the real challenge for the coming years. it is no longer an agenda for developing countries, but shared objectives that apply to all states, including those of the union. we have put the european union's leading role in the future negotiations at the centre of our attention, a role which will become all the more decisive the more it is able to speak with a single, united and strong voice. we wanted to make the fight against all inequalities a top priority of the new agenda, alongside poverty eradication and sustainable development. europe can and must take on the task of promoting a firm fight against inequalities on a global scale, also by setting an example. inequalities that have increased dramatically both within and between states, and which are linked to many of the great challenges we face every day in emergencies, such as migration flows. it is also important to stress inequalities because one of the criticisms of the previous millennium goals is that, although progress has been made, it has been unevenly distributed among different social groups. that is why we clearly support in the report the proposal of the open working group to have a stand-alone objective on reducing inequalities. we wanted to build on the work of the open working group and believe that the objectives should not be reduced but that, if they are to be reorganised, they should not be at the expense of the more ambitious and innovative objectives, including the one on the equality agenda. as a member of the femm committee i am glad that the opinion of the committee has been taken into account and the report makes a strong point, as my predecessors have said, of the central role of women in development policies and the full respect of their rights, including sexual and reproductive rights. many others are the innovative and courageous aspects: the fight against poverty, for example, which we call for not to be measured solely on the basis of income but to consider broader measures of progress and well-being, as well as the desirable raising of the poverty line to two dollars a day; climate change and the need to move with determination and courage towards sustainable production and consumption patterns at last; universal access to quality health and education for all; the need to combat corruption, tax evasion and avoidance, which rob countries of essential resources, including through innovative forms of financing such as the financial transaction tax; and finally the important role of civil society, organisations, local authorities and national parliaments in the new framework, which will be all the stronger the more it is shared and built by more hands. in this regard, we have stressed the need for all actors involved, including the private sector, to be guided at all times by the objectives of development cooperation, respect for human rights, protection of workers and the environment and the principles of transparency and accountability. it is a strong and ambitious report, which we hope will receive the widest possible support from our colleagues (also because next year will be the european year of development), in the knowledge that we are also going to vote on the future of our cooperation policy and in the hope that the union, also with the contribution of the high representative, commissioner mimica and the president of the european council, will be able to make its voice heard in the community of states, in support of a world not only free of poverty, hunger and disease but also fairer, more equal and more attentive to sustainable development and the rights of everyone, because i believe that this is the responsibility we have towards the new generations. answer to a blue-card question. there is an important part of the report that is dedicated to disaster risk reduction (in the original language of the colleague), which is why we have also insisted on the issues of accountability and transparency of all funds and aid. it is certainly a very important subject and is covered in the report.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we very much appreciate the report we are discussing today and we believe that a great deal of work has been done. we believe, however, that environmental sustainability and its impact on human development must be central to the post-2015 development framework. the fight against climate change is a prerequisite for overcoming poverty and ensuring food security and sustainable development. climate change is not just an environmental problem, but it has many effects on a country's health, development and economy. for many developing countries that are not able to manage their risks, reducing climate change means mitigating the risk of natural disasters that directly affect the lives and poverty levels of those areas. we call on the european union, in setting its negotiating strategy for the post-2015 development goals, to place the fight against climate change and actions to address it firmly among its priorities.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent years, important steps have been taken towards the achievement of the millennium development goals. unfortunately, in many countries the goal is still far off. even where progress has been considerable, it has not led to the elimination of very high levels of inequality. certain groups, such as those living in slums or peripheral regions, religious minorities and people with disabilities, continue to be excluded from the achievement of these objectives. i believe that understanding the reason for this exclusion is crucial to making development efforts more effective and inclusive in the future. the feelings of exclusion and alienation that result from this situation can undermine social cohesion and generate disorder and conflict. so i think the global development framework should reflect a greater awareness of the fundamental importance of inclusion: no person, regardless of ethnicity, geography, disability or race, can be denied universal human rights and basic economic opportunities. the european union must lead the process of defining the new development framework with a balance between poverty eradication and the fight against inequalities, with a particular focus on inclusion, which i hope will be an essential element for the implementation of the framework.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner malmström, it is more important than ever to tackle the issue of dual-use goods, on the one hand because of the new tendency of the european union to activism and of the other players to intensify economic and trade relations, on the other hand because of the growing strength and organizational capacity of terrorist groups and finally because of the speed of technological development, which is difficult to keep up with adequate standards. the commission's regulatory effort on dual-use goods must therefore be given the utmost attention and the legislative proposal must be accelerated. but we want to take this opportunity to highlight some concerns, some of which have already been raised. first of all, the need to eliminate any threat arising from the misuse of certain products must be taken into account, but at the same time it must be avoided that there is a distortion of the market which leads to a loss of competitiveness of european producers to the benefit of others whose regulation is less transparent. secondly, restrictions must be based on strict controls both ex ante and ex post and action must be taken in a timely manner to minimise the barriers which still exist in the european market by identifying the most effective measures to support control action for the most sensitive areas. finally, my question is: how can convergence on common standards be promoted globally, because that is the way to make the european union's action as effective as possible?
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, dual-use goods are those products for civilian use which can also be used for military purposes, such as chemicals and remote-control instruments, avionics components and so on. for example, a harmless air navigation guidance system that helps pilots maintain a course can also be used to guide a bomb to its target. warning: we are not talking about weapons here, but about products that are created for civilian use and that are therefore much more insidious, because they are not subject to the same restrictions, but can still contribute to human rights violations in the world. europe is unfortunately a master of hypocrisy in this field too, and while the union has acceded to the european convention on human rights, it also exports surveillance equipment, radar systems and technological components which can be used against our own interests. while europe is full of good words about world peace, european countries sold chemical substances to syria in 2013 with the express consent of their national authorities - substances that were officially intended for civilian use, but that may have been used in the manufacture of chemical weapons. it is therefore obvious that better controls on member states and dual-use goods are needed to establish once and for all what is legitimate to export and to whom. we must also start to regulate the export of surveillance software and technology seriously to prevent the use of made in europe technology to record people at demonstrations or to prevent someone from asserting their rights, as was done during the arab spring. the law must adapt to changing times, which is why i ask the commission to proceed as soon as possible with the revision of the rules on dual-use items, to include more precise definitions, as evidenced by the recent council conclusions, and to extend the application to software and technological products, where necessary, and above all i ask that the application of the regulation be seriously monitored by states which often sell as dual-use items instruments which are genuine weapons.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, there is no doubt that trade in so-called 'dual-use' products should not be treated under the same rules as any other production sector. these goods require a special regulatory regime that is effective in protecting citizens, businesses and governments. this need is all the more felt in a rapidly changing world characterised by the proliferation of new threats to international security and the safety of populations. we therefore welcome the european commission's intention to carry out a legislative review of the current control system. we also hope that it will be preceded by a thorough impact assessment. a balanced system is needed which combines the considerations of international security, the protection of human rights and the need to ensure fair competition between producers at international level. i hope that the commission will do its utmost to promote the convergence of regulations at international level.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, stricter controls on exports of dual-use goods are needed. the european union must ensure the safety of its citizens first and foremost by creating a modern and secure system for the marketing of these products. no general export authorisation should be granted for dual-use technologies produced by the european union, which could be used in a negative way or even used for purposes that violate human rights. at present, exports of dual-use items are not subject to any european authorization system and it is up to each individual state to decide on export controls. at least an ex ante notification system should be established for the most sensitive dual-use technologies. the commission and the member states must make an effort to be transparent and to fill the dramatic legislative gap that exists and to work towards the harmonization of legislation.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, impact assessments are conducted to predict the likely impact of eu legislation on citizens and the economy as a whole. yet they are often controversial and opaque. i believe that a major challenge for the new european commission is to separate its impact assessment mechanisms from the political imperatives that too often guide the development of its proposals and to base them instead on mere scientific evidence. there are countless examples of european policy makers arguing over scientific evidence, even on highly technical issues. i believe, therefore, that a new system of evidence gathering within the commission itself needs to be developed, one which completely disconnects the gathering of evidence from the political imperative. the creation of a special department within the commission with the role of evaluating policy proposals on the basis of pure scientific evidence would be important to ensure that the commission's evaluations are efficient, independent and transparent.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, as a result of the stress tests carried out by the ecb on 113 european banks, 25 failed to pass the tests and fell short of the minimum capital requirements. among these, nine are italian, which unfortunately are among the worst in europe. this may cause problems for the recovery of our economy. in particular, the final outcome of the assessment highlighted the need for capital strengthening measures for the majority of italian banks of over eur 10 billion. the question arises, how will the banking system ensure the necessary flow of capital into the productive system, given that 10 billion of capital can create 125 billion new jobs? the question arises whether, and if so why, the stress test parameters were more stringent than those for other countries. i am afraid of having to look for the answer at the finance table, where italy may not have the same weight as other countries. i hope that action will be taken to avoid penalising the banking systems and, above all, to prevent adverse effects on the real economies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to draw your attention to the fact that in greece the state-owned electricity transmission system operator, admie, is being privatised. a year ago both the chinese state grid corporation and the italian operator terna expressed interest in buying the greek counterpart. however, the state grid corporation of china itself, through the control of state grid international development limited, is now an indirect partner of terna in italy. so we find ourselves in a paradoxical situation, where terna and state grid corporation are allies in italy and simultaneously competitors in greece for the purchase of admie. this is the consequence of the need for the member states to make money by selling off their national and therefore european strategic assets in order to respond to austerity policies, as has already happened in italy and is happening throughout southern europe. i would ask everyone to keep an eye on how the european commission will try to put a lid on this paradox and many others which i cannot discuss here because of time constraints.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the cap and trade system was introduced in the doha round as a tool which was supposed to make it possible to reduce emissions of climate-changing gases, as decided by the kyoto protocol, in the most efficient and economical way. it was thought that leaving the cost of emissions to the market could encourage more virtuous behaviour and penalize companies that did not want to invest in better technologies. since the end of the first trading period, when a tonne of co2 cost a few cents, the instrument has shown its profound limitations. the whole climate and energy package voted in early 2009 is based on co2 cost projections that are far from reality. to combat the climate change that is taking place, we need serious instruments that do not allow the parasitism of brokers and financial markets, the only ones for which the ets is working very well. it is therefore time to start a serious discussion and discussion with all parties on how to overcome the cap and trade system so that we can make full and effective use of the resources available.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, vice-presidents, honourable members of the european parliament, people working in various capacities in this hemicycle, dear friends, i thank you for inviting me to speak before this institution which is fundamental to the life of the european union and for the opportunity you have given me to address, through you, the more than 500 million citizens whom you represent in the 28 member states. i would like to express my particular gratitude to you, mr president, for the warm welcome you have given me on behalf of all the members of this house. my visit comes more than a quarter of a century after that of pope john paul ii. a lot has changed since those days in europe and around the world. the opposing blocs that once divided the continent into two no longer exist, and the wish is slowly being fulfilled that 'europe, by giving itself sovereignly free institutions, may one day expand to the dimensions given to it by geography and even more so by history'. alongside a wider european union, there is also a more complex and highly mobile world. a world that is increasingly interconnected and global and therefore less and less eurocentric. but alongside a larger, more influential union, there seems to be an image of a somewhat aged and compressed europe, which tends to feel less of a protagonist in a context that often looks at it with detachment, mistrust and sometimes suspicion. in addressing you today, i wish to send a message of hope and encouragement to all european citizens, taking as my starting point my vocation as a pastor. a message of hope based on the belief that difficulties can become powerful agents of unity, to overcome all the fears that europe - together with the whole world - is going through. hope in the lord who turns evil into good and death into life. encouragement to return to the firm conviction of the founding fathers of the european union, who wanted a future based on the ability to work together to overcome divisions and to promote peace and communion among all the peoples of the continent. at the heart of this ambitious political project was trust in man, not so much as a citizen, nor as an economic subject, but in man as a person endowed with a transcendent dignity. i would like to stress first of all the close link between these two words: "dignity" and "transcendent". dignity is the keyword that has characterized the recovery of the second post-war period. our recent history is marked by the unquestionable centrality of the promotion of human dignity in the face of the many forms of violence and discrimination which have not been lacking in europe over the centuries. the perception of the importance of human rights is the result of a long journey, including many sufferings and sacrifices, which has helped to form the awareness of the preciousness, uniqueness and unrepeatability of each individual human person. this cultural awareness is based not only on historical events but also on european thought, which is characterised by a rich history of encounter, with many sources from greece and rome, celtic, germanic and slavic substrates, and christianity, which has profoundly shaped them, giving rise to the concept of "person". today, the promotion of human rights is central to the european union's commitment to promoting the dignity of the person, both within the union and in its relations with other countries. this is an important and admirable endeavour, because there are still too many situations in which human beings are treated as objects, whose design, configuration and usefulness can be programmed, and which can then be discarded when they are no longer needed, because they have become weak, sick or old. indeed, what dignity exists when there is no possibility of freely expressing one's thoughts or of professing one's religious faith without coercion? what dignity is possible without a clear legal framework, which limits the domination of force and makes the law prevail over the tyranny of power? what dignity can a man or a woman have when he or she is the object of any kind of discrimination? what dignity can a person find who has no food or the bare essentials of life and, worse still, who has no job that anoints him with dignity? promoting the dignity of the human person means recognizing that he has inalienable rights which cannot be arbitrarily deprived of by anyone, much less for the benefit of economic interests. but we must be careful not to fall into certain misunderstandings which can arise from a misunderstanding of the concept of human rights and their paradoxical abuse. in fact, there is a tendency today towards an ever-widening demand for individual rights - i am tempted to say individualist - which conceals a conception of the human person detached from any social and anthropological context, almost like a "monad" (μονάς), increasingly insensitive to the other "monads" around him. the concept of right no longer seems to be associated with the equally essential and complementary concept of duty, so that one ends up affirming the rights of the individual without taking into account that every human being is linked to a social context, in which his rights and duties are connected to those of others and to the common good of society itself. i therefore believe that it is more vital than ever to develop a culture of human rights which can wisely link the individual, or rather the personal, dimension to that of the common good, to that 'we-all' made up of individuals, families and intermediate groups who come together in social communities. in fact, if the rights of each individual are not harmoniously ordered to the greater good, they end up being conceived without limitations and thus become a source of conflict and violence. to speak of man's transcendent dignity, then, is to appeal to his nature, to his innate sense of right and wrong, to that "compass" written in our hearts and which god has imprinted on the created universe; it means above all looking at man not as an absolute, but as a relational being. one of the diseases i see most prevalent in europe today is loneliness, the disease of those who are unconnected. it is particularly evident in the elderly, who are often left to their own devices, and in young people who lack a point of reference and opportunities for the future. you see it in the many poor people who live in our cities. it is seen in the lost eyes of migrants who came here in search of a better future. this loneliness was further exacerbated by the economic crisis, the effects of which are still felt today, with dramatic social consequences. it is also clear that, in recent years, alongside the process of enlargement of the european union, citizens have become increasingly distrustful of institutions which they regarded as distant and which were committed to establishing rules which they perceived as being distant from the sensibilities of individual peoples, if not even harmful. the general impression is that europe is tired and aging, that it is old and no longer fertile and vibrant. the great ideals which inspired europe seem to have lost their attraction to the bureaucratic technicalities of its institutions. this is accompanied by a somewhat selfish lifestyle, characterized by an opulence that is now unsustainable and often indifferent to the world around them, especially the poorest. it is regrettable that technical and economic questions have prevailed in the political debate, to the detriment of a genuine anthropological approach. the human being is in danger of being reduced to a mere cog in a mechanism which treats him as if he were a consumer good to be used, so that - we often notice this unfortunately - when life is not functional to this mechanism, he is discarded without too much remorse, as in the case of the sick, the terminally ill, the elderly who are abandoned and uncared for, or the children killed before they are born. it is the great misunderstanding that occurs when the absolute of technology prevails, which ends up creating a confusion between ends and means. the inevitable result of the 'throw-away culture' and 'exaggerated consumerism'. on the contrary, affirming the dignity of the person means recognizing the preciousness of human life, which is given to us freely and therefore cannot be traded or bartered. you, in your vocation as parliamentarians, are also called to a great mission, however futile it may seem: to take care of the fragility of peoples and individuals. caring for fragility means strength and tenderness, it means struggle and fecundity in the midst of a functionalist and private model that leads inexorably to the "culture of waste". to care for the fragility of individuals and peoples is to preserve memory and hope; it means taking charge of the present in its most marginal and distressing situation and being able to anoint it with dignity. how can we restore hope for the future, so that the younger generations can have the confidence to pursue the great ideal of a europe united in peace, creative and enterprising, respectful of its rights and aware of its duties? to answer that question, let me use an image. one of the most famous frescoes by raphael in the vatican depicts the so-called school of athens. at its center are plato and aristotle. the first one with the finger pointing upwards, towards the world of ideas, we could say towards the sky; the second one reaches forward, towards the observer, towards the earth, the concrete reality. it seems to me that this is a picture which describes europe and its history well, made up of the continuous encounter between heaven and earth, where the sky indicates the openness to the transcendent, to god, which has always characterized european man, and the earth represents his practical and concrete capacity to face situations and problems. the future of europe depends on rediscovering the vital and inseparable link between these two elements. a europe which is no longer able to open itself to the transcendent dimension of life is a europe which is slowly in danger of losing its own soul and also the 'humanistic spirit' which it loves and defends. it is precisely because of the need to be open to the transcendent that i want to affirm the centrality of the human person, who is otherwise at the mercy of the fashions and powers of the moment. in this sense, i consider to be fundamental not only the legacy that christianity has left in the past to the socio-cultural formation of the continent, but above all the contribution it intends to make today and in the future to its growth. this contribution does not constitute a threat to the secularism of the states and to the independence of the institutions of the union, but an enrichment. the ideals which have shaped it from the beginning, such as peace, subsidiarity and mutual solidarity, a humanism based on respect for the dignity of the person, show this. i therefore wish to renew the readiness of the holy see and the catholic church, through the commission of the european bishops' conferences, to engage in a fruitful, open and transparent dialogue with the institutions of the european union. i am also convinced that a europe which is able to treasure its religious roots, and to grasp their richness and potential, can also be more easily immune to the many extremes that are spreading in the world today, also in writing. - the right to respect for private and family life and the right to the protection of personal data are enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights; article 52 of the charter makes the lawfulness of restrictions on those rights subject to compliance with the principle of proportionality, thus making only those restrictions admissible which are genuinely necessary for the purposes of the general interest as recognised by the union or for the protection of the rights and freedoms of others. in its judgment of 8 april, the court of justice provided some clarifications which, while not providing an answer to the question of the validity of the agreement between canada and the union on pnr, in several respects confirm the doubts raised by the european data protection supervisor. the complexity and sensitivity of the matter make it appropriate to allow the court of justice to express its opinion at this stage, so as to overcome any legal uncertainty and be sure to approve an agreement fully in line with the fundamental rights of citizens. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. the new pnr agreement negotiated with canada is a very balanced text and also strengthens the safeguards on the processing of personal data. in addition, canada has agreed to take a number of unilateral commitments as agreed. the 2010 resolution, where the eu opened negotiations on pnr with canada, set out minimum requirements that canada has fully complied with. thanks to this agreement, we have seen that the pnr has produced good results in terms of the repression of serious forms of crime, such as the seizure of large quantities of cocaine and the fight against the kidnapping of minors and the trafficking of child pornography. accepting the request of the court of justice to examine the compatibility with the treaties - which is why i voted against - would lead to a significant delay in the finalisation of the agreement with canada, even if there would be no consequences as regards the transfer of pnr data to canada. i hope that, in view of the excellent results achieved, a harmonised eu pnr system can be achieved in the near future.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, parliament has been asked to give its opinion, in the consultation procedure, on the proposal for a revision of the regulation on the collection of statistical information submitted to the council by the ecb. this regulation, together with the regulation on the ecb's powers to impose sanctions, forms one of the pillars of the european central bank's statistical activity. the proposal is based on the entry into force of the single banking supervisory mechanism, which gives the ecb new powers and therefore requires an update of the mechanisms for collecting and processing statistical data. once adopted, the legislative act will allow the ecb to use confidential statistical information in a similar way to national central banks, which perform prudential supervisory functions. in addition, the ecb will be able to disseminate confidential statistical information to the national authorities responsible for financial supervision or the stability of the financial system, as well as to the european stability mechanism to the extent and in the level of detail necessary for the performance of their respective tasks. the position adopted by the econ committee on 11 november welcomes the ecb's proposals and supplements them with a number of suggestions aimed at extending the scope of the report. the amendments i have tabled as rapporteur are aimed at ensuring that data are transmitted more appropriately and that their confidentiality is better protected. in particular, one amendment introduces an obligation for authorities and bodies, including the esm, which receive confidential statistical information to take all necessary measures to ensure its protection. the econ committee then approved further amendments reinforcing some points not covered by the ecb recommendation. in particular, it strengthens the transparency of the ecb's statistical acts by requiring the ecb to make public decisions to exempt particular categories of entities from reporting requirements. in addition, it is called for the type of data collected to be extended to include raw data. an important reference to the principle of proportionality is then added in the definition and imposition of statistical reporting obligations. finally, as regards the sanctions part, a clear distinction is made between negligent or intentional behaviour in cases of infringement and the transmission of data by statistical officers, an aspect particularly relevant from the point of view of compliance with the principle of proportionality. the adoption of this revision is therefore of particular importance, as it is part of the broader framework of strengthening the ecb's supervisory tasks in the framework of the banking union project. i hope therefore that parliament will welcome the econ committee's recommendations for rapid adoption by the council and also that the broad consensus which has been reached on the report, for which i thank the shadow rapporteurs and the political groups for their cooperation, will provide the council with further incentive to take the econ committee's recommendations into account.

member of the commission. - mr president, this is the first time (although it is late) for me to stand in front of you and present the current state of the steel industry in europe. i would like to say a few words and present the overview of the current state. as you remember, the commission adopted a year ago, in june 2013, a commission communication action plan for a competitive and sustainable steel industry in europe, the so-called steel action plan. this plan recognised the strategic importance of steel to the eu and emphasised that steel-making has a future in europe, as the european steel industry has many assets in the form of modern plants, advanced products, demanding clients forcing, i hope, constant product innovation and an important domestic market, and of course a skilled workforce. it has also made significant efforts to reduce its environmental impact. the sector, however, faced and still faces major challenges: low demand, increasing energy costs, reliance on imported raw materials, strong and not always undistorted competition and challenging environmental requirements. in its steel action plan, the commission underlined the importance of addressing these challenges at both eu and national level. shortly after the communication on the steel action plan was adopted, the commission formally created in 2013 our high level expert group on steel, with the aim of providing a european platform for dialogue, exchange of information and best practice. in june 2014, a commission staff working document was published which takes stock of the progress made since the adoption of the steel action plan. while highlighting its implementation gaps, it provides an interim overview of the implementation of the actions by the commission, individual member states and industry as well, of course, as by social partners. the majority of the key challenges addressed are unlikely to be overcome in a single year, so the overview is a first snapshot, and implementation continues. in one year since the adoption of the steel action plan, about half of the actions foreseen in it have been implemented. moreover, the fact that the economic situation is slightly improving has led to higher consumption of steel in the main steel-using sectors and has therefore resulted in a better outlook for the steel sector overall. a strong commitment to follow-up underlines the importance of the steel action plan for the sector. the constructive discussions in the meeting of the high level group have highlighted the usefulness and the need to continue the dialogue among major stakeholders in this important industrial area.

address this challenge the commission will promote applied research to identify the cost-effectiveness and monitor the impact of nutrition-sensitive actions. based on the results of these efforts, the commission may decide, during the mid-term review in 2017, to redirect some funds to possibly better-performing actions in order to attain the set objectives by 2025. in front of the challenges ahead, the commission cannot work alone. the commission intends to continue raising awareness of undernutrition issues in international forums like the scaling up nutrition (sun) movement, which has now been joined by 54 countries in the committee on world food security. second, the commission will also strengthen its strategic partnership with fao and who for nutrition and use events like the international conference on nutrition to keep the political momentum on nutrition. third, at country level, the commission has applied the principle of aid effectiveness through the joint programming within the 2014-2020 programming exercise. last but not least, the commission will continue its collaboration with ngos through regular information- and experience-sharing lessons. in conclusion, i am concern. we are dismayed, like all of you, by the daily reports of atrocities specifically targeting women and girls by isis and associated armed groups in iraq. in particular, there are reports of kidnappings, forced marriage, slavery, sexual abuse and forced conversion which are targeting in particular the most vulnerable people belonging to ethnic and religious minorities. the eu, in a formal conclusion of the foreign affairs council and the european council, has repeatedly condemned in the strongest terms these brutal acts and calls for the perpetrators of these gross abuses to be held accountable. we therefore strongly support the work of the office of the un high commissioner for human rights, who has launched an investigation on isis human rights abuses in iraq, and the gathering of strong evidence of violations of international human rights and humanitarian law. the iraqi government should now ensure the investigation of all human rights abuses to avoid immunity on all sides and send a strong message on the importance of respecting the rule of law. this will require reform of the criminal justice system and the steady consolidation of a culture of respect for human rights. an independent judiciary giving a sense of equality to all citizens before the law will be a crucial element in the process of national reconciliation, which is a matter of urgency. many human rights violations currently committed in iraq qualify as crimes against humanity. we therefore strongly recommend to the government to accede to the rome statute or at least accept the jurisdiction of the international criminal court over the current situation and article 12(3) of the rome statute. the eu stands ready to continue supporting the major reforms needed in the area of the rule of law and governance in iraq. a new programme for an amount of eur 10 million was started in early september. in addition, the eu is financing a number of assistance programmes more directly related to the protection of women and children, including an ongoing project on establishing a strategy for the protection of women and assisting victims of trafficking and sexual and gender-based violence. on the humanitarian side, the protection of vulnerable groups, including women and children, is a priority for the european union. the needs of the 2.1 million displaced people and refugees are huge. as the number increased, the eu scaled up its relief efforts. the european union humanitarian action will include medical and psychosocial assistance to victims of all kinds of violence, including sexual and gender-based violence. let me conclude by underlining that the eu will continue to support the government of iraq in such challenging times and will increase its efforts to alleviate the suffering of innocent civilian victims of a horrific wave of violence. in writing. i voted today in favour of the motion for a resolution on the commission's guidelines on impact assessment. impact assessments are carried out to predict the likely impact of eu legislation on citizens and the economy as a whole. yet they are often controversial and opaque. i believe that a major challenge for the new european commission is to separate its impact assessment mechanisms from the political imperatives that too often guide the development of its proposals and to rely instead on mere scientific evidence. there are countless examples of european policy makers bickering over scientific evidence, including highly technical issues. i believe that a new system of evidence gathering within the commission itself is therefore needed, one which completely disconnects the gathering of evidence from the political imperative. the creation of a special department within the commission, with the role of evaluating policy proposals on the basis of pure scientific evidence, would be important to ensure that the commission's evaluations are efficient, independent and transparent.

in writing. it has been 25 years since the un general assembly adopted the un convention on the rights of the child and adolescent. it comprises 54 articles on the subjects of life, protection and development, and is based on the principles of non-discrimination, the well-being and the hearing of the child. the convention changed the way we see children. for the first time, childhood was defined as a protected age. children are considered to be fully-fledged individuals with their own opinions and the right to express them. in the light of the convention's extraordinary importance and the commitment to children of the 194 states that have ratified it, we can offer a positive picture of the progress achieved by the convention. reducing child mortality, the right to education, vaccinations, reducing hiv, birth registration and reducing child labour are among the many advances made by the convention. the greatest progress has been made in africa and asia in the area of the right to life and development. this anniversary is an occasion to celebrate the great strides made, but it must also be a reminder of how much more remains to be done.

i would like to thank mrs ayuso for her work and tell the commissioner that she can count on our group to help her in this matter. as has already been said, the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora provides for a number of safeguards to ensure that international trade in wild fauna and flora does not threaten the survival of species. cites protects more than 35 000 species and 178 countries are members, including all the member states of the european union. the eu can now finally be a party to it and no longer just an observer. it is therefore a due act. this is because the european union has the primary responsibility for applying the convention: is a necessary step to make the protection of biodiversity and endangered species more effective. the preservation, protection and improvement of the quality of the environment are priorities of the union, as laid down in the treaties, together with the prudent and rational use of natural resources and the international promotion of measures to solve environmental problems. in addition, the eu adopts measures for the proper functioning of the internal market and in the field of customs union, common commercial policy. international trade at the expense of endangered species - think of the extermination of elephants and rhinos for tusks and horns, the indiscriminate hunting of fur animals and big cats, the slashing of rare trees for their timber - generates annual revenues of 200 billion dollars. this barbarism impoverishes the earth, enriches some criminal organizations and often fuels wars and terrorism. we therefore welcome the direct involvement of the european union in cites and its accession, as envisaged in the proposal for a council decision, and we thank all the law enforcement agencies that monitor compliance with these rules.
on behalf of the efdd group. we can only agree with the european union's accession to the washington convention, as the environment committee has done with virtually unanimous approval. cites has been ratified by 180 countries worldwide and is probably one of the most effective pieces of legislation to help protect protected species. the occasion of the european union's accession to the convention must, however, be an incentive to do even more, much more, in the area of illegal wildlife trafficking. in 2011, the value of the european market for products of species included in the washington convention lists was estimated at almost eur 500 million. europol notes that in recent years the level of increasingly organised and pervasive criminal activity in the area of illegal wildlife trade has been increasing. the european union is increasingly a consumer but also a producer of illegally acquired natural resources to be placed on the markets. the european database of seizures of cites species contains over 37 000 records, a clear indication of a huge illegal market. an example of this is the massive illegal import of meat from africa, the so-called "bush meat", which in the countries of origin is an important food resource, whereas in our country it is just a fad and a display of a welfare state: we are talking about 270 tons of meat illegally imported through the paris airport alone. so we welcome the union's membership of cites, but we are also proceeding with other initiatives, such as strengthening the rules, improving data collection and tightening penalties for violators.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, by joining the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, the eu is at last equipped with an important instrument for protecting biodiversity. the eu's participation as a legal entity in this system of species protection can only reaffirm the prominent and responsible position that the eu assumes in promoting environmental sustainability. more than 35 000 species are covered by the provisions of the convention. we now have an even more secure legal framework, which also benefits the safety of european citizens, regulating the introduction and import of protected flora and fauna. we are therefore preparing to ratify an instrument which will strengthen the coherence and the negotiating weight of the european union in the international arena, in particular coherence with the lisbon treaty by giving the european commission full competence in the field of trade and the environment. another step towards a stronger eu role in the world for sustainability and environmental responsibility.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union's accession to cites is of fundamental importance in ensuring the safeguarding of biodiversity. although the european union did not immediately accede to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, it has always been committed, since 1 january 1984, to applying it fully. the accession of the european union to cites thus represents the evolution and maturation of a natural and logical process which will finally enable the union to be adequately represented and to guide the work of the convention and to play its role effectively. by joining cites, the union will further strengthen its leadership in environmental, animal welfare and environmental policy, ensuring that international trade in endangered species does not undermine their survival at community level. i believe that accession, which would allow the commission to play a key role in the negotiations during the conferences of the parties, would increase the coherence and unity of the european union's action on cites-related issues and would lead to a greater alignment of the member states' positions. i am therefore convinced that accession must be seen as a logical and necessary step for the eu to be fully able to pursue the objectives it has set itself in the framework of its environmental policy.
in writing. trade in protected species is still a reality and animals need to be protected from commercial practices that may put them at risk. that is what cites is for, a convention that has already been ratified by many countries, but which has only recently been able to be ratified by the european union. as my colleague marco affronte said a moment ago, there is still a lot to be done to protect these species and we of the five star movement will certainly not let our contribution be in vain. i would point out that the council, in its request for assent to parliament, referred only to article 192 of the treaties, the protection of the environment, and not to article 207, international trade. since this is a convention which regulates trade, i repeat, trade in animal and plant species in order to protect them from practices which may endanger them, it is important that the legal basis for international trade be considered as well, because the cites convention pursues both the objectives of legal and non-harmful trade and the protection of animals. and it is only by including all possible fields of application that the convention will be even more effective.
on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i support everything that mr eickhout has said. i will add a few technical points, if i may, because not all fossil fuels are simply harmful to the environment and to health: some of them are even worse! they're devastating to the environment and to health. i am talking about oil sands and shale gas. a study recently published in the journal atmospheric environment has shown that in the large oil sands and chemical processing area in canada, air samples were taken in which volatile organic chemicals were found to be up to 6 000 times higher than normal. the levels of 1,3-butadiene and benzene, which are very potent carcinogens, were 322 times higher in the under-wind than in the over-wind, and in the population living in those areas, the medical records collected over a little more than ten years have shown a considerable increase in leukemia and non-hodgkin's lymphoma, especially as we approached the pollution peaks. the commission proposal for the calculation of emissions does not, however, take any account of oil sands and shale gas. ladies and gentlemen, you have been elected, for the most part, to defend the citizens and their own environment: but how can you still tolerate a commission that does such things?
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission proposal on the methods and reporting obligations under the fuel quality directive has several shortcomings. it does not allow differentiation between the intensity of greenhouse gases and different raw materials and, consequently, neither does it allow the reporting of the actual emissions of individual fuels. the new calculation methods proposed give canadian tar sands, for example, which are highly polluted, an average greenhouse gas intensity value lower than their actual emission value and will therefore favour their importation into the european market. in the light of these considerations, i therefore believe that the objection to the proposal from the european commission on the implementation of the fuel quality directive is justified. however, i believe that even in assessing the commission's proposal we must not forget the general context in which it is placed, namely that of energy security, which, following the recent events in russia and ukraine, cannot but be at the top of the european union's agenda. i think, however, that the commission must continue to work to encourage the development of low-carbon fuels and innovative technologies that improve the environmental performance of fuel suppliers.

member of the commission. - mr president, i thank the honourable members for their very important remarks on this important implementing measure. i listened to all of them very carefully, and i can assure you that they will all be analysed with respect. but please just allow me one clarification. illegal cabotage is a serious infringement in the context of fair competition. member states are obliged to penalise it and consider it when assessing good repute. however, it is not part of this classification, where seriousness of infringement is defined on the basis of risk of fatalities or serious injuries. cabotage infringement is not linked to such a road-safety risk. i would also like to point out that, when assessing good repute, member states should, however, also consider infringements against the national social rules, including those on pay and employment conditions. nevertheless, we should all keep in mind that this is just one step. we already made clear that the agenda of this commission includes addressing social dumping, which has no place in the european union, but we will do so in consultation with social partners and with adequate tools at our disposal. but it is now time for you to decide whether you want the exchange of information to start now – allowing for better enforcement – or if you prefer to delay this further. but at the same time, please allow me to thank you for your very positive and very constructive comments and for offering to help with very good cooperation in the future, to make sure that transport stays safe and competitive and is a key driver of european future prosperity.

in writing. the stability pact must be respected, but new investment is needed to revive europe and jobs. the real betrayal of future generations is to deprive them of the infrastructure essential to growth and well-being, to leave them with a legacy of failing infrastructure, poor schools, inadequate health care and compromised growth potential. to avoid this situation, a flexibility clause should be inserted in the stability pact and the new european fund for strategic investments should be activated. a deeper and fairer monetary and economic union requires a review of the rules of the six pack and two pack, the texts which introduced the obligation to balance the structural balance and on which policies to redress excessive debt and deficit imbalances in the eu countries were based. there is room for improvement in the transparency and complexity of policy making and its impact on growth, imbalances and convergence. the fiscal compact, which permanently institutionalises the austerity regime imposed in europe following the crisis, must be revised, and the limited fiscal room for manoeuvre provided for by the maastricht treaty and the stability pact must be definitively abolished.

the cites convention protects some 35,000 species of flora and fauna from extinction. the european union's accession to cites is a very important step, not so much because it becomes a full member of the convention, thus playing an active role within it, but rather because the union will be able to take a leading role at international level on environmental policy, especially for the protection of biodiversity where the european union has the most advanced legislation. the international trade in exotic species is worth several billion euros a year, and europe is the world's largest importer of some species, such as the boa constrictor, and the second largest importer of felines. cites is the most important instrument in the fight against the smuggling and illegal trade of many species of flora and fauna. the union's accession to the convention will only strengthen this struggle. for these reasons i voted in favour of the recommendation.
