in writing. i voted against eu membership of cites. the signature of treaties and conventions should be the exclusive responsibility of the member states, which should have the right to legislate on these matters autonomously and in accordance with their commercial interests.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the accession of the european union to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). since the european union has committed itself since 1 january 1984 to fully apply the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), although it has not formally acceded to it, i believe that its accession represents a natural development in a process which will finally enable the european union to be adequately represented in the work of the convention and to play its role effectively. by joining cities, the union will further strengthen its leadership in animal protection and environmental policy, ensuring that international trade in endangered species does not undermine their survival at community and international level. i also believe that accession can increase the coherence and unity of the european union's action on cites-related issues and lead to a greater alignment of member states' positions.

in writing. ‒ the agreement on the european economic area (eea agreement) was signed on 2 may 1992 and entered into force on 1 january 1994. by virtue of the act of accession of the republic of croatia, the republic of croatia undertakes to accede, under the conditions laid down in the act, to the agreement on the european economic area, in accordance with article 128 of the agreement. the eea agreement brings together the eu member states and the three members of the european free trade association iceland, liechtenstein and norway into a single market. the eea agreement provides for the inclusion of eu legislation on the four freedoms the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital in all eea states. in addition, the agreement provides for cooperation in other important areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture, collectively known as 'accompanying and horizontal' policies. the agreement guarantees equal rights and obligations in the internal market for eea citizens and economic operators. in view of this, i could only vote in favour of croatia's membership of the european economic area.

in writing. ‒ the consultation procedure asks parliament to give an opinion on the appointments proposed by the european commission to the board of the 'single resolution committee'. the president is german and the vice-president is finnish. the board is defined by regulation (eu) no 806/2014 which lays down uniform rules and a uniform procedure for the resolution of credit institutions and certain investment firms. it acts to regulate the so-called 'single resolution mechanism' introduced by regulation (eu) no 1093/2010 establishing the european supervisory authority (european banking authority). i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the candidates for membership of the single resolution board. the commission notes that the bank's capital needs are not covered by the banking communication, which is not yet available. the innovative profile of this body is that the composition of its executive body does not directly reflect mechanisms of intergovernmental compromise, but rather draws on those more purely managerial logics that have never been applied, or at least stated, at the level of the european union with equal vigour: the chairman and the other four members are appointed on the basis of merit, competence, knowledge of banking and financial matters and experience in financial supervision and regulation and banking resolution.
in writing. ‒ the establishment of a crisis resolution committee is a due act towards those who have sacrificed so much because of austerity policies. the troika's resolution of banking crises has not been transparent, so we support the appointment of the single committee as it centralises decision-making power and makes it possible to identify those responsible when the solutions adopted do more harm than good.
in writing. ‒ the candidates were examined by their colleagues in the committee on economic and monetary affairs and found to be suitable for the tasks assigned to them. i have also seen the documents and i share their conclusions: i have given them my confidence at the moment, by voting in favour; but i am prepared to do my best to ensure that they act in the interests of europe and above all of the european businesses and citizens who need to get out of this crisis.
in writing. i voted in favour of the commission's proposal to appoint six members to the single resolution board, the independent authority responsible for managing the resolution of failing banks. this committee, which together with the national authorities has centralised resolution power for the member states, plays a very important role in the proper, effective and consistent functioning of the single resolution mechanism (srm). as provided for in regulation (eu) no 806/2014, and in particular in relation to the senior tasks to be performed, members shall be appointed on the basis of merit, competence, knowledge of banking and financial matters and experience in financial supervision/regulation and resolution of institutions. the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy has been asked to draw up a report on the economic situation in the community.
in writing. ‒ the single resolution board (srb), the second pillar of the banking union, will be responsible for preparing plans for the 'orderly failure' of banks in difficulty, after the ecb, which is responsible for supervision, has signalled the risk of default. after the positive hearings of candidates held in the committee on economic and monetary affairs (econ) in recent weeks, i have decided to approve the appointment of the six members of the single resolution authority for banks.

in writing. council regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 allows the mobilisation of the contingency margin as a last resort tool to respond to unforeseen circumstances. the political agreement on the ceilings for the mff 2014-2020 was reached at european council level in february 2013 and, in the course of subsequent negotiations with the european parliament, the contingency margin was confirmed. the global payment margin does not apply for the year 2014 and therefore the mobilisation of the full contingency margin for 2014 of eur 4 026,7 million remains the only available instrument to address the impact on the budget of unforeseen circumstances occurring after the payment ceilings of the mff have been set and to reduce the significant gap between the level of the authorised payment appropriations and the additional and unforeseen payment needs for the current year. for these reasons i would vote in favour.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of mobilising the contingency margin for 2014 in order to unblock the execution of arrears in cohesion policy payments. despite the strong reservations about the misuse of this margin, which should be used for emergencies and certainly not to meet payments long scheduled in the budget, i can only support this emergency solution, which allows the payment of overdue invoices for a total amount of eur 3 168.2 million, for the benefit of citizens and businesses already exhausted by the impact of the crisis. given that the 2014-2020 programming period started with a payment delay of eur 23.4 billion, i hope that more appropriate instruments will soon be adopted to deal with this paradoxical situation, which only seriously undermines the union's credibility in the eyes of its citizens and the very effectiveness of cohesion policies.

in writing. i voted against. the commission has a spending margin of only eur 0,7 billion, and has therefore proposed to finance the remaining 4 by exceeding the annual ceilings for the financial year 2014 by using the contingency margin. however, the amounts thus mobilised should be fully compensated by a reduction in the ceilings of subsequent years in order to maintain the overall ceilings for 2014-2020. this is essentially an extraordinary measure of anticipation to be used as an extrema ratio. the united kingdom, the netherlands, denmark, finland, austria, sweden, france and germany criticised the commission's proposal, considering it to be legally unfounded and, in any event, premature and inappropriate. on the other side are the net beneficiary states. the compromise solution reached in the trilogue provides for a total amount of eur 3.85 billion, composed of: 0,7 margin of available expenditure; 2,8 use of the contingency margin; 0.35 the commission's proposal to the council for a regulation on the european parliament and council directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work.

in writing. - i would like to thank my colleagues eider gardiazabal rubial and monika hohlmeier for the difficult work they did during 2014 to ensure that europe had an adequate budget. at the end of a long negotiation, which was marked by the failure of the conciliation procedure, an agreement was reached thanks to the sense of responsibility of parliament and the work of the italian presidency. the proposal provides for 145.3 billion in commitment appropriations and 141.2 billion in payment appropriations. the agreement is not what we expected but, given the economic conditions in the member states, it was the best compromise that could be reached. resources for research (horizon 2020), the programmes for the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme), education (erasmus), cohesion and frontex have been safeguarded and increased.
in writing. - i welcome the agreement reached between the commission, the council and parliament on the eu budget for 2015. the tough negotiations dragged on until the last minute led to a more than satisfactory conclusion for parliament, which succeeded in passing the payment plan as one of the main lines of the 2015 budget. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the euro as a currency for the exchange of goods and services. the council's proposed cuts, which would have reduced the margins for investment in view of the delicate economic and financial situation, were also halved.
in writing. on 8 december, after difficult negotiations, parliament, the commission and the council finally reached an agreement on the community budget for 2015. the report, signed by colleagues gardiazabal rubial and hohlmeier, clearly sets out the strengths and weaknesses of the new 2015 spending package. i find particularly agreeable the reference to the need to reform the european union's own resources system, with the aim of finally overcoming the current impasse in the budget negotiations, and to the need to reform efforts in the coming years to reduce unpaid invoices to a sustainable level. in view of these considerations, i felt it was my duty to give my consent to the document.

in writing. - i voted against the new budget of the european union because i strongly believe that the accumulated debts must first be settled and then future trends and investments seriously planned. the agreement reached and the result of the conciliation between parliament and the council must be regarded as a failure, since many of the priorities expressed, such as employment and productive investment, have not been maintained. the council's often intransigent and unrealistic approach has created a vicious circle, which continues to involve severe cuts in the union budget, which then have to be remedied by numerous amending budgets because of the real needs of the member states.

in writing. the list proposed by the european commission on the classification for serious infringements of european road transport rules does not adequately take into account infringements related to illegal cabotage and other important aspects of road safety related to compliance with social rules in the road sector, in particular with regard to social dumping. for these reasons i voted in favour of the objection tabled by the committee on transport to the list. i also think it is of the utmost importance that the commission should propose a new list as soon as possible in order to provide a complete list enabling the member states to sanction the same type of infringement in a uniform manner. the commission will have to show that it really wants to build a social europe capable of combating illegal practices which lead to 'unfair' competition between the different member states. greater compliance with all eu road rules will have an immediate impact in reducing the number of fatalities on our roads and ensure fair competition between european logistics companies.

in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution today, which calls on the commission to withdraw its draft regulation and to present a new list of serious infringements of eu rules which can lead to the loss of the honour of the road haulage operator. the commission's course is dangerous: it has been decided to indicate in the delegated acts the cases in which the carrier loses his good repute and thus the possibility of carrying out his work. if the indication is mandatory, anything not included is allowed, i.e. anything not indicated as serious will not be such as to allow the suspension of the service authorization. the sanctions framework must be common and comprehensive, otherwise there is a risk that individual member states will take individual steps which will end up creating differences in treatment between countries. for example, other rules relating to illegal cabotage, which is a problem in the european union, should also be included in the list as serious infringements. if this is not considered 'serious', it will have social consequences on the business side and for social dumping.

in writing. the list of serious road traffic offences presented by the commission appears to be partial and not exhaustive. the exclusion of cabotage and the failure to ensure the application of social legislation are the major weaknesses. the legislation on driving hours is european and the free market and therefore the possibility of cabotage is european. it follows that any solutions must also be addressed at european level. both illegal cabotage and non-compliance with social and labour standards create potential risks to life, as they are closely linked to poor and degraded living and working standards. the adaptation to european regulations, the opening of borders to the often unfair competition of foreign carriers, the rise in operating costs and the unsustainable taxation are just some of the problems affecting the sector. the aim of europe must be to support road transport, to facilitate the activities of companies in the sector and to simplify bureaucratic procedures in a period, the present one, in which the road transport world is experiencing a widespread and deep crisis.

in writing. i voted against this resolution which would impose on each fuel supplier the burden of individually calculating the ghg intensity of its products depending on the original raw material used to produce them. this is with the stated purpose of discouraging the use of canadian tar sands. therefore, each fuel supplier (whether an sme, a service station owner, a supermarket or an oil company) should have a reporting system that associates each volume of petrol and diesel sold with the original raw material. this is unrealistic and would result in a huge administrative burden for both fuel suppliers and the member states, which are required to monitor. moreover, the most 'underdog' operators could benefit from the practical impossibility of verifying the data declared, to the detriment of the more rigorous operators. finally, eu refineries would see the cost of raw materials increase compared to their competitors in third countries, with a further loss of competitiveness and the consequent possible closure.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, europe has a duty to make every effort to ensure the greatest possible security for its citizens. this guarantee inevitably involves addressing the security challenges that our society faces on a daily basis. while we appreciate the european union's commitment to tackling these challenges, we cannot help but denounce the timid attention paid to a phenomenon which, sometimes subtly, sometimes overtly, is rapidly spreading across the continent. i am referring to the spread of corruption, the activities of criminal organizations, whose first outlet in countries which think they are immune to it is money laundering. i believe that not enough has been done in the fight against the mafia and that we need a collective awareness, which will lead us to take a holistic approach to these issues. the commission's reports, which are very good, must be followed by the facts. and so we are starting to adopt all possible legislative initiatives, from the preventive confiscation of the illicit proceeds of criminal organizations and the discipline of the crime of association with mafia-type criminals to the protection of whistleblowers to combat corruption.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the resolution reiterates that freedom, security and justice are objectives to be pursued in parallel. the new strategy will have to ensure full respect for fundamental rights and principles, which has not always been the case in the past, but it will also have to be an effective strategy and of course subject to exhaustive judicial safeguards. but above all it must be an effective strategy. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to meet its commitments to the united nations. the fight against trafficking in human beings, organised crime, money laundering and corruption should be tackled, including through closer cooperation in criminal matters between states and between eu agencies, greater use of instruments such as joint investigation teams and improved circulation of relevant information, in compliance with the safeguards that will soon be enshrined in the data protection directive. that is why i supported the resolution.
in writing. i am voting in favour of renewing the internal security strategy. the actions cover organised crime, terrorism, cybercrime, border security and disasters.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution today because i welcome the preparation of a new internal security strategy (iss) which must adapt to the new security threats that have emerged in recent years, applying an integrated approach to priority areas such as cyber security, trafficking in human beings, the fight against terrorism and organised crime, money laundering and corruption. it is essential that there is a thorough analysis of new and emerging security threats, which should be carried out by europol in close cooperation with the other relevant union bodies and member states. i would ask the commission to assess the current instruments in the field of internal security and to analyse the gaps in them. as regards the worrying increase in eu citizens travelling to conflict areas to join terrorist organisations and subsequently returning to the eu, i am convinced that this phenomenon creates new types of risks to the internal security of the union, which must be tackled with determination through a multidimensional approach.
in writing. the challenges we face in this era also see the eu as a model for something that is seen as evil in other parts of the world. the efforts of individual member states to ensure their internal security must therefore be coordinated and perhaps made synergistic by the common objective of preserving the safety of european citizens. i voted in favour of this resolution because it has been able to argue this simple principle.
in writing. - the current geopolitical situation is of particular concern because of various conflicts and upheavals involving many countries in the eu's neighbourhood. in addition, many of today's security challenges have become cross-border and cross-sectoral, beyond the immediate and effective response capabilities of individual member states: a common european approach is therefore needed. i hope that the new internal security strategy (iss) for 2015-2019 will be forward-looking and strategic, easily adaptable to changing situations, but above all capable of responding effectively to the many emerging threats, such as the fight against terrorism, trafficking in human beings, organised crime, money laundering and corruption. i also hope that judicial cooperation in criminal matters will be developed, as will mutual trust between member states. it should not be forgotten that the european parliament, as a full actor in the field of security policy and in accordance with the provisions of the treaty of lisbon, will have the full right to express its position on priorities and actions in the field.
in writing. the news is telling us what urgent issues need to be prioritised in the new internal security strategy. i voted in favour of this resolution because, firstly, we must improve our capacity to analyse natural hazards. the union should work on a credible early warning mechanism. the commission will also be making a special effort to combat violence against women and children: there are still too many cases of violence. it is also clear that the threats are now global and do not concern individual regions or even member states. europe is the victim of external threats and at the same time we are witnessing more and more cases of european citizens embracing the causes of wars across borders. without forgetting that our citizens who are engaged in voluntary or humanitarian work abroad are the first victims of terrible violence. a truly effective action plan is therefore needed, which takes account of the internal and external dimensions of security. we must join forces: the european parliament has already made a number of proposals to the council and the commission. our citizens have a right to feel safe. it is the perception of security that our citizens have that we have to deal with. this is where mistrust or faith in europe comes from.
in writing. the lisbon treaty gives our institution the role of a full actor in the field of security policy, as well as the power to participate actively in the definition of priorities in order to achieve a comprehensive, targeted and effective eu security policy. in this resolution, parliament takes note of the fact that the security situation in europe has changed radically in recent years and that threats are more diverse than in the past. in the light of these considerations, we urged the commission to ensure that the new internal security strategy for 2015-2019 is forward-looking and strategic and easily adaptable to changing situations. therefore, it focuses not only on existing security threats but also on emerging ones such as cybersecurity, human trafficking and the fight against terrorism and interlinked problems such as organised crime, money laundering and corruption. the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms is a fundamental point for us: all preventive policies and repressive measures must strike the right balance in order to preserve freedom, security and justice.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the report by mr claude moraes because the motion for a resolution which has been tabled emphasises the need to carry out a detailed analysis of the current threats to european security in order to provide adequate protection for all community citizens. the commission is also proposing that the new internal security strategy (iss) should focus on external threats as well as those emerging within the community's borders. i also agree with the reference to the need to strike a fair balance between preventive and repressive policies in order to guarantee freedom, justice and security.
in writing. - the european union needs a dynamic and effective security system that can adapt rapidly to international changes. the threats to the security of our countries come mainly from outside. the fight against terrorism and the continuing threat of attacks unfortunately brings to the agenda of this house a subject which must make us reflect on possible solutions in a particular international context in which the eu certainly remains the safest place in the world as a whole. the security threats must therefore be addressed with a strong common strategy, which is why i support the renewal of the eu's internal security strategy.
in writing. the internal security strategy (iss) for the period 2010-14 is coming to an end. the new ssi, valid for the period 2015-2019, is being prepared. the motion for a resolution tabled by the libe committee, of which i am a member, stresses the need for a thorough analysis of the current threats to european security in order to offer all community citizens adequate protection. the document calls for the new ssi to focus not only on potential external threats but also on those emerging within the community's borders. the reference to the need to strike the right balance between preventive policies and repressive measures, so that freedom, security and justice are adequately preserved, is particularly welcome. my vote in favour of the resolution is based on a full sharing of its contents.

in writing. - the homeland security strategy and the proposed resolution seem to me to be a program that mimics american counterterrorism in too many ways. it is self-celebration and is run by closed agencies (essentially europol), without consulting the bodies that should be entrusted with the definition of threats to the union: the council, national parliaments and the european parliament. the resolution also deals almost exclusively with repressive measures. there's almost nothing about prevention. the word 'fundamental rights' barely appears in the 'declarative' paragraphs of the resolution and without citing specific articles of the charter. in the meantime, member states remain free to do what they want, with initiatives on a purely voluntary basis or seemingly common actions such as 'mos maiorum', for which the states are answerable to no one. for these reasons i voted against this resolution.

in writing. today i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a comprehensive eu approach to migration, in the light of the urgency of implementing the comprehensive strategy for cooperation with third countries. in 2014, more than 3,000 people died in the mediterranean in a desperate attempt to cross it for a better life. as if that were not enough, these flows have become a breeding ground for crime, which has given rise to a veritable human trafficking aimed at exploiting irregular migration. the european union must make every effort to save the lives of these people and to ensure that all member states comply with international agreements on rescue at sea, by showing humanitarian solidarity and a real commitment by financing and contributing to the operations of the new joint programme 'triton' coordinated by frontex.
in writing. this text is very important for italy and i voted in favour of it because it once again enshrines the principle of solidarity between states in the reception of migrants. italy, as a country situated on the main migration routes, has no human choice but to accept. however, in a system of shared borders, it is right that everyone does his part not only in terms of providing resources but also in terms of absorbing labour from other countries. this is a subject which must be closely monitored so that subsequent legislative resolutions take due account of our position.
in writing. - how much longer is this gonna go on? how long will we see hundreds of men, women and children arriving on our shores or dying at sea? italy has been crying out for years for help. the reception centres are collapsing and the landings are only increasing. on the other side of the italian coast there are only countries in the grip of serious political instability. this requires concrete action, in particular strong criminal sanctions against human trafficking and the smuggling of migrants, both into and within the eu, and the launching of resettlement programmes that can benefit from european funding. but it's not enough. we need a fair distribution of responsibility, we need solidarity between member states and we do not want to leave the countries affected by landings, such as italy, to shoulder all the responsibility. i can only vote in favour of the motion for a resolution because it sets out a series of actions to be taken. but we know that the problem to be solved is upstream: the european union must strengthen its partnerships with transit countries such as libya, but above all it must help restore stability and democracy in those countries still affected by serious conflicts.
in writing. according to the international organization for migration, at least 3,072 people died in the mediterranean in 2014. every effort should be made to save the lives of persons in danger and to ensure that member states comply with their international obligations in the field of rescue at sea, in order to develop a comprehensive strategy for cooperation with third countries, in particular those in sub-saharan africa, north africa and the middle east, with regard to humanitarian, financial and political assistance, including in the field of law enforcement, and to seek clarification on the role of regional protection, resettlement and return policies, including migration management agreements between countries of origin and transit. in order to deal with the root causes of migration, i could only vote in favour of this resolution. i am voting in favour because third countries must respect international law on the rescue of lives at sea and must ensure the protection of refugees and respect for fundamental rights.
in writing. at least 3,419 migrants have lost their lives in the mediterranean sea since january. with conflicts in libya, syria and iraq, europe has become the main destination for migrants by sea, and the mediterranean has become the "world's deadliest route". i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the european union must show more solidarity with the member states which are hosting the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers, while at the same time taking its fair share of responsibility in relation to immigration to prevent further loss of life at sea.
in writing. the resolution is not controversial and is in fact in the direction we want of a global approach, not just italian, to the issue of immigration. i shall vote in favour, although it will most likely be completely useless, since it will be yet another appeal without a real response from the member states.
in writing. the broad support of this house for the resolution is a confirmation of the need to develop a comprehensive approach to migration. it is our responsibility to ensure safe and legal access to the asylum system in our territories, while also seeking to find new channels of legal migration. we have seen an exponential increase in the number of deaths in the mediterranean in recent years and have therefore called loudly for every effort to be made to avoid further tragedies at sea. operation mare nostrum has been commendable and recognised by all member states; the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. we have also made it necessary that the search and rescue obligations be effectively respected and that appropriate funding be allocated to this end in the medium and long term. in the light of the recent scandals concerning the use of funds, including european funds, intended for emergency management, in particular for actions concerning migration and asylum, we have called for a careful analysis of how these funds are spent, also in order to avoid the repetition in the future of scandalous and criminal forms of appropriation to the detriment of the most vulnerable categories.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the report by mr claude moraes because it fully reflects the idea that the european union should implement a series of measures aimed at defining a holistic approach to the problem of illegal migration. today's vote makes it clear that the position we have taken over the last few months is broadly shared by our colleagues in the european parliament. the management of this policy must be shared by all the eu states and the results achieved during the italian presidency are proof of this. we cannot allow organized crime to kill more human beings on the crossings of hope.
in writing. the tragedy of lampedusa still weighs like a stone on the conscience of public opinion and the political class. although more than a year has passed since that terrible event, the european union is still struggling to provide a plausible answer to the problem of immigration to the community's shores. my support for this resolution is a true act of conscience. it fully reflects the idea that speculation and exploitation linked to the phenomenon of migration must be definitively prevented by implementing a shared and responsible strategy involving all the member states of this union. the resolution accurately reflects the need to act, in a coordinated and responsible manner, in the name of the will to put an end to a slaughter that civil society can no longer afford to be complicit in. i particularly appreciated the reference in the document to the need to support member states which are receiving a greater number of refugees and asylum seekers.
in writing. we welcome the motion for a resolution calling for a unified european approach to migration and for greater efforts to prevent further loss of life at sea. it is now imperative that all the member states assume collective responsibility for a phenomenon of such immense proportions, which costs thousands of lives every year and which has hitherto been the priority of the only european border states, such as italy. in addition to a new shared approach to migration, we stress the need to examine the overall strategy for cooperation with third countries and the obligation for these countries to respect fundamental rights and to ensure the protection of refugees.
in writing. i vote in favour of the resolution on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a holistic approach by the european union to the migration problem. there is a need for a fair sharing of responsibility towards the member states which receive the highest number of refugees and asylum seekers and there is also a need to combat human trafficking and to establish a system of sanctions against trafficking and smuggling by member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a comprehensive eu approach to migration, as i believe that migration promotes contact between different ethnic groups, religions and cultures. in the past, the cultural differences between the two shores of the mediterranean were perceived as a source of mutual contamination. today, however, the mediterranean is seen as a mere frontier to be patrolled to prevent the risks of irregular and disorderly immigration. migration should instead be seen as an opportunity, because the european countries are facing a demographic decline and the high birth rate of the populations of the southern shore of the mediterranean is a wealth for europe because it would make it possible to fill the imbalance in our demographic pyramid. europe needs immigrant labour because of its ageing demographic structure. concerted action is needed to make the most of the migration opportunity. the burden should not be borne exclusively by the member states bordering on europe: the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states.
in writing. reiterating the importance of these policies in the mediterranean and the need for a final solution, i will only express my favourable opinion on the text if the amendments proposed by my group are accepted.
in writing. i welcome the resolution on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a holistic eu approach to the migration problem. this is a balanced text which we have agreed in the libe committee following a constructive debate to which i have contributed. the approach is humanitarian and pragmatic: the principle of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility is invoked towards the member states receiving the highest number of refugees and asylum seekers in absolute or relative terms. the joint undertaking will also be responsible for the implementation of the eu-us joint undertaking for the protection of the marine environment, which is a joint undertaking of the european union and the member states. the need to combat human trafficking and to establish a system of sanctions by the member states against trafficking and smuggling, and the need to establish cooperation with third countries affected by the migratory phenomenon, in order to try to identify together the right strategies on return and asylum, is emphasized. finally, it is important to underline that there is a proposal to find concrete solutions on resettlement, including flows management agreements.
in writing. - the resolution is being drafted in a very difficult political and institutional context: the post-stockholm council programme and the initiatives proposed by the commission focus on the fight against irregular immigration. in view of the recent adoption of the asylum package (2013), there are no tools or initiatives to review its shortcomings. it is at this point that several political groups (gue/ngl, alde, s&d, green and the 5 stars in the efdd) conceived the idea of a resolution on the mediterranean which would allow for a thorough reflection on immigration and asylum issues, without simply waiting for the (very weak or absent) reforms proposed by the commission. the idea is to give the european parliament a real 'proactive' power in this field, by giving the libe commission a leading role and the financial resources to be able to do so. that is why paragraph 12 of the motion is so important: i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. i therefore abstained, because the necessary saving of the paragraph has nevertheless involved some heavy compromises with the ppe and the ecr.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it is important to develop a comprehensive approach to migration, strengthening the fair sharing of responsibility and solidarity with the member states which receive the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers. the eu and its member states must make every effort to prevent further tragedies at sea and it is necessary to provide appropriate funding for search and rescue activities. it is essential to examine a possible overall strategy of cooperation with third countries, in particular those in sub-saharan africa, north africa and the middle east, as regards humanitarian assistance, and an analysis of how funds allocated to actions concerning migration and asylum, border control, the fight against the smuggling of migrants and trafficking in human beings are spent is essential in order to target union resources effectively. strong sanctions must be established against trafficking in human beings and migrants, both to and within the european union, and against persons or groups exploiting vulnerable migrants, by finding new channels of legal migration. for the reasons i have outlined, i therefore supported the report.
in writing. with this resolution, the european union seems to finally acknowledge the tragic situation regarding migration flows in the mediterranean sea, which in the first nine months of 2014 alone has claimed at least three thousand lives as a result of desperate attempts to cross. europe has shown no solidarity in dealing with this problem, leaving italy to deal with this humanitarian, social and criminal emergency on its own. immigration has also become a very lucrative business, based on the utter desperation of people willing to leave everything (or little) they had to seek a better future elsewhere. hopes are often dashed, and sometimes they are cut off along with the very existence of these individuals who remain victims of injustice, cruelty and human greed. the solution is not easy, but the approach must certainly be changed at the outset, since the path chosen so far has proved unsuccessful. europe must be the protagonist in all this and cannot continue to pretend that these are national issues linked to a single country: i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this.
in writing. - immigration, particularly irregular immigration, should be a growing concern for the european union. not only because of the difficulties member states have in receiving migrants, but because of the migrants themselves, who often end up as victims of unscrupulous traffickers. i support the strong call for a comprehensive approach to the problem: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the situation in the baltic sea is not worsened. the numbers of the disappointing "mare nostrum" operation, launched by italy, bear witness to this: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i hope that the council will take them up. i also agree with the request for an analysis to be carried out to see how the funds allocated to internal affairs have been spent on measures relating to migration and asylum, border control, the fight against trafficking in human beings and human trafficking and return. i hope that the competent national authorities will respond to the call to 'show solidarity' by contributing to prevention and support operations, in full awareness that we are talking about a 'european' problem.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am speaking on behalf of many associations which are denouncing the khartoum process and the outsourcing of border controls for the purpose of refusal of entry in breach of european law. they are particularly afraid of agreements with the eritrean dictatorship, from which 30% of the 150 000 refugees who have arrived in italy are now fleeing. we have already seen how the export of democracy is a disaster, a fraud. the export of migrants to concentration camps in eritrea or sudan will also produce disasters and frauds. the khartoum process is described by the italian presidency as a historic leap forward. the leap is towards new agreements with transit countries to block departures, under the pretext of outsourcing the right of asylum. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the protection of the environment.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the khartoum process has revealed the pitfalls and hypocrisy of a difficult cooperation based on a fragile framework. the strategy that is being proposed to control the flow of migrants from east africa appears to be lacking in human rights protection. on the one hand, it declares its intention to combat the activities of criminal networks which profit from migrants and human trafficking; on the other hand, there is dialogue and involvement with repressive, bloodthirsty and freedom-threatening regimes, which are the main cause of migration flows. just think of eritrea, a de facto military dictatorship, with thousands of political opponents in prison, or sudan, where genocide and crimes against humanity have been committed for decades. other governments, such as ethiopia, egypt and somalia, have also shown themselves to be lax in respecting human rights. eritrea and libya have never ratified the 1951 geneva convention relating to the status of refugees, despite stating their willingness to promote cooperation on asylum and international protection on the basis of the principles of international law, by referring to the convention itself. libya, one of the countries where thousands of migrants are concentrated trying to reach europe, did not even participate in the meeting in rome on 28 november. the joint declaration of the khartoum process was signed on that occasion, with the aim of setting up reception centres outside europe's borders. the cases of asylum seekers should be examined here, with a view to their subsequent resettlement in europe. rather than tackling the causes of migration, the aim seems to be to find agreements on how to deal with migrants before they reach europe, risking a repeat of the libyan-italian agreement between gaddafi and berlusconi. there is a fear that if the reception centres are set up in countries where there is a serious democratic and civil emergency, they may, in the absence of adequate controls, become ghettos and refugee camps where the protection of human rights cannot be guaranteed. a comprehensive approach to immigration is needed, aiming not only at unhypocritical cooperation with third countries but also at ensuring safe and legal pathways and amending european asylum legislation, with particular regard to the most vulnerable, such as children.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the enormous flow of migrants facing europe makes it necessary to adopt new multilateral cooperation mechanisms with the countries of origin and transit of migrants, towards proposals that should be sustainable and lasting. no state, no organization can provide effective answers on its own. a plan must be based on dialogue between states and common resources, but above all on political will, also in order to rescue thousands of migrants from the hands of the merchants of death. we will never be able to really tackle the causes of this flow of refugees unless we forcefully raise the issue of respect for human rights in the countries of origin of migrants and above all within a comprehensive and holistic approach to immigration. for this reason i have reservations about the final conclusion drawn in the khartoum case. i am referring to the possibility of setting up refugee camps, which could be used for reception or detention, and here we need to be clear about the asylum seeker, who must always be accompanied by a process of verifying that human rights are being respected and, above all, by adherence to all international conventions. what will be the role of the european parliament? the memory of libya's agreements with the italian government is still alive. we would not under any circumstances be prepared to accept such a violation of human rights. today we all know what the gaddafi government has been called.

in writing. the regulation of the special incentive scheme for sustainable development and good governance (spg+), to which the republic of the philippines has applied to participate, sets out the obligation of third countries to implement the objectives adopted by regional fisheries organisations, one of which is the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. i voted today in favour of this resolution which does not grant gsp+ status to the philippines, because the republic of the philippines is considered a non-cooperating third country in the fight against illegal fishing. i think it is essential to stress the absolute need to ensure the coherence and credibility of european policies, in order to avoid discrimination and unfair competition for european fishermen and to protect european consumers. the issue of illegal fishing is certainly one that applies to every country and we cannot set a precedent. if we want to ask our fishermen to make efforts on sustainability, we cannot turn a blind eye to other countries, like the philippines, which do not respect the rules.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on the application of a system of generalized tariff preferences to the philippines. i agree with the objections to the commission's delegated regulation, particularly in relation to the human rights violations in that country, as stated in the report of the un special rapporteur, in particular on human rights trafficking. i also agree with the assessment that the concept of the responsibility of the marketing state should be developed more fully as a means of closing markets to iuu fishery products.
in writing. i voted against the objection put forward by some colleagues to deny the philippines the special incentive arrangement for sustainable development and good governance (spg+). i believe that the granting of the gsp+ scheme to the philippines, on the basis of compliance with the criteria set out in the recent reform of the european system of generalised preferences (gsp), can be a serious test for the manila government and a significant encouragement from us to continue with even greater conviction on the path taken to improve the implementation of international conventions on respect for human rights, labour rights and, in this particular case, to curb the phenomenon of illegal fishing in the country. it is equally clear that the granting of the special gsp+ scheme to the philippines will require the eu to keep the philippine government's commitments under constant review and, in the event of non-compliance, the decision taken today can and must be reviewed.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the commission delegated regulation of 19 august 2014 amending annex iii to regulation (eu) no 978/2012 of the european parliament and of the council applying a scheme of generalised tariff preferences to the philippines. i believe that the european commission's comments on the violations of fundamental human rights in the philippines are particularly worrying and therefore call for an amendment to the current text.
in writing. on 28 february 2014, the commission received a request from the republic of the philippines to participate in the gsp (general system of preferences). i have decided to support this resolution because i fully share the view that this request can only be accepted if the philippines makes a concrete commitment to eliminate illegal fishing. the basis for this is the assumption that the commission is not empowered to grant preferential access to the european market for fishery products from the philippines without a guarantee of their legal origin.
in writing. i regret today's vote because i believe that the gsp+ request of the republic of the philippines should not be accepted at this time, given the non-cooperative state in the fight against illegal fishing. the eu cannot allow preferential access to the european market for fishery products without a guarantee of their legal origin. we cannot set a precedent for this, especially in view of the efforts we have asked our fishermen to make in the area of sustainability. despite the signs of progress in this country, we cannot ignore a whole series of problems and violations which concern in particular the problem of trafficking in persons, especially women and children, for the purpose of exploitation of labour in various sectors including agriculture, construction and fisheries. i hope, however, that if the yellow card turns into a red card, the decision will be taken to abolish the gsp+ system.
in writing. we voted against this motion for a resolution on the application of the generalised system of preferences plus (gsp+) to the philippines, because on the one hand we believe that, as the philippines has ratified the 27 un/ilo conventions required for the granting of the programme, there is no formal obstacle and, on the other hand, we are convinced of the usefulness of gsp+ in supporting the economic, political and social development of the philippines. in addition, it should be noted that the gsp+ mechanism has recently been renewed and made more stringent, with new sanction possibilities that may go as far as withdrawal of the programme. politically, the granting of the programme is the most effective way of improving the situation in the country, which was further complicated by typhoon hagugit in early december, and of having the possibility of influencing certain strategic choices through monitoring and sanctioning mechanisms. it should also be remembered that the granting of gsp+ is not a gift, but only the starting point of a long-term process aimed at improving economically, politically and socially a state in difficulty.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is still taking place in the philippines, which is guaranteed the system of generalised tariff preferences with the eu. the philippine government is called upon to prevent and eradicate this practice, not only to ensure environmental sustainability, but also to protect competition and protect european consumers. in view of the fact that the philippines should be suspended from gsp+ status until it demonstrates that it is actively cooperating in the fight against illegal fishing, i would like to vote in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour because i believe it is right to protect the activity of european fishing vessels from unfair competition from fishermen from countries which do not respect our own rules on fishing and the exploitation of the labour force.
in writing. before granting the gsp+ tariff preferences to the philippines, i believe it is important to ensure that the country is actively cooperating with the eu in the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. we cannot allow honest fishermen and fish producers to suffer unfair competition from the import and sale of tuna and other fish caught illegally in philippine waters. first of all, we must give the commission, and in particular dg mare, time to clarify and complete the inquiry which is under way. let us not forget that the fight against illegal fishing is one of the cornerstones of the european union's action to prevent the overexploitation of fish stocks, to safeguard marine habitats and thus to ensure sustainable fishing. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will then be able to take a decision on the matter. when the philippines demonstrates that it has made real progress in adopting effective management and control measures to tackle the problem of illegal fishing, we can reassess the request for further tariff concessions.
